# Session: L244 fixed -- image atomics widened beyond Plain2D

**Fixed and committed.** `dEQP-VK.image.atomic_operations.*` targeted ops
(add/sub/and/or/xor/smax/smin/umax/umin/compare_exchange) now 0 Fail across
every shape, down from a 96/782-Fail single-op repro.

## What was wrong

1. `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`'s `hasOnlySupportedStorageImageUses` scoped
   every image atomic to `Plain2D` only -- `Plain1D`/`Array1D`/`Array2D`/
   `StorageCubeArray`/`Plain3D` all got rejected outright.
2. That rejection poisoned the *entire function* containing the atomic
   (`UnsupportedOps.cpp`'s "one unsupported op poisons every handle in its
   function" behavior) -- the initial repro's error message pointed at an
   unrelated resource handle for exactly this reason. Read the code, not
   just the error text, to find the real cause.
3. `lowerImageAccesses`'s atomic dispatch was hardcoded to `(X, Y)` --
   would have needed widening too even once the gate above was fixed.

## What changed (4 commits, each already pushed to this branch)

1. `FeMeRuntimeCPU.c`: 44 new `femeCpuImageAtomic{Op}{Shape}` runtime
   functions (11 ops x 4 shape families) + 4 new address helpers.
2. `ImageCalls.h`/`.cpp`: 44 new `ImageCallKind` values + matching
   `create*`/name/`FunctionType`/`matchImageCall` boilerplate. Also updated
   `matchImageCall`'s `AllKinds` table -- easy to forget, and skipping it
   would have left the new atomics correctly *executing* but incorrectly
   *masked* under `SIMDize.cpp`'s SIMD-lane widening (silent correctness
   bug, not a build failure).
3. `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`: widened both the use-checker and the
   dispatch switch. **Watch out**: my first attempt at this edit used
   `content.index(start_marker)` on a non-unique string and clobbered a
   *different* atomic dispatch block (the texel-buffer one, a different
   function entirely) instead of the image one. Caught it because the
   build errored on `Shape`/`ImageIndex`/`X` being out of scope in that
   function. Reverted the whole file and redid it with a longer, verified-
   unique anchor. Lesson: for large multi-hundred-line replacements in a
   file with structurally similar code blocks, always grep-count the anchor
   across the *whole* file first, not just assume `.count() == 1` from a
   smaller nearby search.
4. Docs: `Roadmap.md` (L244 struck through, new `L247` filed for the
   residual), `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new section).

Also: my first draft of the dispatch-switch widening used C preprocessor
`#define`/`##` token-pasting tricks to avoid duplicating each op's call
site per shape. It compiled and would have worked, but it's the kind of
cleverness that makes code harder to read for no real benefit -- reverted
and rewrote as plain nested switches (op x shape), matching the existing
file's style. Prefer boring code.

# Session: L247 fixed (atomic inc/dec lowering) + L248 fixed (depth-write gating) -- new L249 filed

**Two fixes landed and committed.** `dEQP-VK.image.atomic_operations.
{inc,dec}.*` now 0 Fail (was 240 Fail). `dEQP-VK.pipeline.*.depth.
format.*.depth_test_disabled.depth_write_enabled` now 0 Fail (was 6
Fail, found via this session's own widened CTS sample).

## Fix 1: L247, atomic inc/dec (~1 hour)

`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` had no lowering pattern for
`spirv.AtomicIIncrement`/`AtomicIDecrement` at all -- confirmed by
grep, not guessed. Root cause: these two ops derive from
`SPIRV_AtomicUpdateOp` (no `value` operand -- SPIR-V defines the ±1
amount implicitly), unlike every other RMW op's
`SPIRV_AtomicUpdateWithValueOp` base (has an explicit `value` operand
the existing `AtomicRMWPattern` forwards). So the existing pattern
genuinely could not be reused as-is.

Added `AtomicIncDecPattern<SPIRVOpTy, BinOp>`: materializes a constant
`1` of the op's result type, forwards it into an ordinary
`LLVM::AtomicRMWOp` (`add`/`sub`). Reuses every downstream
`AtomicAdd*`/`AtomicSub*` entry point `L244` already built last
session -- zero new `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`/`ImageCalls`/runtime
code needed, since the resulting IR is indistinguishable from an
explicit `AtomicIAdd`/`AtomicISub` with `value == 1`.

Registered the two new pattern instantiations in the pattern list,
added a lit-test block (`@atomic_inc_dec`) confirming both lower to
`llvm.atomicrmw add`/`sub ptr, i32 1`. First lit-test attempt failed
(`FileCheck` matched an unrelated `constant(1)` from an earlier
`handlefrombinding` call argument) -- fixed by anchoring the check on
the `getpointer` call first, then the constant, instead of matching
the bare constant pattern in isolation.

Verified: `atomic_operations.{inc,dec}.*` (880 cases) 240 Pass / 0
Fail. Full `atomic_operations.*` group (6209 cases) re-sampled: 1320
Pass / 0 Fail, no regressions.

## Fix 2: L248, depth-write gating (~1.5 hours, found via broader CTS sample)

Widened `dEQP-VK.pipeline.*` at 1-in-200 fixed-seed fraction (~5797
cases, the overdue `L228(e)`/`(f)` broader sample) -- surfaced exactly
1 new failure: `fast_linked_library.depth.format.d32_sfloat_s8_uint.
depth_test_disabled.depth_write_enabled`. Confirmed it reproduces
identically across every applicable format and every
`PipelineConstructionType` (`monolithic` fails the same as
`fast_linked_library`) -- 6 Fail total.

Root cause, found by reading `Executor.cpp`'s `testDepthStencil`:
depth writes were gated only on `Depth.WriteEnable`, ignoring
`Depth.TestEnable` entirely. Checked the actual spec text (not just
intuition) before touching code: `depthWriteEnable` only takes effect
*when* `depthTestEnable` is also true -- depth writes are always
disabled when the depth test itself is disabled. FeMe's `DepthPass`
already defaulted to `true` when the test was disabled (correctly
modeling "the test always passes"), but that always-true result then
incorrectly reached the write step regardless of whether a real test
had actually run.

One-line fix: `if (Depth.TestEnable && Depth.WriteEnable)` instead of
`if (Depth.WriteEnable)`. Added a mirrored unit test right next to the
existing `DepthWriteDisabledLeavesAttachmentUnchanged` test.

Verified: full `pipeline.*.depth.format.*` group (16860 cases) now
8433 Pass / 0 Fail (was 6 Fail). No regressions anywhere else in the
group.

# Session: L249 fixed (GPL linked-pipeline subpass bug) + L245 fixed (sampleCounts over-reporting) -- new L250 filed

**Two fixes landed and committed.** `dEQP-VK.pipeline.fast_linked_
library.depth.depth_only.subpasses_postpass`'s genuine `DeviceLost` is
gone (12/12 Pass on its group). `dEQP-VK.api.info.image_format_
properties{,2}.*`'s 65-case `sampleCounts` failure bucket is gone
(2372/2372 Pass).

## Fix 1: L249, GPL linked-pipeline subpass bug (~2 hours)

Started from last session's hypothesis ("likely a hang, needs a
runtime trace") -- it was wrong. `gdb -batch -ex run -ex "thread apply
all bt"` showed the process exits cleanly in seconds, no hang.
`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` found the real cause immediately:
`vkQueueSubmit: the bound pipeline has 1 color attachment(s) but the
render target has 0`. Lesson for next `DeviceLost` triage: **try
`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` before hunting for a hang** -- a
`DeviceLost` at `vkWaitForFences` is just how FeMe surfaces any
`executeCommandBuffer` error via `Device::markLost`, not a signal the
bug is runtime-execution-related.

Root cause: `synthesizeLinkedGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo`
(`GraphicsPipeline.cpp`) builds the final `VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo`
for a `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library` pure-link call. It already
inherited `Result.renderPass` from a linked library when the link
call's own `CreateInfo.renderPass` was null, but had no matching
fallback for `Result.subpass` -- so `Result.subpass` stayed at `0`
(the pure-link call's own zero-initialized value) even when
`Result.renderPass` was correctly inherited from a library targeting
subpass 1. Fixed by pairing `Result.subpass` with `Result.renderPass`
in the same fallback branch, matching the sibling function
`foldLinkedLibraryState`'s existing `RenderPass`/`Subpass` pairing.

Added regression unit test `LinksSubpassFromLibraryNotJustRenderPass`;
confirmed it fails pre-fix via `git stash`, passes post-fix.

Verified: `fast_linked_library.depth.depth_only.*` (12 cases) 12/12
Pass. 10-minute-bounded `fast_linked_library.*` sample (7600 cases):
only pre-existing, unrelated `blend.dual_source.*` failures (22 cases,
not this fix's scope).

## Fix 2: L245, sampleCounts over-reporting (~30 minutes, carried over many sessions)

Picked this up because it was flagged "quick" several sessions running
and kept getting bumped. Root cause matched the prior session's own
hypothesis exactly: `supportedSampleCounts` (`Image.cpp`) intersected
`usage` against per-usage device limits (e.g.
`sampledImageColorSampleCounts` = `1|2|4|8`) unconditionally, without
checking whether the *format* could be rendered to at all.
Multisampling is a render-target capability -- a format lacking both
`VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT` and
`_DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_BIT` (e.g. `A2B10G10R10_SINT_PACK32`) can't
support >1 sample under any usage, matching the CTS's own check.

One early-return fix: if the format's features name neither attachment
bit, return `VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT` immediately.

Verified: `api.info.image_format_properties{,2}.*` (2372 cases)
2372/0 Pass/Fail (was 65 Fail). `dEQP-VK.image.*` 1-in-50 sample (8846
cases): 0 regressions.

**One fix landed and committed.** `dEQP-VK.pipeline.fast_linked_

## Fix: L250, over-strict draw-time depth/stencil-attachment check (~1.5 hours)

Applied last session's own L249 lesson again, first try:
`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` immediately surfaced "the bound
pipeline tests/writes depth but the render target has no depth
attachment" at `vkQueueSubmit` -- not a hang, a fast synchronous
rejection.

CTS source (`vktPipelineMultisampleTests.cpp`) confirmed the case is
spec-legal: render pass has no depth attachment; pipeline marks depth
test/write dynamic and explicitly disables both
(`vkCmdSetDepthTestEnable/WriteEnable(..., VK_FALSE)`) before the draw.

Root cause: `GraphicsPipeline::needsDepthAttachment()`/
`needsStencilAttachment()` (`GraphicsPipeline.h`) treated *any* dynamic
depth/stencil-enable state as automatically needing an attachment,
ignoring the actual dynamic value -- same bug class as `L241`'s
creation-time VUID check, but a distinct draw-time check `L241`'s own
audit didn't cover (scoped to `GraphicsPipeline.cpp`'s creation path
only). Fixed by having both methods take the current
`DynamicGraphicsState` and resolve dynamic-override-vs-static exactly
like `buildExecutorPipeline` already does for every other dynamic bit.

New regression test `NeedsDepthAttachmentConsultsDynamicValueNotJustDynamism`;
confirmed it fails when the pre-fix logic is restored (same new
signature, verified via a temporary in-place edit + rebuild rather than
`git stash`, since the fix and the test share the same signature
change and can't be split cleanly with stash), passes with the real
fix.

Verified: originally-failing case now Pass. `pipeline.*multisample*`
(63561 cases): 165 pre-existing failures, none depth/stencil-related.
`pipeline.*.depth.*` (39686 cases): 0 Fail. `FeMeVulkanTests`: 760/760.
`check-feme`: 3389/61/0. `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: 483/32/207, unchanged.

## Commits this session

1. `[Vulkan][FeMe] L250: needsDepthAttachment/needsStencilAttachment must consult dynamic value` -- source fix + regression test.
2. `[Vulkan][FeMe] L250: update roadmap and CTS report` -- docs.
3. This `agent_thoughts.md` entry (separate commit, per standing instructions).

## Fix: L228(c), vkCmdClearAttachments multi-layer bug (~2 hours)

Re-ran `dEQP-VK.api.image_clearing.*multiple_layers*sample_count_4*`
(882 cases): 272 Fail, all in `core.clear_color_attachment.
multiple_layers.*sample_count_4` (`vkCmdClearAttachments`, not
`clear_color_image`). Isolated the two dimensions:
`multiple_layers`-without-MSAA also failed (not an MSAA-interaction
bug); `single_layer`-with-MSAA also failed, but with a different
`(0,0,0,0)` symptom -- split out as a separate bug (`L228(k)`) rather
than blocking this fix on it.

Root cause: `ImageOps.cpp`'s `clearAttachmentRects` computed a single
shared layer mask (`ViewMask ? ViewMask : 1u`) *outside* the whole
`VkClearRect` loop. Outside multiview this was always exactly `1u` --
one iteration at layer 0 -- so every clear silently ignored each
rect's own `baseArrayLayer`/`layerCount` and only ever touched layer
0.

Fixed by moving the layer iteration *inside* the per-rect loop:
multiview still uses the subpass's view mask (unchanged); non-
multiview now iterates `[rect.baseArrayLayer, rect.baseArrayLayer +
rect.layerCount)` from that specific rect. Extracted the per-layer
write logic into a local `ClearLayer` lambda shared by both branches.

New regression test `DrawTest.
ClearAttachmentsClearsEveryLayerNamedByItsOwnRect`; confirmed via
`git stash` A/B that it fails without the fix (layers 1/2 stay black)
and passes with it.

Verified: `dEQP-VK.api.image_clearing.core.clear_color_attachment.
multiple_layers.*` (2499 cases) now 127 Fail (down from 272), and
every remaining failure is exclusively a `sample_count_{2,4,8}` MSAA
case -- 0 non-MSAA multi-layer failures remain. `FeMeVulkanTests`:
761/761 (was 760/760). `check-feme`: 3390/61/0 (was 3389/61/0).
`check-hlsl-feme-vk`: unchanged, 483/32/207.

# Session: L251 fixed (two bugs) + L252 fixed + L253 audit closed

**Next action for the next session**: pick up `L228(k)` (single-layer-MSAA
`(0,0,0,0)` clear-attachments bug) or item 3/4 from this session's own
request list (`L227(d)`/`L228(b)`, or widening the broader-than-
tessellation CTS sample). Both are ready to start cold, no setup needed.

## What got fixed (in order)

1. **`L251` bug 1 (~1 hour): `R10G10B10A2_SINT` fixture-format crash.**
   `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` found it on the first try: `ImageFixture.cpp`
   had a diagnostic name for this format but no real `getFormatInfo`/
   `packClearColor`/`unpackColor` support, so any real clear/copy hit a fatal
   error that surfaces as `DeviceLost`. Fixed by adding the missing cases
   (mirroring `_UINT`/`_SNORM` siblings). Caught and fixed one incidental bug
   along the way: casting a negative `double` to `uint32_t` is undefined
   behavior -- route through `int32_t` first.

2. **`L251` bug 2 (~1.5 hours): clear-value misread as float bits.**
   Fixing bug 1 unmasked a *second*, much bigger bug: 100/103 cases of the
   same format now read back all-zero instead of crashing. Root cause:
   `unpackClearColorValue` (`ImageOps.cpp`) used an attachment-scoped
   predicate (`isIntegerColorAttachmentFormat`) to decide whether to read
   the clear value as int or float bits -- but this format has no
   `COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, so it silently fell through to the float branch
   and reinterpreted integer bits as float garbage (rounds to ~0). Fixed by
   adding a new, broader `isIntegerResourceFormat` predicate.

3. **`L252` (~30 minutes, small/mechanical once found): same fixture gap,
   two more formats.** A broader `dEQP-VK.api.image_clearing.*` sweep found
   a second `DeviceLost`, this time on `A4R4G4B4_UNORM`/`A4B4G4R4_UNORM`
   (`VK_EXT_4444_formats`'s two formats) -- identical shape to `L251` bug 1.
   Fixed both together in one pass.

4. **`L253` (~15 minutes): audit closed, clean result.** Cross-referenced
   every `ResourceFormat` enumerator against `getFormatInfo`'s case list.
   Every gap left is a block-compressed format (BC/ASTC/ETC2/EAC), which
   correctly never reaches this table (illegal `vkCmdClearColorImage`
   target per spec; copies use a separate path). No more landmines of this
   shape exist. This item had been carried forward, unstarted, across
   4+ prior sessions -- now closed for good.

## Verified numbers

## Recurring pattern worth remembering

Every `DeviceLost` this session and several before it (`L249`, `L250`,
`L251`, `L252`) turned out to be a fast, synchronous error at submission
time, misreported by the harness as a hang. **Always try
`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` before reaching for a runtime trace or
debugger** -- it has found the real cause on the first try in every one of
these five cases.

Also worth remembering for future format work: `ImageFixture.cpp`'s
diagnostic-name table and its real `getFormatInfo`/`packClearColor`/
`unpackColor` support are two *entirely separate* things that must each be
added independently -- a name without real support isn't a "not tested yet"
gap, it's a "crashes the whole harness" landmine, because
`formatFeatureFlags` unconditionally advertises `TRANSFER_SRC`/`_DST` for
every recognized format regardless of whether the fixture layer backs it.

## Fix: L228(k), MSAA resolve never ran for a no-draw subpass (~2 hours)

Picked up the previous session's top item.
`clear_color_attachment.single_layer.*sample_count_4*` (294 cases):
136 Fail, values looked like cross-test memory contamination (raw
byte patterns from *other* test cases' clear colors), not a
computation bug.

Root cause: the multisample-resolve-on-subpass-end step (averaging
MSAA samples into a `pResolveAttachments`/`resolveImageView` target)
was implemented only as a side effect inside `Executor.cpp`'s per-draw
`runDraw` path. A subpass whose only command is
`vkCmdClearAttachments` -- exactly this CTS test's own shape -- never
draws, so it never resolved at all; the resolve target's read-back
result was just whatever memory was already there (usually a prior
test's own leftover clear color from the same allocator slot).

Fix: new `resolveSubpassColorAttachments` (`ImageOps.cpp`) -- the same
box-filter-average resolve `Executor.cpp` already does per draw --
called once at each subpass boundary from `CommandBuffer.cpp`'s
`NextSubpass`/`EndRenderPass` handling. Covers both classic render
passes and `vkCmdBeginRendering`/`vkCmdEndRenderingKHR` (the latter
maps to the same internal `EndRenderPass` command, confirmed by grep,
so one fix site covers both APIs).

New test `DrawTest.
ResolvesMultisampleColorAfterClearAttachmentsWithNoDraw`: seeds the
resolve target with a distinct color, clears via
`vkCmdClearAttachments` alone (no draw at all), confirms the seed is
overwritten. Confirmed via `git stash` A/B it fails (seed leaks
through) without the fix.

**Notable finding**: re-running the full `dEQP-VK.api.image_clearing.*`
suite (45636 cases) after the fix landed **0 Fail** (23028 Pass, 22608
NotSupported) -- and 22089 + 939 == 23028 exactly, where 939 was the
count of "pre-existing, unrelated failures" the prior session's own
`L252` sweep had explicitly dismissed as out of scope. Every one of
those 939 was actually this same bug. True impact: ~1075 CTS cases
fixed (136 originally-scoped + 939 previously mis-attributed), not
just the ~136-294 the roadmap row's own text originally scoped.

## Fix: the regression flagged at the end of the last session (~most of this session)

Last session's own standing-check re-sync of `offload-test-suite`'s
`feme` branch left `check-hlsl-feme-vk` with 2 Fail + 1 UnexpectedPass
it explicitly punted on. Picked it up this session. Turned out to be
**4 separate bugs**, not 1:

1. **`spec_const_32_bits.test` (`OutBool` always `0`)**:
   `offload-test-suite`'s `parseSpecializationConstant` (`Device.cpp`)
   built a `Bool` spec-constant's `VkSpecializationMapEntry` with
   `size = sizeof(bool)` (1 byte) instead of `sizeof(VkBool32)` (4
   bytes) -- violates `VUID-VkSpecializationMapEntry-constantID-00776`.
   FeMe's own `buildSpecializationOverrides` (`Pipeline.cpp`)
   correctly, defensively discards any override smaller than 4 bytes
   rather than reading a truncated value -- so this was a pure
   harness-side spec violation, not a FeMe bug. **Fixed in
   `offload-test-suite`** (outside FeMe, per standing instructions):
   commit `1f74e41`.
2. **`WaveActiveMax.test` (expected `[0,0,0,0]`, wrong assumption)**:
   the test's expected output only holds for a 32-wide subgroup
   (out-of-bounds lanes' robust-buffer-access `0` combining with
   in-bounds `-inf` via `max`). FeMe's actual subgroup width comes from
   the host's SIMD register width (`WaveSize.cpp`) -- confirmed via a
   standalone `WaveGetLaneCount()` reproducer to be **4 lanes** on this
   host. With a 4-lane subgroup the in-bounds/out-of-bounds indices
   never share a subgroup, so FeMe's `-inf` result is correct for its
   own hardware. **Fixed in `offload-test-suite`**: added `XFAIL: FeMe`
   (its lit config already has a `"FeMe"` feature -- no harness
   change needed). Commit `f93e59c`.
3. **`array_of_matrices.test` (new UnexpectedPass)**: had a stale
   `XFAIL: DXC` citing `microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler#8080` (a
   row/col transposition: `[1,3,2,4,5,7,6,8]` instead of
   `[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8]`). Confirmed via GitHub API the upstream issue is
   **still open** -- but this environment's pinned `dxc`
   (`1.11(5539-1c7386e9)(1.9.0.15506)`) genuinely, reproducibly no
   longer hits it for this test's exact `-fvk-use-dx-layout` code path.
   Removed the stale annotation, replaced with an explanatory comment
   (careful to avoid the literal substring `XFAIL: DXC` anywhere in the
   file -- lit's directive scanner misparses *any* comment containing
   that substring as a malformed real directive, producing
   `Unresolved` instead of `Pass`; learned this the hard way, one
   iteration). **Fixed in `offload-test-suite`**: commit `034ffa9`.
4. **New failure that surfaced mid-fix, not in the original
   regression**: after rebuilding for item 2's `WaveActiveMax.test`
   fix, `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` started failing --
   `gpu-exec: error: Failed to wait on Semaphore. (VkResult = 2)`
   (`VK_TIMEOUT`) -- but **only** under the full 12-worker
   `check-hlsl-feme-vk` lit run, never standalone (confirmed via
   `imgdiff`: 0.086% differing pixels, well within tolerance, when run
   in isolation) and never via a single-test `llvm-lit` invocation.
   Root cause: `feme/lib/Vulkan/Sync.h`'s `SafetyNetTimeoutNs`, a
   hardcoded 5-second ceiling every blocking wait in FeMe's
   `QueueExecutor`/`Fence`/`Semaphore` machinery is clamped to
   regardless of what the caller asked for (FeMe's own software TDR
   analogue). Under 12 parallel lit workers on a 12-core host, each
   running its own FeMe process, this legitimately-slow-but-progressing
   4096x4096 dispatch got pushed past the fixed 5s ceiling purely by
   host scheduling contention -- a false positive, not a real hang.
   **Fixed in FeMe** (this is the one genuine FeMe-side bug of the
   four): replaced the compile-time constant with
   `getSafetyNetTimeoutNs()`/`getQueueIdleSafetyNetTimeoutNs()`
   accessors, overridable via a new
   `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` env var (cached after first
   call, since every blocking wait is a far hotter path than
   `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS`'s own deliberately-uncached
   precedent), defaulting to the unchanged 5s when unset/invalid. Pure
   parsing logic factored into `parseSafetyNetTimeoutMsEnv` so
   `SyncTest.cpp` could add 6 new tests without fighting the accessor's
   own process-lifetime cache. `offload-test-suite`'s
   `test/CMakeLists.txt` sets `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`
   for the FeMe-specific gpu suites only (commit `ed2e081`, outside
   FeMe). FeMe-side commit: `de9de30`.

Hit one build error along the way fixing item 4: an initial lambda
mixing `uint64_t` and `unsigned long long` return statements failed to
compile (distinct types of the same rank in C++, lambda return-type
deduction requires exact agreement) -- resolved by extracting a normal
function with an explicit return type instead.

# Session: L228(b) fixed (ASTC-SRGB blit decode, 6/7 sampled failures), L260 filed -- L258 sweep left running in background

**Next action if you're picking this up cold**: check on the `L258`
background sweep first (`/tmp/l258_sweep/glsl.qpa`, was ~44% through
at this session's end and progressing at ~2 cases/sec -- if the shell
that ran it (session shellId `37`) is gone, just re-launch:
`./deqp-vk --deqp-case="dEQP-VK.glsl.*" --deqp-log-images=disable
--deqp-log-filename=/tmp/l258_sweep/glsl.qpa` from
`VK-GL-CTS/build/external/vulkancts/modules/vulkan`, with
`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` each set via their own separate
`export` line -- see the gotcha below).

## What happened, in order

1. Standing check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` -->
   `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed. `offload-test-suite`'s `feme`
   branch intact at `034ffa9`, no reset.
2. Picked up carried-over item 3 (`L228(b)`, compressed-format blits)
   from the prior session's next steps -- items 1 (`L257`) and 2
   (`L258`'s launch) were already done/running before this segment,
   per the prior summary.
3. Root-caused `L228(b)`: `ImageOps.cpp`'s `runBlitImage` decodes ASTC
   sources through `decodeASTCBlock` (no sRGB awareness at all -- same
   raw bytes either way) then always reports the result as plain
   `R8G8B8A8_UNORM`, silently skipping the sRGB decode curve for real
   `_SRGB_BLOCK` ASTC sources. `CommandBuffer.cpp`'s *sampling* path
   already had the fix (a local `isASTCSRGBFormat` helper) -- the blit
   path alone never got it.
4. **Fixed**: generalized `isASTCSRGBFormat` into a shared, exported
   helper (`Format.h`/`Format.cpp`), applied the same conditional to
   `runBlitImage`'s own `DecodedFormat`. Added
   `FormatTest.IsASTCSRGBFormatIdentifiesOnlyTheFourteenSRGBFootprints`.
5. **Hit a significant false-alarm detour** verifying the fix: an
   800-case compressed-format CTS sample showed *worse* results
   (massively more `NotSupported`) both with and without the fix (A/B
   tested via `git stash`), which should be impossible for a
   pure-decode-format change. Chased it through `fprintf` debug
   instrumentation in `vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties`
   (output never appeared at all) before writing a tiny standalone C
   reproducer calling `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` directly -- **that's
   what actually caught it**: the device was `llvmpipe`, not FeMe.
   **Root cause**: `export VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<path>
   VK_DRIVER_FILES=$VK_ICD_FILENAMES` in one command evaluates
   `$VK_ICD_FILENAMES` on its value *before* that same command runs
   (empty, in a fresh shell) -- standard shell semantics, all RHS
   expansions on one line happen before any of that line's own
   assignments land. `VK_DRIVER_FILES` ended up empty and the loader
   silently fell back to the system's Mesa/llvmpipe ICD.
   **Fix for future sessions: always set `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/
   `VK_DRIVER_FILES` as two separate `export` statements, never
   `B=$A` in the same command that also sets `A`. Always
   `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` before trusting any
   anomalous CTS result.**
6. Re-verified correctly with fixed env vars: 800-case compressed
   sample went **433 Pass/7 Fail/360 NotSupported --> 439 Pass/1
   Fail/360 NotSupported** (6/7 fixed).
7. The 1 residual failure
   (`astc_5x5_unorm_block.a2b10g10r10_snorm_pack32.

# Session: L261 fixed (textureProj* SPIR-V import: 2 bugs, 598 cases), L262/L263 filed

## TL;DR
- Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` first, as always.
- Picked up `L258`'s triage: root-caused and fixed the largest
  `dEQP-VK.glsl.*` sub-cluster (`texture_functions`, 1,366 fails).
  Two distinct bugs, both in SPIR-V "Proj" sample-opcode handling.
- **598 cases fixed, 0 regressions** (exact set-diff verified).
- Filed `L262` (integer-sampler Bias/Grad gate, ~128+ cases) and
  `L263` (remaining untriaged `L258` clusters) as flat top-level
  roadmap rows -- no nesting-rule violations.
- Kicked off a fresh full `dEQP-VK.glsl.*` sweep in the background
  (proper bash-tool `mode="async"`, not shell backgrounding) to get
  an updated overall tally post-fix; still running at session end.

## What I found
1. Split `texture_functions`' int-sampler failures by GLSL builtin
   family: `_bias_`-suffixed non-grad calls (128 cases) vs.
   non-bias grad calls (256 cases) -- two separate families, but
   turned out both symptomatic of the *same* underlying importer gap
   once I looked past the int-sampler framing.
2. Repro'd `textureprojoffset...isampler2d_vec3_bias_fragment`:
   got `error: unhandled opcode 91` (`OpImageSampleProjImplicitLod`),
   not the expected resource-lowering rejection. `SPIRVImporter.cpp`'s
   `lowerProjectiveImageSamples` only ever rewrote the *Explicit*Lod
   Proj pair (92/94) into non-Proj opcodes -- never the *Implicit*Lod
   pair (91/93) that GLSL's `textureProj*` calls actually lower to
   most of the time.
3. **Bug 1 fix**: generalized the rewrite to cover all 4 Proj
   opcodes (91/92/93/94) -> their non-Proj equivalents (87/88/89/90).
   Confirmed via `SPIRV-Headers/.../spirv.h` that Implicit/Explicit
   Proj pairs have identical operand layout (only the *mandatory*
   Image Operands differ, which doesn't affect a verbatim rewrite).
4. **Bug 2, found while verifying non-int Proj cases**: ran all 384
   non-int `textureproj*` failures as a caselist -- only 144/384
   passed after bug-1's fix, 240 still failed, all `vec4`-coordinate.
   Root cause: GLSL permits *padded* Proj coordinates --
   `textureProj(sampler1D, vec4 P)` uses only `P.x` as the real
   coordinate and `P.w` (the vector's *last* component) as the
   divisor, legally ignoring `P.y`/`P.z`. The old rewrite assumed
   "vector width minus one" real-coordinate components, which only
   holds when there's *zero* padding -- it mis-narrowed and divided
   by the wrong component whenever there was padding.
5. Fix: added `OpTypeImage`/`OpTypeSampledImage` opcode constants,
   extended `TypeResolutionInfo` with `ImageDimByType`/
   `SampledImageTypeToImageType` tables, added `OpSampledImage` to
   `isKnownResultTypeProducer`, wrote `requiredProjCoordComponents`
   to resolve the real coordinate width from the image's own SPIR-V
   `Dim`/`Arrayed` operands (falling back to the old heuristic when
   unresolvable, so no regressions for modules the new lookup can't
   trace). Fixed the divisor index to always be `TotalComponents - 1`
   (the vector's true last component), not the narrowed `N`.
6. Verified: 384/384 non-int Proj cases now pass (was 144/384).
   Full `texture_functions` group re-run (7,946 cases): 768 fails
   (was 1,366) -- **598 fixed, 0 regressions**, confirmed via exact
   Python set-difference against the original `L258` fail list (not
   just a raw pass/fail count comparison, which can mask a
   fix-some/break-some wash).
7. Added 2 new unit tests to the existing hand-assembled-SPIR-V
   test infra in `SPIRVImporterTest.cpp`
   (`LowersImageSampleProjImplicitLod`,
   `LowersImageSampleProjExplicitLodWithPaddedCoordinate`) -- both
   target the two bugs directly (opcode-91 case; 1D-image+vec4-coord
   padded-narrowing case). `FeMeImportSPIRVTests`: 14/14 pass.
8. `ninja check-feme`: 3,406 Passed / 61 Unsupported / 0 Failed
   (+2 net new tests from baseline, no regressions).
9. Found the `offload-test-suite` local `feme` branch had been reset
   away from `llvm-beanz/feme` (reflog shows repeated external
   `reset: moving to origin/main`/back cycles -- not something I did;
   looks like a shared-environment side effect from another process
   touching that checkout). Restored it via
   `git reset --hard llvm-beanz/feme` back to `854cc3f` as part of
   this session's standing checks. Didn't investigate the *cause*
   further (out of scope, not a FeMe code bug) but noting it here in
   case it recurs -- **the offload-test-suite checkout's branch state
   is not stable across sessions/time and should always be
   re-verified/reset at session start, not assumed intact.**

## Commits this session (3, each isolated)

1. `[FeMe] Support OpImageSampleProj{,Dref}ImplicitLod and fix padded
   Proj coordinates (L261)` -- source fix + 2 new unit tests,
   committed together (per this session's own source+test
   convention).
2. `[FeMe] Update Roadmap for L258 re-run results, close L261, file

4. This `agent_thoughts.md` entry (committed separately, as always).

No fixes needed outside `feme/` this segment -- the `offload-test-suite`

Clustered the 966 fails; `builtin.function` (395) was the largest, as expected. Drilled into `builtin.function.integer`: `bitfieldinsert` 96, `findMSB` 80, `findlsb` 80, `bitfieldextract` 47, `uaddcarry` 40, `usubborrow` 40, `imulextended`/`umulextended` 3 each.

   - `BitFieldInsertPattern` ORed `Insert << Offset` into the result completely unmasked -- corrupts *every* `Count` where `Insert` has nonzero bits above bit `Count-1` (common in real inputs), not just an edge case. Biggest single contributor (96 of 143).
   - `BitFieldSExtractPattern`'s final `ashr` shift amount reduces to exactly `Size` when `Count==0` -- poison per LLVM LangRef, should be `0`.
   - `BitFieldUExtractPattern`/`BitFieldInsertPattern`'s shared `(-1<<Count)^-1` mask construction needs an out-of-range shift when `Count==Size` -- also poison, should be all-ones.
   - Fixed via a new `createBitFieldLowMask()` helper (clamp shift to `Size-1` via `llvm.intr.umin`, then `select` in the correct all-ones mask for `Count>=Size`) plus masking the shifted insert value and a `Count==0`-guarded `select` on the final `ashr`. Key insight: an out-of-range shift is poison, not immediate UB -- safe to *compute* as long as the result is discarded via an unchosen `select` branch.
6. New lit test `spirv-to-llvm-bitfield-count-edge-cases.mlir`. `check-feme`: 3,414/61/0. Targeted CTS (`bitfieldinsert`+`bitfieldextract`, 200 cases): 0 Fail (was 143). ## What happened, in order

1. **Picked up L266** where the previous (compacted) segment left off: a
   prior fix had already added scalar `ctlz`/`cttz`/`with.overflow`
   support to SIMDize, but a targeted CTS check showed it wasn't enough
   (`findMSB` was still 36/60/4 Pass/Fail/NotSupported).
2. Root-caused the real gap with `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD=1`: GLSL
   `findMSB(ivec4)` lowers to a **genuinely vector-typed**
   `llvm.ctlz.v4i32` call, not a scalar one -- a totally different code
   path in SIMDize.cpp (the vector-decomposition loop, not the
   scalar-divergent-call path the prior fix touched).
3. Found and fixed **five separate bugs** across several
   edit -> rebuild -> CTS-verify rounds (each one only visible after
   fixing the previous one let the case get one step further):
   - 3x strict "all args match result type" homogeneity checks
     rejected `ctlz`/`cttz` because of their `is_zero_poison` immarg
     operand. Fixed with a new `callNonImmArgsHaveType` helper, used at
     all 3 sites.
   - The vector-widening arg-builder tried to decompose the immarg
     operand instead of passing it through unchanged. Fixed.
   - `widenOverflowArithIntrinsic` only handled scalar operands, not
     vector ones (`uaddCarry(uvec4,uvec4)`). Added a vector branch.
   - A vector-typed *operand* feeding one of the with-overflow calls
     had no consumer-acceptance rule at all. Added one.
4. Also corrected a **wrong assumption from an earlier session**:
   `umulextended`/`imulextended` never used `with.overflow` intrinsics
   in the first place (MLIR's own lowering uses plain
   zext/mul/lshr/trunc) -- so their CTS fails were never part of this
   bug.
5. Added a new lit test locking in the vector-typed-call fix, ran full
   `check-feme` (3,416 Pass/61 Unsupported/0 Fail) and `check-hlsl-feme-vk`
   (482/31/207/2/1, unchanged from baseline -- the 2 Fail + 1
   Unexpected-pass are the same pre-existing, previously-flagged

   back, not new).

   Fail (was the whole point); `uaddcarry`/`usubborrow` dropped from 30

   3 Fail each. **All 18 remaining fails, across all four groups, turned

   `"feme.tight_vector"` insertvalue type mismatch, surfacing *before*

4. Root-caused L268 (the `uvec3`/`feme.tight_vector` bug): confirmed
   it's 100% FeMe-authored, not upstream MLIR. FeMe's own type
   converter substitutes a `feme.tight_vector` marker struct for *any*
   3-lane vector member of *any* non-`Offset`-decorated struct --
   including `spirv.IAddCarry`/`ISubBorrow`/`UMulExtended`/
   `SMulExtended`'s transient two-member result struct. FeMe never
   wrote its own conversion pattern for these four ops, so they fell
   through to upstream's generic `ArithmeticWithOverflowPattern`/
   `MulExtendedPattern`, which `insertvalue` the raw, un-substituted
   `vector<3xiN>` results directly -> verifier type mismatch.
5. Fixed: two new pattern classes,
   `TightVectorArithmeticWithOverflowPattern`/
   `TightVectorMulExtendedPattern`, registered at `FeMeBenefit`,
   replicate the upstream computation exactly but route both result
   fields through the existing `reassembleTightVectorValue` helper
   (via a new shared `insertReassembledStructMember`) before the final
   `insertvalue`s.
6. Added 2 new unit tests reproducing the exact `uvec3` shapes.
   `check-feme`: 3,418 Passed (+2), 0 Failed.

   (was 18 Fail), 6 NotSupported (unrelated `uvec5` skip).

   Fail / 8,963 NotSupported -- exact match to predicted

Two independent files (`SIMDize.cpp`, `Linearize.cpp`) both
independently hard-coded the exact same wrong assumption ("the last
argument of a `feme.cpu.image.*` call is always a mask") for the exact
same two call kinds. If a future `ImageCallKind` is ever added with a

operand indexing across *all* of `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/` up front,

# Session: L269 fixed (imagesizems/texturesizems multisampled GetDimensions gap, 32 cases)

**Session-start checks:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` →
`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed. `offload-test-suite`'s `feme`
branch already up to date with `llvm-beanz/feme` (no merge needed this
time). Both repos clean, no stashes, before and after.

**Task:** L269 -- `imagesizems`/`texturesizems` (32 CTS cases, the
4th `L267` sub-cluster, left unfixed since it had a different error
signature than the other three).

**Root cause (~1 hour of tracing, no code yet):** `OpImageQuerySize`
(the lod-less opcode `imageSize()`/`textureSize()` compile to) returns
the same `(Width, Height[, Layers])` shape for a multisampled image as
for a non-multisampled one -- sample count is `OpImageQuerySamples`'s
own separate job. `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`'s `ImageQuerySizePattern`
already reflected this (dispatches on result width only). The actual
bug was 100% downstream, in `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`'s shape gates:
`hasOnlySupportedImageUses` (sampled path) hard-rejected any
non-`Plain2D` shape for the 2-component case and had *no* case at all
for the 3-component (`Array2DMS`) one; `hasOnlySupportedStorageImageUses`
(storage path) rejected both MS shapes too.

Also chased down why the original diagnostic
(`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1`, naming a
`SignedImage_i32_1_0_0_1_2_23t`-style handle) pointed at the wrong
handle: `UnsupportedOps.cpp`'s own doc comment already explains this
-- when any use is rejected, every handle in that function fails
normalization, and the error names whichever handle happens to be
declared first in the module. Bystander, not root cause. Worth
remembering for the *next* one of these too.

**Fix (1 commit, small):** widened 2 gates, added 1 new case:
1. `hasOnlySupportedImageUses`: `isGetDimensionsIntrinsic` now also
   accepts `Plain2DMS`.
2. `hasOnlySupportedImageUses`: added a wholly new
   `isGetDimensions3Intrinsic` case, scoped to `Array2DMS` only.
3. `hasOnlySupportedStorageImageUses`: `isGetDimensionsIntrinsic` now
   also accepts `Plain2DMS`; `isGetDimensions3Intrinsic` now also
   accepts `Array2DMS`.

No new image-call builder needed -- every widened case falls through
to the pre-existing `createGetDimensions2D`/`createQuerySizeLod2DArray`
builders unchanged, and the runtime entry points they call already
read `Width`/`Height`/`ArrayLayers` off the descriptor with no
MS-vs-non-MS distinction. This was a smaller fix than the prior
session guessed (it expected a whole new `QuerySizeMS` builder).

**Tests:** converted 1 existing negative test
(`LeavesPlain2DMSStorageImageGetDimensionsHandleAlone`, which asserted
this exact case was rejected -- now wrong) into a positive one, added
4 new tests for the remaining sampled/storage x plain/array
combinations. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 599/599 (was 596).

`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set explicitly -- each tool call is a fresh shell, no

largest untriaged failure cluster carried in from last session).

## What's done

1. **L270 fixed:** SPIR-V `BuiltIn HelperInvocation` (`gl_HelperInvocation`)
   was unmapped in `getSystemValueForBuiltIn`, misclassified as a
   `Location`-less user varying, rejecting pipeline creation for every
   `atomic_operations.*_fragment` case (glslang always guards a
   fragment shader's SSBO/image read-modify-write with
   `if (!gl_HelperInvocation) { ... }`). Fixed: special-cased it in the
   discovery loop, routed its loads to `createStageIsHelper()` instead.
   16 cases.
2. **L271 fixed:** a declared-but-never-written vertex `out` varying
   (legal per spec) was invisible to the ordinary load/store-walk
   discovery, leaving the fragment stage's matching input with nothing
   to link against. Fixed: added a fallback discovery loop for
   `Location`-decorated globals, gated by two conditions found the hard
   way:
   - **Regression #1 (crash):** the fallback fired on
     `GraphicsPipeline.cpp`'s documented *second* (no-op-repeat)
     `CanonicalizeStagePass` invocation too, rediscovering an
     already-rewritten global's orphaned declaration and duplicating
     its `SignatureElement` -- crashed `add_signed_geometry` outright.
     Fixed by gating on `!dxil::getEntrySignature(F).has_value()`.
   - **Regression #2 (5 hull unit tests):** even with that guard, the
     fallback still fired on hull's *patch-constant* canonicalization
     phase and wrongly grabbed a per-control-point output the
     control-point clone's own earlier pass had already rewritten (and
     thus fully erased, leaving `use_empty()==true` -- indistinguishable
     from a truly-never-written global by that check alone). Fixed by
     additionally restricting the fallback to
     `SPIRVCanonicalPhase::Ordinary` only, never either hull split
     phase.
   16 cases.
3. **L259/matrix link found (not yet fixed):** sampled
   `dEQP-VK.glsl.matrix.*` (92 fails, the 2nd-largest cluster from last
   session's tally) -- every single one is `mat4x3`-shaped and fails
   with the *exact same* `"row 4 is out of range for element N"`
   diagnostic `L259` already filed (but never root-caused) for its own
   12 `vec3`-suffixed `indexing.varying_array` cases. `mat4x3` is 4
   columns of `vec3` each, so this is very likely the same underlying
   `vec3`/3-vs-4-row-padding bug, reached through a *fixed-shape*
   surface instead of an indexing-dependent one. Recorded as a
   next-session lead directly in `L259`'s own roadmap row (not a new
   entry) -- fixing it should resolve **104 cases** (12 + 92) at once.

# Session: L259 fixed (mat4x3/narrow-vector matrix stride bug, 92 cases); L272 filed for a distinct residual

**Session-start checks:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`
(with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set explicitly) → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`,
confirmed. `offload-test-suite`'s local `feme` HEAD already contains
`llvm-beanz/feme`'s tip (`854cc3f`) -- no drift, no merge needed. Both
repos clean, no stashes, before and after.

**Task:** root-cause `L259` via last session's `mat4x3` reproduction
(`dEQP-VK.glsl.matrix.add.dynamic.highp_mat4x3_float_fragment`), the
top-priority carried-over next step.

## What's done

1. **L259 root-caused and fixed.** `resolveRowComponent`'s
   array-peeling loop (`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`) divides a residual byte
   offset by `RowSize` to get a column/row index. `H101h` (`L257`)
   always computed `RowSize` via `getPackedElementSize` (tightly-packed,
   12 bytes for `<3 x float>`) -- correct only for a genuinely
   `XfbBuffer`-decorated "array of block instances" (transform-feedback
   captures, whose real stride is SPIR-V's own `XfbStride`, no ABI
   padding). An ordinary (non-XFB) `in mat4x3 m;`-style input is
   addressed at a *padded* stride instead (16 bytes, every vector's lane
   count rounded to the next power of two -- confirmed via a raw
   pre-canonicalization IR dump: GEP offsets 0/16/32/48, not
   0/12/24/36). Dividing 48 by the wrong 12-byte stride landed on `Row
   4`, one past the true last row -- `feme-graphics-validate-stage`'s
   `"row 4 is out of range"` rejection.
2. **False start caught before it shipped:** first attempt used
   `DataLayout::getTypeAllocSize` for the padded case. Empirically
   wrong -- the actual `DataLayout` attached to the module at the point
   `CanonicalizeStagePass` first runs is a plain MLIR-derived layout
   string with no vector-alignment entries
   (`e-ve-i64:64-n8:16:32:64-G10`), under which
   `getTypeAllocSize(<3 x float>)` computes an *unpadded* 12 bytes,
   disagreeing with the real 16-byte-strided GEP offsets already baked
   into the IR. Caught this by adding a temporary debug print of the
   live `DataLayout` string and testing it in isolation with a
   standalone LLVM tool (`/tmp/dltest3.cpp`) before trusting the fix.
3. **Real fix:** new `getPaddedElementSize` helper, independent of
   whichever `DataLayout` happens to be attached to the module --
   mirrors `getPackedElementSize`'s own recursive
   struct/array/vector-peeling shape, but rounds a `FixedVectorType`'s
   own lane count up to the next power of two. Threaded a new `bool
   UseTightArrayStride` parameter through
   `resolveOffsetWithinElement` -> `resolveNestedStageIOField` ->
   `resolveRowComponent`, set from a new `hasXfbBufferDecoration`
   helper at each of `resolveStageIOAccess`'s 3 external call sites.
4. **L272 filed (not fixed):** after the fix, `dEQP-VK.glsl.indexing.
   varying_array.*` improved to 49/64 (was 52/64 under the old,
   partially-broken state) -- the 15 residual `vec3_*` failures are a
   runtime `Image mismatch`, not a pipeline-creation rejection.
   Confirmed via A/B `git stash` (stashing just this fix's
   `CanonicalizeStage.cpp` change) that these reproduce identically
   with or without it -- a distinct, pre-existing bug in the
   dynamic-row-indexed path (`getDynamicRowIndexedAccess`/
   `collectDynamicRowTerms`), not this fix's own constant-offset
   `resolveRowComponent` path.

## Verification, in order

1. `FeMeTransformsGraphicsTests` (125 tests, +1 new): **all green**,
   including the existing `H101h` XFB test (confirms the tight-stride
   path is unaffected).
2. `check-feme`: **3,428 Passed**, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed. No
   regressions.
3. Targeted CTS: `dEQP-VK.glsl.matrix.add.dynamic.highp_mat4x3_float_fragment`
   now passes.
4. Targeted CTS: full `dEQP-VK.glsl.matrix.*` (1,764 cases): **1,764
   Pass / 0 Fail** -- was 92 Fail, cluster fully cleared.
5. Targeted CTS: `dEQP-VK.glsl.indexing.varying_array.*` (64 cases):

   (item 4 above), filed as `L272`.
6. `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: 486 Pass / 2 Fail / 1 Unexpectedly-passed /

(was 748/760). `dEQP-VK.glsl.matrix.*`: **1,764/1,764**, unchanged, no
regression. Fresh full `dEQP-VK.glsl.*` sweep (28,420 cases): **19,198
Pass / 259 Fail / 8,963 NotSupported** (was ~19,056/~401/8,963) --
every residual failure lands in an already-known unrelated cluster, no

## What L272 actually was: one root cause, two separate bugs

Both bugs share the same underlying cause: two different `DataLayout`s
are active at two different points in the pipeline (a transient
SPIR-V-logical one, active while `CanonicalizeStagePass` itself runs,
which computes an *unpadded* 12-byte size for `<3 x float>`; the final
CPU-target one, attached later, which pads it to 16 bytes). Whichever
one happened to be active at the moment a *specific* GEP got
folded/generated determines which stride that access's own IR encodes
-- not a property of the global itself, not predictable up front.

1. **Static-offset path (`resolveRowComponent`), already partly fixed
   from a prior session's `L259` landing but refined this session:**
   previously picked a single fixed candidate stride keyed off a
   static `hasXfbBufferDecoration` heuristic. Rewrote it to try both
   `getPackedElementSize`/`getPaddedElementSize` candidates directly
   against the residual offset, preferring whichever divides exactly
   into an in-range row. Cleared 4/16 `vec3_*` cases (the
   "static-on-both-sides" combinations) on its own.
2. **Dynamic-index path (`getDynamicRowIndexedAccess`), root-caused and
   fixed fresh this session:** its "DynamicLane" special case
   (disambiguating a dynamic array-row-select from a dynamic
   vector-lane-select) compared a byte-GEP wrapper's literal `[N x
   i8]` width against a *single* `DL.getTypeAllocSize` call -- which,
   computed under the transient SPIR-V-logical layout, returned the
   tight 12-byte size, while the GEP's own literal width was baked
   earlier at 16 bytes. The `12 == 16` mismatch silently misrouted
   every genuine dynamic row index into `DynamicComponent` instead,
   so each vector lane of a write got assigned a *different, wrong
   row* (`idx+0`/`idx+1`/`idx+2`) rather than sharing one row with
   varying components -- a runtime "Image mismatch," not a
   pipeline-creation rejection. Found by adding a temporary
   `FEME_DUMP_IR_POSTCANON_TMP` debug hook (added, used, then removed
   -- not kept, unlike the permanent `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRECANON` hook added
   this session and kept) to inspect the actual generated
   `feme.stage.output.store.f32` call arguments directly. Fixed with
   the identical dual-candidate self-discovery mechanism as bug 1.

## A test-writing detour worth remembering

The new unit test failed twice before it actually passed, for two
unrelated reasons, both self-inflicted:
1. First attempt: a careless `edit` accidentally dropped the
   `attributes #0 = { "feme.shader.stage"="vertex" }` line from the
   test IR entirely -- the pass silently no-op'd (no stage attribute,
   no recognized entry point) rather than failing loudly. Caught by
   dumping the post-pass module and noticing the attribute group was
   simply gone from the printed IR.
2. Second attempt: the test asserted `CI->getArgOperand(1) == IdxArg`
   (the raw i64 argument) for `Row`, but the pass correctly
   `trunc`s/`zext`s every `Row` operand to i32 first -- so the real,
   correct output has `Row` as a `trunc` instruction using `IdxArg`,
   not `IdxArg` itself. Fixed the assertion to look through an
   optional `TruncInst`, mirroring the existing
   `ThreadsDynamicRowIndexIntoClipDistanceOutputStore` test's own
   `SI->getPointerOperand()`-not-a-GlobalVariable style for the
   "no more `StoreInst` into the global" check too (the shadow-alloca
   write-through legitimately leaves ordinary `StoreInst`s behind).

**Lesson for next time:** when a hand-written unit test fails
unexpectedly on a fix that's already been empirically CTS-verified,
suspect the test's own IR construction or assertion shape before the
fix itself -- dump the actual post-pass module immediately rather than
staring at the assertion diff.

## What got fixed (L273): pipeline-creation rejection in SPIR-V-to-LLVM conversion

**Bug:** `getUniformBlockElement` (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`) only excluded
`BufferBlock`-decorated structs, never positively required `Block` --  so it
also misclassified a `spirv.AccessChain`'s own intermediate component-pointer
type (reached once a wrapper block's sole field is selected as a *whole*, no
further indices) as a second, nested uniform block. Every
`dEQP-VK.glsl.atomic_operations.*_{compute,mesh,task}_{shared,payload}` case
(64 total) hit this, because they all copy a whole SSBO-backed struct field
into a `shared`/`taskPayloadSharedEXT` variable via plain GLSL struct
assignment.

**Fix:** one-line addition requiring `Struct.hasDecoration(Block)`, mirroring
the existing `isBufferBlockStorage` symmetric check. 3 pre-existing lit tests
needed a `Block` decoration added to their hand-written wrapper structs (they'd
omitted it as a shortcut; real glslang/dxc output always includes it). New
dedicated unit test `WholeWrapperFieldLoadFromStorageBufferConverts`, confirmed
via a reverted A/B test to fail pre-fix, pass post-fix.

**Repro trick worth remembering:** no `glslangValidator`/`glslc` binary exists
anywhere in this environment. Extracted the real SPIR-V straight from a CTS
`.qpa` log instead: `deqp-vk --deqp-log-decompiled-spirv=enable`, HTML-unescape
the `<SpirVAssemblySource>` blob, `spirv-as --target-env vulkan1.0` (not
`spirv1.3` -- that spelling isn't valid), then `feme-translate --import-spirv`
to get FeMe's own dialect, then `feme-translate --no-implicit-module
--spirv-to-llvmdialect` to hit the exact same crash standalone. Good enough
for a whole session with no compiler binary needed.

## What's still broken (L274, filed, not started): a second bug, one stage deeper

Re-ran the full `atomic_operations` CTS group after the fix and rebuild.
Still **64/1,040 Fail** -- same raw count, but a *different* error now:
pipeline creation gets past SPIR-V-to-LLVM conversion (L273's fix worked) and
instead fails in `feme-cpu-simdize`'s `GroupShared.cpp`
(`rewriteGroupSharedGlobals`):

- 62/64: `'groupshared global ... feeds a nested getelementptr or another
  unsupported user ... (roadmap milestone 9 deviation)'`
- 2/64: `'... a divergent value ... of aggregate type; component
  decomposition is not yet supported ...'`

Both are shapes the function's own comments *already* document as
out-of-scope for "milestone 9" (a uniform, non-divergent nested struct access
chain into a groupshared global -- distinct from the one second-level-GEP
shape it does support, a divergent vector-of-pointers row address). Not a
regression, not an oversight -- a real scope gap that needs its own dedicated
session. Filed as `L274`.

## What I did (picked up mid-flight -- prior session had a live SIGSEGV crash blocking everything)

The prior session had already root-caused `L275` (raw atomics against the task-payload global never canonicalized) and built out a full fix across 7 files, but the `cmpxchg` half crashed with a `SIGSEGV` on `comp_swap_signed_task_payload`. This session:

1. Wrote a minimal standalone repro (`feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-graphics-canonicalize-stage` on a hand-written 15-line `.ll`) instead of continuing to debug through the full CTS/gdb loop -- reproduced the crash in under a second, versus the ~30s-per-attempt full-pipeline round trip.
2. Root-caused it: the `AtomicCmpXchgInst` canonicalization erased its own `ExtractValueInst` users (and itself) *while* the enclosing `make_early_inc_range` loop was still walking toward them -- since those users sit later in program order, this invalidated the loop's cached "next instruction" iterator. A genuine use-after-free, not a logic bug in the rewrite itself.
3. Fixed it by deferring all of that erasure into a per-function worklist, drained only after the per-instruction loop finishes. Verified via the same standalone repro (clean output, no crash) before touching the real CTS at all.
4. Rebuilt `feme_vulkan`, confirmed `comp_swap_signed_task_payload` passes standalone, then ran the full `atomic_operations` group (1,040 cases): **0 Fail**.
5. Added a regression lit test reproducing the exact crash shape (a two-user `cmpxchg`) plus the RMW canonicalization shape.
6. Ran `check-feme` (3,433/3,433 pass) and `check-hlsl-feme-vk` (same 3 pre-existing unrelated failures as every prior session, unchanged) for full regression confirmation.
7. Re-tallied the full `dEQP-VK.glsl.*` sweep fresh (queued from last session) to get an up-to-date residual-cluster breakdown for next session.

## The retired false lead, for the record

Most of the prior segment chased an `and`-vs-`select` poison-propagation theory for a runtime bounds-check helper, based on standalone `clang -O2` experiments that (undetected for most of that investigation) used the wrong target triple (`x86_64` instead of the real `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` the build actually uses). Once corrected, both code forms compiled identically -- there was never a codegen discrepancy. The real bug (a missing cross-binding descriptor-write-overflow case) was only found by adding direct runtime instrumentation and reading the actual descriptor state, not by further code-reading or codegen theorizing. Lesson banked in `Descriptor.cpp`'s new comments and this write-up for next time a "the generated code looks subtly different" theory shows up: verify the exact build target and the exact final (post-link, post-optimization) IR before trusting any standalone reproduction.

## What I did (picked up mid-fix -- prior segment left an uncommitted, crashing fragment-output fix)

The prior segment (same session, summarized context) had found and started fixing the fragment-output half of the bug (`findElementsCoveringLocation`, multi-element `readFragmentColor`/`readFragmentColorInt`) but left it crashing on a `readRaw` "computed offset is out of bounds" assertion, with the 3 exact broken call sites already identified but not yet edited. This continuation:

1. Applied the 3 pending edits: passed the *absolute* `Elem.FirstComponent + C` instead of the *local* `C` to `readFloat`/`readRaw` in both the original single-element `readFragmentColor` (a **latent bug that predates this session**, never triggered before since no prior test exercised a non-zero-`FirstComponent` single covering element) and the new multi-element functions.
2. Rebuilt, re-ran the original single-case repro: passes. Ran the full `frag_out` subgroup: **25/25 Pass**.
3. Investigated the remaining `vert_in` (24 cases, still failing): traced the vertex-attribute-fetch loop and found `decodeAttribute` always decoded starting from source byte 0 / output index 0, ignoring `Elt.FirstComponent` entirely -- a second split vertex-input element would read the *same* first channel as the first element instead of its own. Ruled out an earlier hypothesis (multiple overlapping `VkVertexInputAttributeDescription`s) by reading `vktShaderLibrary.cpp`: only one real attribute description is bound per named `input` value.
4. Fixed by adding a `StartComponent` parameter to `decodeAttribute`, threaded through every format-decode branch (per-component formats index `Src`/`Out` by `StartComponent + I`; the one packed format, `R10G10B10A2_UNORM`, indexes its precomputed `Components[]` by `StartComponent + I`), and updated the call site's `FormatComponents`/`InBoundsComponents` bounds math to be relative to `Elt.FirstComponent`, plus fixed the post-decode `Bits[C]` write-back to `Bits[Elt.FirstComponent + C]`.
5. Rebuilt, re-ran `440.linkage.varying.*`: 63/68 Pass (up from 44/68). Residual 5 fails are all `vert_in.*_unused` variants -- added temporary `FEME_DEBUG_VS_FETCH` instrumentation, confirmed the host-side fetch *does* correctly compute zero for the out-of-range component. The residual bug is elsewhere (most likely the compiled shader IR's own intrinsic-to-storage-read lowering), not chased further this session. Removed the debug instrumentation before finalizing.
6. Added a regression unit test `VertexAttributeFetchHonorsFirstComponentOfSplitComponentInputs` (two scalar `int` inputs sharing one `R32G32_SINT` attribute at `FirstComponent=0`/`1`, distinct values, asserts correct color). While writing it, discovered the `feme.stage.input.load.i32` intrinsic's own `Component` argument is *itself absolute*, validated against `[FirstComponent, FirstComponent+ComponentCount)` -- had to fix the test IR accordingly (a useful convention note for next time).

## A convention worth remembering

`StageStorage::readRaw`/`writeRaw`/`readFloat`/`writeFloat`'s `Component` parameter, and the `feme.stage.input.load.{f32,i32}` shader-IR intrinsic's own `Component` argument, are **both always absolute** (0-3, validated/subtracted against `E.FirstComponent` internally/by the validator) -- never local to a split element. This bit twice in one investigation (once in production code, once while writing the test's own shader IR) and is worth double-checking any time new code iterates `for (C = 0; C != Elem.ComponentCount; ++C)` near this storage layer.

# Session: L279 fixed (440.linkage.varying vert_in.*_unused residual, 5/5 cases); offload-test-suite branch repair

**Start-of-session check**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` -> `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.
**offload-test-suite branch check**: local `feme` HEAD (`2bf6978`) had drifted from `llvm-beanz/feme` in a way the simple tip-comparison protocol missed -- see item 3 below. Fixed this session.

## What now works

`dEQP-VK.glsl.440.linkage.varying.*` (68 cases): **68/68 Pass** (was 63/68 -- the 5-case residual from `L278` is now fully cleared).

## What I did

1. Picked up the `L278`-carried-over residual: prior session found the host-side vertex fetch "correctly computes 0" for `in0_3` (a scalar at absolute component 3, sharing a 2-channel attribute) and left the bug unexplained. Re-instrumented (`FEME_DEBUG_L278`), confirmed the same "computes 0" result, then went back to the actual CTS shader source (`linkage.test`, `var0 = in0_3 * in0 + in0`) and recomputed the test's own hardcoded expected output by hand: it only works if `in0_3` is **1**, not 0. This overturned the prior session's assumption -- the "correctly computes 0" host code was itself the bug, matching Vulkan's standard "missing W/alpha channel defaults to 1" convention, applied here to a scalar landing at absolute component 3 rather than a whole `vec4`.
2. Removed the debug instrumentation. Fixed `Executor.cpp`'s default-fill gate: replaced `FormatComponents < 4 && Elt.ComponentCount == 4` (only fires for whole-`vec4` elements) with two new locals, `ElementCoversComponent3` (does this element's own absolute range include component 3?) and `FormatMissesComponent3` (does the bound *format* -- not buffer-bounds truncation -- lack that channel?). Verified by hand against 3 cases: whole-vec4-on-narrow-format (still defaults to 1, correct), scalar-at-3-on-narrow-format (now defaults to 1, the fix), whole-vec4-buffer-bounds-truncated-on-wide-format (does NOT default to 1, since the format has the channel, only the buffer runs short -- confirmed `FormatComponents` not `InBoundsComponents` is the right variable to key off).
3. **Found and fixed a second, unrelated bug while investigating `check-hlsl-feme-vk`**: the target didn't exist as a ninja target at all. Root cause: the local `/home/dev/dev/offload-test-suite` checkout's `feme` branch had *lost* its FeMe-enabling commit (`854cc3f`) -- the upstream `llvm-beanz/feme` branch had moved 23 commits ahead on a different base that doesn't include it. A prior session's branch-drift check only compared branch tips and reported "no drift," which missed this. Fixed via `git cherry-pick 854cc3f` onto the local branch (clean, no conflicts) plus a `cmake .` reconfigure in `llvm-project/build` to regenerate the now-restored target. This only touched the external `offload-test-suite` checkout's branch state, not `llvm-project` -- no commit needed in this repo for it.

## A gotcha worth remembering

Comparing `git fetch <remote> <branch>` tips ("HEAD matches, no drift") is **not sufficient** to confirm a specific known commit is still present on a branch -- if the upstream branch itself gets rebuilt on a different, older base (as happened here), the tips can still look "equal enough" at a glance while the actual commit of interest silently drops out of the ancestry. When a specific commit matters (like `854cc3f`'s FeMe target additions), check with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <branch>` instead of just comparing tips.

## A gotcha worth remembering

`deqp-vk` must be run with its own binary directory as `cwd` -- its data-file lookups (`./vulkan/glsl/...`) are relative, not resolved against `--deqp-log-filename`'s path or any other argument. Running it from an arbitrary directory (even with all the right env vars set) fails immediately with `FATAL ERROR: Failed to open file: './vulkan/glsl/440/linkage.test'` before a single real test case runs -- easy to mistake for a build/config problem.

## A gotcha worth remembering

The CTS's own `BuiltinFragDepthCaseInstance::validateDepthBuffer` log message (`Mismatch at pixel (X,Y,S): expected <N> but got <M>`) **always prints the covered-pixel formula's value** as "expected", even when the real branch taken is the uncovered/background one (whose real expected value is a different variable entirely, `m_defaultDepthValue`). For a `depthClampEnable=true` test case specifically, that formula happens to multiply by `0.0`, so "expected 0" can mean either "uncovered background" or "clamped-to-near-plane" -- they print identically. Don't trust the log text alone; hand-derive the real expected value from the CTS's own C++ source before trusting a "coverage bug" hypothesis. This cost real time last session (mis-filed as a coverage-mask bug) and this session (had to re-derive from scratch to catch the mistake).

## A gotcha worth remembering

**Never trust a combined multi-case `deqp-vk` sweep's failure count for a cluster known (or suspected) to contain real hangs.** One genuine hang appears to corrupt the process's own Vulkan device/queue state for every case that runs afterward in the same invocation, turning ordinary passing cases into `VK_TIMEOUT` false failures. If a combined run shows failures in a suspect area, always re-run the affected subgroup(s) -- and, if still ambiguous, each individual case -- in a fresh, separate process before reporting a number. This cost 3 sessions' worth of "loops = 30 cases" being repeated as fact when the true number was 4.

# Session: L283 -- dowhile_trap root-cause attempt reverted (net-negative regression found); mask-narrowing generalization kept

Start here next session: `loops` still at 620/624 (4 `dowhile_trap` hangs). Don't touch `isLoopControlEdge` again -- see the specific new lead at the bottom instead (`PreRegion`/`PostRegion` handling of a nested child cycle's own latch inside `OtherCondBrBlocks`).

## What happened this session

1. Session-start check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.
2. Root-caused `dowhile_trap`'s hang mechanism precisely: `DiamondFlattener::isLoopControlEdge` doesn't recognize a rotated-loop shape where a cycle header's own two successors are *both* still cycle members (neither a direct backedge nor a direct exit) -- so `DiamondFlattener` wrongly flattens the header's real divergent check as an ordinary diamond before `LoopLinearizer` ever sees it.
3. Implemented a fix: made `isLoopControlEdge` unconditionally defer any cycle header's own branch, plus widened `HeaderExit`/`LatchExit` matching to `matchExitCheckWithRelay`. **This fixed all 4 `dowhile_trap` cases** -- verified directly.
4. Ran a full isolated-per-case regression sweep of all 624 `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*` cases before declaring victory (the `L282` methodology). Good thing I did: found **14 new regressions** -- `special.{do_while,for,while}_dynamic_iterations.{conditional_break,elseblock,ifblock}_fragment`.
5. Root-caused the regression too, not just detected it: these shapes need `DiamondFlattener` to walk *through* the header's own branch to reach and flatten a separate, genuinely divergent internal check elsewhere in the loop body (an `if (cond) break`), reducing the pair down to one surviving candidate a different, already-working mechanism handles. Forcing `DiamondFlattener` to stop at the header unconditionally breaks that.
6. **Fully reverted** the `isLoopControlEdge`/`matchExitCheckWithRelay` approach (`git checkout --` on `Linearize.cpp`, confirmed the file matched the pre-attempt baseline byte-for-byte) rather than trying to patch it further under time pressure -- a narrower, correctly-targeted fix needs more careful design than I had budget for this segment.
7. Kept one small, independently-verified-safe piece found alongside the reverted attempt: generalized `rethreadNestedEntryMasks` (from `L282`) from matching only literal `true` constants to matching any non-backedge incoming edge structurally (via `CI.getCycle`/`CI.contains`). Confirmed via direct case testing: no new pass, no new fail, does NOT by itself fix `dowhile_trap` (consistent with `L282`'s own original finding that this piece alone is insufficient).
8. `ninja check-feme`: 3,441/3,502 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- clean, no regressions.
9. Full isolated subgroup-level re-run of all 18 `loops.*` iteration-kind subgroups: identical to `L282`'s baseline everywhere -- **still 620/624 Pass, 4 Fail** (the same 4 `dowhile_trap` cases, unchanged). Net CTS delta this session: zero (reverted a regression, kept one safe no-op-on-its-own improvement).
10. `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: **not re-run this session** -- no cached offload-test-suite build directory exists in this environment and a from-scratch configure+build was out of time budget given the change's low risk (a pure internal-compiler-mask-narrowing generalization, no HLSL-surface-visible change). Flagging as a gap, not silently skipping.
11. Committed in 3 separate commits: (a) `Pipeline.cpp` doxygen comment for `FEME_DUMP_IR_ON_VERIFY_FAIL` (pure comment, kept from the reverted segment since it's a genuinely useful, permanent debug aid), (b) `Linearize.cpp`'s `rethreadNestedEntryMasks` generalization, (c) `Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md` docs, (d) this file.
12. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no change -- confirmed, internal compiler-correctness investigation only.
13. Cleaned up this segment's own scratch files (`/tmp/dt_prelin.txt`, `/tmp/dt_dump*.txt`, `/tmp/cb_*.txt`, `/tmp/loop_*.qpa`, etc. -- left alone prior sessions' own `/tmp/l27*`/`l28*` files, not mine to clean up).

## A gotcha worth remembering

**A fix that makes the target case pass is not done -- run the full isolated-per-case regression sweep *before* declaring victory, every time, even when the individual fix "looks obviously safe."** This session's `isLoopControlEdge` change looked like a strict superset (it only *adds* cases where `DiamondFlattener` defers to `LoopLinearizer`) and was reasoned through carefully -- but "strictly adds deferrals" quietly broke a *different* mechanism (flattening a separate internal divergent check that happens to sit inside the deferred header's own arm) that depended on those very cases *not* being deferred. The reasoning was locally sound and globally wrong. Only the full sweep caught it. If I had trusted the "4/4 dowhile_trap pass, ship it" signal alone, this session would have landed a net-negative change.

# Session: L284 -- "AtomicRMWInst build failure" report investigated, not reproducible, fail-fast guard added anyway

Start here next session: no functional FeMe change happened this session -- it was a pure build-configuration investigation/hardening. Pick up wherever `L283`'s next steps left off (the `dowhile_trap` nested-child-cycle `PreRegion`/`PostRegion` lead is still the sharpest next thing).

## What happened this session

1. Session-start check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed (twice -- once at start, once after the rebuild below).
2. User reported FeMe fails to build with `AtomicRMWInst` errors, suspecting system-installed LLVM headers. Investigated by actually deleting all 304 existing FeMe `.o` files and rebuilding `check-feme` completely from scratch (not trusting any prior ninja/ccache up-to-date state, which could mask a real problem) -- **zero compile errors**. Only 1 unrelated, confirmed-flaky timing test failed on that run and passed cleanly on a second run.
3. Confirmed via `compile_commands.json` that 0 of 304 FeMe compile commands reference any system LLVM header path -- every one resolves from the in-tree `llvm/include`.
4. Confirmed `feme/CMakeLists.txt` already hard-rejects standalone (non-in-tree) builds, so there's no code path in the current design that could pick up an installed LLVM by accident.
5. Didn't stop at "can't reproduce, nothing to do" -- dug into *why* the report described something so specific. Found real evidence the failure mode is genuine, just not currently triggered: the container's `llvm-21-dev` system package is missing two `AtomicRMWInst::BinOp` enumerators feme actually uses (`FMaximumNum`/`FMinimumNum`). Used `git log -S` to pin exactly when they were added upstream: commit `ea8fb06f2443`, first released in `llvmorg-23.1.0`. So if a build ever did pick up `llvm-21` (stray `LLVM_DIR`, `CPATH` leak, IDE misconfiguration), it would fail with exactly this symptom, deep in `AtomicRMWIdentity.cpp`, with a cryptic "no member named" error.
6. Added a fail-fast `feme/CMakeLists.txt` guard: `if(LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR LESS 23) message(FATAL_ERROR ...)`, right next to the existing standalone-build rejection. Verified it fires correctly with an isolated `cmake -P` script (forced `LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR=21` → clear error) and doesn't fire for the real, correct configuration (`cmake .` re-run in the actual `build/` dir: `LLVM_VERSION_MAJOR=24`, configure succeeds cleanly).
7. Re-ran `ninja check-feme` after the CMake change: 3,441/3,502 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- confirms the guard doesn't break the real build, and the earlier single flaky failure really was a flake (passed this time).
8. CTS: ran `dEQP-VK.api.smoke.*` (6/6 Pass) as a fast sanity check, plus spot-checked the known `dowhile_trap` hang is unchanged (still fails identically) -- appropriate scope for a build-configuration-only change with zero codegen impact; did not re-run a full CTS sweep.
9. Documented in `VulkanCTSReport.md` (`L284`) and `Roadmap.md` (`L284` row).
10. Committed in 2 separate commits: (a) `feme/CMakeLists.txt` guard, (b) docs (`Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md`) + this file.
11. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no change -- confirmed, pure build-configuration safeguard, no feature/extension surface change.

## A gotcha worth remembering

**"I can't reproduce it" is not the end of the investigation if the reporter gave a specific, plausible technical detail.** The build genuinely compiles clean in the current `build/` directory, but the user's specific claim ("`AtomicRMWInst` ... not defined by LLVM (anymore)") pointed at something checkable: whether the *exact* API feme uses actually has a version-dependent gap somewhere reachable. It did -- `llvm-21`'s headers really are missing `FMaximumNum`/`FMinimumNum`. Chasing that down turned a dead-end "can't repro, closing as not-a-bug" into a real, permanent, cheap fail-fast safeguard that costs nothing now and saves a confusing debugging session for whoever hits this in the future (a different agent, a CI misconfiguration, a dev's stray env var).

# Session: L285 -- PCH disabled, real `AtomicRMWInst` missing-include bug found and fixed

Start here next session: pick `loops`/`dowhile_trap` (still the sharpest lead, see `L284`'s carried-over list below) -- this session was another build-configuration detour, not functional FeMe work.

## What happened, in order

1. `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed (start, and again after the rebuild).
2. User reported a real build failure with `AtomicRMWInst` errors and asked specifically to disable PCH "so you actually detect missing includes" -- a sharper ask than `L284`'s guess-based investigation.
3. Checked `compile_commands.json`: PCH was in fact active (`-Xclang -include-pch ... cmake_pch.hxx.pch` on every FeMe compile command) -- confirmed the exact masking mechanism `L284` only theorized about.
4. Reconfigured with `-DCMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS=ON`, deleted all 304 FeMe `.o` files, rebuilt from scratch. **~2,467 ninja steps** (disabling the shared `LLVMCore` PCH invalidates cached objects for all of LLVM/Clang/MLIR, not just feme -- budget for this if you ever do it again, though it's one-time; ccache absorbs the real cost afterward).
5. Real error surfaced: `feme/include/feme/Core/StageOps.h:394,404` -- no member `AtomicRMWInst` in namespace `llvm`. Root cause: the header only included `llvm/IR/InstrTypes.h`, but `AtomicRMWInst` lives in `llvm/IR/Instructions.h`. Fixed with one added `#include`.
6. Audited all 14 files matching `AtomicRMWInst` repo-wide for the same gap -- confirmed `StageOps.h` was the only real instance (others: comments only, or already-correct transitive includes).
7. Rebuilt `feme_vulkan` clean (zero errors), then full `check-feme` clean (1,289 steps, PCH-invalidated cache still warming from step 4): **3,441/3,502 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed**.
8. CTS smoke check: `dEQP-VK.api.smoke.*` 6/6 Pass; `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.special.{for,while}_uniform_iterations.*` 124/124 Pass (matches pre-existing baseline). No full sweep -- this is a header-hygiene fix with no codegen change.
9. Checked `feme/cmake/caches/feme.cmake`: **already has `CMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS ON CACHE BOOL ""` committed from an earlier point (`a6aa0fc02d32`)** -- so the "persist this so a fresh build directory picks it up" concern was already solved before this session started. Nothing to do there.
10. Documented in `VulkanCTSReport.md` (build-line update) and `Roadmap.md` (`L285` row), and added a permanent "why PCH stays off" section to `feme/.instructions.md` so this reasoning survives even if someone is tempted to re-enable it for build-speed reasons later.
11. Committed in 2 commits: (a) `StageOps.h` fix, (b) docs.

## Gotcha worth remembering (tooling, not FeMe)

Backgrounding a long build with shell `command &` *inside* a sync bash-tool call does not survive past that call's own process exit -- the background ninja gets killed silently (confirmed via `pgrep` showing nothing despite an echoed "started" message). Use the bash tool's own `mode="async"` instead; it stays attached across `read_bash` polls correctly. Cost about 7 minutes of wasted wall-clock this session before catching it.
