# Session: L286 -- `dowhile_trap` fixed, `loops` cluster fully closed (was 30, tracked since L277)

`vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed (start, before CTS runs, and again at session end).

## What happened, in order

1. Picked the top carried-over item: root-cause `dowhile_trap`'s 4-case hang, the `loops` cluster's last residual failure.
2. Used empirical trace-debugging instead of live `gdb` this time: added temporary prints gated behind the existing `FEME_DEBUG_LINEARIZE_TRACE` env var, rebuilt via ccache/ninja (~4s per cycle), reran the ~3s repro. Much faster than attaching `gdb` to a hung process.
3. Found the outer cycle's `CondBr` was already gone by the time `LoopLinearizer::linearizeCycle` ran on it -- traced backward and found `DiamondFlattener`, a wholly separate pass that runs *before* `LoopLinearizer`, had already converted it.
4. Root cause: `DiamondFlattener::validate` deliberately stops at a nested cycle's header and records a `CycleBoundaryMasks` entry (the correct per-lane "should this lane enter the nested cycle" mask) -- but that mask was never passed to `LoopLinearizer`, a separate pass with fresh state. `LoopLinearizer::makeActivePNPair` always seeded a cycle's entry mask with a bare `true` instead.
5. Fixed by threading the mask across the pass boundary: new `DiamondFlattener::getCycleBoundaryMasks()` accessor, new required `LoopLinearizer` constructor parameter/member `DiamondFlattenedEntryMasks`, `makeActivePNPair` consults it before falling back to `true`.
6. Wrote a new regression unit test. First attempt (both outer and inner loop divergent) passed even *without* the fix -- the outer loop being its own cycle let `LoopLinearizer`'s own same-pass `rethreadNestedEntryMasks` (from `L282`) mask the bug by a different path. Fixed by making the outer loop *uniform* (constant trip count) so only the diamond-to-cycle path is exercised. Confirmed via `git stash` A/B: fails pre-fix, passes post-fix.
7. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 601/601. `check-feme-transforms-cpu-linearize` lit: 39/39. `check-feme` (full target): 3,442/3,503 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed.
8. CTS: isolated full `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*` re-run: **624/624 (100%) Pass**. The 30-case `loops` cluster `L277` first identified is now fully closed.
9. Broader regression spot-check attempt: ran the full `dEQP-VK.graphicsfuzz.*` group (~757 cases) in one combined process -- hit the already-documented (`L282`) cascading-false-failure artifact again (a long, dense run of consecutive `Fail`s; confirmed by re-running several of those cases individually in fresh processes, each passing cleanly). Killed the stuck combined run instead of waiting it out. Fell back to isolated single-case runs of the 3 specific repros `L282`'s own reverted `isCycleHeaderBranch` attempt had regressed, plus the original `DiamondFlattener::validate` stack-overflow repro: all 3 `cov-function-*` cases pass; `increment-value-in-nested-for-loop` still fails, but cleanly (a diagnosed "unsupported shape" error, not a crash/hang) -- exactly the expected pre-existing behavior, not a new regression.
10. Updated `Roadmap.md` (new `L286` row; marked `L277`'s own row "done", resolved by `L286`) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new `L286` section). `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no change needed -- internal compiler-correctness fix, no new feature/extension surface.
11. Committed in 2 commits: (a) `Linearize.cpp` fix + new unit test, (b) docs.
12. Cleaned up `/tmp` scratch files and confirmed no stray `deqp-vk`/`gdb` processes remain.

## Gotcha worth remembering

A combined-process CTS run over a large group (~757 cases) is still unreliable for a trustworthy per-case tally, even after `L282`'s cascading-false-failure finding -- it can still silently wedge/slow partway through and produce a long run of spurious fails. For any future "spot-check a big group for regressions" task, either isolate each case into its own process from the start, or accept a *targeted* subset (specific known-risk repro names) rather than trusting a full combined run's raw pass/fail count without individually re-verifying any long fail streak.

## Gotcha worth remembering

**Stale cluster tallies accumulate silently.** `builtin` and `texture_gather` had both been carried on next-steps lists for many sessions as "unexplored" or "N cases failing," but were already fully resolved -- one as a side effect of unrelated fixes, one because a prior session's CTS path guess matched 0 cases and nobody noticed the count was never actually re-verified. **Lesson: when picking up a carried-over cluster from an old next-steps list, always re-run the CTS group fresh before investigating** -- don't trust an inherited case count without reproducing it, even (especially) for small clusters that look "obviously still broken."

**New-opcode-support debugging produces a very deep yak-shave.** This session's single CTS symptom (`error: unhandled opcode 5381`) required two separate upstream-project commits (MLIR, then LLVM) before FeMe's own 2-file fix was even possible. When a FeMe repro fails with "unhandled opcode" or "failed to legalize... marked illegal," check both layers immediately (does MLIR's SPIR-V dialect have the op at all? does an LLVM intrinsic exist for the lowering target?) rather than assuming the gap is single-layered.

# Session: `L292` deep root-cause, fix attempted and reverted (unsafe in isolation)

## Do this first next session

Implement `L292`'s fix as **one combined change**, not two. Gap (1) alone
(header-is-always-a-cycle-boundary) regresses tests. Gap (2) (the
exit-mask placeholder/patch mechanism) must land in the same commit.
Start at `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/Linearize.cpp:1353`
(`DiamondFlattener::flatten()`).

## State right now

1. `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`.
   Confirmed at session start and end.
2. No code committed this session. `Linearize.cpp` is back at baseline
   (`check-feme`: 3,443/3,504 Pass, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed, confirmed
   clean after reverting the attempted fix).
3. `Roadmap.md`'s `L292` row and `VulkanCTSReport.md` both updated with
   the full root-cause writeup and the reason the fix was reverted
   (docs-only commit, see below).

## What I found (root cause, now fully confirmed, not just suspected)

`L292` = 5 cases, `dEQP-VK.glsl.demote.dynamic_loop_{always,deriv,dynamic,texture,uniform}`.
All fail at runtime (image mismatch), not build time. All 5 share the same
final symptom: the real per-invocation framebuffer-gating call,
`feme.cpu.stage.return.masks`, at the loop's exit block, is hardcoded to
constant `true`/`true` -- never narrowed by `demote`, no matter what ran
inside the loop.

Two layered bugs, both in `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/Linearize.cpp`:

**Bug 1 -- `DiamondFlattener` misclassifies the loop header's own branch.**
`isLoopControlEdge(Cur, Target)` only checks if `Target` is *directly* the
header or *directly* outside the cycle. `StructurizeCFG` sometimes inserts
a synthetic `Flow` dispatch block between the header's branch and the
loop's real continue/exit targets -- so *neither* of the header's direct
successors passes the check, and `DiamondFlattener` "flattens" the header's
own iteration decision as if it were an ordinary two-way diamond.

**Bug 2 -- the exit mask is baked in before `LoopLinearizer` ever runs, with no patch mechanism.**
This is the one that actually produces the wrong CTS output. Proven via
`dynamic_loop_dynamic` (divergent condition inside the loop, uniform loop
exit): `LoopLinearizer`'s existing divergent-handling code path *does* run
and *does* correctly compute a narrowed per-iteration mask -- but the exit
block's `return.masks` call never sees it, because `DiamondFlattener::run()`
already built that call using `CycleBoundaryMasks[Header]` (the *pre-loop
entry* mask, a plain constant `true`/`true`) as an **immutable constant
argument**, before `LoopLinearizer` even starts. There is currently no
mechanism to retroactively correct it.

**Bug 3 (uniform-condition cases only, e.g. `dynamic_loop_always`) --
`LoopLinearizer` has no code path at all for "uniform loop exit, but body
has a mask-narrowing op."** It unconditionally bails (`return false`) the
moment neither the header nor latch exit check is divergent, regardless of
whether the body narrows anything.

## Why the attempted fix didn't work

I fixed bug 1 alone first (header branch is always a cycle boundary, in
both `validate()` and `flatten()`). Built, tested:
- CTS outcome: **unchanged**, all 5 still fail (expected -- bug 2/3
  untouched).
- `check-feme`: **2 new failures** (`loop-break-structurized.ll` lit test,
  `LinearizeTest.NestedCycleInsideFlattenedDiamondArmInheritsOuterDiamondsMask`
  unit test). Confirmed by running `check-feme` before/after.

Reverted immediately (`git checkout -- Linearize.cpp`), rebuilt, confirmed
baseline clean again. **Lesson: bug 1 cannot ship alone.** Something else
in the existing (passing) test suite relies on the *old*, technically-wrong
classification producing a result that happens to be correct for those
shapes -- changing the classification without also fixing how the exit
mask gets computed/threaded breaks them.

## The actual fix design for next session (not yet implemented)

1. In `DiamondFlattener::flatten()`, when it hits a cycle boundary (the
   header, per bug-1's fix), create **two fresh, uniquely-identifiable
   placeholder instructions** for Live/SideEffect -- use
   `new FreezeInst(Masks.Live, ...)` / `new FreezeInst(Masks.SideEffect, ...)`
   constructed directly (NOT via `IRBuilder::CreateFreeze`, which
   constant-folds `freeze(constant)` back to the constant immediately,
   destroying the placeholder's unique identity before it can be patched).
2. Store these in a **new** map, separate from `CycleBoundaryMasks`
   (which must keep serving its existing job: seeding `LoopLinearizer`'s
   own entry-mask phi unchanged) -- call it something like
   `CycleExitPlaceholderMasks`, keyed by `Header`.
3. Make the cycle's exit-root `flatten()` walk (in `run()`) seed its
   `EntryMasks` from this new placeholder map, not the raw
   `CycleBoundaryMasks` constant.
4. Expose both maps via getters; in `LinearizePass::run()`, after
   `LoopLinearizer::run()` finishes, walk the placeholder map: for each
   `Header` with a placeholder, look up `LoopLinearizer`'s own
   `HeaderActiveMasks[Header]` (needs a new getter too) and, if present,
   `replaceAllUsesWith` + `eraseFromParent()` each placeholder with the
   real final mask. If `LoopLinearizer` never touched that header (an
   ordinary ignore-this-loop case with nothing to narrow), the placeholder
   just stays as `freeze(true)` forever -- semantically identical to the
   original constant, so this is safe to apply unconditionally to *every*
   cycle boundary, not just the 5 failing cases.
5. Extend `LoopLinearizer::linearizeCycle` with a new path for bug 3:
   before the `!HeaderDivergent && !LatchDivergent → return false` bail,
   check whether the cycle's body contains any mask-narrowing stage op
   (reuse/restrict `hasStageMaskOps`'s callee-scan logic to the cycle's own
   blocks). If yes, thread Live/SideEffect via a loop-carried header phi
   (reuse `makeActivePNPair`/`applyStageMasks`/`freezeLoopCarriedValues`/
   `addLatchIncoming`, same machinery as the divergent path) **without**
   touching the real uniform branch at all, then record
   `HeaderActiveMasks[Header] = Masks` same as the existing success paths.
6. Before calling this done, run an existing *passing* divergent-loop-demote
   CTS case (if one exists) before/after to make sure the new placeholder
   plumbing doesn't change its (currently correct) output -- I have not
   confirmed one exists yet; search the demote/discard CTS groups for a
   passing loop+demote combination to use as the regression canary.
7. Rebuild, re-test all 5 `dynamic_loop_*` cases, then run full
   `check-feme` to confirm 0 regressions before committing.

## Gotcha worth remembering

**A structurally-correct-looking classification fix can still be unsafe to
ship alone if something downstream of it has a separate, independent gap.**
Always run the *full* regression suite (`check-feme`, not just the targeted
CTS cases you're trying to fix) immediately after any `Linearize.cpp`
change, even one that looks purely like "stop misclassifying this edge
case" -- the cycle-boundary/mask-threading machinery in this file has
enough cross-cutting invariants that a locally-correct change can still
break something non-obviously-related elsewhere in the same pass.

# Session: L292 regression root-cause and fix (L294) -- 2026-10-01

**Start here next session:** triage the remaining 8 `ifblock`/`elseblock`
loops cases. See step 3 below for exactly where to look.

## What happened this session

1. Picked up an unverified regression flagged at the end of the prior
   session: after landing `L292`'s `dynamic_loop_*` demote fix
   (`d17caf8182dc`), a broader `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*` sweep (624 cases,
   previously 624/624) had dropped to 590/624 -- 34 new failures, all in
   `special.{for,while}_dynamic_iterations.*`.
2. Confirmed real, not flaky: built true `HEAD~1`, ran
   `conditional_break_fragment` directly -- Pass. Rebuilt committed
   `L292` state, same case -- Fail. Regression is real, introduced by
   `L292`'s own `recoverRelayExitCheck`.
3. Root cause: `recoverRelayExitCheck` recognized a relay stub as a valid
   exit arm by shape alone (pure relay block, unique predecessor), never
   checking it actually reaches `ExitBlock`. Loops whose body has its own
   `if`/`break` check sharing the *same* `StructurizeCFG` `Flow` dispatch
   block as the loop's own re-entry check have a stub that looks right
   but lands back on that shared dispatch block instead.
4. Fixed in two stages (both landed, commit `29f5626e8433`):
   - Generalized the existing single-divergent-exit mask-narrowing to also
     cover `Header`'s own relay-recovered check when a second, genuinely
     separate divergent exit exists elsewhere. Fixed 6 cases
     (590 -> 596/624).
   - Tightened `recoverRelayExitCheck` to chase the relay chain (bounded
     depth 8, same as `uniformRelayChain`) and require it actually lands
     on `ExitBlock`. Fixed 20 more cases (596 -> **616/624**).
5. 8 cases still fail: `special.{for,while}_dynamic_iterations.
   {ifblock,elseblock}_{fragment,vertex}`. Confirmed via fresh IR dumps:
   `Header`'s own trip-count recheck is genuinely divergent *and* is not
   an exit at all -- it's a second divergent decision sharing one
   physical `Flow` dispatch block with the body's own `if`/`else` check.
   This is a new, harder shape (two divergent decisions, one shared
   dispatch block), not a mechanical extension of what's already there.
6. Verified and committed: 601/601 unit tests, all 39 Linearize lit
   tests, `check-feme` 3,445/3,505 Passed / 61 Unsupported / 0 Failed,
   `demote.*` still 30/30, `loops.*` 616/624 (up from 590/624).
7. Updated `Roadmap.md` (new `L294` entry) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new
   section) to match. Committed in 2 small commits (code fix, then docs).

## What happened this session

### Part 1: `ifblock`/`elseblock` (L295) -- 2 more hours spent, nothing landed

1. Resumed mid-investigation from the inherited summary: `Header`'s own
   divergent trip-count recheck funnels both successors unconditionally
   into the same shared `Flow` dispatch block, which makes the loop's
   *real* exit decision via a `phi`. Neither successor resolves to
   `ExitBlock` directly, so `HeaderExit` stays unrecognized and
   `collectUniformPassThroughRegion` correctly refuses to pass through.
2. **Attempt 1** (`DiamondFlattener` veto): tried vetoing
   `isLoopControlOrHeaderRelayEdge`'s relay-chase classification whenever
   both of a block's successors reach the same post-dominator via a
   plain unconditional chain. Fixed all 8 cases, but regressed
   `loop-break-structurized.ll` -- that test has the *exact same*
   block-topological shape, yet needs the opposite treatment. The two
   shapes are IR-structurally identical and only distinguishable by
   whether `Flow`'s own branch condition is itself divergent (checked
   via `FEME_DEBUG_LINEARIZE_TRACE`'s `OtherCondBrBlocks=[...]` trace).
   A block-topology-only veto can never make that distinction. Reverted.
3. **Attempt 2** (`recoverRelayExitCheck` relay-chase extension): made
   the chase hop through one more `CondBr`-terminated pure-relay block
   when its condition is a phi with a provably-constant incoming value
   for the arriving predecessor. This correctly recognized `Header`'s
   branch as an exit check without regressing `loop-break-structurized.ll`.
   But it made things *worse*: all 8 cases went from a clean compile-time
   diagnostic to a **silent wrong-pixel runtime image mismatch**.
4. Root-caused attempt 2's bug via a hand-built standalone `.ll`
   reproducer: `Header`'s relay stub doesn't land directly on
   `ExitBlock` like every previously-supported shape -- it lands on
   `Flow`, an intermediate block that *also* merges real loop-carried
   per-iteration values via its own phis (not just the live/side-effect
   mask phis the existing code already knows to preserve). Once
   `Header`'s branch is replaced, those phis silently collapse to their
   one remaining incoming value, discarding the "freeze my output once
   I've individually stopped iterating" semantics -- using a stale,
   wrong-iteration value.
5. Reverted attempt 2 in full. `Linearize.cpp` is back to its exact
   `L294`-landed state (confirmed via `git diff`, 0 lines). Re-verified
   the revert restores the clean diagnostic failure (not the silent
   wrong-pixel one) and `ninja check-feme` matches the `L294` baseline
   exactly: 3,445/3,506 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed.
6. **Design sketch for a real fix (next session, not yet implemented):**
   generalize the existing `ExitBlockRelayValues` capture-and-select
   mechanism beyond literal `ExitBlock` to *every* intermediate block the
   relay chase passes through. For each such phi fed by the relay
   predecessor: capture its relay-arm value (`OldVal`) and its
   other-arm value (`FreshVal`) *before* removing the predecessor, build
   `select(HeaderStaying, FreshVal, OldVal)`, RAUW the phi's downstream
   uses with that select, then let the predecessor removal proceed
   (the now-unused phi collapses harmlessly). This is exactly
   `DiamondFlattener`'s own standard SSA-merge idiom, applied surgically
   at just this one merge point instead of re-flattening the region.
7. Documented in `Roadmap.md` as `L295` (two failed approaches +
   design sketch for a third).

# Session: L297 -- `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` root-caused and fixed -- 2026-10-01

Device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. ✓

## Win: Mandelbrot renders again

`Basic/Mandelbrot.test` was solid black (91% pixel mismatch) since
some session after `L124p`'s original fix. Now passes. Root cause and
fix below.

## What was wrong

1. `ExitBlockRelayValues` (in `linearizeCycle`'s `HeaderDivergent`-
   coexists-with-`CheckBlock` path) can capture **two different**
   values for the same `ExitBlock` phi -- one from `Header`'s own
   uniform-timeout exit, one from `CheckBlock`'s own genuinely
   divergent exit -- whenever both relay through the same intermediate
   dispatch block one hop before `ExitBlock`.
2. The old restore loop kept whichever capture ran first (`Header`'s,
   always first in program order) and silently dropped the other.
3. Once the dead original relay chain got cleaned up, the phi
   collapsed to `Header`'s flat constant -- permanently losing the
   per-lane "did this lane take the divergent exit" signal. Mandelbrot's
   own `Diverged` flag is exactly this signal.

## How it was found (≈2 hours)

1. Built a 4-thread minimal HLSL repro (`for` + data-dependent `break`
   + post-loop `if`) -- seconds to iterate vs. Mandelbrot's 16M threads.
2. Dumped pre-linearize and post-linearize IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRELINEARIZE`/
   `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD`) -- found `xor i1 true, true` where a real
   per-lane value should have been.
3. Added `FEME_DEBUG_PEEL_TRACE` to `peelConstantFlowPredecessors` --
   confirmed the peel step itself still produces a correct phi; the bug
   is strictly later, in the `HeaderDivergent`/`CheckBlock` restore
   loop.
4. Read `ExitCheck::RelayBlock`'s own doc comment ("the real *last*
   hop") -- this told me `CheckExit->RelayBlock` is the intermediate
   dispatch block itself (`Flow3`), not one hop further out as I'd
   guessed in the prior session -- which made the actual bug ("two
   different captures for the same phi, first-wins drops the second")
   obvious once I looked at the restore loop with that fact in hand.

## The fix (≈1 hour to implement + verify)

1. Tag each `ExitBlockRelayValues` entry with its origin (`Header` vs.
   `Check`).
2. Add a new loop-carried boolean phi `ExitedViaCheck` (threaded like
   the existing `Live`/`SideEffect` masks): `true` once this lane's
   exit was via `CheckBlock` specifically, `false` otherwise. Computed
   as `Masks.Live AND NOT Staying`, OR-accumulated each iteration.
3. When a phi has both a `Header`- and `Check`-origin capture that
   differ, merge via `select(ExitedViaCheck, CheckValue, HeaderValue)`
   instead of picking one arbitrarily.

This was **not** the "generalize `ExitBlockRelayValues` to every
intermediate relay block" idea two prior sessions tried and reverted
(see `L295`'s entries) -- that approach tried to chase *further* through
the relay chain. The actual bug needed no chasing at all: both captures
were already landing on the *same* phi, just getting clobbered by each
other. Much smaller, much safer change than what was previously
attempted.

## Verification

- Minimal repro: `[1003,1002,1001,1000]` (was `[0,0,0,0]`). ✓
- `Basic/Mandelbrot.test`: Pass (was Fail). ✓
- `ninja check-feme`: 3446/3446, 0 regressions, +1 new IR-level
  regression test (confirmed it fails without the fix, passes with it).
- `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*`: 616/624, same known 8 `ifblock`/`elseblock`
  cases as before (`L295`'s open item) -- unchanged.
- `dEQP-VK.glsl.demote.*`: 30/30 -- unchanged.
- `check-hlsl-feme-vk` under `-j1`: Mandelbrot now passes; same 10
  pre-existing unrelated failures as `L296`'s baseline. (Default `-j`
  still flakes Mandelbrot via a known `VK_TIMEOUT` sandbox-parallelism
  artifact -- confirmed via `-j1` re-run, same methodology `L296` used.
  Not a real failure.)

# Session: L298 -- `WaveActiveBit{And,Or,Xor}.convergence.test` root-caused and fixed -- 2026-10-01

Device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. ✓

## Win: all 3 `WaveActiveBit*.convergence.test` cases pass, plus 2 bonus fixes

`WaveActiveBitAnd/BitOr/BitXor.convergence.test` were failing since
`L296`'s triage flagged them. Now all 3 pass. Also confirmed, as a
side effect, `inc_counter_array.test` (separately-tracked atomic-
counter-ordering suspect) now passes too -- not independently
re-root-caused, but consistent with the same divergent-loop masking
gap this session fixed.

## What was wrong

1. `WaveActiveBitAnd`'s own divergent-trip-count-loop sub-case (`Out5`:
   each thread iterates `TID.x` times) returned `[65520,0,0,0]` instead
   of `[65520,15,15,15]`.
2. `LoopLinearizer::linearizeCycle`'s final fallback branch (no
   separate `CheckBlock` elsewhere in the cycle -- `DivergentCandidates`
   empty) called `applyStageMasks` on `Header`/`Latch`/`ExitBlock`
   only, **never on the loop body blocks in between**.
3. The loop body's own `llvm.spv.wave.reduce.and.i32` call got no
   masking `select` at all -- every lane's raw value (including
   already-finished, logically-inactive lanes') got ANDed in
   unconditionally, zeroing the result.
4. A stale comment at this exact spot claimed the body "would have
   been rejected already" if it contained anything mask-affecting.
   Checked: no such rejection exists anywhere in this code path. A
   real, previously-unnoticed gap, not an intentional restriction.

## How it was found (≈1.5 hours)

1. Compiled a standalone HLSL repro via the real `/usr/local/bin/dxc`
   (`-T cs_6_5 -spirv` -- in-tree `clang-dxc` has an unrelated,
   pre-existing `-spirv-ext=all` driver bug blocking `-spirv` entirely).
2. Dumped pre/post-linearize IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRELINEARIZE=1
   FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD=1` -- both are boolean stderr-print flags, not
   file paths).
3. Found the loop body's wave-reduce call had no masking `select`,
   unlike the shader's 3 other (non-loop) `WaveActiveBitAnd` sites.
4. Traced into `Linearize.cpp`, found the fallback branch's bare
   `rethreadNestedEntryMasks`-only loop never called `applyStageMasks`.
   Confirmed via `FEME_DEBUG_LINEARIZE_TRACE=1`: this loop really does
   take this exact fallback branch (`HeaderDivergent=1
   OtherCondBrBlocks=[]`), not the `CheckBlock`-coexist branch `L297`
   fixed.

## The fix (≈1 hour)

1. Compute `BodyRegionStart` (from `Header`'s own exit check to
   `Latch`).
2. Reuse `collectUniformPassThroughRegion` (already proven in the
   `CheckBlock`-coexist branch for exactly this purpose) to both
   validate the body really is a uniform-control-flow pass-through
   (diagnose + bail if not -- closes the missing safety check) and
   enumerate its blocks.
3. Call `applyStageMasks` (the actual fix) + `rethreadNestedEntryMasks`
   (preserved, for a nested child cycle's own header) on every block in
   the validated region.

Distinct bug from `L297`: that one was a conflict (two captures for
the same phi, first-wins). This one is an omission (body blocks never
got `applyStageMasks` at all). Same neighborhood of `linearizeCycle`,
different failure mode -- confirmed, not assumed, per this session's
own standing instruction to verify before assuming "same bug as L297".

## Verification

- Minimal repro: `[65520,15,15,15]` (was `[65520,0,0,0]`). ✓
- New IR-level regression test
  (`wave-reduce-masked-in-divergent-trip-count-loop.ll`): confirmed to
  **fail without the fix** (`git stash` A/B on `Linearize.cpp` alone,
  rebuilt `feme-opt`, re-ran, no masking select present), **pass with
  it**.
- `ninja check-feme`: 3447/3447, 0 regressions (+1 new test).
- `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*`: 616/624, same known 8 `ifblock`/`elseblock`
  cases (`L295`'s open item) -- unchanged.
- `dEQP-VK.glsl.demote.*`: 30/30 -- unchanged.
- `check-hlsl-feme-vk` under `-j1`: 721/727 (up from `L296`'s own
  477/727 baseline, after upstream test-content churn). Confirmed
  `WaveActiveBitAnd/BitOr/BitXor.convergence.test` all pass; also
  `Mandelbrot.test` (`L297`) and `inc_counter_array.test` (bonus, not
  independently re-root-caused) now pass. Remaining 6 failures: the
  same already-documented, pre-existing issues (4
  `InterlockedCompareExchange{,.resources}.32.test`/
  `InterlockedCompareStore{,.resources}.32.test` milestone-9
  barrier-in-divergent-control-flow limitation, plus

  lit-annotation issues).

## Wins this session

1. **L293's residual `fwidth` cases (3 cases): closed, confirmed non-bug.** Extracted exact pixel diffs from the qpa's own `<Text>` lines (no image-diffing needed for `derivate` tests). Root cause: ~6e-7 raw per-lane differences (a few float32 ULPs) get amplified by a per-channel display-space remapping before thresholding, pushing just the alpha channel over threshold. Same class as the earlier `L287` `cosh`/`sinh` finding. Docs updated, committed as `7212549e`.
2. **`check-hlsl-feme-vk` repaired.** The `854cc3f` cherry-pick a prior session claimed to have done was **not actually present** in the local `offload-test-suite` checkout (verified: `grep -n "FeMe" CMakeLists.txt` found nothing before re-cherry-picking). Re-cherry-picked it, reconfigured llvm-project's cmake, confirmed `check-hlsl-feme-vk` exists and runs: 481 Passed / 207 Unsupported / 31 XFAIL / 7 Failed / 1 UnexpectedPass (727 total).

## L265 (ASTC alpha decode bug): still open, but now deeply understood

**What I found:** `ASTCDecode.cpp`'s decode pipeline is **spec-correct**, not buggy. Bit-exact-verified every single stage (raw ISE extraction, `unquantizeColorValue`, `bitTransferSigned`, CEM-13 endpoint construction + swap + `blueContract`) against a from-scratch Python re-implementation of the spec — all match. The actual failure mechanism: a blit's bilinear blend of 4 decoded alpha texels lands on a mathematically **exact** IEEE-754 `0.5` (not a rounding-amplified near-tie — verified at `%.20g` precision), hitting the 2-bit-SNORM-alpha quantization boundary. This needs `0.5 -> 1` (away from zero) to match the reference, but `L260`'s existing fix (`roundTiesToEven`, `0.5 -> 0`/even) is needed by a *different* case (`astc_5x5`, re-confirmed still passing unmodified this session). **No single global rounding rule satisfies both.** Spec text doesn't mandate a tie direction either way.

**What this means for next time:** stop re-deriving the decode math by hand — it's already proven correct. The open question is narrower now: find a structural difference between the `astc_5x5`/`L260` case and the `astc_8x8`/`L265` case that would justify a *scoped* special case (not a global rule flip), or find a non-tie-related root cause in the blit sampling itself that would avoid landing on an exact tie in the first place (not found this session — would need comparing against what a real GPU/reference ASTC decoder's own bilinear filtering order produces for the same input, which I did not have time to set up).

**Caught my own mistake mid-session:** while re-deriving `bitTransferSigned` by hand (not re-reading the source), I had the two statements backwards and got a wildly wrong partition-0 endpoint. Re-reading the actual source line-by-line caught it — a good reminder that "manually re-derive from memory" is a weak verification method; always re-read the actual source before trusting a by-hand trace, especially multiple edits deep into a session.

No code change made for `L265` — all debug instrumentation (`fprintf`/`getenv` traces in `ASTCDecode.cpp` and `ImageOps.cpp`) was reverted via `git checkout` before committing anything; confirmed clean via `git diff`. `L260`'s fix was not touched. Docs committed as `9523bb15`.

# Session: L299 -- `InterlockedCompareExchange`/`InterlockedCompareStore` regression root-caused and fixed

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## Wins this session

1. **Branch drift re-repaired.** `offload-test-suite`'s `feme` branch had drifted back to `origin/main` again (same recurring external/automated reset pattern as every prior session). Re-cherry-picked `854cc3f` as local commit `d0974dd`, reconfigured llvm-project's cmake. `check-hlsl-feme-vk` works again.
2. **Both `Interlocked*` regressions fixed.** `InterlockedCompareExchange.32.test` and `InterlockedCompareStore.32.test` now pass again (and their `.resources.32` siblings). Root cause: two related gaps in `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/EntryWrapper.cpp`'s `matchLoopShape`/`buildWrapperForLoop` (a header phi's value read a second time inside the header itself, for use only by the post-loop suffix, wasn't recognized as safe; fixing that then exposed a missing `loopvarN`-threading case for that same kind of header-derived value reaching the suffix). Full writeup: `feme/docs/Roadmap.md`'s new `H174` (parent `H163`).
3. **Verified clean:** `check-feme` 3448/3448 passed (0 failed). `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: only the known pre-existing `Mandelbrot.test`/`spec_const_32_bits.test`/`WaveActiveMax.test` failures remain, no new regressions. CTS: `dEQP-VK.compute.pipeline.*` (20502 cases) and its `*barrier*` subset (941 cases) both 0 Failed.

## How I found it (useful method, re-use next time)

Don't reconstruct the failing IR by hand from HLSL -- it never matches the real compiled shape. Use the documented recipe in `feme/.instructions.md`:
1. Run the failing case once under `llvm-lit -v --filter <name>` so its `Output/` artifacts exist.
2. `FEME_DUMP_IR=1 ./bin/offloader <pipeline.yaml> <spirv.o> 2>dump.ll` dumps the exact module `EntryWrapperPass` sees.
3. `./bin/feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-wrap-entry -S dump.ll` reproduces the failure standalone, seconds-long iteration instead of a full ICD rebuild.
4. For "why does this shape-matcher decline," temporarily wrap each `return std::nullopt;` in the matcher with an env-gated `errs()` print showing the line number (`sed`/Python one-liner, reverted via `git checkout` before any real fix lands) -- pinpointed the exact failing check in minutes instead of a long manual CFG trace.

# Session: L305-L307 -- env-var methodology bug, descriptor-layout-lifetime crash, mirror-blit off-by-one

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed, via a sourced helper script (see "Lesson" below).

## The scary one: this session's own CTS runs were silently invalid for a while

**What happened:** `export VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/path/to/feme_icd.json VK_DRIVER_FILES=$VK_ICD_FILENAMES` on a **single line** does not do what it looks like. Bash expands `$VK_ICD_FILENAMES` against its value *before* that same line's own assignment runs, so `VK_DRIVER_FILES` silently got the environment's *old* value, not FeMe's path. Every CTS batch this session ran that way was actually hitting the system's real `llvmpipe`, not FeMe -- including a whole `VK_KHR_maintenance8` "false advertisement" investigation that turned out to be real llvmpipe behavior, nothing to do with FeMe at all.

**Fix:** two separate `export` lines (or a three-variable pattern), never one combined line. Wrote `/tmp/feme_env.sh` with the safe pattern:
```sh
export FEME_ICD=/home/dev/dev/llvm-project/build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json
export VK_ICD_FILENAMES="$FEME_ICD"
export VK_DRIVER_FILES="$FEME_ICD"
```
**Source this at the start of every future bash call that runs `vulkaninfo` or `deqp-vk`** -- each tool call is a fresh shell, nothing persists.

**Lesson for next session:** `vulkaninfo --summary` can report the right device even when the fuller env-var state used for the *actual test run* is broken -- the summary check alone is not proof the test run itself used the right device. Worth a periodic cross-check, not just blind trust in the one check.

## Wins this session (once pointed at the real device)

1. **Found and fixed a real use-after-free crash (`L305`).** `vkCreatePipelineLayout` stored a raw pointer to each `VkDescriptorSetLayout`; the spec allows destroying that handle right after pipeline-layout creation, and CTS's `descriptor_set_layout_lifetime` test does exactly that, then creates a pipeline from the still-live layout -- segfault in `SHA256::update` via a dangling pointer. Fixed by having `PipelineLayout` deep-copy each set's bindings into its own `std::optional<DescriptorSetLayout>` at creation time. Both CTS cases now Pass.
2. **Found and fixed a real wrong-rendered-output bug (`L306`).** Re-running `copy_and_blit.core.blit_image.*` (73,839 cases) turned up 54 failing `mirror_*` cases (flipped blit regions). Root cause: the destination-coordinate formula `DstX0 + X * DstStepX` is only correct when unmirrored; when mirrored, `DstX0` is still the *exclusive* bound (same convention as unmirrored), so the first real pixel is `DstX0 - 1`, not `DstX0` -- the old code wrote one pixel out of bounds and skipped the axis' own pixel 0. Fixed with a small `mirroredCoord` helper. All 54 cases now Pass.
3. **Confirmed `L265`'s ASTC tie-break bug is broader than thought** -- the same 12-case failure pattern now also includes `astc_10x5`/`astc_12x12`, not just `astc_5x5`/`astc_8x8`. Documented, not re-attempted (several prior sessions already struck out on a scoped fix).
4. **Found two more things via `copy_and_blit.core`'s small subgroups (222 fails, 7,872 cases sampled):**
   - 36 cases (`depth_stencil_msaa_copy`/`resolve_image`) are the *same* already-tracked multisample image-creation gap (`L280`/`L281`) -- just confirmed it's general, not depth-specific.
   - 162 cases (`use_after_copy.*_msaa`, many color formats) are a **new** bug: pipeline creation fails to legalize `spirv.ImageFetch` with a `Sample` operand against an arrayed+multisampled image. This is a missing SPIR-V-to-LLVM lowering case, not yet root-caused -- filed as `L307` (todo), looks like real compiler work, not a quick fix.
5. Both fixes verified: targeted CTS re-runs (0 regressions in either), full `ninja check-feme` (3450/3450 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed), full `ninja check-hlsl-feme-vk` (unchanged baseline: 2 pre-existing unrelated fails, 1 pre-existing unrelated unexpected-pass -- same as every recent session, no `feme`-branch drift).

# Session: L307 -- root-caused and fixed the `use_after_copy.*_msaa` legalization gap

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed, via `/tmp/feme_env.sh`'s safe three-line export pattern (recreated fresh this session -- `/tmp` does not persist).

## The win: `L307` closed, 196 cases fixed

Picked up last session's #1 next step: `OpImageFetch` with a `Sample` operand against an arrayed+multisampled sampled image failed SPIR-V-to-LLVM legalization outright, surfacing as 162 pipeline-creation failures in `dEQP-VK.api.copy_and_blit.core.use_after_copy.*_msaa`.

Turned out to be **two stacked gaps**, not one:

1. **MLIR pattern gap** (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`): `ImageLoadPattern`'s `Sample`-operand handling (added under `H19g` for a *storage*-image `OpImageRead`) was hard-gated to `ImageReadOp` only via `if constexpr`. `ImageFetchOp` (a *sampled*-image `texelFetch()`) never got it, despite MLIR's own `SPIRVImageOps.td` having no restriction against it. Fix: drop the `if constexpr`, compute `HasSample` for both ops.
2. **CPU-lowering gap** (`SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`): even with (1) fixed, `hasOnlySupportedImageUses` still explicitly rejected any fetch against `Plain2DMS`/`Array2DMS` *sampled* shapes -- a deliberate gap `L73` left open ("unstarted follow-on work"). Fix: widen the zero-mip-fetch acceptance branch to include these two shapes, with the correct 3-wide/4-wide coordinate.

**Nice surprise:** (2) needed zero new runtime code. Once accepted, the fetch's IR (`getpointer` + `load`) is identical in shape to a storage image's `OpImageRead` against the same `Plain2DMS`/`Array2DMS` shapes (already supported since `H19g`/`H19m`) -- the existing `feme.cpu.image.load.2d(.array).v4f32`/`.v4i32` runtime calls already document themselves as serving "sampled or storage" and already take a `Sample` operand. No new `ImageCallKind`, no new `FeMeRuntimeCPU.c` function.

attachment-write path as `L281` had guessed (that path was already
correct). The CTS test validates depth by *sampling* the depth
attachment through a `COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER` whose view keeps the
combined format verbatim, which is what actually reaches the broken
decode table.

**Lesson learned (reusable):** a test passing is not proof of correct
behavior underneath it. The depth-clamp-enabled sibling cases here
passed for the wrong reason (CTS sign-flips depth so clamp always

returns 0" behavior) -- only the `_no_depth_clamp` variant, needing

double-checking any "this already passes" assumption against what
specific value the test is actually asserting, not just pass/fail.

# Session: L309 fixed (multisample depth/stencil image-creation gap); L310 opened (deeper coverage bug found underneath it)

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed with `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` as 3 separate `export` statements (not combined).

**What got done, in order:**

1. Root-caused the `fragdepth` multisample depth-image-creation gap (`L280`/`L307`(a)): `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp` advertised `sampledImageDepthSampleCounts`/`sampledImageStencilSampleCounts` as `VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT`-only, under a stale `H8f`/`R30` rationale ("nothing reads a single sample from a shader yet"). `L73`/`L307` had already made that false -- the shape-based (not format-based) `Plain2DMS`/`Array2DMS` per-sample sampled-fetch lowering they added already covers depth/stencil formats too.
2. Fixed it: widened both limits to `1|2|4|8`, matching the color/integer limits. One-file fix, `feme/lib/Vulkan/PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp`.
3. Updated 3 unit tests that asserted the old (now-wrong) rejection behavior, in `ImageTest.cpp`/`EntryPointsTest.cpp`.
4. Built + ran `FeMeVulkanTests` (773/773 Pass) and `ninja check-feme` (3,454/3,515 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed) -- clean.
5. Committed in 2 small commits (code fix, then test updates).
6. Re-ran CTS `dEQP-VK.glsl.builtin_var.fragdepth.*` (45 cases) to confirm the fix actually closes cases -- **this is the important part**: it didn't. Still 18 Pass/9 Fail/18 NotSupported, same as before. But the *nature* of the 9 failures changed: `vkCreateImage` no longer rejects them (confirmed via isolated re-run), so the originally-targeted bug genuinely is fixed -- it just unmasked a second bug underneath.
7. Spent the rest of the session root-causing the second bug (not yet fixed, see below).
8. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L309` done, `L310` open) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (both sections) and committed as a 3rd commit.
9. Ran `ninja check-hlsl-feme-vk`: 486 Pass/31 XFAIL/207 Unsupported/2 Fail/1 XPASS -- matches the standing baseline (`Mandelbrot.test` happened to pass this run, consistent with its known flakiness; `spec_const_32_bits.test`/`WaveActiveMax.test`/`array_of_matrices.test` unchanged, all pre-existing and out of this project's scope).

**Win: the image-creation gap really is gone.** Any app that creates a multisample depth/stencil image with `SAMPLED_BIT` usage now succeeds, where it used to hard-fail at `vkCreateImage`. That's real, tested, and committed.

**L310, the new bug (not fixed, ~half a session invested in triage):**

Once image creation succeeds, the same 9 cases fail with `expected <nonzero> but got 0` -- looks exactly like `L308`'s old symptom shape, but it's a different bug. Ruled out a generic decode/addressing gap (the `L308` class of bug) because:
- `D32_SFLOAT` already had a decode table entry before `L308` even existed.
- The same shape-based fetch-lowering path `L307` validated against 196/196 *color*-format multisample cases is what's used here.
- Mapping the qpa's one reported mismatch back through the test shader's own `imageCoord` addressing formula shows **exactly one (pixel, sample) pair mismatches per topology, regardless of sample count (2/4/8)** -- not a consistent fraction of samples, which a real addressing/decode bug would produce.

**Leading hypothesis:** a rasterizer sample-coverage edge-case at the test's own (non-full-viewport) primitive boundary -- FeMe's rasterizer and the per-sample-shaded fragment path may disagree about which one sample is covered at a boundary pixel, so that sample keeps the depth-attachment's clear value (`0`) instead of the shader-written depth. Not proven. Structurally similar to the existing `isTopLeftEdge`/`H4j` tie-break logic, but for sample coverage, not edge ownership.

**Not yet distinguished:** write-side (the render pass's own per-sample depth write) vs. read-side (the validation pass's own per-sample coverage when it re-invokes the shader per `gl_SampleID`). Full narrative in `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s `L310` section.

# Session: L310 root-caused and fixed (`SideEffectMask` per-pass narrowing); `image_clearing` CTS sample clean; `feme` branch bumped to new upstream tip

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed with `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` as 3 separate `export` statements.

**Win: `L310` is fixed.** All 27 supported `dEQP-VK.glsl.builtin_var.fragdepth.*` cases now pass (was 18 Pass/9 Fail/18 NotSupported). `ninja check-feme`: 3,455/3,516 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported.

**Root cause (the short version):** `Executor.cpp`'s per-sample-shading loop builds a narrowed `PassInvocations` copy for each sample pass. It correctly narrows `PassInv.Coverage` (the mask gating the depth/color write) to just that pass's one sample bit, but forgot to narrow `PassInv.SideEffectMask` (the mask gating the shader's own resource stores, e.g. a marker-image write) the same way -- it stayed at the whole-quad "was *any* sample of this lane covered" value for every pass. So a pixel with one covered and one uncovered sample ran its marker-write side effect for *both* samples, while only writing real depth for the genuinely-covered one. The CTS's own marker-based validation took the (over-broad) marker at face value, expected a real depth value for the falsely-marked sample, and got the clear value (`0`) instead -- exactly the `"expected <nonzero> but got 0"` symptom.

**What got done, in order:**

1. Built a minimal, isolated regression test (`ExecutorTest.SideEffectMaskNarrowsToThePassSpecificSampleNotTheWholeLane`): a 1x1-pixel, 2-sample pipeline with a real geometric edge covering sample 0 but not sample 1, a shader that writes an unconditional raw-buffer marker before its color output. Confirmed it reproduces the bug pre-fix (`MarkerBuffer[1] == 1`, should be `0`).
2. Fixed `Executor.cpp`: compute `PassSideEffectMask` from `Quad.SampleMask[Lane] & SampleBit` (same source `PassInv.Coverage`'s own narrowing already uses) and assign it to `PassInv.SideEffectMask`, right alongside the existing `Coverage` narrowing.
3. Re-ran the new test: passes. Re-ran `FeMeGraphicsTests` in full: 382/382 Pass.
4. Committed the fix + test as one commit.
5. Ran `ninja check-feme`: 3,455/3,516 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported -- clean, +1 for the new test.
6. Re-ran CTS `dEQP-VK.glsl.builtin_var.fragdepth.*`: 27 Pass/0 Fail/18 NotSupported -- all 9 previously-failing cases now pass.
7. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L310` → done, full narrative) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (`L310` section updated from "investigated, not yet root-caused" to "root-caused and fixed", with the full mechanism/fix/verification writeup). Committed as a 2nd commit.

The local checkout was already sitting at the new tip (no action needed, the daily reset script had already picked it up) -- confirmed via `git cherry-pick d0974dd` reporting "already applied"/no-op, then `git cherry-pick --skip` to clear the attempt cleanly.

# Session: L311 fixed (multisample input-attachment-only image rejection); `synchronization.op` + remaining `copy_and_blit` groups sampled clean

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed with `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` as 3 separate `export` statements.

**Win: closed out the broader-CTS-sampling backlog that had carried across several sessions, and found/fixed one real bug doing it.**

**What got done, in order:**

1. Sanity-checked the build first: `ninja check-feme` matched the known baseline (3,455/3,516 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported) before touching anything.
2. Ran `dEQP-VK.synchronization.op.*` (20,131 cases) in one shot, per the prior session's own suggestion: **14,694 Pass / 0 Fail / 5,437 NotSupported.** Clean, no bugs, ~a few minutes wall-clock.

Ran all 8 remaining unsampled `copy_and_blit` top-level groups as a background batch (`copy_commands2`, `dedicated_allocation`, `multiplanar_xfer`, `copy_memory_indirect`, `device_address`, `sparse`, `dynamic_state`, `reinterpret`). 6 of 8 came back entirely clean (0 Fail). 2 groups (`copy_commands2`, `dedicated_allocation`) each had exactly 3 failures.
4. Mapped all 6 failures back to their test names via `awk` over the qpa logs: all 6 are the **same bug**, one per multisample count (`2_bit`/`4_bit`/`8_bit`) in each of the two groups: `resolve_image.whole_copy_before_resolving_no_cab.{2,4,8}_bit`, failing at `vkCreateImage` with `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`.
5. Isolated the failing case standalone, then traced `vktApiResolveTests.cpp` to find the exact trigger: a multisample `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` image created with usage `TRANSFER_SRC_BIT | TRANSFER_DST_BIT | INPUT_ATTACHMENT_BIT` -- deliberately **no** `COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT` (a legal combination: reading an earlier pass's attachment output without writing it in this pass).
6. Found the root cause in `Image.cpp`'s `supportedSampleCounts`: every attachment-shaped usage bit (`SAMPLED_BIT`, `STORAGE_BIT`, `COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, `DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_BIT`) had its own branch narrowing the sample-count mask and setting `Constrained = true` -- except `INPUT_ATTACHMENT_BIT`, which matched nothing. An image whose only attachment usage was `INPUT_ATTACHMENT_BIT` left `Constrained` false and fell through to the hardcoded `VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT`-only default, wrongly rejecting the 2/4/8-sample request even though `framebufferColorSampleCounts` etc. are all `1|2|4|8` on this device.
7. Fixed it: added an `INPUT_ATTACHMENT_BIT` branch mirroring `COLOR_ATTACHMENT_BIT`/`DEPTH_STENCIL_ATTACHMENT_BIT`'s own `HasDepth`/`HasStencil`-keyed limit selection. One function, `feme/lib/Vulkan/Image.cpp`.
8. Added 2 regression tests (`ImageTest.cpp`): `AcceptsMultisampleInputAttachmentOnlyImage` (color) and `AcceptsMultisampleInputAttachmentOnlyDepthImage` (depth). Confirmed both via `git stash` A/B: crash on `EXPECT_EQ` pre-fix, pass post-fix.
9. Built + ran `FeMeVulkanTests` (targeted `ImageTest` filter, 6/6 Pass) and full `ninja check-feme`: 3,457/3,518 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported (+2 for the new tests, 0 regressions).
10. Committed the fix + tests as one commit.

# Session: L312 fixed (Bresenham-mode lines ignored LineWidth); `rasterization`/`texture` groups sampled, two new untriaged findings

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed with `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` as 3 separate `export` statements.

**Win: `L312` is fixed.** `LineRasterizationMode::Bresenham` now honors `LineWidth` per the real spec instead of hardcoding every line to 1 pixel wide. 12 CTS cases newly pass. `ninja check-feme`: 3,458/3,519 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported.

**Root cause (the short version):** `Pipeline.h`'s own doc comment claimed Bresenham-mode lines are spec-mandated to always be 1 pixel wide, citing "the width of the line is not adjustable, and it is always as if it were 1.0." That citation is **stale** -- it's core Vulkan 1.0's pre-`VK_EXT_line_rasterization` wording. The real spec's "Bresenham Line Segment Rasterization" section (confirmed from the `KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs` source directly, since rendered-HTML fetches kept resolving to the wrong chapter) requires a width-`w` Bresenham line to offset the 1-pixel walk by `-(w-1)/2` in the minor direction and replicate each step into a `w`-fragment row/column.

**What got done, in order:**

1. Ran the requested scoping pass first: generated a full CTS case-list XML (`deqp-vk --deqp-runmode=xml-caselist`), streamed it through a Python `iterparse` parser to get exact per-group case counts for all 56 top-level `dEQP-VK.*` groups, cross-referenced against `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s own prior mentions. Picked `rasterization` (15,019 cases) and `texture` (25,669 cases) -- both never sampled, both explicitly on the user's own suggestion list.
2. Launched both as parallel background `deqp-vk` runs.
3. `rasterization` finished first: 390 Pass / 94 Fail / 14,535 NotSupported. Grouped the 94 failures by name prefix: 73 were `bresenham_line*_wide`/`_with_adjacency` variants.
4. Isolated the cleanest repro (`bresenham_lines_wide`): qpa reported "Detected width of 1, expected 5" at dozens of sample points.
5. Found `Pipeline.h`'s "always 1 pixel" design comment -- the suspected root cause -- but needed to confirm it against the *current* spec before touching anything, since CTS's own `bresenham_lines_wide` test construction (`vktRasterizationTests.cpp`) clearly expected width-dependent behavior.
6. Spent real effort confirming the spec text: `web_fetch` on `VkLineRasterizationMode.html`/`primsrast.html` kept resolving to unrelated chapters (shading-rate-image content, wrong anchor). `web_search` gave a plausible-sounding but ultimately contradictory answer. Settled it by shallow-cloning `KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Docs` and `grep`-ing `chapters/primsrast.adoc` directly for "Bresenham" -- found the authoritative "Bresenham Line Segment Rasterization" section with the exact offset-and-replicate algorithm.
7. Rewrote `emitLineSegment`'s `Bresenham` branch in `Executor.cpp`: determine x-major/y-major via `abs(Dx) >= abs(Dy)`, compute integer width `W = clamp(round(LineWidth), 1, 64)` (64 matching `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp`'s own `lineWidthRange[1]`), offset the walked endpoints by `-(W-1)/2` in the minor direction, emit `W` fragments per walked step instead of 1.
8. Corrected `LineRasterizationMode`/`RasterState::LineWidth`'s doc comments in `Pipeline.h` to match.
9. Added `ExecutorTest.RendersAWideBresenhamHorizontalLine` (width-3 horizontal line, confirms a 3-row band). Ran it + the existing `RendersABresenhamDiagonalLine` in isolation: both pass.
10. Ran full `ninja check-feme`: 3,458/3,519 Passed, 0 Failed, 61 Unsupported (+1, 0 regressions). Committed the fix + test.
11. Re-ran the full `rasterization` CTS group: 402 Pass / 82 Fail / 14,535 NotSupported (was 390/94). Confirmed exactly the 12 plain `*_wide` (no stipple/adjacency) cases newly pass.
12. Diffed the remaining 82 failures against the original 94: all stipple/adjacency combinations, including some with **no** width component at all (`dynamic_stipple.bresenham_lines`). Standalone repro confirmed a genuinely different bug: "Invalid fragment count"/"missing fragments" against the diamond-exit rule (227 vs. 233 expected). **Not fixed this session** -- documented as a new, separate finding (see next steps).
13. Checked on the `texture` group's background run: it had actually finished (25,646/25,669 cases) but the `deqp-vk` process itself **crashed** on an MLIR assertion (`Dim must not be SubpassData or Buffer`) building a `SampledImageType` for a texel-buffer sampled image, at `dEQP-VK.texture.texel_buffer.uniform.packed.a2b10g10r10-uint-pack32`.
14. Triaged the 131 real `Fail`s that did run before the crash: 9,668 Pass / 131 Fail / 15,846 NotSupported. Grouped by prefix: 106 `texture.shadow.*` (depth-comparison sampling), 16 `texture.explicit_lod.2d.sizes.*` (mipmap filtering), 5 `texture.multisample`. Confirmed one of each cluster reproduces standalone, but did not root-cause either -- out of this session's time budget, genuinely new untriaged work.
15. Updated `Roadmap.md` (new `L312` row, done; new `L313` row, not started, for the texture findings) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (full `L312` writeup + a separate `texture` findings section). Committed as a 2nd commit.
16. Updated `FeMeGraphicsDesign.md`'s "Status (roadmap F5, line rasterization)" section, which also repeated the stale "always exactly 1 pixel wide" claim -- committed as a 3rd commit.
17. Checked `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no change needed (`VK_EXT_line_rasterization`/`VK_KHR_line_rasterization` were already advertised; this is a correctness fix to an already-exposed mode).

**This session made no code changes outside `feme/`** -- the `texture` crash is a candidate for an isolated upstream-LLVM reproducer (it's an MLIR assertion, not FeMe-specific code), but wasn't root-caused far enough this session to confirm whether the bug is actually in FeMe's own SPIR-V lowering or genuinely in MLIR's `spirv` dialect itself -- needs more investigation before it can be isolated and fixed outside `feme/`.

# Session: L314 fixed (MLIR `SampledImageType` Dim::Buffer crash, outside `feme/`) -- `texture.*` group now runs crash-free

**Win:** `dEQP-VK.texture.*` (25,669 cases) used to abort the whole
`deqp-vk` process at case 25,646/25,669. It now runs to completion
every time: 9,669 Pass / 141 Fail / 15,859 NotSupported, 0 crashes.

## What was wrong

1. `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`.
   Confirmed, per standing instruction, before anything else.
2. The crash: `deqp-vk --deqp-case='dEQP-VK.texture.texel_buffer.uniform.packed.a2b10g10r10-uint-pack32'`
   aborted with `error: Dim must not be SubpassData or Buffer`, then an
   MLIR assertion in `SampledImageType::get`.
3. Traced it to **MLIR core, not `feme/`**:
   `mlir/lib/Dialect/SPIRV/IR/SPIRVTypes.cpp`'s
   `SampledImageType::verifyInvariants` unconditionally rejected
   `Dim::Buffer` sampled images, even though its own comment says that
   restriction is SPIR-V-1.6-only. A GLSL `samplerBuffer` (what a
   uniform texel buffer compiles to) is a `Dim::Buffer` sampled image
   and is legal pre-1.6 -- confirmed against two real upstream reports
   of the exact same spec-version nuance (`glslang` #2956,
   `SPIRV-Registry` #139).
4. Because SPIR-V deserialization builds this type via the unchecked
   `SampledImageType::get` (not `getChecked`), the bad rejection
   doesn't fail gracefully -- it asserts and kills the process. That's
   why the `texture` group run died partway through instead of just
   reporting one `Fail`.

## What I did about it

1. Fixed `SampledImageType::verifyInvariants` (`SPIRVTypes.cpp`) and
   the matching textual parser (`SPIRVDialect.cpp`) to only reject
   `Dim::SubpassData` unconditionally -- dropped the unconditional
   `Dim::Buffer` rejection, since that half of the spec rule is
   version-gated and this type has no version context to check it
   against. Left the version-gated half to version-aware validation
   elsewhere (e.g. `spirv-val`), which does have that context.
2. Updated the 2 existing lit tests whose expected diagnostics named
   the old "SubpassData or Buffer" message, and added 2 new
   positive-path tests (`image-ops.mlir`, `types.mlir`) confirming a
   `Dim::Buffer` sampled image is now accepted.
3. Verified: `mlir/test/Dialect/SPIRV/` + `mlir/test/Target/SPIRV/`
   lit suites 122/122 Passed; `MLIRSPIRVToLLVMTests` 3/3 Passed;
   `ninja check-feme` 3,458/3,519 Passed, 0 Failed, 0 regressions.
4. Committed the fix alone, touching only `mlir/` files
   (`c0314ba407ec`), per the standing cross-subproject-fix rule --
   no `feme/` source changes were needed.
5. Re-ran CTS: the standalone repro no longer crashes (now a graceful
   `Fail` -- a separate, unrelated functional bug, see below). Full
   `texel_buffer` group (23 cases): 0 Pass / 10 Fail / 13 NotSupported.
   Full `texture.*` group: 25,669/25,669 cases complete, 0 crashes.
6. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L313` marked partially-done, new `L314`
   entry for this fix, new `L315`/`L316`/`L317` entries splitting out
   what's left) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new `## L314` section with
   full root-cause narrative and verification numbers), committed
   separately (`c5e4079569f9`).
7. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no
   change needed -- this is an infrastructure crash fix in tooling
   FeMe depends on, not a FeMe feature/extension-surface change.

## Commits this session

1. `c0314ba407ec` -- MLIR fix (`mlir/` only, isolated, self-contained,
   own tests).
2. `c5e4079569f9` -- `feme/docs/` updates recording the fix.
3. This `agent_thoughts.md` entry (next commit).

## What happened this session

Mandatory device check: confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`.

Picked up `L315` (`texture.shadow.*`, 106 failures) as directed. Spent
the whole session on it and **did not find the bug**, but ruled out
3 of 4 candidate pipeline stages, which is real progress even though
nothing shipped:

1. Hand-derived (from CTS's own test-generation constants) that the
   failing sub-case likely has an implicit LOD just barely past the
   mag/min filter boundary (~0.14, should pick `MinFilter`/nearest,
   FeMe appears to pick `MagFilter`/linear instead).
2. Wrote a new unit test calling the runtime's `SampleCmp1D` directly
   with those exact hypothesized numbers. **It passed** -- the runtime
   math is correct in isolation. Committed as

   lowering is correct for this shape too.

   --feme-convert-spirv-to-llvm` -- the `Dim1D`+`Grad`+`Dref` SPIR-V-

   only has `Dim2D` `Grad` cases.)

So: three separate, independently-tested stages of the pipeline are
each individually correct for the hypothesized failing shape. The bug
is either in the one stage not yet checked (SPIR-V binary → MLIR

the `DUdX`/`DUdY` values I hand-derived, and the actual root cause is
upstream of all of this (e.g. in how the shader's own derivative/
`interpolate()` math gets compiled). That's why the recommended next
step is to **measure the real value directly** instead of continuing
to hand-verify more lowering code.

## What happened this session

Mandatory device check: confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (first try
needed explicit `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES`
exports in the same command -- same gotcha as every session, still
worth restating since it's easy to forget in a fresh shell).

Picked up `L315` again (top of last session's list). Spent the
session on direct empirical measurement instead of more hand-derivation,
and made real progress even though the bug is **still not found**:

1. **Confirmed which of the 6 `FilterCase` sub-cases actually fails.**
   Previous sessions only ever hypothesized `texNdx=1, lodX=0.14`
   (`Test2`) was the failing one -- never actually confirmed it, since
   `deqp-vk`'s default output only reports one overall Pass/Fail. Ran
   with `--deqp-log-images=enable` and read the per-sub-case log
   directly: **`Test2` is confirmed to be the only failing sub-case**,
   exactly matching the long-standing hypothesis. Decoded its embedded
   PNG images (`rendered`/`reference`/`errmask`) pixel-by-pixel: the
   reference is a clean, hard 4-column binary grid (0 or 255 per
   pixel); FeMe's rendered image matches it everywhere *except* a
   handful of specific pixels (roughly one every ~3.6 pixels, matching
   the expected minified grid-column period) showing smoothly-blended
   intermediate gray values instead of a hard jump.
2. **Discovered the shader is a compute shader, not a fragment
   shader** (`compute_1D_SHADOW`, `gl_GlobalInvocationID`-driven),
   doing its own manual perspective-correct barycentric interpolation
   (`interpolate()`) to compute `texCoord`/`dPdx`/`dPdy` by hand,
   since compute shaders have no `dFdx`/`dFdy`. This was a genuinely
   new finding -- every prior session's reasoning implicitly assumed a
   fragment shader with hardware derivatives.
3. **Built a reusable standalone repro**: hand-written HLSL
   replicating the exact `interpolate()`/`dPdx` shape, compiled via
   `dxc -T cs_6_0 -spirv`, run through `feme-run --heap=<yaml>`
   (no full CTS harness, no Vulkan device needed at all for this
   isolated piece). This is genuinely reusable infrastructure for any
   future "is the shader computing the right scalar value" question.
4. **Got the real per-pixel `dPdx`/`dPdy` empirically**, for all 64
   output pixels of the failing sub-case (not hand-derived, not
   hypothesized -- read directly out of `feme-run`'s own output):
   `dPdx` is consistently positive, ~0.034434 at every single pixel
   (float-epsilon jitter only, never near zero, never sign-flipping);
   `dPdy` is consistently ~0 (float-epsilon noise) everywhere,
   including at the specific pixels that show the blending artifact.
   This closes out the single biggest open item from last session's
   list (`L318`(a)/(b)) and **matches the long-standing hand-derived
   hypothesis almost exactly** -- so the derivative math genuinely is
   correct, this isn't where the bug is.
5. **Falsified the "`ClampedLod` sign-flip" theory directly**: since
   `femeRTUseLinearFilter` picks `MagFilter` vs `MinFilter` purely off
   `ClampedLod`'s sign, and the real `dPdx`/`dPdy` are stable and
   positive everywhere, `ClampedLod` cannot be flipping sign at the
   blended pixels. Whatever is happening, it isn't this.
6. **Falsified the "nearest/point-sample path can blend" theory by
   re-reading the code directly**: `femeRTSampleCmp1DAtLevel`'s
   `UseLinear=false` branch does one texel fetch, one compare, and
   returns the raw `0.0`/`1.0` result -- there is no code path there
   that can produce an intermediate value. Whatever's producing the
   gray pixels, it cannot be this function's nearest-filter branch
   working correctly on the wrong level either, since even then the
   *output value itself* would still be binary.
7. **Falsified the "wrong `MipFilter` mapping" theory and the
   "trilinear-blend-across-differently-shaped-levels" theory**: read
   `Sampler::Sampler`'s `VkSamplerCreateInfo`→descriptor conversion
   directly (`Image.cpp`) -- `MipFilter` is correctly derived from
   `mipmapMode`, not accidentally aliased to `minFilter`/`magFilter`.
   Also read CTS's own texture-fill code and confirmed `fillWithGrid`
   is called independently per mip level at that level's own native
   resolution (each level has its own hard 4-column grid, not a
   blurred/averaged downsample of its parent) -- so even a mistakenly
   -triggered trilinear blend wouldn't explain gray values landing
   exactly at the same normalized grid-column boundaries.
8. **Spot-checked the one remaining unverified stage**
   (`SPIRVImporter.cpp`): its only Dref/Grad-relevant rewrite,
   `lowerProjectiveImageSamples`, only touches the `OpImageSampleProj*`
   opcode family; this shader uses the plain, non-`Proj`
   `OpImageSampleDrefExplicitLod` directly, so that pass is a no-op
   here and the real import path is unmodified upstream MLIR
   deserialization -- de-prioritized as a FeMe-specific suspect, though
   not exhaustively eliminated.
9. Was in the middle of reading CTS's own geometry-upload code
   (`ComputeBackend::createFrameResources`) to double-check this
   session's repro's own vertex-order/`texCoord`/`w` assumptions
   against ground truth when a context compaction interrupted the
   read -- this is the one loose thread left, and the clear place to
   resume.

Net: **four more hypotheses ruled out with real evidence this
session** (LOD sign-flip, point-sample blending, wrong MipFilter
mapping, trilinear-blend-across-levels), on top of the three already
ruled out last session (runtime math given correct inputs,
`SPIRVResourceLowering`, `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns`). That's seven
individually-tested, individually-clean pipeline stages, and the bug
is *still* reproducing in the real CTS run. This is genuinely
confusing and is the strongest signal yet that the bug either needs a
full end-to-end repro (not another isolated-stage check) or lives in
an assumption this session's repro made that doesn't match the real
test (hence prioritizing the interrupted geometry-verification read
as the very next step).

No code changes landed this session -- this was pure investigation
(repro-building and falsification), consistent with the instruction
to only commit real changes. Working tree is clean except for this
file and the roadmap doc update, committed separately below.

# Session: L315 full-pipeline repro attempt blocked by a new structural finding (L318/L319); feme-run gains `samplers:` heap YAML

**Device check**: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` confirmed first, per standing
instruction.

**Start here next session**: investigate why `feme-run`'s own JIT path
rejects a register-bound sampled-image handle (`llvm.spv.resource.
handlefrombinding` on a `spirv.Image`) that the real `feme::vulkan`
driver clearly handles fine -- this is now the #1 blocker for any
full-pipeline repro work on `L315`. See "L319" below for where to look
first. Estimated time: half a day to a day; it needs real tracing
through two separate pipeline-setup code paths to find the divergence.

## What got done

1. **Finished `L318`'s one open item** (~1 hour): verified the standalone
   repro's vertex-order/`texCoord`/`w` assumptions bit-for-bit against
   real CTS source (`vktTextureTestUtil.cpp`, `gluTextureTestUtil.cpp`).
   All correct, no discrepancy found. This closes out the last
   not-yet-confirmed assumption from prior sessions' narrowing work.

2. **Built `feme-run`'s missing `samplers:` heap YAML key** (~2 hours):
   `SamplerEntry`/`buildSamplerStorage`, wired into
   `DispatchResources::SamplerHeap` (which already existed in the
   runtime ABI, just never populated by this tool). New lit test
   `Tools/feme-run/heap-sampler.ll`. Committed separately
   (`b3c8deb593a3`). `ninja check-feme`: 3,460/3,521 Passed, 0 Failed,
   0 regressions.

3. **Used the new feature to attempt the planned full-pipeline repro**
   (~1.5 hours) -- a real `dxc -spirv`-compiled `SampleCmpGrad`/
   `Texture1D`/`SamplerComparisonState` shader, run end-to-end through
   `feme-run`, not hand-written LLVM IR or isolated-stage unit tests.
   **Found a structural blocker, not the hoped-for repro**:
   `feme-run --reference` fails outright with `unsupported raised
   operation: ... is a register-bound resource handle the FeMe CPU
   target cannot normalize`. Reproduced identically for a plain
   non-comparison `SampleLevel` call too, ruling out anything
   `SampleCmpGrad`-specific -- this is a general gap in how `feme-run`'s
   JIT path normalizes *any* traditionally-bound (`register(tN)`/
   `register(sN)`) sampled-image handle compiled from real SPIR-V.

## Why this matters (the actual finding)

The real CTS `compute_1D_SHADOW` shader clearly executes correctly for
the vast majority of its own sub-cases (only ~106 of many more produce
the blended-pixel artifact `L315` is chasing) -- so the real
`feme::vulkan` driver's `vkCreateComputePipelines` path *does*
normalize this exact resource shape successfully. `feme-run`'s own JIT
entry point (`main()` -> `JITEngine::create` -> `feme::cpu::
runPipeline`) evidently goes through a **different, less-complete**
resource-normalization code path than the real driver does. This is
the same *class* of bug `H8` already found once (a pass invocation/
ordering difference between `feme::cpu::runPipeline` and `feme::
vulkan::compileGraphicsStage`), just in a different pass.

This retroactively explains something that had been nagging across
several prior `L315` sessions: every individually-isolated pipeline
stage checked out clean, yet no full end-to-end `feme-run`-based repro
had ever been built or succeeded. The tool could never execute this
shape at all -- isolated-stage testing was the *only* avenue
available, not a methodology choice, and that avenue is now
exhausted.

A smaller, separate bug surfaced along the way: `feme-run`'s
non-`--reference` (SIMD) JIT path does **not** report this same
normalization error -- it silently dispatches and produces an
all-zero result instead. The reference path's diagnostic is correct;
the SIMD path should report the identical error rather than silently
no-op.

# Session: L319 closed (reframed) + L320 found/fixed -- first working SampleCmp repro, L315 still open

## What got done (2 real bugs fixed, both committed)

1. **`L319` closed** (`d18ba923b320`, already committed before this session started): `feme-run --reference` was missing 4 passes (`RootConstantLoweringPass`/`SPIRVResourceLoweringPass`/`SPIRVPushConstantLoweringPass`/`SPIRVSubpassLoweringPass`) that `runPipeline` already ran. Reframed the whole hypothesis this session: it was never a `feme-run`-vs-`feme::vulkan` divergence (both the real driver and `feme-run`'s normal JIT path call the same `CompiledStage::create` non-`Reference` branch) -- it was `feme-run`'s own two modes diverging. **The real Vulkan driver was never broken by this.**
2. **`L320` found and fixed** (`99f644ad1144` + `393cac7efc71` roadmap update): fixing `L319` let a register-bound `Texture1D` shader actually run for the first time, which immediately produced all-zero output instead of real texel data. Root cause: `feme-run`'s heap YAML had `images:`/`samplers:` keys for the *bindless* heap only -- no way to describe a traditionally-bound (`register(tN, spaceM)`) image/sampler, so it resolved to a zero-filled reserved prefix. Added `image-bindings:`/`sampler-bindings:` YAML keys mirroring the existing `bindings:` pattern. 2 new lit tests, both pass.
3. **First-ever working full-pipeline `SampleCmp` repro** (not committed as code, just a finding): built a real `dxc -spirv` `Texture1D::SampleCmp`/`SamplerComparisonState` shader with bracketed depth values (0.1/0.3/0.5/0.7 vs. ref 0.4, `compare-func: greater`) so the correct answer is non-uniform (`1,1,0,0`) -- got exactly that. **The comparison-sampling math itself is correct** for this basic case.
4. **Re-ran the actual failing CTS case** (`dEQP-VK.texture.shadow.1d.nearest_mipmap_nearest.equal_d16_unorm`) after both fixes: **still Fail, unchanged.** Narrows the remaining bug: it's not comparison math, it's something the compute-shader repro can't exercise -- most likely implicit-derivative/mip-level selection (a compute shader has no screen-space derivatives; the real CTS case is a fragment shader using implicit derivatives against `nearest_mipmap_nearest`).

# Session: L315 root-caused and fixed -- 106 texture.shadow.* failures all cleared

**Next action:** pick `L317` (`texel_buffer`'s 10 remaining functional failures) next -- it's the largest untouched, already-scoped item left. See "State for next session" below for the full ranked list.

## What got done (the big one: L315 is finally closed)

1. **Found the actual bug**, after ~5 sessions of this investigation circling it: `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`'s lowering of `llvm.spv.resource.samplecmp`/`.samplecmp_clamp`/`.samplecmpbias`/`.samplecmpbias_clamp` (SPIR-V's `OpImageSampleDrefImplicitLod` with no `Grad` operand -- exactly what a fragment shader's `SampleCmp`/`SampleCmpBias` compiles to) **always passed zero-constant derivatives** (`DUdX`/`DUdY`/`DVdX`/`DVdY` and their `Plain1D`/`Array1D`/`Cube`/`CubeArray` siblings), permanently forcing mip level 0 regardless of the sampler's own `nearest_mipmap_nearest`/`linear_mipmap_linear` filter. The CPU runtime (`femeCpuImageSampleCmp2DF32` et al.) already correctly computes a real implicit LOD from derivatives *if given any* -- it just never was. The ordinary (non-`Dref`) sample path already solved this exact problem via `getOrSynthesizeSample2DDerivatives`/`getOrSynthesizeSample1DDerivatives`/`getOrSynthesizeSampleCubeDerivatives` (`ImageCalls.cpp`); the `Dref` path simply never called them.
2. **Found this by comparing code, not by chasing a repro** -- the prior ~4 sessions' worth of investigation (building `feme-run` repros, capturing real `dPdx`/`dPdy` values, verifying geometry assumptions bit-for-bit) all turned out to be unnecessary once I actually diffed the `Dref` lowering against the already-correct ordinary-sample lowering side by side. Worth remembering for next time a bug resists reproduction: side-by-side code comparison against a known-working sibling path can beat building ever-more-elaborate repros.
3. **Fixed it**: call the same `getOrSynthesize*Derivatives` helpers for the `!DrefHasGrad && !DrefExplicitLod` case, for all five shapes. `Cube`/`CubeArray` needed their call moved *inside* their own `switch (Shape)` arms (after each arm's own `C2` extraction) rather than the shared pre-switch block -- doing it earlier inserted a redundant, duplicate `extractelement` of `Coord`'s third component, which a pre-existing lit test (`spirv-resource-lowering-image-samplecmp-shapes.ll`) caught immediately on the first `check-feme` run. Fixed before landing.
4. **Added a real regression test**: `samplecmp_fragment` in `spirv-resource-lowering-image-samplecmp.ll`, a `"feme.shader.stage"="fragment"`-tagged function, confirming real `feme.stage.derivative.x.coarse`/`.y.coarse` calls are synthesized where the pre-existing `samplecmp` case (no fragment-stage attribute) still correctly gets zero constants -- both cases now coexist in the same file as a before/after pair.
5. **CTS impact is the largest single-session fix this whole multi-session investigation has had**: re-ran the full `dEQP-VK.texture.shadow.*` group (5,377 cases): **577 Pass / 0 Fail / 4,800 NotSupported** (was 106 Fail in this exact group). The specific long-standing repro case, `dEQP-VK.texture.shadow.1d.nearest_mipmap_nearest.equal_d16_unorm`, now passes.

# Session: L317 closed -- combined texel-buffer handle split created a spurious sampler binding

## Mandatory device check

`vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` with `FEME_ICD`/`VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` exported inline → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## What got done: L317 is closed, 10/10 texel_buffer failures fixed

1. **Picked up where the prior session (interrupted mid-investigation by context compaction) left off.** That session had already traced `L317`'s 10 `texel_buffer` failures down to a `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` rejection (`"shader's (set 0, binding 0) requirement is not satisfied by its VkPipelineLayout"`) and identified the real shader shape (GLSL's `uniform samplerBuffer` + `texelFetch()` -- a single combined `{image, sampler}` struct handle, no `OpSampledImage`), but hadn't confirmed what actually happens downstream, and was stuck on a `feme-translate` tool-invocation error.
2. **Unblocked the tool chain first.** `feme-translate --spirv-to-llvmdialect`/`--spirv-to-llvmir` kept failing with `"expected a 'spirv.module' op, got 'builtin.module'"` no matter how the input was wrapped. Found the actual working chain: `feme-translate --import-spirv` (works) → `feme-opt --feme-convert-spirv-to-llvm` (the pass `test/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/*.mlir`'s own `RUN:` lines use) → extract the inner attribute-bearing module from `feme-opt`'s doubly-wrapped output → plain upstream `mlir-translate --mlir-to-llvmir` (not a `feme-translate` flag at all). This is the right tool for a from-scratch SPIR-V → real-LLVM-IR repro; worth remembering for next time.
3. **Confirmed the root cause empirically.** `splitCombinedSampledImageHandles` (`SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`, added under `H13d`) correctly splits a combined-struct `handlefrombinding` call into separate image/sampler handles when it sees only `extractvalue` users -- but it did this **unconditionally**, synthesizing both halves even when only one (`extractvalue ..., 0`, the image) was ever read. The synthesized-but-unused sampler handle still got classified and recorded (`hasOnlySupportedSamplerUses`'s `for (users())` loop is vacuously true for zero uses), producing a *second*, spurious `(set 0, binding 0)` `Sampler`-class `BoundResourceRange` alongside the real `Buffer`-class one. `validateBoundRanges` then rejects the pipeline because the real layout only has one descriptor there.
4. **Fixed it**: `splitCombinedSampledImageHandles` now computes `NeedsImage`/`NeedsSampler` from the real `extractvalue` index set and only synthesizes the half(s) actually read.
5. **Added a real regression test** (not just an IR-shape check): `LowersCombinedTexelBufferHandleWithoutSpuriousSamplerRange` mirrors the exact repro shape and asserts, via `ResourceInfo::fromModule`, exactly one `BoundResourceRange` (`Buffer`-class) -- confirmed two before the fix, one after. Needed linking `FeMeTargetCPU` into `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` for the test to call `ResourceInfo::fromModule` directly.
