# Session: L321 closed -- isLinearChain couldn't handle a barrier-free diamond inside a loop body

## Mandatory device check

`vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/`VK_DRIVER_FILES` exported inline → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## What got done: L321 closed, 3/5 of L316's texture.multisample cluster fixed

1. **Picked up `L316`** (`texture.explicit_lod.2d.sizes.*` 16 cases + `texture.multisample` 5 cases, handed over from the prior session as the top-ranked next step). Ran both groups first to get exact failing case names and counts: `explicit_lod.2d.sizes.*` confirmed 16/288 Fail (all non-power-of-two sizes `31x55`/`57x35`, `*linear_mipmap*_repeat*`); `texture.multisample` confirmed 5/10 Fail (2 `NotSupported` on `shaderInt64`, 3 more `NotSupported` on sample count).
2. **Picked the smaller, more tractable cluster first**: `texture.multisample`'s 3 `invalid_sample_index.sample_count_{2,4,8}` failures all hit the same pipeline-creation diagnostic (`feme-cpu-wrap-entry: ... barrier inside non-linear control flow ...`), distinct from the 2 `atomic.storage_image_r32{i,ui}` failures (a different, resource-normalization rejection).
3. **Reproduced standalone** via the documented `FEME_DUMP_IR` recipe: dumped the real post-SIMDize module, fed it to `feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-wrap-entry` directly -- no CTS/Vulkan needed to iterate.
4. **Root-caused**: the shader's real shape is two sequential loops (an "initialize" loop with a barrier-free `if (...) color = ...;` diamond body, a barrier, then a structurally identical "verify" loop). `walkBarrierFreeArm` (used by `isLinearChain`) only tolerated a mid-arm `CondBr` in one narrow pre-existing shape (H94b's widened-reduction case) -- a plain barrier-free diamond inside a loop body hit neither that shape nor a fresh exit, so it failed outright even though the loop is fully splittable.
5. **Fixed**: `walkBarrierFreeArm` now falls back to the existing general acyclic-region matcher (`matchBarrierFreeRegion`, H163) when it hits an unrecognized mid-arm `CondBr`, absorbing the nested diamond and continuing from its exit. Had to loosen the "stop at a 2+-predecessor block" rule too, since a region's own internal merge point legitimately has 2+ predecessors that are all this same arm's own blocks.
6. **New regression test**: `EntryWrapperTest.SplitsLoopWithDiamondBodyBeforeBarrier`, confirmed via `git stash` A/B to fail pre-fix (region split never happens) and pass post-fix.

## A detour that found a second bug (tracked, not fixed)

My first draft of the regression test used a *single* loop (diamond body, barrier only in a trailing block after the loop) -- this crashed with an LLVM IR-verifier assertion (`Uses remain when a value is destroyed!`) in a completely different code path (`buildWrapperForLoop`/`matchLoopShape`), reproducing identically with or without my fix. Confirmed pre-existing, not a regression, by stashing my fix and re-running: same crash. Rewrote the test to use two sequential loops (the real CTS shape) to avoid this path entirely, and tracked the crash as its own roadmap item (`L323`) rather than silently dropping it.

# Session: L316 closed (precision-bits root cause), L322 closed (no code change), L323 reproduced

Mandatory device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU
Vulkan Device`, confirmed at session start.

## What got done: L316 fixed, L322 confirmed already-fixed, L323 reproduced

1. **`L316`** (`texture.explicit_lod.2d.sizes.*`'s 16 NPOT mipmap-filtering
   failures, handed over as best next pick): root-caused to a device-limits
   mismatch, not a math bug. `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp` advertised
   `subTexelPrecisionBits`/`mipmapPrecisionBits = 4` (spec minimum), but
   FeMe's runtime (`FeMeRuntimeCPU.c`) always computes bilinear/mip weights
   as full unquantized `float` -- never quantizes to 4 bits at all. VK-GL-CTS's
   `vktSampleVerifier.cpp` builds its pass/fail tolerance band *from the
   advertised bit count*, so a narrower-than-reality advertised precision
   makes the verifier's own search space too coarse to bracket FeMe's (more
   precise, but correct) output. Confirmed numerically for the `31x55` case:
   true weight ≈0.9727, but 4-bit quantization only offers 0.9375/0.0 nearby.
2. **Fix**: raised both limits to 8 (matches lavapipe/SwiftShader, confirmed
   via web search -- real software rasterizers report 8 for the same reason).
   Two-line device-limits change, no runtime math touched.
3. **New test**: `PhysicalDeviceInfoTest.TexelAndMipmapPrecisionBitsReflectUnquantizedFiltering`.
4. **`L322`** (multisample atomic storage-image handle gap, handed over as a
   split-out unknown): re-ran with `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` --
   both `storage_image_r32{i,ui}` cases **already Pass**. No
   `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp` commits since `L317` exist to explain this
   directly -- most likely a side effect of `L321`'s own
   `walkBarrierFreeArm` fix from a prior session (same dispatch shader
   exercises both the diamond-body control flow `L321` fixed and this
   atomic handle). Verified the full `texture.multisample.*` group: 4
   Pass/0 Fail/6 NotSupported (genuinely unsupported, `shaderInt64`/sample
   count). No code change -- docs-only commit recording the re-verification.
5. **`L323`** (loop+trailing-barrier diamond crash, handed over as a
   split-out unknown): built a minimal standalone IR reduction (one loop,
   barrier-free diamond body, barrier only in a block *after* the loop) as
   a temporary gtest, ran it, confirmed the crash: `UNREACHABLE executed at
   llvm/lib/IR/Value.cpp:99!` -- "Use still stuck around after Def is
   destroyed: br i1 %cond, label %true, label %merge" -- originating in
   `buildWrapperForLoop` (`EntryWrapper.cpp`, starting line 2295).
   **Reverted the test immediately** via `git checkout --` since it aborts
   the whole process (not a normal `EXPECT_` failure) and must never be
   committed to the suite. Recorded the full repro IR + crash backtrace in
   both `Roadmap.md` and `VulkanCTSReport.md` so next session can start
   from a working reduction instead of re-deriving it. Not fixed this
   session -- root cause (which erasure runs before `%true`'s terminator
   is rewritten) not yet pinpointed.

# Session: L324 -- Bresenham half-open diamond-exit rule fix

Device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU
Vulkan Device`, confirmed (mandatory, done first).

## What got done

1. **`L324` fixed and committed** (2 commits: `8b7b37781bc1` code,
   `2987b267040c` docs). Root cause: Vulkan's Bresenham diamond-exit rule
   is half-open -- a segment's own final pixel (`p1`) must not be
   drawn, so connected strip segments don't double-draw shared
   endpoints. FeMe's `Executor.cpp` drew both endpoints inclusive. For
   one isolated line this +1 excess hid inside the CTS's own tolerance;
   for `lines_with_adjacency`/`line_strip_with_adjacency` (2+ segments
   per draw) the excess compounded and broke the tolerance.
2. Fix: moved the end-of-walk check before fragment emission (skip the
   last pixel, except the degenerate single-pixel segment). Updated
   `RendersABresenhamDiagonalLine` (4→3 pixels) and added
   `BresenhamLineStripDoesNotDoubleDrawASharedVertex` (additive blending
   to catch double-draws coverage checks can't see).
3. Verified: `FeMeGraphicsTests` 384/384; `check-feme` 3,468/3,528
   Passed (+1), 0 regressions; CTS `rasterization.*` 402→414 Pass,
   82→70 Fail (exactly the 12 targeted `no_stipple.bresenham_*_with_adjacency*`
   cases, confirmed 0 regressions via Python set-diff, not eyeballing).
4. Roadmap.md/VulkanCTSReport.md updated with the `L324` entry (done)
   and a new `L325` entry documenting the remaining 49/70 stipple
   failures as the clear next chunk, not yet investigated.
5. Confirmed offload-test-suite `feme` branch drift is unchanged
   (`854cc3f`, same hash as last session's confirmed non-issue check) --
   no action needed, not a new divergence.

   `adj_*.png`, etc.).

# Session: L325 fixed (40/49 cases) -- Bresenham stipple counter was distance, not an integer count; L326 split out

Device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU
Vulkan Device`, confirmed (mandatory, done first).

## What got done

1. **`L325` fixed and committed** (2 commits: `02fa2a87666f` code,
   `adf201a68ec4` docs). Root cause: the spec's "Line Stipple" section
   defines the stipple counter `s` as an integer, with *mode-dependent*
   increment rules -- Bresenham increments `s` by exactly 1 per
   produced fragment (a pure step count); Rectangular/RectangularSmooth
   increments it once per unit-length arc-length subdivision (a
   distance measure). `Executor.cpp` used the same distance-based `Arc`
   formula for both modes -- correct for Rectangular, wrong for
   Bresenham on any non-axis-aligned line (up to `sqrt(2)` distance per
   step at 45 degrees), picking the wrong stipple-pattern bit.
   Cross-confirmed against `VK-GL-CTS`'s own reference rasterizer
   (`rrRasterizer.cpp`'s `SingleSampleLineRasterizer::rasterize`):
   `m_stippleCounter++` increments once per walked step, shared across
   width-replicated fragments.
2. Fix: dedicated `StippleCounter` float for the Bresenham branch,
   incremented by `1.0f` once per walked step (after width replication),
   returned directly instead of the shared distance-based `ArcEnd`.
   Rectangular/RectangularSmooth untouched.
3. Added `BresenhamStippleCounterCountsFragmentsNotDistance` (45-degree
   diagonal, `StippleFactor=1`, pattern `0b1000`). Confirmed via `git
   stash` A/B: fails pre-fix exactly as hand-predicted (`floor(3*sqrt(2))
   == 4`, not `3` -- pixel `(3,3)` wrongly unlit), passes post-fix.
4. Verified: `FeMeGraphicsTests` 385/385 (+1); `check-feme` 3,469/3,530
   Passed, 0 Failed, 0 regressions. CTS `rasterization.*`: 414→454
   Pass, 70→30 Fail. Of the 49 originally-scoped stipple cases, 40 now
   Pass.
5. **The remaining 9 are a different bug, split into `L326`** (not
   fixed this session): all `*stipple*.bresenham_line_strip_wide`.
   Confirmed via `--deqp-log-images=enable` these pass stipple-pattern
   and fragment-count checks cleanly -- they fail line-width
   verification instead ("Detected width of 65, expected 64"), a
   one-row overlap at a wide Bresenham line-strip's segment join.
   Unrelated to `L325`'s fix; root cause not yet found.
6. Confirmed offload-test-suite `feme` branch drift is unchanged
   (`854cc3f`) -- no action needed.
7. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no
   change needed -- `VK_KHR_line_rasterization`/stipple features were
   already advertised; this is a correctness fix only.
8. Cleaned up this session's `/tmp` scratch files.

No outside-FeMe issues found this session -- nothing to isolate/fix
separately.

# Session: L326 root-caused (not fixed) -- DDA vs. exact diamond-exit-rule mismatch, split into L327/L328

**Device check**: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

**Next action for whoever picks this up**: read `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s
`L326` section, then start on `L327` (port
`doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` standalone, with unit tests for each
corner case, before touching the working renderer at all).

## What happened this session

1. Re-reproduced `L326`'s 9 failing `*stipple*.bresenham_line_strip_wide`
   cases. Diffed Reference vs. Result PNGs pixel-by-pixel instead of
   trusting the verifier's own text ("Invalid line width... Detected
   width of 65, expected 64" was misleading -- the real bug is a whole
   extra walked row, not a geometric width error).
2. Added temporary debug instrumentation, captured ground-truth
   per-segment values, hand-simulated FeMe's own stipple algorithm in
   `numpy.float32`. Result: FeMe's own math is internally consistent.
   This is **not** an arithmetic bug like `L325` was.
3. Read `VK-GL-CTS/framework/referencerenderer/rrRasterizer.cpp` in
   full. Found the real cause: FeMe's Bresenham walk uses classic
   integer DDA (an approximation); the reference uses an exact
   fixed-point diamond-exit test (`doesLineSegmentExitDiamond`, ~250
   lines, `int64_t` subpixel arithmetic, 4 diamond-corner tie-break
   cases) evaluated against the *whole* line segment, not incremental
   steps. For segment 1's shallow non-45-degree slope these two
   methods pick a different effective step count, which shifts the
   stipple counter by one for the rest of the segment -- matching the
   observed symptom exactly.
4. **Did not implement a fix.** A bit-exact fix means porting
   `doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` itself (hundreds of lines, intricate
   corner-case logic), not a quick patch. Doing that under time
   pressure risks a subtly-wrong implementation that passes this one
   reduction but silently miscompiles other slopes. Reverted the debug
   instrumentation, left the working tree clean.
5. Split the remaining work into two scoped roadmap items instead of
   one "unknown effort" item:
   - `L327`: port the diamond-exit-test primitive standalone, unit
     test it against each of the reference's corner cases, before
     touching `emitLineSegment` at all.
   - `L328`: wire `L327`'s primitive into `emitLineSegment`, replacing
     the DDA walk with a bounding-box-and-diamond-test walk, preserving
     `L324`'s half-open rule and `L325`'s stipple-counter semantics
     (both still apply, now per diamond-test-passing position instead
     of per DDA step).
6. Committed one docs-only commit (`Roadmap.md` + `VulkanCTSReport.md`)
   with this analysis. No `feme/` source change this session -- the
   debug instrumentation was reverted, not committed.

## Why no code commit this session

The honest move here was stopping before writing code, not shipping a
rushed port. `L327`/`L328` are now concrete enough that a future
session can start immediately on `L327` without re-deriving any of
this.

   port `doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` + its helpers
   (`toSubpixelCoord`/`SubpixelLineSegment`/corner-case table) from
   `rrRasterizer.cpp` into a new `feme/lib/Graphics/` file. Unit test
   each of the 4 corner-exit/start/end sub-cases independently before
   moving to `L328`. Do not touch `emitLineSegment` yet.
2. **`L328` (a few hours, depends on `L327`)**: replace
   `emitLineSegment`'s Bresenham DDA walk with a
   bounding-box-and-diamond-test walk using `L327`'s primitive.

   the full `rasterization` CTS group for regressions.
3. **`L265` (a few hours, lowest priority, many sessions carried over,

4. **Rasterization's remaining 21 scattered failures** (`stencil`,

# Session: L327 -- ported the exact diamond-exit-rule primitive (standalone, not wired in)

**Device check**: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed at start and
re-confirmed at end, per protocol.

**Next action for whoever picks this up**: read `Roadmap.md`'s `L328`
entry (the performance caveat is the important part), then start
wiring `feme::graphics::doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` into
`emitLineSegment` using a **narrowed candidate window**, not a literal
port of the reference's brute-force bbox sweep.

## What happened this session

1. Picked up `L327` exactly as scoped last session: port
   `doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` standalone, don't touch
   `emitLineSegment` yet.
2. Read `rrRasterizer.cpp`'s full `init()`/`rasterize()` bodies (not
   just the `doesLineSegmentExitDiamond` function itself) to understand
   the complete algorithm context before porting anything.
3. Added `feme/include/feme/Graphics/LineRasterization.h` +
   `feme/lib/Graphics/LineRasterization.cpp`: a direct, bit-for-bit
   port of the reference's diamond-exit-test and all its helpers
   (corner-case tables, bound tables, side/angle-range tests). Used
   `llvm::countl_zero` in place of the reference's `deClz64` -- the
   only non-mechanical substitution.
4. Added `LineRasterizationTest.cpp` with 5 tests: horizontal/vertical
   half-open-rule checks, a 45-degree diagonal **cross-validated
   against `ExecutorTest.RendersABresenhamDiagonalLine`'s own
   CTS-confirmed output** (same endpoints, same expected pixel set --
   strong independent confidence, not just "the new code agrees with
   itself"), a shallow-slope case matching `L326`'s own failing shape
   (expected values derived by hand from standard Bresenham rounding
   *before* running the test, then confirmed to match -- not
   back-filled from whatever the code produced), and a far-reject case.
5. `ninja check-feme`: 3,474/3,535 Passed (+5 new tests), 0 regressions.
6. Committed in 2 commits: (a) code + tests, (b) docs
   (`Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md`, striking `L327` through,
   updating `L328`'s scope).
7. **Found an important design constraint while reading `rasterize()`
   in full**: the reference's own walk tests *every* `(x, y)` pair in
   the segment's bounding box -- a brute-force `O(length^2)` sweep for
   long near-45-degree lines. Fine for a reference-only software
   rasterizer; **not** fine to port verbatim into a real driver.
   Documented this in both `L327`'s own write-up and `L328`'s updated
   scope, with a concrete proposed design (keep the existing `O(length)`
   DDA major-axis stepping, test only a small window of nearby
   minor-axis candidates via the new exact primitive at each step).
8. Did **not** attempt `L328` (the actual wiring) this session --
   deliberately. The design is sound but the integration itself
   (preserving `L324`'s half-open rule, `L325`'s stipple-counter
   semantics, and `L312`'s width-replication, all simultaneously,
   while also building and validating the new narrowed-window search)
   is a distinct, substantial task better started fresh rather than
   rushed at the tail of this session.
9. Checked `offload-test-suite` branch drift: still a non-issue (local
   `d0974dd` cherry-pick matches upstream `854cc3f`'s content).

## Why this is the right stopping point

`L327` is a complete, independently verifiable, low-risk deliverable
on its own (a pure addition, zero behavior change, thoroughly tested
against known-good ground truth). `L328` is where the actual risk
lives (it touches the already-working renderer) and now has a concrete
design plus an identified pitfall to avoid -- a clean handoff rather
than a half-finished integration.

# Session: L328 -- wiring the exact diamond-exit rule into Bresenham lines

**Done this session**: `L328` landed. `emitLineSegment`'s Bresenham
branch (`Executor.cpp`) now uses the exact `doesLineSegmentExitDiamond`
primitive (`L327`, already ported last session) instead of a pure DDA
walk, tested over a narrow `+/-2`-pixel candidate window per major step
and deduped with a `DenseSet` so it stays `O(length)` instead of the
reference's own `O(length^2)` brute-force sweep.

**Result**: all 9 of `L326`'s known `*stipple*.bresenham_line_strip_wide`
failures now pass. Full `rasterization` CTS group: 463 Pass/21 Fail
(was 454/30), exactly +9/-9, 0 regressions. `check-feme`: 3,474/3,535
Passed, 0 Failed, both before and after. Committed in two pieces:
`6d3f51477b53` (the rewrite + the one regression-test fix it needed)
and `86f832e5076d` (docs).

**A process note, not a code note**: mid-session I ran `clang-format`
on the whole `Executor.cpp` file to format the new code, and it
silently reformatted ~440 unrelated lines across the entire file (an
apparent column-width/style drift between the file's actual prior
formatting and what `clang-format` now produces for it). I reverted
with `git checkout --`, which -- because the L328 rewrite itself had
never been committed or staged -- discarded that rewrite along with the
unwanted reformatting. Recovered it from the detailed design notes
already on record (this session's own continuation summary) rather
than redoing the investigation from scratch; the second attempt used
`clang-format -i --lines=N:M` scoped to just the changed function, which
kept the diff to the intended ~84 lines. **Lesson for next time: commit
or at least `git add -N`/stage work before running a whole-file
formatter on a file that might not already match the formatter's
current output, specifically so a bad revert never has a chance to
delete uncommitted work.** No work was actually lost this time only
because the design was well-documented beforehand -- do not rely on
that safety net again.

## Next steps

1. **(a few hours)** `L265` -- ASTC alpha-decode tie-break (4 block
   sizes). Lowest priority, many sessions carried over, unchanged.
   Needs a Mesa/lavapipe reference-decoder comparison.
2. **(a few hours each, 21 cases total)** Rasterization's remaining

(`color_at_{beginning,end}.{depth_bounds,depth_never,stencil_never}`).

   (`ResourceInfo.h`), computed by scanning for stores/atomics not

# Session: L331 fixed -- depth-bias rounded away by compounded fill-path interpolation

**Device check**: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` -- confirmed.

**Branch-drift check**: `offload-test-suite`'s `feme` branch still
`854cc3f`, unchanged -- no action needed.

## What's fixed

`dEQP-VK.rasterization.depth_bias.d24_unorm_constant_one_greater` now
passes. It was the last remaining item from last session's handoff.

Full `rasterization` CTS group: 475 Pass/9 Fail (was 474/10), exactly
+1/-1, 0 regressions. `check-feme`: 3,481/3,542 Passed (+1 new test), 0
Failed, 0 regressions.

## Root cause

The fill (triangle) rasterizer added the depth-bias offset to each of a
triangle's 3 vertex depths *before* bary-interpolating them per
fragment. In exact math, biasing 3 vertices and then interpolating is
identical to interpolating first and biasing the result once -- linear
interpolation commutes with a uniform shift. In float32 it is not
identical: three independently-rounded multiply-and-sum terms can
swallow a bias that a single scalar addition would have preserved. This
only shows up on sloped (non-flat) geometry with a small bias
(`depthBiasConstantFactor == 1.0`) -- exactly the failing CTS case's
shape.

Fix: stopped mutating the shared per-vertex `Depth[]` array. Added
`ScreenTriangle::DepthBiasOffset`, set once at triangle setup, added
exactly once to the already-interpolated per-fragment depth (before the
depth-clamp). `Point`/`Line` polygon modes (no further interpolation of
their own) keep biasing per-vertex, just now inline at their own call
sites instead of through the shared mutated array.

## Two dead ends worth remembering (both instructive, both fully
reverted)

1. Tried changing the `depthBiasR` constant from the spec-literal
   `2^-N` to the "true" UNORM step `1/(2^N-1)`. Looked right in Python
   double-precision math. **Completely inert in real float32 math** --
   the two constants differ by ~7e-15, far below the ~3e-8 rounding
   granularity at the relevant magnitude. Confirmed with a standalone
   `g++ -O2` test program, not Python. Lesson: verify numeric fixes in
   the actual arithmetic precision the bug lives in, not a more precise
   stand-in.
2. Tried quantizing `NewDepth` onto the stored depth's grid before
   comparing (`quantizeDepthForCompare`). Changed behavior, but wrong
   direction: regressed a previously-passing sibling case
   (`d24_unorm_constant_one_less`) while the target case still failed.
   Wrong model -- the bug isn't about comparison-domain mismatch, it's
   about where in the pipeline the bias gets rounded away.

## Commits (this session)

1. `2a78c51dd5d0` -- the fix + new unit test
   (`DrawTest.MinimalDepthBiasSurvivesSlopedInterpolationOnFixedPointDepth`,
   confirmed via `git stash` A/B to fail without the fix, pass with it).
2. `12ce936b8408` -- `Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md` `L331` entries.

No design-doc change needed (no section describes the per-vertex vs.
post-interpolation choice; this was purely a bug fix, not a design
deviation). No `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`
change needed (fix to already-exposed core Vulkan 1.0 behavior, no new
surface).

# Session: L334 fixed -- TriangleStrip/TriangleFan provoking-vertex position bug (+ L335 line_continuity triage)

**Device check**: confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` at session start and
again at session end, per standing protocol.

**Start state**: handoff listed `maintenance5.non_strict_line*` as item
1. That was already fixed and committed earlier this same session
(L333, see commits `c62f49671809`/`1b4e6e33ca2e`) before this summary
window started -- the remaining open work this entry covers is items
2-3: the other scattered `rasterization` failures.

## What got fixed: L334

**3 of 5 remaining `rasterization` failures are one bug, not three.**
`flatshading.{triangle_fan,triangle_strip}` and
`provoking_vertex.draw.default.triangle_fan` all trace back to
`Executor.cpp`'s `emitStripSegment`/`emitFanSegment` putting the wrong
vertex in position 0 of each assembled triangle.

**Lesson learned mid-session, worth flagging**: my first hypothesis
(from a web search) was that `TriangleFan`'s provoking vertex is
always the pivot vertex 0. That's wrong. Don't trust a single web
search for spec details that feed a fix -- I pulled the actual
`vertexpostproc.adoc`/`drawing.adoc` source from the Vulkan-Docs repo
and cross-checked against `vktRasterizationProvokingVertexTests.cpp`'s
own hardcoded test data before touching code. Correct equations:

- `TriangleStrip`: `p_i = {v_i, v_{i+(1+i%2)}, v_{i+(2-i%2)}}` --
  position 0 is always `v_i`; only positions 1/2 swap on odd `i`.
  FeMe swapped positions 0/1 instead.
- `TriangleFan`: `p_i = {v_{i+1}, v_{i+2}, v_0}` -- pivot `v_0` is
  **last**, not first. FeMe put the pivot first, always.

**Fix**: `emitStripSegment`'s odd-triangle case `{T+1, T, T+2}` ->
`{T, T+2, T+1}`; `emitFanSegment`'s `{Start, T, T+1}` ->
`{T, T+1, Start}`. Both are pure relabelings (odd/even permutations
respectively) -- zero geometry/winding change, confirmed by the CTS
numbers showing only the 3 target cases flipped.

**New tests**: `ExecutorTest.cpp`'s
`FlatShadesTriangleStripWithCorrectProvokingVertex`/
`FlatShadesTriangleFanWithCorrectProvokingVertex`, using a new
`buildFlatColorPipeline` helper (flat-interpolated color varying).
Verified via `git stash` A/B test: fail pre-fix, pass post-fix.

**Verified**:
- `FeMeGraphicsTests`: 393/393 Pass (+2 new).
- `FeMeVulkanTests`: 778/778 Pass (unchanged).
- `ninja check-feme`: 3,484/3,545 Pass, 0 Fail, 61 Unsupported.
- Targeted CTS (`flatshading.triangle_fan`, `flatshading.triangle_strip`,
  `provoking_vertex.draw.default.triangle_fan`): 3/3 Pass (was 0/3).
- Full `rasterization.provoking_vertex.*`/`rasterization.flatshading.*`:
  20/20 supported Pass.
- Full `rasterization` group: 482 Pass/2 Fail/14,535 NotSupported
  (was 479/5/14,535), exactly +3/-3, 0 regressions.

**Commits** (code+test, then docs, each separate):
1. `afeac15352d8` -- `Executor.cpp` fix + `ExecutorTest.cpp` tests.
2. `7d530219292c` -- `Roadmap.md` L334 entry + `VulkanCTSReport.md` L334 section.

No `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md` change
needed -- internal primitive-assembly correctness fix, no new
feature/extension surface. No design-doc deviation.

## Triaged but not fixed: L335 (`line_continuity`, 2 cases)

The last 2 `rasterization` failures, `line_continuity.{line-strip,
polygon-mode-lines}`, are a different class of problem from L333/L334
-- **not** a rendering-correctness bug, a **compiler/backend gap**.

Root cause: these are Amber-script tests whose pass/fail verdict comes
from a *compute-shader verification pass* (a flood-fill connectivity
check over the rendered framebuffer), not the draw itself. That
compute shader calls `barrier()` from inside nested `if`/`while`
control flow -- a seed-pixel `if` guard plus a flood-fill `while` loop
with multiple barriers at different nesting depths. This trips FeMe's
CPU-backend region-splitting pass's documented limit: it only supports
a straight-line wave body or a single uniform loop, not a sequence of
independently-barrier-guarded branches plus a barrier-guarded loop.

This is the same limitation category as prior `R24` (diagnose-only)
and `H72` (different shader shape, partially fixed) work -- i.e. a
known hard architectural gap, not a quick triage win. Did not attempt
a fix this session; scope is a real compiler/backend restructuring-pass
change, deserving its own dedicated session.

**Commit**: `b9201954e435` -- `Roadmap.md` L335 breakdown entry +
`VulkanCTSReport.md` L335 triage section. Investigation only, no code
changed.

## Next steps (ranked)

1. **(dedicated session, compiler/backend work)** `L335` --
   `line_continuity.{line-strip,polygon-mode-lines}` (2 cases). Extract
   a minimal standalone HLSL/SPIR-V reproducer isolating just the
   barrier-in-nested-if-and-while pattern (skip the full Amber
   flood-fill algorithm, too slow to iterate on). Then survey the
   region-splitting pass's current supported shapes (straight-line,
   single uniform loop) vs. what's needed (sequential multi-branch-
   then-barrier, barrier-guarded loop body) to scope the change. Add
   unit tests for the new shape(s) before touching CTS again.
2. **(a few hours, lowest priority, many sessions carried over)**

   session.

   Tessellation `user_defined_io` triage. Also still open:
   `shader_input_output`/`misc_draw`/`common_edge`/

# Session: L336 -- tessellator boundary-ring ULP-exactness fix

Fixed `L336`. `dEQP-VK.tessellation.*`: 601 Pass / 76 Fail / 438
NotSupported (was 577/100/438) -- 24 cases flipped, 0 regressions.
Commits: `ea5220b65b79` (code+tests), `70419fff31f2` (docs).

## What happened

1. Picked up handoff item 1 (`user_defined_io`, "largest untriaged
   chunk"). Ran it: **54/54 Pass already**. Handoff's "27 cases" was
   stale -- fixed as a side effect of an earlier session (L332/L333/
   L334, exact one not pinned down). No action needed.
2. Re-triaged the *whole* `tessellation` group fresh instead of
   trusting any other stale number: 577/100/438, same buckets as
   documented before (`invariance` 62, `shader_input_output` 15,
   `misc_draw` 13, `tesscoord` 6, `common_edge` 3, `winding` 1).
3. Took the biggest same-looking cluster:
   `invariance.outer_edge_index_independence` (24 cases). Log showed
   two vertex sets printing identically (`{0, 0.333333, 0.666667, 1}`
   both sides) yet failing exact `std::set` equality -- a float ULP
   mismatch, not a logic bug.
4. Root cause (`Tessellator.cpp`): boundary-ring builders computed a
   "backwards" edge's complementary coordinate as `1.0f - K/N` (divide
   then subtract) instead of `(N-K)/N` (subtract-as-integers then
   divide). These are not bit-identical in general. Confirmed via a
   Python float32 experiment: `N=3,K=2`: `1.0f - 2.0f/3.0f` ->
   `0x3EAAAAAA`, but `1.0f/3.0f` -> `0x3EAAAAAB`. 1 ULP off.
5. Fixed `appendQuadBoundaryRing`, `appendTriangleBoundaryRing`,
   `appendTriangleRingBoundary` -- all three used the same bad
   pattern.
6. Added 2 regression tests, `TessellatorTest.cpp`. A/B'd via
   `git stash` -- both fail pre-fix, pass post-fix.

## Dead end I nearly shipped

First version of the triangle test checked *every* generated point
(including the interior concentric ring's) against the 4 canonical
boundary values `{0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}`. It kept failing post-fix with
`0.555555`/`0.222222` values that looked like a second bug. Spent a
while chasing that as "maybe `CumulativeScale`'s own `1.0f - 2.0f/N`
has the same bug" before realizing: the interior ring's points are
*supposed* to be inset toward the centroid, they're not supposed to
equal the boundary canonical set at all. Fix was to the test, not the
code -- scope the check to only points with a `0.0f` coordinate (true
boundary points). Lesson: when a new test fails in a way that doesn't
match the bug you just fixed, check whether the test itself is
checking something that was never true, before assuming there's a
second bug.

# Session: L341 -- `outer_edge_symmetry` root-caused, found irreconcilable with `L336`, reverted

**Session-start check**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` ->
`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## What happened (short version)

Picked `invariance` triage (38 failing cases, flagged top priority by
last 3 handoffs in a row). Root-caused the dominant sub-cluster
(`outer_edge_symmetry`, 36 of 38) down to the exact float32
double-rounding bug. Built a fix. The fix worked in isolation (28/28
non-isoline cases fixed) but broke a *different* already-fixed CTS
property (`outer_edge_index_independence`, `L336`'s fix, 12 cases) and
one existing unit test. Spent the rest of the session proving, with a
minimal reproducer and exact arithmetic, that **these two properties
cannot both hold** -- not a bug I could code around. Reverted the fix
completely. Net CTS delta this session: **zero** (clean revert,
confirmed by rebuild + `FeMeGraphicsTests`: 396/396 Pass).

This is a negative result, but a solid one -- it's a load-bearing
reason not to re-attempt the same approach next time, so it's worth
reading in full once, by whoever picks up `invariance` next.

## The proof, for whoever doubts it

1. CTS's `outer_edge_symmetry` test: shader computes `1.0f - x`
   (real float32 subtraction) on one half of an edge, compares to our
   own value on the other half, via exact `std::set` equality.
2. CTS's `outer_edge_index_independence`/`common_edge` tests (fixed by
   `L336`): require every edge/patch sharing a segment count `N` to
   produce bit-identical boundary values via **direct division**
   `(N-K)/N` (integer-subtract-before-divide -- this is what `L336`
   already guarantees, don't touch it).
3. For `N=3, K=1`: direct `(N-K)/N` = `0.66666669`. Shader's
   `1.0f - (1.0f/3.0f)` = `0.66666663`. **1 ULP apart.** Whenever
   `outer_edge_symmetry` was failing (i.e. this gap exists for that
   `N`), fixing it means picking the `0.66666663` value --
   which immediately breaks `outer_edge_index_independence` for that
   same `N`, because that test demands `0.66666669`.
4. Checked whether a smarter single formula escapes this: it would
   need `K/N + (N-K)/N == 1.0f` exactly for all `K,N` (both direct
   division). False for 84,426 of 125,249 `(K,N)` pairs checked up to
   `N=500` (exact double-precision check -- an earlier draft of this
   check was wrong because it re-rounded the sum through `float32`
   and hid the mismatch; redo in double if you re-derive this).

**Conclusion: no per-point formula fixes both. A fix needs a
genuinely different (non-division-based) coordinate algorithm, or
accepting `outer_edge_symmetry` as a documented limitation.**

# Session: L342/L343 fixed -- isoline `outer_edge_symmetry` + `inner_triangle_set` (both `invariance` residuals closed out, except `L341`'s known-irreconcilable 24)

`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## What happened (short version)

Picked up `L341`'s own next-steps #3 then #2, in that order. Both
landed clean, no regressions, two small separate commits each (fix +
docs).

1. **Isoline `outer_edge_symmetry`** (12 cases, `L342`). `L341` proved
   the quad/triangle version of this bug is unfixable without breaking
   `outer_edge_index_independence`. Isolines are structurally exempt
   from that requirement (`createInvarianceTests` only registers it
   `if (triOrQuad)`) -- so this was worth checking in isolation, and it
   worked. Two wrong attempts first (both numerically disproved in
   Python before touching C++ -- do this, it's cheap): reusing `L341`'s
   reverted pair-based helper, and a mis-posed round-trip check that
   accidentally required `1.0f - (1.0f - x) == x` (not a general
   float32 identity). The fix that worked: the CTS shader applies
   `1.0f - V` exactly *once*; define the small-half value as *literally*
   that same subtraction of the large half's own value, don't
   re-derive it as an identity. Bit-identical by construction, not
   luck.
2. **`inner_triangle_set`** (2 cases, `L343`). Found via direct code
   reading, not an isolated repro this time: `H7x`'s own
   "all-factors-exactly-1" fast path (added for a `gl_CullDistance`
   bug, several sessions back) ignores the fractional-odd spacing
   epsilon rule, which always forces a real interior ring when the
   inside factor rounds to 1 -- even when outer edges are also 1. That
   made the all-exactly-1 patch produce zero inner triangles while
   every neighboring outer-edge value (holding inside fixed) produced a
   real one, breaking the invariance. Fix: exclude `FractionalOdd` from
   the fast path's trigger condition. Re-verified `H7x`'s own target
   (`clip_cull_distance`, 256 cases) still passes unchanged, since that
   test suite uses `equal_spacing`/`Integer`, never `FractionalOdd`.

# Session: L339 fixed -- TCS per-vertex patch-constant outputs + a dangling-pointer segfault (L344 opened for 2 residuals)

**Win: `cross_invocation_per_vertex_{int,uint,float,vec3,vec4}` now 5/5 Pass (was 0/5, all 5 segfaulting the whole `deqp-vk` process).**

## What shipped (5 commits, already pushed to this branch)

1. ABI surface: `RuntimeABI.h`/`ResourceHeap.{h,cpp}`/`StageArgsLayout.h`/
   `PatchPipeline.h` grew a `PerVertexOutputLayout`/`PerVertexOutputs`
   structure-of-arrays block (mirrors the existing per-patch `Outputs`
   block, one slot per output control point instead of one shared slot).
2. `CanonicalizeStage.cpp`: classification (`HasStoreInPhase`-driven)
   plus two bugfixes -- see "Two bugs found" below.
3. `PatchPipeline.cpp`: links the new per-vertex output block into the
   domain stage's ordinary per-vertex input, alongside the existing
   hull-stage link (mutually exclusive filters so neither double-claims
   the other's elements).
4. `PatchConstantWrapper.cpp`: re-invokes the patch-constant phase once
   per output control point (mirrors `HullWrapper.cpp`'s wave loop)
   whenever the signature needs it, instead of always once.
5. New unit test: `CanonicalizeStageTest.SplitsHullEntryCapturingMixedUseAlloca`.

Docs already updated and committed: `Roadmap.md` (L339 updated, L344
opened), `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new `## L339` section).

## Two bugs found while landing this

1. **Double classification.** `addElement` (which builds the real
   `SignatureElement`) calls `classifySPIRVElement` a *second* time,
   independent of the discovery loop, and was silently passing the
   default `HasStoreInPhase=false` -- overriding the correct
   classification every time. Any future parameter added to that
   function must be threaded through both call sites, not just one.
2. **A real segfault**, not a logic bug: a shader-source-level local
   variable written before `barrier()` and read after it (`T d =
   T(gl_InvocationID); ...; barrier(); ... = d + ...;`) compiles to an
   `alloca` with users split across both phases. Neither existing
   capture path (ordinary-SSA-by-copy, or all-in-Region-alloca-clone)
   applies, so it fell through to the generic path: capturing the
   alloca's raw *address* through a synthetic global. The patch-constant
   phase is a genuinely separate call, dispatched after the producing
   phase's stack frame has unwound -- dereferencing that reloaded
   pointer is a real use-after-free. It "worked" for years by timing
   accident (single-invocation patch-constant phase, one lane reading
   freshly-freed memory before anything overwrote it); this session's
   own multi-invocation change exposed it as a hard crash.
   - Diagnosis method that actually worked: `gdb -batch -ex run -ex
     "x/10i $pc" -ex "info registers"` (backtraces are useless here --
     no debug symbols for JIT code -- but the faulting instruction's
     disassembly plus register dump shows the bad address directly,
     e.g. `ld1 {v7.s}[2], [x22]` with `x22=0x2`). Paired with
     `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRENORM=1` (pre-SIMDize IR, easiest to read the
     original shape) and `FEME_DUMP_IR=1` (post-SIMDize, shows the
     actual per-lane `extractelement`+`load` pattern that crashes).
   - Fix: capture the alloca's *value* (load at the barrier, guaranteed
     after every pre-barrier store) through the global instead of its
     address, then clone a fresh alloca into the patch-constant phase
     pre-populated with that value.

## Verification

- `ninja check-feme`: 3,491/3,552 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed (up
  from the pre-session 3,490/3,551 baseline), ccache + assertions
  confirmed on.
- Targeted CTS: `cross_invocation_per_vertex_*` 5/5 Pass (was 0/5).
  `cross_invocation_per_patch_*` unaffected, still 0/5 Pass (not

- Broader `tessellation` group (1,114 cases): swept ~800 of 1,114

- `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`: confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan

- `offload-test-suite` branch-drift: re-checked, unchanged -- local

# Session: L344 item (1) fixed -- hull per-invocation diagonal-write gather (L345 opened)

**Session-start check**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

## What's done

Fixed `cross_invocation_per_patch_{int,uint,float,vec3,vec4}` (5
cases, `L344` item 1). All 5 pass now. Previously 0/5.

Root cause: `HullWrapper.cpp` always stores a per-invocation output
using this invocation's own flat index, ignoring Frequency. For a
`patch`-qualified array written per-invocation
(`in_te_data0[gl_InvocationID] = value`), each invocation's own copy
only ever gets one real row written — the rest is garbage. The
patch-constant phase always reads invocation-slot 0, so it only ever
saw 1/3 of the real array, nondeterministically.

Fix, 3 parts, 2 commits:
1. `CanonicalizeStage.cpp` — classify such reads as `Input`/`PerPatch`
   instead of `PatchOutput` (commit `4fa335a51006`).
2. `StageLink.cpp`/`.h` + `PatchPipeline.cpp`/`.h` — new
   `copyLinkedPatchFrequencyElements` gathers the diagonal into one
   real array and replicates it to every dest slot; new
   `HullToPatchConstantDomain` fallback link keeps the domain stage's
   own `patch in` consumer working after (1) stopped producing a
   `PatchOutput` element for it (commit `48bb38760165`).
3. Docs: `Roadmap.md` (commit `ed668c2a3cfb`), `VulkanCTSReport.md`
   (commit `20574b2906e0`).

New unit test: `StageLinkTest.
GathersPatchFrequencyDiagonalAndReplicatesToEveryDest`.

Verification:
- `FeMeGraphicsTests`: all passing (+1 new test), 0 regressions.
- `ninja check-feme`: 3,492/3,552 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed —
  up by 1 Pass from the 3,491/3,552 baseline (the +1 is this session's
  new unit test, not a CTS case; `check-feme` doesn't run the real
  Vulkan CTS).
- Broader `dEQP-VK.tessellation.shader_input_output.*` sweep (26 of
  28 cases, excluding the `mat4x3` crash below): 25/26 Pass. The one
  failure is `L344` item (2), the already-tracked "only one
  group-sync barrier supported" limitation — unrelated, pre-existing,
  not touched this session.

New technique worth keeping: `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD=1` dumps LLVM IR
right before SIMDization. This is what cracked the case — it showed
the patch-constant phase's input load always uses a constant `0` for
the invocation operand, which is what pointed at "only slot 0 is ever
read" as the real bug shape.

## New bug found, NOT fixed, split out as `L345`

`cross_invocation_per_patch_mat4x3` crashes the whole `deqp-vk`
process: `Fatal glibc error: malloc.c:2371 (sysmalloc): assertion
failed` — heap corruption, not a graceful failure.

Checked it's not something I caused: `git stash`'d all this session's
changes, rebuilt, ran it again — same crash, byte-for-byte identical.
Pre-existing. `L339`'s own report had called this (and its
`cross_invocation_per_vertex_mat4x3` sibling) a "SIMDize hang" when
hit during an earlier sweep — my `gdb -batch -ex run -ex bt` says it's
actually a hard abort inside `buildFilteredStorage`/`runPatchPipeline`,
not a hang, so that earlier label was probably a test-runner timeout
on an already-aborted process, not a real infinite loop.

Best guess, unconfirmed: a matrix-typed (not scalar/vector),
array-of-matrices, `PerPatch`-frequency element's `RowCount`/
`ComponentCount` conflates the array dimension with the matrix's own
row dimension somewhere in `addElements`/`buildStageStorage`, causing
an out-of-bounds write that corrupts the heap allocator's own
metadata well before the later, unrelated allocation that actually
aborts.

## Next steps

1. **(dedicated session, new, real memory-safety bug)** `L345` —
   `cross_invocation_per_patch_mat4x3` heap corruption. Start with
   `MALLOC_CHECK_=3` or ASan to catch the actual out-of-bounds write

2. **(unknown, 300 cases)** The broader `tessellation` group sweep is

# Session: L347 fixed -- `tess_factor_barrier_bug` self-read poison; tessellation sweep closed out again

**Start here next session:** `L339` (TCS barrier-splitting, 14 cases,

## What's done, concretely

1. Confirmed `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` ==
   `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (mandatory check, every session).
2. Finished root-causing `misc_draw.tess_factor_barrier_bug` (picked up
   from a prior session's investigation, not this session's own find):
   a per-vertex `Output` global written pre-barrier, then *self-read
   and partially overwritten* post-barrier
   (`gl_out[gl_InvocationID].gl_Position.xy = (... + gl_out[gl_
   InvocationID].gl_Position.xy) / ...;`). `splitTessellationControlEntry`
   moves the pre-barrier store into a different function (the
   control-point phase) than the post-barrier self-read (the
   patch-constant phase) -- no dominating store left in the
   self-read's own function, so `PromoteMemToReg` correctly (by plain
   SSA rules) synthesized `undef`/`poison` instead of the real value.
3. Fixed it: new `StageOpKind::OutputLoad` stage op (the load-side
   counterpart of the existing `OutputStore`), plus a
   `ShadowValueMap::SeedFromOutputLoad` flag in `CanonicalizeStage.cpp`
   that seeds the self-read's shadow alloca at function entry with a
   real `feme.stage.output.load` call, before any rewriting runs.
   Proven safe unconditionally: every `Output`-direction element
   reaching this code path is guaranteed a real store later in the same
   function by construction, so an unseeded case just becomes an
   unused dead store, not a correctness gap.
4. Touched 6 other files to keep every exhaustive `switch (StageOpKind)`
   correct: `StageOps.h`/`.cpp` (the new op + builder),
   `PatchConstantWrapper.cpp` (the new lowering, reusing `L339`'s own
   `PerVertexOutputs` storage), `ValidateStage.cpp`, `SIMDize.cpp`,
   `WaveUniformity.cpp` (one new case each). `Linearize.cpp`/
   `ReferenceLowering.cpp` needed no change (confirmed via grep -- both
   already treat a plain stage-IO load generically).
5. Added a regression test
   (`CanonicalizeStageTest.SplitsHullEntryPatchConstantPhaseOutputSelfRead`)
   reproducing the exact shape in miniature. Verified it actually
   catches the bug: manually disabled the new seeding flag, confirmed
   the test fails with the real symptom (`insertelement <4 x float>
   %2, float undef, i64 3`), then re-enabled the fix and confirmed it
   passes again.
6. Verified: `dEQP-VK.tessellation.misc_draw.tess_factor_barrier_bug`

## One thing worth knowing before you touch `ShadowValueMap` again

The new `SeedFromOutputLoad` seeding only covers the *scalar*
(constant-`Row`/`Component`) shadow-alloca path in `getOrCreate`. The
`DynamicAllocas` fallback (genuinely dynamic indices) is NOT seeded --
documented in both `CanonicalizeStage.cpp`'s own comments and
`FeMeGraphicsDesign.md`'s new L347 subsection, but not yet hit by any
known CTS case. If a future session finds a dynamically-indexed
self-read-after-barrier-write case failing the same way, that's the
first place to look.

# Session: L340 follow-up -- switch_domain_origin_*_fast_lib fixed (L348), fill_overlap_* still open

## What's fixed

`dEQP-VK.tessellation.misc_draw.switch_domain_origin_*_fast_lib`: 4/4 Pass (was 0/4).
Run it yourself:

```
cd /home/dev/dev/VK-GL-CTS/external/vulkancts/data
export VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/home/dev/dev/llvm-project/build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json
deqp-vk --deqp-case="dEQP-VK.tessellation.misc_draw.switch_domain_origin_*_fast_lib"
```

## Root cause (for the next person who hits a similar bug)

1. `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library` fast-link path deep-copies each library
   part's state via `captureGraphicsPipelineLibraryState` (`GraphicsPipeline.cpp`).
2. That function stripped `VkPipelineTessellationStateCreateInfo::pNext`
   unconditionally (`Copy.pNext = nullptr;`) when deep-copying -- a correct
   policy for most chained structs, but wrong for
   `VkPipelineTessellationDomainOriginStateCreateInfo`, which is real,
   meaningful pipeline state.
3. Result: a library part built with `LOWER_LEFT` silently became
   `UPPER_LEFT` (the spec default) once fast-linked.

This is the exact same bug class `VkPipelineRenderingCreateInfo` already had
a fix for (`GraphicsPipelineLibraryState::RenderingCreateInfo`) -- I copied
that pattern: capture into a dedicated field, fold across link, re-chain at
reconstruction.

## Work done, in commit order

1. `GraphicsPipeline.{h,cpp}`: added `TessellationDomainOrigin` field +
   wired capture/fold/reconstruct. (commit `533eb7172282`)
2. `GraphicsPipelineTest.cpp`: added
   `LinksLibraryWithLowerLeftTessellationDomainOrigin`, confirmed via
   `git stash` A/B that it fails pre-fix, passes post-fix.
   (commit `7fa087360e05`)
3. `Roadmap.md` + `VulkanCTSReport.md`: new `L348` entry, struck through
   `L340` item 3. (commit `83d08daaab0e`)

`ninja check-feme`: 3,499/3,560 Passed, 0 Failed, 0 regressions.
Also re-ran the full 836-case `pipeline_library.graphics_library.*` group
before/after: identical 520/28/287 split both times -- this fix doesn't
touch anything else in that much bigger test surface.

## `fill_overlap_*` (10 cases): still open, deepened this session

Spent real time on this before pivoting to the fix above. Summary of what's
ruled out:

- **Not** a crack/overlap bug -- existing `TessellatorTest.cpp` unit tests
  already combinatorially rule this out.
- **Not** a `round()` SPIR-V lowering bug -- confirmed via
  `glslangValidator`+`spirv-dis` the shader uses unambiguous
  `GLSLstd450 Round`, correctly lowered by upstream MLIR (not FeMe code).
- **Likely, not confirmed**: FeMe's `tessellateQuad` always splits each
  interior grid cell along the same `A-C` diagonal. Vulkan spec says this
  choice is implementation-defined. Tried alternating by `(I+J)%2` parity
  (both phases) -- didn't fix it, barely moved the needle.
- Pixel-diff heatmap shows a multi-cell "staircase" along the domain
  diagonal, not a thin hairline -- this is bigger than one ambiguous
  triangle, so the diagonal-choice theory alone may not be the whole story.

**My best guess for next steps**: this needs someone to actually port (or at
least closely compare against) the CTS reference tessellator's own
interior-triangulation algorithm -- I found it's Microsoft's D3D reference
`CHWTessellator` (vendored into Mesa's `tessellator.cpp`), which uses a
"concentric ring spiral" approach structurally different from FeMe's simple
rectangular grid. I only partially read through it. This is a dedicated
session, not "a few hours."

     the requested `1`. Root cause: `parseSpecializationConstant`
     (`lib/API/VK/Device.cpp`) built its `VkSpecializationMapEntry` for
     `DataFormat::Bool` using `Entry.size = sizeof(bool)` (1 byte on this
     platform). The Vulkan spec requires `sizeof(VkBool32)` (4 bytes) for
     boolean spec constants. FeMe's own `buildSpecializationOverrides`
     (`Pipeline.cpp`) correctly refuses to read a value unless the entry
     is at least 4 bytes, so the override silently no-op'd. Fixed to use
     `VkBool32`. This is a genuine Vulkan-spec-conformance bug in
     offload-test-suite, not a FeMe bug -- any correctly-spec-checking ICD
     would hit the same silent failure.
   - `WaveActiveMax.test`'s `NegInfs` sub-case (all lanes `-inf`): FeMe
     correctly returns `-inf` (the mathematically consistent
     max-reduction of an all-identity-value input), not the `0` other
     tested drivers happen to return for this specific edge case -- the
     same category of divergence the test already XFAILs for
     `Lavapipe && host-arm64` (another software Vulkan implementation on
     the same architecture). Added `XFAIL: FeMe && host-arm64`.
   - `array_of_matrices.test`'s stale `XFAIL: DXC` (referencing
     `microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler#8080`): the currently-checked-out DXC
     now produces correct output; the test was Unexpectedly-Passed.
     Removed the stale annotation.
   Each fix is its own commit in `offload-test-suite`, verified with
   `git show --stat HEAD` after each (per the standing process note from
   a prior session about `git add -p` + pathspec-less `git commit`
   silently re-including unstaged changes -- did not hit that this time,

   `deqp-vk --deqp-case=dEQP-VK.tessellation.misc_draw.fill_overlap_quads_equal_spacing_draw --deqp-log-images=enable`,

3. **The diagnostic changed everything.** ErrorMask showed a small,
   symmetric staircase of ~12x12px error blobs along one diagonal only --
   not a wholesale shape mismatch. That meant the test is a plain
   golden-image fuzzy-compare (threshold 0.002) of a `gl_TessCoord`-phase-
   banded color, tolerant of *any* correct triangulation -- not a
   topology-exact check against the reference's own point ordering. The
   prior "needs a literal port" conclusion had compared algorithms against
   each other without first confirming what the test actually checks.
   - Root cause: FeMe's `tessellateQuad` always split every interior grid
     cell along the same `A-C` diagonal. The CTS shader's phase function has
     a discontinuity along *both* of the domain's corner-to-corner
     diagonals; a uniform-direction split interpolates smoothly across one
     diagonal but incorrectly crosses the other -- exactly the staircase
     seen in the ErrorMask.
   - Fix (`feme/lib/Graphics/Tessellator.cpp`): pick each cell's split
     diagonal from its own center's *normalized domain position*
     (`(u-0.5)*(v-0.5) >= 0` -> keep `A-C`, else switch to `B-D`), not raw
     grid index (asymmetric `N`x`M` grids need the real position, not an
     index-parity rule -- `L348` already tried `(I+J)%2` and it didn't
     help, consistent with this).
   - Added `TessellatorTest.QuadInteriorCellDiagonalMirrorsAcrossBothDomainDiagonals`
     with a deliberately asymmetric 9x7 grid to catch the
     position-vs-index distinction directly.

## State

  Device` at session start.

  (unchanged all session -- no code landed).

## What happened

1. Picked up handoff item 1: root-cause `fill_overlap_triangles_*`'s
   centroid-blob defect.
2. Confirmed (pixel sampling + a standalone dump tool calling
   `feme::graphics::tessellate` directly) the defect is a real blend-
   ratio mismatch, not a topology gap/overlap -- ring/triangle counts
   pass the Euler-formula check exactly.
3. Fetched Mesa's reference `CHWTessellator` and traced
   `StitchRegular`'s `DIAGONALS_MIRRORED` connectivity by hand. Found
   FeMe's `bridgeEdge` is asymmetric for the `Mo == Mi + 2` ring-to-ring
   case (fans almost the whole edge toward one corner); the reference
   mirrors it (half toward each corner).
4. Implemented `bridgeEdgeMirrored`/`bridgeRingsByEdgeMirrored`, wired
   it into every ring-to-ring bridge. Structurally correct (Euler check
   passes, 0 `check-feme` regressions).
5. Re-ran the CTS case. **No improvement**: still 4/6 failing, pixel
   count unchanged/slightly worse (956px vs. ~770px). Defect changed
   from a red/green blend-ratio mismatch to an exact green/blue channel
   swap at identical magnitude -- points to a floating-point boundary-
   tie at a ring-seam phase boundary, not a diagonal/topology bug.
6. Reverted the code (`git checkout --`, confirmed clean diff).
7. Wrote up the full negative result in `FeMeGraphicsDesign.md`'s
   Status subsection, `Roadmap.md` (new `L351` row), and a new `L351`
   section in `VulkanCTSReport.md`. Committed docs only (`2abaa2ab2156`).

## Why no code fix landed

The mirrored-topology hypothesis was the natural next step from last
session's handoff, and it was worth testing directly rather than
guessing -- but the A/B result is unambiguous: same failure count,
slightly worse pixel count, and a qualitatively different defect
signature. Shipping it would add real code complexity (a second
bridging algorithm, a new invariant to maintain) for zero measurable
benefit. Reverting and documenting the ruled-out path is the right
call here, not force-fitting a "fix" that doesn't fix anything.

# Session: L352 -- `fill_overlap_triangles_*` fixed (IEEE754 centroid tie), all 6 cases now Pass

**Fixed.** `fill_overlap_triangles_*` (6 cases) now 6/6 Pass. This
closes the entire `fill_overlap_*` cluster (10 cases across quad +
triangle domains, open since `L340`).

## What was wrong

1. Prior sessions (`L350`/`L351`) had been diagnosing the **wrong**
   failing tess-level case (case 0, `inner=9,outer={9,9,9}` -- which
   actually passes) instead of the real one (case 1,
   `inner=8,outer={13,15,18}`). Caught this by reading the raw `.qpa`
   log's own tess-level text directly instead of assuming image order.
2. Root cause, once on the right case: `Tessellator.cpp` builds the
   triangle domain's degenerate center point as `(1/3,1/3,1/3)` using
   `1.0f/3.0f`. In float32, `3.0f * (1.0f/3.0f)` rounds to **exactly**
   `1.0f`. The test's TES does
   `int(3.0*min(u,v,w) * numConcentricTriangles) % 3` to pick a color
   band, relying on that product staying strictly below `1.0`. FeMe's
   exact `1.0` overflows the bucket count by one at that one vertex,
   flipping its color.

## The fix

One new constant, `CentroidThird` (one float ULP below `1.0f/3.0f`),
used everywhere the triangle centroid is built. Moves the centroid's
screen position by ~1e-7 relative, invisible, but keeps the TES's math
in range. `feme/lib/Graphics/Tessellator.cpp` +
`feme/unittests/Graphics/TessellatorTest.cpp` (new regression test
`TriangleCenterPointThreeTimesMinIsStrictlyBelowOne`).

## How it was found

Built a standalone CPU-only re-implementation of the whole test
(tessellate + TES formula + barycentric rasterize), linked straight
against `libFeMeGraphics.a`, bypassing Vulkan entirely
(`/tmp/l351_dbg/render.cpp`, now cleaned up -- re-fetch/rewrite if
needed again). Matched FeMe's real GPU output to 2/65536 px, proving
the bug is 100% inside `Tessellator.cpp`. This technique is worth
reusing for any future tessellation/shading pixel-diff investigation --
faster and more conclusive than hand-tracing or Euler-formula checks.

## Verified

- `fill_overlap_triangles_*` (6 cases): 6/6 Pass (was 2/6).
- Full `dEQP-VK.tessellation.*` (1,114 cases): 646 Pass/30 Fail/438
  NotSupported -- 0 regressions, all 30 remaining failures are
  pre-existing/tracked (`L337`, `L341`, `L346`, `L344` item 2).
- `ninja check-feme`: 3,501 Passed/61 Unsupported/0 Failed (+1 test).
- `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` at session start: `FeMe CPU
  Vulkan Device`, confirmed.

Commits (2, both already pushed to this branch):
1. The `Tessellator.cpp` fix + unit test.
2. Docs: `FeMeGraphicsDesign.md`, `VulkanCTSReport.md` (`L352` entry),
   `Roadmap.md` (`L352` row + `L340` item 2 marked resolved).

## Next steps

1. **(~a dedicated session)** `L344` item 2 / `L335` -- N-barrier
   generalization, 1 case (`shader_input_output.barrier`). Carried
   over many sessions, fully scoped in `FeMeGraphicsDesign.md`'s
   Status subsection. Needs someone to actually spend the multi-file
   implementation session.
2. **(~a few hours, lowest priority, many sessions carried over)**
   `L265` -- ASTC alpha-decode tie-break, 12 cases. Next unattempted
   angle: compare decoded 4-texel neighborhoods pixel-by-pixel between
   `astc_5x5` and `astc_8x8` for a structural property correlating
   with tie direction.
3. **(~a dedicated session, new idea from this session)** Audit other
   even-inner-tess-factor CTS tests for the *same* centroid-tie bug
   class masked by a less color-sensitive shader (this bug existed in
   every even-`N0` triangle-domain patch, not just this one test family
   -- only became *visible* here because of this test's exact
   phase-bucket coloring). A quick way to start: grep the already-known
   36 `invariance.outer_edge_symmetry` failures and any other

4. **(~a few hours, overdue)** The broader-than-tessellation CTS

# Session: `query_pool.occlusion_query.*` fully fixed (L353/L354) -- a depth-quantization tie-break and a stale-synchronous-assumption race/crash

**Confirmed device at session start**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (had to explicitly set `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<build>/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json`; the system default is lavapipe).

## What's done

1. **L353 (depth-quantization tie-break)**: `D16_UNORM` depth attachments store `0.5` as `0.500007629` (32768/65535, `std::lround` half-away-from-zero at the exact `32767.5` tie). A redraw at the same conceptual depth then spuriously failed `GREATER_OR_EQUAL` comparing raw `0.5` against the already-quantized stored value. Fixed: added `quantizeDepthForFormat()`, quantize the incoming fragment depth before `compareOp` in `testDepthStencil`. 1 new test, A/B-verified (fails without fix).
2. **L354 (query-pool race/crash)**: `vkGetQueryPoolResults`'s own comment said this ICD "never needs to actually wait" for `VK_QUERY_RESULT_WAIT_BIT` -- stale since `L228(h)/(i)` made `vkQueueSubmit` genuinely async (per-queue worker thread). It sampled availability once and returned `VK_NOT_READY`, so CTS tore down render targets a worker thread was still using -- segfault/abort, non-deterministic, made worse by a stale `shadercache.bin` adding timing noise. Fixed: gave `QueryPool` a mutex/condvar (mirroring `Fence`), added a real blocking `waitAvailable()`, called it from `vkGetQueryPoolResults`. 4 new tests including a real cross-thread blocking case.
3. **Verified**: full `dEQP-VK.query_pool.occlusion_query.*` (441 cases, 385 applicable) → **385/385 Pass, 0 Fail, 0 crashes**, 5x reruns + post-rebuild reconfirm. `ninja check-feme`: **3506 Passed/61 Unsupported/0 Failed** (+5 new tests), 0 regressions.
4. **4 commits landed**: `c8d7125` (L353 fix), `22678e1` (L354 fix), `47b7278` (docs: Roadmap.md L353/L354, VulkanCTSReport.md sections, FeMeVulkanDesign.md note on QueryPool joining the mutex/condvar-guarded object list), this one (agent_thoughts.md).
5. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: no change needed for either fix (internal correctness only).

## Key technique learned this session (reusable)

**Debug info in a Release build without reconfiguring**: extract the exact `ninja -t commands <target>` compile/link/archive lines for just the files you need, `sed -i 's/-O3/-O0 -g/'`, run those lines manually, manually re-run the capture `ar`/link lines too -- **do not** call `ninja` again afterward, it'll detect the `.o` as stale and silently reclobber with original flags. Got a full `gdb bt full` with source lines this way in a project that otherwise has no `-g`.

**Stale on-disk cache as crash-symptom noise**: if a crash's *location* is inconsistent across runs with zero code changes, check for a stale shader/pipeline cache from a different build before concluding "unreproducible race" -- in this case the cache noise was layered on top of a genuinely real race, not a substitute explanation for it.

**Confirmed device at session start**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (`VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<build>/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json` set explicitly; system default is lavapipe).

Second commit got to 6 failed (4 of 10 fixed total).
4. **New tests**: `ResourceInfoTest.ArtifactAbiVersionIsSeven` (renamed), `ResourceInfoTest.ComputeSideEffectFlagsReadsEarlyFragmentTestsAttribute`, `ExecutorTest.ExplicitEarlyFragmentTestsStillWritesDepthWhenShaderDiscards`.
5. **Verified**: `check-feme` 3511 Passed/61 Unsupported/0 Failed (3572 total, +2 new tests vs. 3509 baseline), 0 regressions, both before and after the second (`FSDepthOut`/etc.) commit. `dEQP-VK.fragment_operations.early_fragment.*`: 18/54 Pass (was 10 Failed, now 6 Failed). `dEQP-VK.fragment_operations.*` broader group (151 cases): 112 Pass/6 Fail (same 6)/30 NotSupported/3 Warnings, 0 regressions elsewhere.
6. **4 commits landed this part of the session**: core fix + tests, the `FSDepthOut`/`FSStencilRefOut`/`FSSampleMaskOut` follow-up fix, docs (`Roadmap.md` L356 row + `VulkanCTSReport.md` L356 section), this one.
7. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: checked, no change needed -- `EarlyFragmentTests` is core SPIR-V, not an extension; confirmed via grep that neither file mentions it.

## New finding, not investigated: the remaining 6 `samplemask_*` cases

`samplemask_{early,no_early}_fragment_tests_depth_samples_{2,4,8}` still fail *after* this fix, and **both** variants fail (including `no_early`, which never declares `early_fragment_tests` -- so this is provably not about the execution mode at all). Depth-resolve values come back fractional (`0.0565194`, `0.328374`, `9.15541e-05`) instead of the expected clear value `0.5f`, pointing at an MSAA depth-resolve bug. These pipelines use `sampleShadingEnable = true` + `pSampleMask = 0x1` (API-level mask restricting coverage to sample 0) + a multisample depth-stencil attachment with a separate resolve target -- a distinctly more complex per-sample-shading path than the 4 cases this session fixed. Not chased further; likely its own dedicated session (per-sample depth storage/resolve correctness, possibly interacting with `Quad.SampleMask`/per-sample coverage plumbing in `Executor.cpp`).

## Technique reinforced this session

**Don't trust your own "the spec disallows this" comment without checking** -- the first-pass fix's comment asserted `FSDepthOut`/`FSStencilRefOut`/`FSSampleMaskOut` can't coexist with `early_fragment_tests` at all, written confidently but never verified. Re-running the actual CTS group after the first commit (discard_early_fragment_tests_depth/stencil still failed) was what caught it; a `web_search` then confirmed the real rule (shader-computed values are simply ignored, not disallowed). Lesson: always re-verify the *specific* failing cases after a partial fix, even when the committed change already shows 0 regressions elsewhere -- "0 regressions" is not the same as "fully fixed," and a CTS group re-run is cheap insurance against a plausible-sounding but wrong spec assumption baked into a comment.

without this shows `llvmpipe`, not FeMe).

## What now works

The 6 cases this session was handed:
`dEQP-VK.fragment_operations.early_fragment.samplemask_{early,no_early}_
fragment_tests_depth_samples_{2,4,8}` all **Pass**. Run it yourself:

```

VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/home/dev/dev/llvm-project/build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json \
  ./deqp-vk -n "dEQP-VK.fragment_operations.early_fragment.samplemask_*_fragment_tests_depth_samples_*"
```

Full `depth_stencil_resolve` CTS group (22,611 cases, minus 372 unrelated
`compatibility_*` cases -- see below): **738 Pass / 0 Fail / 21,501
NotSupported**, zero `DeviceLost`. `check-feme`: 3,516/3,577 Passed, 0 Failed
(+5 new tests).

## What was built, in commit order

1. `9dab3ebaf343` -- `RenderPass.{h,cpp}`: parse/validate
   `VkSubpassDescriptionDepthStencilResolve`.
2. `f5783bc08670` -- `CommandBuffer.cpp`/`PreparedDraw.h`/`Executor.cpp`:
   execution-side resolve plumbing.
3. `98e7a5f8337d` -- `EntryPoints.cpp`: advertise `SAMPLE_ZERO_BIT` support.
4. `f97820f93c65` -- new unit tests (`ExecutorTest.cpp`, `RenderPassTest.cpp`).
5. `7c3f576ee06c` -- Roadmap/ExtensionInventory/FeatureInventory docs.
6. `9fa16ce71e64` -- **bug fix 1**: relaxed over-strict resolve-format
   validation (CTS requests both resolve modes even when the format only
   has one aspect -- that's spec-legal, a silent no-op, not an error).
7. `4e8707ba59c2` -- **bug fix 2**: split `PipelineRenderTargets::
   DepthStencil` into independent `DepthFormat`/`StencilFormat` fields
   (see below), + 2 new regression tests.
8. `8ec2065a7dc6` -- `VulkanCTSReport.md` entry.

## The two bugs found via CTS, in plain terms

**Bug 1** (format validation): FeMe required a resolve attachment's format
to support *both* depth and stencil whenever *either* resolve mode was
requested. Spec says: if the requested mode's aspect isn't in the format,
just skip that aspect's resolve silently. Fixed to only require the format
to support *some* recognized aspect.

**Bug 2** (the interesting one): `PipelineRenderTargets` had one field,
`DepthStencil`, standing in for "is there a depth/stencil attachment."
Both dynamic rendering (`depthAttachmentFormat`/`stencilAttachmentFormat`
are independently settable to `UNDEFINED`) and classic render passes (a
subpass's single attachment reference can have a format supporting only
one aspect, e.g. `S8_UINT`) can produce "stencil is declared, depth is
not" -- but the conflated field couldn't represent that, so it wrongly
concluded "depth is declared too" whenever stencil was. The CTS test for
this always sets `depthTestEnable = VK_TRUE` regardless of which aspect
it's testing (legal -- "no depth attachment" just makes the test a no-op),
which exposed the bug as a draw-time hard error. That hard error then
**permanently kills the whole device** (`Sync.cpp`'s `makeSubmissionTask`
-> `Device::markLost()`), which is why one bad test case was aborting the
entire CTS run instead of just failing. Fixed by splitting into
`DepthFormat`/`StencilFormat`, each independently gated by
`isSupportedDepthAttachmentFormat`/`isSupportedStencilAttachmentFormat`.

**Takeaway for future `DeviceLost` triage**: check the *first* failing
case in a caselist, not later ones -- the device can't recover once lost.
`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` prints the real internal error on
stderr (`Diagnostics.cpp`'s `logCreationFailure`, silent by default) and
was essential for both bugs above.

## New untriaged finding (not fixed this session, out of scope for K6)

The `compatibility_*` subset of `depth_stencil_resolve` (372 cases) tests
resolving against an image created with an alternate-but-bit-compatible
format (e.g. `X8_D24_UNORM_PACK32` swapped in for `D24_UNORM_S8_UINT`).
FeMe doesn't support this yet (`"depth attachment format is not yet
supported (mechanical, added on demand)"`), and -- worse -- hitting this
during `vkQueueSubmit` currently surfaces as `DeviceLost` rather than a
clean error, which aborts the whole run if these cases aren't excluded.
Not a regression from this session's change; just newly visible because
this was the first time anyone ran this specific CTS group broadly.

  `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set picked up Mesa `llvmpipe` instead! Re-ran with

## L357 (recap, since I didn't do the original root-causing this session)

Two call sites in `CommandBuffer.cpp` bound a depth/stencil resolve
`ResolveView` based only on resolve *mode* being non-NONE, never checking
whether the resolve attachment's own *format* actually supports that
aspect. `compatibility_*_testing_stencil` CTS cases substitute a
stencil-only `S8_UINT` resolve target while still requesting a depth
resolve -- reached `Executor.cpp`'s depth path with no case for it, hard
error, `DeviceLost` for the whole device (not just the one test). Fixed by
gating on `isSupportedDepthAttachmentFormat`/
`isSupportedStencilAttachmentFormat` of the *resolve* attachment, same as
already done for the primary attachment.

Verified via A/B `git stash` that the new `DrawTest.cpp` regression test
(`DepthStencilResolveSkipsAspectResolveAttachmentDoesNotHave`) genuinely
catches it (`VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` pre-fix, passes post-fix including a
correct stencil-resolve readback). Full `depth_stencil_resolve` group
(22,611 cases): 750 Pass/4 Fail (known out-of-scope CTS registration gap,
not FeMe's bug)/21,857 NotSupported, **0 DeviceLost**. `check-feme`:
3517/3578, 0 regressions.

Committed as 3 small commits: the fix, the test, the docs.

## L358: Event::Signaled data race

Found by doing exactly what handoff item 3 asked: grep for "synchronous"
comments near objects touched by both the host thread and a
`QueueExecutor` worker thread. `Sync.h`'s `class Event` has:

```cpp
bool Signaled; // <-- no mutex, no atomic, nothing
```

...set/reset from the host (`vkSetEvent`/`vkResetEvent`/`vkGetEventStatus`
in `Sync.cpp`) *and* from a worker thread executing a submitted command
buffer's `vkCmdSetEvent`/`vkCmdResetEvent`/`vkCmdWaitEvents`
(`CommandBuffer.cpp`'s `Cmd.Events[0]->set()`/`reset()` and
`runWaitEvents`). Textbook data race -- UB per the C++ memory model, not
just a "maybe stale read" timing bug.

The tell: `class Semaphore` sits *immediately below* `Event` in the same
file and already does this correctly with `std::mutex` +
`std::condition_variable`. Whoever wrote `Semaphore` clearly knew the
cross-thread shape needed protection; `Event` just never got the same
treatment. Same shape as the `L354` `QueryPool` bug, different object.

**Why this one is sneaky**: it never showed up as a CTS failure. Ran the
full `dEQP-VK.synchronization.*event*` group (1,642 cases) and
`dEQP-VK.api.*event*` (31 cases) after the fix -- both 100% pass, same as
presumably before (no prior broad run exists to diff against, but no
`Fail` at all in either group now). A plain-bool race on x86-64 "happens
to work" often enough that it can hide for a very long time; this was
found by code audit, not by chasing a failure. That's exactly the point
of handoff item 3 -- worth keeping on the backlog, there could be more.

Fix: `std::atomic<bool>` with acquire/release ordering (no full mutex
needed -- `runWaitEvents` only does a single poll, never blocks/spins, so
there's no condition-variable-style wait to protect). `Sync.h` already
had `<atomic>` included, so this was a genuinely tiny diff.

New test: `EventTest.SetFromAnotherThreadIsObservedByIsSignaled` in
`SyncTest.cpp`, same shape as `QueryPoolTest`'s `L354` precedent -- spawn
a `std::thread` that sleeps then sets the event, poll `isSignaled()` from
the main thread with a 5s timeout. Worth noting honestly: this test
*cannot* prove the race's absence on its own (UB doesn't reliably
reproduce without a race detector) -- its real value is pinning the
correct atomic implementation in place so nobody "simplifies" it back to
a bare `bool` later. Did not confirm whether ThreadSanitizer is wired up
anywhere in this build; that would be the actual tool to *prove* this
class of fix, not just a polling test. Worth checking in a future
session if this becomes a recurring pattern.

`check-feme` after the fix: 3518/3579, +1 test, 0 regressions.

Committed as 2 commits (fix, then test) + 1 doc commit for
`VulkanCTSReport.md`. Did not touch `Roadmap.md` for this one -- it's not
tied to any feature/milestone row, just a cross-cutting correctness
hardening fix, so a roadmap addendum didn't make sense the way it did for
`L357`/K6.

   audit is still only half-done: only `Event` has been checked beyond
   the already-known-fine `Fence`/`Semaphore`/`QueryPool`. Still
