# Session: `L359` triangle-strip-adjacency fix verified/committed + upstream MLIR nested-spec-constant-composite bug found and fixed

## tl;dr

- Picked up a verified-but-uncommitted `L359` fix (`TriangleStripWithAdjacency`
  windowing) from a compacted prior segment. Committed the fix, its test
  update, and docs in 3 small commits.
- Triaged handoff item 1 (`memory_model.*` races, ~24 cases mentioned, actual
  count 73 of 18,530). Root-caused 70 of them down to an **upstream MLIR
  bug**, not FeMe: `spirv::Deserializer::processSpecConstantComposite`
  never checked whether a composite spec constant's constituent was
  *itself* another composite spec constant. Fixed it, in its own
  `mlir/`-only commit per the "isolated outside-FeMe fix" rule.
- That fix did **not** flip the CTS cluster (confirmed via before/after
  CTS re-run, identical 73 Fail both times) -- found a second, deeper
  bug at the same error site (`OpSpecConstantOp` result as a composite
  constituent) that's architecturally harder to fix. Documented, not
  fixed, flagged for next session.
- `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` check: done with explicit
  `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set, confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`.

## L359 (recap -- fix was already written before this session started)

Two bugs in `TriangleStripWithAdjacency`'s `getStripPrimitiveCount`/
`splitStripPrimitiveAdjacency` (`Pipeline.cpp`): odd `IndexCount` was
rejected outright (should floor), and the 6-vertex-per-primitive window
was assumed to be a simple sliding window when the real rule (per
`GL_EXT_geometry_shader`'s Table 10.X1) special-cases first/middle/last
primitives by odd/even index. This session just verified (full rebuild,
13/13 `triangle_strip_adjacency` cases now pass, `dEQP-VK.geometry.*`
190/200 Pass with the 1 remaining Fail confirmed pre-existing/unrelated,
`check-feme` 3518/3579 0 Fail) and committed what a prior segment had
already worked out and left uncommitted.

## New this session: upstream MLIR nested-spec-constant-composite bug

Handoff item 1 said "triage `memory_model.*` races (~24 cases)". Actual
count: 73 Fail out of 18,530 (most of the suite is `NotSupported` since
`vulkanMemoryModel` isn't advertised). Split into two very different
failure modes:

**Cluster A (70 cases, `fence_fence.atomicwrite` variants)**: pipeline
creation fails with `OpSpecConstantComposite constituent must be a
previously defined constant or specialization constant, but found <id>
N`. Traced this error string to `mlir/lib/Target/SPIRV/Deserialization/
Deserializer.cpp` -- **not FeMe code at all**, genuinely upstream MLIR.
`processSpecConstantComposite`'s constituent-resolution loop only
checked `getSpecConstant` (scalar) and `getConstant` (plain), never
`getSpecConstantComposite`. But `spirv::SpecConstantCompositeOp`'s own
doc comment says constituents can be "another spec constant (scalar or
composite)" -- the composite case was just never implemented. Classic
"doc comment describes the intent, code doesn't match it" bug.

Built an isolated reproducer first (always do this before touching
upstream code): a `.mlir` round-trip test with a spec-constant vector
nested inside a spec-constant array and a spec-constant struct.
Confirmed it fails without a fix, bisected to prove the fix makes it
pass, ran the full `Target/SPIRV` + `Dialect/SPIRV/IR` suites (122/122,
0 regressions) plus `check-feme` (3518/3579, 0 regressions) before
committing. One-line functional fix, big comment explaining why.

**Then the surprising part**: rebuilt the ICD with the fix, re-ran the
exact same CTS cluster -- **identical 73 Fail, byte-for-byte same test
list**. The fix was real (proven by the isolated test) but didn't touch
this CTS cluster at all. Used the same temporary-`fprintf`-behind-
`getenv` debug technique from `L359` to find out why: the actual
constituent at the failing `<id>` is an `OpSpecConstantOp` *result*
(an arithmetic expression over spec constants, like a workgroup-size-
derived offset), not a composite. SPIR-V's spec explicitly allows this
("Constituents must be ... a specialization constant or
constant-creation instruction", and `OpSpecConstantOp` counts), but
MLIR's `spirv.SpecConstantComposite` op has no way to represent it --
its constituents are a plain `ArrayAttr`, no SSA operands, while
`spirv.SpecConstantOperation` only exists as an inline op materialized
inside a function body with no module-scope symbol to reference. Fixing
this needs an actual op/dialect redesign, not a lookup-table addition --
correctly scoped as "found, documented, not fixed this session."

**3 more cases** (`message_passing.permuted_index.*`) hit a totally
different error (`failed to legalize operation 'spirv.AtomicStore'...
explicitly marked illegal` for `Uniform`-storage-class atomics) --
confirmed distinct from the composite-constituent bug, not investigated
further.

## Process notes

- The "fix outside FeMe in its own isolated commit" rule worked exactly
  as intended here: the MLIR deserializer commit touches only
  `mlir/lib/...`/`mlir/test/...`, has its own test, and stands on its
  own merits regardless of whether it ever lands a FeMe CTS win. Good
  example of "fix real bugs you find along the way even if they don't
  solve your original problem."
- Don't assume a fix for bug #1 at an error site is the *whole* bug just
  because the symptom (error message/line number) is identical --
  always re-run the actual failing cases after a fix, not just the new
  unit test, before declaring a CTS cluster resolved. (Same lesson as
  the `L359` self-correction a few sessions back, now generalized: a
  fix that's *locally* correct and *tested* can still be the wrong fix

# Session: ThreadSanitizer finds a real Fence/Semaphore/QueryPool destroy race (L361), broader CTS sweep 12/39 groups clean

**Device check:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` confirmed (explicit `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set first -- the env var gotcha from 2 sessions ago is now muscle memory).

**Win of the session:** ThreadSanitizer found and I fixed a real, reproducible data race nobody caught in ~15 prior sessions of manual thread-safety auditing. `FeMeVulkanTests` now passes 792/792 clean under TSan (was: 2 race warnings, every run).

## What happened, in order

1. Picked up where the prior session left off: `build-tsan/` (a separate `-DLLVM_USE_SANITIZER=Thread` build dir) was already built. Ran `FeMeVulkanTests` under it.
2. **Found it:** `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race` x2, both the same shape -- `vkDestroyFence`'s `~Fence()` (`pthread_cond_destroy`, main thread) racing against the `QueueExecutor` worker thread's `Fence::signal()` (`pthread_cond_broadcast`, `Sync.h:154`).
3. Root cause: `signal()` set the signaled flag *inside* a `lock_guard`, then called `CV.notify_all()` *after* that guard released the lock. A waiter in `Fence::wait` can reacquire the mutex, see the flag true, and return -- before the signaling thread ever gets to its own `notify_all()` call. If the host thread then destroys the `Fence` (totally legal Vulkan: "it's signaled, I'm done with it"), the destructor tears down the condition variable while the worker thread is still mid-call on it. Classic "notify outside the lock" footgun, except here the lock-holder's own object can be destroyed by someone else the instant the lock releases.
4. Grepped `Sync.h`/`QueryPool.h` for every `notify_all`/`notify_one` call site. Found 2 more with the exact same shape: `Semaphore::signalBinary`, `Semaphore::signalTimeline` -- plus `QueryPool::markAvailable`, same bug in a completely different file. All four had a `wait`/`wait_for` counterpart and a caller-destroyable lifetime.
5. Fixed all four: moved `notify_all()` inside the same `lock_guard` scope that sets the state. Checked `QueueExecutor`'s own `notify_all` calls too -- those are safe, because its destructor `Worker.join()`s the only thread that could still touch the CV, and `join()` can't return until `run()` itself returns.
6. Rebuilt both `build/` (main) and `build-tsan/`. Both: 792/792 pass. Two consecutive TSan reruns after the fix: **0 warnings**, versus 2/2 reproductions before it.
7. Ran full `check-feme` (forces all test deps to rebuild first): 3519 Passed / 61 Unsupported / 0 Failed.
8. Committed the fix + `VulkanCTSReport.md`/`Roadmap.md` updates as `L361` (one commit, `8c8bddeedaf8`).

Then picked up handoff item 6 (the long-overdue broader-than-tessellation CTS sweep):

9. A background script (`/tmp/cts_sweep/run_sweep.sh`, carried over from before compaction) had already ground through several groups while TSan work was happening in the foreground. Let it keep running the rest of the session.
10. Parsed results for 12 of ~39 top-level groups as they finished: `synchronization`, `synchronization2`, `compute`, `ssbo`, `ubo`, `rasterization`, `sparse_resources`, `mesh_shader`, `ray_query`, `ray_tracing_pipeline`, `subgroups`, `wsi`. **10 fully clean** (0 Fail).
11. **2 groups had Fails, both triaged to ground, neither a new bug:**
    - `rasterization.line_continuity.*` (2 Fail) -- reproduced standalone, exact match for the already-tracked `L335` region-splitting-doesn't-support-nested-barriers limitation. Not new.
    - `mesh_shader.ext.misc.many_mesh_work_groups_*` (in-sweep `VK_TIMEOUT` + truncated log, looked like a crash) -- re-ran isolated, **3/3 Pass clean**. The in-sweep failure's timestamp lines up exactly with this same session's own concurrent `ninja -C build-tsan` full rebuild + TSan test run, both CPU-heavy. This is almost certainly the exact oversubscription scenario `Sync.h`'s own safety-net comment already describes. Didn't chase further given the clean isolated repro.
12. Documented both sweep batches in `VulkanCTSReport.md`, 2 separate commits as results came in (`41061b3a2084`, `022b00141cf6`).

## Visible state right now

- `build/` and `build-tsan/` both exist, both fully built, both green.
- `/tmp/cts_sweep/run_sweep.sh` **is still running in the background** (shellId lineage: started under 21/29 two sessions ago, still the same underlying process). Currently on `draw`. If you resume this session or start a new one quickly, check `/tmp/cts_sweep/progress.log` before relaunching anything -- it might already be further along.

# Session: fixed mat2 heap corruption (L363), root-caused (not fixed) 2 more transform_feedback crashes

**Device check:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` confirmed (`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set explicitly first).

**Win of the session:** Fixed `dEQP-VK.transform_feedback.fuzz.2_level_array.mat2.geometry`'s heap corruption (`double free or corruption`). Real Pass now, verified by valgrind + a new unit test + a full `check-feme` clean run (3520/3581 Passed, 0 Failed).

## What happened, in order

1. Resumed mid-investigation from before context compaction: a second `transform_feedback` crash (`nested_structs_instance_arrays.31`) was already being traced, and an uncommitted `isShapeCompatible` fix for the *first* crash (mat2) existed but wasn't committed yet.
2. Added one more debug print (`[resolve-offset-array-of-struct]`) to finish tracing `nested_structs_instance_arrays.31`'s Row math. Rebuilt, re-ran: **every Row value landed in-bounds** against the widened storage (`RowCount=6`) -- the storage-widening attempt from before compaction was NOT sufficient on its own.
3. Re-ran under valgrind anyway to see the new crash signature: now a **24-byte overrun past the widened 112-byte block** (previously an exact-boundary overrun against the unwidened 56-byte block). This means there's a **second, compounding under-sizing bug**, not yet identified -- the Row math itself is correct now, but something else still over-writes.
4. Given this attempted fix (1) doesn't fully fix the target crash and (2) still regresses `all_instance_array.12` (confirmed: Fail, exact match for a previously-documented regression), reverted it entirely: `git checkout -- feme/lib/Transforms/Graphics/CanonicalizeStage.cpp feme/lib/Graphics/StageStorage.cpp`.
5. **Mistake caught immediately:** that `git checkout` also wiped the mat2 fix's real source change (`isShapeCompatible`), since both were uncommitted in the same file. Only the unit test (a separate file) survived. Re-derived and re-added the fix from the test's own doc comment + expected behavior.
6. First re-attempt still failed the new unit test (`SeenRows = {0,1,4,5,8,9,12,13}` instead of `{0..7}` -- an off-by-factor-2 pattern). Traced through `isShapeCompatible`'s recursion by hand: the missing case was the *reverse* pairing from what the original comment described -- `Declared` being a real vector (`<2 x float>`, since a `mat2`'s own declared member type is never itself marker-substituted) matched against `Actual` being an *unwrapped-marker array* (`[2 x float]`), not the other way around. Added that missing symmetric case. Unit test passed clean afterward (133/133 in `FeMeTransformsGraphicsTests`).
7. Rebuilt `feme_vulkan`, confirmed target case: **Pass**. Confirmed `all_instance_array.12`'s *pre-existing* failure (not a crash, just a data mismatch) is **unchanged** by this fix -- did a temporary full-baseline rebuild (swap in the pre-fix source via `git show <parent>:...`, no actual `git stash` since the fix was already committed by then) to prove it, not just assumption.
8. Ran `ninja -C build check-feme`: 3520 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- clean.
9. Committed the mat2 fix + its test (`57a50dfe89ca`).
10. Tried to re-run the broader `transform_feedback` CTS group to confirm no regressions. First attempt used the wrong flag (`--deqp-case-filter` doesn't exist; it's `--deqp-case` with glob support). Second attempt crashed partway through on a **different, previously-unknown** case: `basic_arrays.1` (`double free or corruption`). Confirmed via the same baseline-swap technique that this crash is **pre-existing**, not caused by this session's fix.
11. Documented everything (`L363` roadmap row, `VulkanCTSReport.md` section) and committed docs separately (`438af8d3a80c`).

## Visible state right now

- `feme/lib/Transforms/Graphics/CanonicalizeStage.cpp`: only the `L363` fix remains (clean, committed). No debug instrumentation left in the tree anywhere -- double-checked via `git diff --stat` after the accidental-revert scare.
- 3 commits this session: `57a50dfe89ca` (L363 fix + test), `438af8d3a80c` (docs). This entry will be commit 3.
- Two confirmed-pre-existing, still-open crashes in `transform_feedback.fuzz.random_geometry`: `nested_structs_instance_arrays.31` (root-caused down to "a second compounding under-sizing bug past the now-correct Row math," not yet found) and `basic_arrays.1` (not investigated at all beyond confirming it's pre-existing). Neither blocks anything else; both are isolated to this one fuzz subgroup.

## Lesson learned, worth remembering

`git checkout -- <file>` to revert an *unwanted* exploratory change will also silently wipe any *wanted*, still-uncommitted change in the same file. When an investigation has both a validated fix and ongoing exploratory debug prints mixed together uncommitted in the same file, **commit the validated fix first**, before starting further exploratory edits on top of it -- don't rely on `git diff` review alone to separate them before a revert.

# Session: fixed basic_arrays.1 heap corruption (L364), confirmed nested_structs_instance_arrays has a second crash variant

**Device check:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` confirmed (`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set explicitly first).

**Win of the session:** Fixed `dEQP-VK.transform_feedback.fuzz.random_geometry.basic_arrays.1`'s heap corruption (`double free or corruption`). The whole `basic_arrays.*` group (50 cases) now runs to completion with no crash -- previously aborted the whole process. Verified by valgrind + a new unit test + a full `check-feme` clean run (3521/3582 Passed, 0 Failed).

## What happened, in order

1. Resumed mid-investigation from before context compaction: debug `fprintf`s were already in place in `StageStorage.cpp`/`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`, and a manual trace had produced a hypothesis (that the prior session's `L363` fix caused this crash) that directly contradicted the prior session's own claim (that `basic_arrays.1` is pre-existing, unrelated to `L363`).
2. Reconciled the contradiction by re-deriving the trace from the actual debug output (`/tmp/basic_arrays1_debug.log`, already captured) instead of guessing further: the observed `Row` values (`2,3,4,5` for byte offsets `64,88,112,136`) were actually **self-consistent** with `isShapeCompatible`'s matching behavior -- `L363` was not the cause. The real bug was one level up: `resolveRowComponent` was dividing the *wrong* byte offset.
3. Used `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRECANON=1` (an existing, previously-undiscovered env var) to dump the real pre-canonicalization LLVM IR for this exact case. Found the smoking gun directly: `@spirv_var_34 = external addrspace(8) global <{ [64 x i8], [4 x [2 x <3 x float>]] }>` -- a **lone** (non-array) struct with a 64-byte leading pad ahead of the real array member.
4. Traced `getEffectiveStageIOValueType`'s own doc comment, which explicitly names an "(or lone-instance)" case -- but the actual remap code (`resolveStageIOAccess`) only ever subtracted the pad for the *array-of-block-instances* shape (`isa<ArrayType>(GV->getValueType())` guard). The lone-struct case fell through unhandled, leaving every `ByteOffset` 64 bytes too large.
5. Confirmed the math: `resolveRowComponent`'s self-discovering stride mechanism "coincidentally" divided the inflated offset cleanly (64/32=2 is a valid-looking row index, just wrong), which is why this didn't look like an obviously-malformed input -- it silently landed 2 rows deeper than it should have for every store, overflowing `StageStorage` on the last one.
6. Fixed it: added the missing lone-struct branch, subtracting the pad's `Gap` once (no per-instance stride division, since there's only one instance -- unlike the existing array-of-instances `remapByteOffsetPastLeadingPad` helper).
7. Rebuilt, re-ran with debug prints still active: `Row` values are now `0,1,2,3` at byte offsets `0,24,48,72` (pad-adjusted) -- exactly right. **No crash.** The case now fails with an ordinary content mismatch instead (`Mismatch at offset 64 expected 72 received 0`) -- ruled out as a crash-adjacent artifact, confirmed to be a separate, not-yet-investigated bug.
8. Added a regression unit test (`RewritesLoneLeadingPadBeforeTightArrayOfVectorsMember`), mirroring the existing `RewritesArrayOfBlockInstancesWithLeadingPadBeforeTightMatrixMember` test's style but for the lone-struct shape. Removed all debug `fprintf`s from both files (confirmed `StageStorage.cpp` diff is empty afterward -- no artifact instrumentation left behind).
9. Ran `FeMeTransformsGraphicsTests`: 134/134 pass. Ran `ninja check-feme`: 3521/3582 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- clean (one more test than the prior session's 3520/3581 baseline, from this session's own new test).
10. Regression-checked by hand: `all_instance_array.12` (pre-existing, unrelated `Mismatch at offset 68` -- unchanged), `2_level_array.mat2.geometry` (still Pass), `basic_arrays.0` (still Pass).
11. Ran the full `basic_arrays.*` group (50 cases): completes clean, 6 Pass / 43 NotSupported / 1 Fail (`.1` itself, the now-isolated content-mismatch).
12. Attempted the broader `random_geometry.*` sweep: progressed 713 cases (106 Pass / 28 Fail / 578 NotSupported) before hitting a **different** crash, `nested_structs_instance_arrays.2`'s own `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected` -- a new symptom, but almost certainly the same architectural root cause as the already-tracked `nested_structs_instance_arrays.31` (`L363`'s own open item: array-of-block-instances shape, not the lone-instance shape this session fixed).
13. Committed the fix + unit test (`555d9376a0fd`), then docs (`cb93fe0eaae9`).

## Visible state right now

- `feme/lib/Transforms/Graphics/CanonicalizeStage.cpp`: only the `L364` fix remains, clean, committed. No debug instrumentation left anywhere -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` on `StageStorage.cpp` showing zero changes after cleanup.
- 2 commits this session: `555d9376a0fd` (L364 fix + test), `cb93fe0eaae9` (docs). This entry will be commit 3.
- `nested_structs_instance_arrays.31`/`.2` (both architecturally the array-of-block-instances shape, not the lone-instance one fixed this session) remain open, confirmed to be **at least two distinct crash symptoms** (`double free or corruption` vs. `malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected`) within the same subgroup -- still needs the dedicated session `L363`'s own handoff already called for.

## Lesson learned, worth remembering

`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRECANON=1` (an existing env var in `GraphicsPipeline.cpp`, previously undiscovered by several prior sessions' worth of debugging this exact crash cluster) dumps the real pre-canonicalization LLVM IR straight from a live `deqp-vk` run -- far faster and more reliable than reasoning from `fprintf`-based Row/Component traces alone when a type-shape mismatch is suspected. Should be the *first* tool reached for next time, not a late-session discovery: it immediately revealed the exact leading-pad struct shape that several rounds of manual arithmetic had failed to converge on.

# Session: fixed all_unordered_and_instance_array.2's trailing non-offset nested struct tightening (L370)

**Confirmed device:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (via `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=.../feme_icd.json` -- plain `vulkaninfo --summary` still shows `llvmpipe`).

## What's done

1. Fixed `all_unordered_and_instance_array.2` (top-priority carried-over item, left open by `L369`).
2. Reused `L369`'s signature-blob decoder technique (new this session: rewrote it as a standalone Python script, `/tmp/parse_sig.py`, from `feme::serializeSignature`'s exact binary layout) plus `FEME_DUMP_IR_POSTCANON` + `FEME_DEBUG_DUMP_SPIRV_MLIR` dumps to pin the bug down fast: expected value at offset 100 (`48`) was the first stored value of the struct's *last* declared member (a non-`Offset` `{i32, mat2x2}` nested struct) -- that member's real offset should be 100, not the 104 FeMe computed. A genuine extra 4 bytes of padding baked into the nested struct's own *converted LLVM type*, not a member-index remap bug like `L369`'s.
3. Root cause: `convertOffsetStructTypeIgnoringDecorations`'s first, naive per-member conversion attempt recursed into a nested struct member via a plain recursive call, letting `layOutStructIfOffsetsMatch`'s own non-offset branch silently insert a natural-alignment interior gap (the `i32` padded up to the `mat2x2`'s 8-byte real-vector alignment) -- invisible to the enclosing struct's own offset validation, which only checks where each member *starts*. Since this nested member is the enclosing struct's *last* member, nothing after it could collide with the oversized body, so the naive attempt "succeeded" and the file's existing "tight" retry tiers never ran.
4. Fix: convert a nested struct member via `getTightNestedStructType` instead of the naive recursive call, specifically when the enclosing struct has explicit per-member `Offset`s but the nested member doesn't (`Type.hasOffset() && !NestedStructTy.hasOffset()`).
5. First attempt was too broad (keyed only on the enclosing struct's `hasOffset()`) and broke an existing unit test (`NestedNonOffsetStructInteriorPadRemapsInnerMember`, a plain offset-less `Input` interface struct that genuinely needs the natural/untightened layout with its real interior pad). Narrowed the condition to also require the nested struct itself have no offsets of its own -- re-verified against the existing `spirv-to-llvm-struct-trailing-gap-packed.mlir` lit test (nested struct *with* its own offsets, must keep naive conversion) too.
6. **`all_unordered_and_instance_array.2`: Pass** (was: `Mismatch at offset 100 expected 48 received 0`).
7. New unit test `TrailingNestedNonOffsetStructWithMatrixMemberTightlyPacks`, modeled on the real CTS shape, placed right after `L369`'s own `NestedNonOffsetStructTightEmbeddingRemapsMemberIndexCorrectly` test.
8. `ninja check-feme`: 3525/3586 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- no regressions (one test added vs. `L369`'s baseline).
9. Full 850-case `random_geometry.*` fuzz sweep: 242 Pass, 2 Fail, 0 crashes -- up from `L369`'s 241/3/0 baseline.
10. Committed in 4 commits: fix (`2bcae67`), unit test (`d8b115b`), docs (`b0dbfd5`), this file (pending).

- `nested_structs_instance_arrays.{2,31}`'s own remaining mismatch (`Mismatch at offset 56 expected 75 received 0`, `L368`'s own handoff item): confirmed **not** the same root cause as this fix (different offset, unaffected by this session's change) -- still the already-flagged `array of block instances` architectural gap, not yet root-caused. Reproduced again this session to confirm, did not dig further (still a dedicated-session item per many prior handoffs).

Canonicalization confirmed correct for this field in earlier sessions, so likely `Executor.cpp`'s XFB-capture loop, not `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` (the last two sessions' fixes were both in the latter and both left this one untouched). Start with the same signature-decoder + `FEME_DUMP_IR_POSTCANON`/`FEME_DEBUG_DUMP_SPIRV_MLIR` combo that worked for both `L369` and `L370`.

# Session: fixed nested_structs_instance_arrays.{2,31}'s multi-member XFB block-array stride for good (L371)

**Confirmed device:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (via `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=.../feme_icd.json` -- plain `vulkaninfo --summary` still shows `llvmpipe`).

## What's done

1. Fixed `nested_structs_instance_arrays.{2,31}` -- the single most-carried-over item across many sessions (`L368`'s own handoff, carried unchanged through `L369`/`L370`).
2. Root cause: `L366`'s own fix (several sessions ago) deliberately left `SignatureElement::XfbBufferArrayStride=0` for every decomposed member of this genuine *multi*-member "array of block instances" shape, reasoning (wrongly) that all instances pack back-to-back into one shared buffer. Disproved this by direct comparison: dumped `.2`'s pre-canon LLVM IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRECANON=1`), confirmed instance 1's store lands at byte offset 56 -- one full `XfbStride` further into the global's own flat storage, not packed after instance 0's own bytes. Compared against the already-passing single-member `instance_array_basic_type.mat4.vertex` case (same shape one member smaller) -- confirmed dEQP binds both the same way: N separate XFB buffer bindings, not back-to-back packing.
3. Fix: `AddBlockElement` (`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`'s `TakeBlockPath` loop) now computes each decomposed leaf's own per-instance row count (`getStageIORowShape(EltTy).RowCount`, on the un-widened type) and threads it through as `XfbBufferArrayStride`, instead of hardcoding 0 -- exactly mirroring the already-working single-member mechanism.
4. Also pinned down *why* `L366`'s own earlier attempt at a nonzero stride crashed (`double free or corruption`): it passed the instance **count** as the stride, not each leaf's own **per-instance row count** -- `Executor.cpp`'s `(Instance, InnerRow) = (Row / Stride, Row % Stride)` split only works with the latter.
5. **`.2` and `.31`: both Pass** (were: `Mismatch at offset 56 expected 75 received 0` and the `.31` analogue).
6. New unit test `MapsArrayOfBlockInstancesWithMultipleMembersToXfbBufferArrayStride` (`CanonicalizeStageTest.cpp`), a simplified 2-member/2-instance version of this shape. Learned along the way: a vector-valued stage-IO member decomposes into one `OutputStore` call *per component* in the rewritten IR, not one per member -- tripped up my first assertion attempt.
7. `ninja check-feme`: 3526/3587 Passed, 61 Unsupported, 0 Failed -- no regressions (one test added vs. `L370`'s baseline).
8. Full 850-case `random_geometry.*` fuzz sweep: **244 Pass, 0 Fail, 0 crashes** -- full clean sweep, up from `L370`'s 242/2/0 baseline. Every previously-known failure in this specific sweep is now fixed.
9. **New this session:** ran the full `dEQP-VK.transform_feedback.*` group (133,719 cases) for the first time -- previous sessions only ever sampled `fuzz.random_geometry.*` directly. Confirmed zero regressions from this fix, but surfaced two new, not-yet-triaged pre-existing clusters: `xfb_pointsize` family (~1,920 fails, likely uninitialized `gl_PointSize` capture) and `fuzz.random_vertex.*`/non-square-matrix `single_basic_*` cases (44 fails, a *different* vertex-shader-only fuzz variant from the geometry one this fix lives in). Full detail in `VulkanCTSReport.md`.
10. Committed in 4 commits: fix (`59cde38`), unit test (`7ab363f`), roadmap+CTS-report docs (`ba7aa13`), broader-sweep-finding docs (pending at commit time), this file (pending).

# Session: fixed xfb_pointsize (L372) and xfb_clipdistance/culldistance (L373) BuiltIn XFB bugs

**Confirmed device:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (via `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=.../feme_icd.json` -- plain `vulkaninfo --summary` still shows `llvmpipe`).

## What's done

1. Fixed `xfb_pointsize_*` (L372) -- the top-priority handoff item, 81 runnable cases, the largest unaddressed cluster found in any sweep so far.
2. Root cause: `addElements`'s per-member decomposition loop only ever threaded the whole-variable's `XfbBuffer`/`XfbOffset`/`XfbStride` decorations down to a *non*-`BuiltIn` member, under an explicit but wrong design comment claiming a `BuiltIn` member never carries real XFB decorations "in practice." `layout(xfb_buffer=0, xfb_offset=0) out gl_PerVertex { float gl_PointSize; };` is exactly a counterexample.
3. Fix: split the synthesis into two independently-gated halves. `Location` fabrication stays gated on `!MemberD.BuiltIn` (still correct, avoids `Location` collisions). `XfbBuffer`/`XfbOffset`/`XfbStride` threading is now unconditional.
4. `xfb_pointsize_*`: 81/81 runnable **Pass** (were: all Fail, `received:<garbage>`).
5. While confirming no regression to the related `xfb_clipdistance`/`xfb_culldistance`/`xfb_clip_and_cull` cluster (162 cases), found via `git stash` A/B that it's a **separate** pre-existing bug -- same family, different symptom (`received:1 expected:0`, a real but wrong value, not garbage).
6. Committed fix (`e1ab5e0a`) and unit test `ThreadsXfbCaptureDecorationsThroughBuiltInBlockMember` (`4ebc9bb`) separately, then docs (`1dd1f17`).

# Session: fixed LinearizePass relay-block PHI/predecessor crash (L374), found 2 new unconfirmed leads (L375, L376)

**Confirmed device:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (via `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=.../feme_icd.json` -- plain `vulkaninfo --summary` still shows `llvmpipe`).

2. Root cause: `ExitBlock->removePredecessor(RelayBlock, true)` was called eagerly without ever disconnecting `RelayBlock`'s own terminator, leaving it alive with a real edge to `ExitBlock` but no phi entry -- `EliminateUnreachableBlocks` then hit a `PHINode::removeIncomingValue` assertion trying to detach it a second time.
3. Fix: mirrored the sibling, already-correct `CheckBlock` code path -- capture the leftover phi value keyed on `RelayBlock` (wherever it lives), but only manually remove the predecessor keyed on `Header`/`Latch` (the block whose terminator is actually being erased right now).

Added `LinearizesLoopWhoseHeaderRelayIsPeeledDirectlyToExit` (`LinearizeTest.cpp`) -- honestly documented as general regression coverage, **not** a literal crash reproducer (confirmed via `git stash` A/B that the synthetic reduction doesn't itself hit the original assertion -- the real CTS case remains the authoritative regression evidence).

## Gotchas discovered

- `deqp-vk --deqp-case="A.*~B.*"` is **not** an exclusion syntax (silently matches 0 cases) -- use the separate `--deqp-exclude-case=...` flag instead.
- `api.*` and `pipeline.*` are enormously larger than `spirv_assembly.*`/`synchronization.*` (267K and 1.17M cases respectively, vs. ~69K/146K) -- a "broader CTS sweep" of these groups needs deliberate subgroup-level sampling planned up front, not a blind full-group run; this session discovered the scale problem but didn't yet solve it.
- `git reset --soft` + selective re-staging for split commits (rediscovered from a prior session's notes): always follow with a plain `git reset` (mixed) before re-adding individual files, or a `git commit` after `reset --soft` silently re-commits everything that was already staged.

# Session: fixed L377 loop-mask dominance bug, triaged L378 into it (2026-10-06)

**Confirmed device:** `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via explicit `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`/
`VK_DRIVER_FILES` (checked at session start and again before the final CTS
reruns below).

**Next action for the next session: open `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/Linearize.cpp`,
read the new `L377(a)` comment block in the roadmap, and start designing the
per-predecessor `ExitBlockRelayValues` generalization described there.** About
a day of focused work, not an afternoon -- this is a real SSA-merge redesign,
not a mechanical fix.

## What's done (all committed, 5 commits)

1. Root-caused `L377`'s dominance-verifier bug to the exact mechanism: a
   loop-body-internal divergent exit check (`CheckBlock`) is not always the
   sole entry into its own "stay in loop" continuation, because an earlier,
   legitimate constant-predecessor-peeling fold can redirect a different
   block straight into that continuation, bypassing `CheckBlock`'s own check.
2. Fixed it the safe way: `linearizeCycle` now checks
   `DT.dominates(CheckBlock, CheckExit->StayInLoop)` and diagnoses the shape
   instead of emitting invalid IR. Added a lit test + a unit test, both from
   the real reduced IR. `ninja check-feme`: 3,589/3,592 Passed, 0 Failed.
3. Reran both affected CTS families to completion (150,668 cases,
   ~35 minutes): **31,024 Pass / 31,024 Fail / 88,620 NotSupported / 0
   crashes** -- same split as before, but a full-log grep (not a sample)
   confirms every single one of the 31,024 failures now hits the clean new
   diagnostic. Before this fix, these cases risked an actual dominance-
   verifier crash/invalid-IR path depending on exact shape details; now they
   fail gracefully and are correctly diagnosed every time.
4. Triaged `L378` (the 7,454-case sampler long tail) instead of just
   splitting it blind: ran `sampler.view_type.*` (74,616 cases, ~8 minutes)
   and the two smaller real sub-trees to completion. **Found all 7,453
   `view_type.*` failures carry `L377`'s own exact diagnostic string** --
   same bug, not an independent sampler issue. Only one case in the whole
   7,454-case family (`max_sampler_lod_bias.shader_bias`) is a real,
   separate, not-yet-root-caused wrong-pixel bug.
5. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L377` not struck through, new `L377(a)`/`L378(a)`
   sub-entries, `L378` struck through as triaged), `FeMeCPUDesign.md` (new
   milestone-6 deviation bullet), and `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s triage section.
6. Final `check-feme` rerun this session: 3,589/3,592 Passed, 3 Unsupported,
   0 Failed -- clean.

## Why this matters more than "one bug fixed"

`L378` looked like a second, independent 7,454-case bug family. It wasn't --
it was the same `L377` bug showing up under a different pipeline-creation
path. Running the actual CTS sub-trees instead of guessing from case names
saved a whole redundant investigation. **Net effect: the 38,478 cases
`L377`+`L378` originally covered are now one compiler bug (`L377(a)`), not
two**, plus one unrelated 1-case wrong-pixel bug (`L378(a)`).

## What's still open (ranked)

1. **`L377(a)`** (the real fix, ~1 day): make the `CheckBlock`-not-sole-entry
   shape actually linearize instead of just diagnosing it. This is what
   would flip most of the 38,478 cases above from Fail to Pass. Design
   sketch: generalize `ExitBlockRelayValues`/`RelaySource` to treat the
   bypass edge as a second relay source, computing `CheckBlock`'s own
   derived values per-predecessor and merging them at the consumption point
   instead of assuming one source. **Worth checking first: does this share
   a root cause with `L295`'s still-open "two divergent decisions sharing
   one dispatch block" design problem?** Both are about a value computed in
   one block needing to dominate a use reachable via a second, bypassing
   path. If so, one fix might close both.
2. **`L378(a)`** (~1-2 hours once picked up): `max_sampler_lod_bias.shader_bias`
   wrong-pixel bug. `shader_bias_compute` (same LOD-bias logic, compute
   pipeline) passes, so this is likely graphics-fragment-path-specific.
   Next step: `--deqp-log-images=enable` and diff against the golden image.
3. **Stability triage (46 pipeline SIGSEGV + 328 renderpasses DeviceLost) --
   not started this session.** No case names are recorded anywhere from the
   original full-suite run that produced these counts, only aggregate
   numbers. Finding them requires either (a) a full `pipeline.*`/
   `renderpasses.*` rerun (the `pipeline` group alone is ~1.1M cases; at

## What's done (all committed, 6 commits: 5 code/test + 1 docs)

1. Picked up last session's `L377(a)` handoff and implemented the real fix:
   `LoopLinearizer::linearizeCycle` now actually linearizes the
   `CheckBlock`-not-sole-entry shape instead of diagnosing it.
2. **Caught a critical gap the first attempt missed.** The initial fix
   (redirect the bypass edge into `CheckBlock` via a phi) made `opt
   -passes=verify` and all unit/lit tests pass -- but running the real CTS
   reproducer end-to-end still failed, now with a *different* error:
   `feme-cpu-simdize` rejected a still-physically-intact divergent branch
   (`ChainGate`'s own `CondBr`) that the first fix never actually removed,
   only bypassed. This is exactly the `L295` silent-miscompile lesson in
   action: a fix that verifies clean can still be functionally incomplete.
   Only the real end-to-end CTS run caught it.
3. Fixed it for real: detect `ChainGate`, require its bypass region to be
   pure/side-effect-free glue (every block `size()==1`, single predecessor),
   build a `select`-based merged condition, replace `ChainGate`'s `CondBr`
   with one `UncondBrInst` into `CheckBlock`, delete the dead bypass blocks,
   rewire `CheckExit` to the new merged condition. Falls back to the old
   diagnostic for any shape that doesn't match.

   (`...image.dedicated_allocation...r16_sfloat.count_1.size.127x1_compute`):
   **Pass (Result image matches reference)** -- correct pixels, not just a
   clean pipeline build.

   for the `select`-based merge) and the unit test (renamed, flipped
   `EXPECT_TRUE(SawError)` to `EXPECT_FALSE`) to match. `ninja check-feme`:
   3,589/3,589 Passed, 0 Failed, 3 Unsupported -- clean.

   total): `pipeline.monolithic.image.*` (122,912 cases: 46,112 Pass / **0

   cases: 15,936 Pass / **0 Fail** / 11,772 NotSupported),
   `pipeline.monolithic.sampler.view_type.*` (74,616 cases: 15,078 Pass /
   **0 Fail** / 59,538 NotSupported). All three: 0 crashes, 0 DeviceLost.
   This flips all 31,024 `L377` cases and all 7,453 `L378`-folded-into-`L377`
   cases from Fail to Pass.
7. Independently reran `sampler.max_sampler_lod_bias.*` (10 cases: 7 Pass /
   **1 Fail** / 2 NotSupported) -- confirmed `L378(a)`'s wrong-pixel bug is
   still open and genuinely unrelated to this fix.
8. Re-verified `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: 445 Pass / 31 XFAIL / 200 Unsupported /
   3 Fail / 1 XPass -- matches the known pre-existing baseline exactly
   (`Mandelbrot` golden-image flakiness, `spec_const_32_bits`/`WaveActiveMax`

The first `L377(a)` attempt looked done: valid IR, all tests green. It
wasn't. `feme-cpu-simdize`'s "zero divergent branches" requirement is

is complete until the real end-to-end case passes with correct pixels, not
just until the verifier and tests are quiet.**

Not a real bug in the fix itself. Running this exact lit test here
(same commit) **passes**, and produces IR with the same total line count
(282 vs. the user's reported 281, off by a harmless EOF/attribute-line
difference) and identical overall structure. The only difference is the
exact numeric suffix on two `.linearized<N>`-named operands feeding
`%chain.merge`. Those names come from `DiamondFlattener::flatten`'s
`PN.getName() + ".linearized"` naming scheme (`Linearize.cpp:1773`):
LLVM auto-uniquifies same-named values within a function by appending a
whole-function-wide counter, so the exact number assigned to any one
`.linearized`-named value depends on how many *other* such values this
same function's *other*, unrelated diamonds happen to produce first.
That ordering is not guaranteed stable across different LLVM/platform/
compiler builds (confirmed no in-process non-determinism here: 5 repeated
invocations in this environment gave identical output every time, so
whatever shifts the count only varies *across* builds, not across runs of
the same binary) -- the test should never have hardcoded those exact
suffixes, since they were never semantically meaningful to the thing the
test actually verifies (that `ChainGate`'s branch is gone and `CheckBlock`
is entered via a merged boolean, not literally which temporary numbers
LLVM's printer happens to assign the two operands).

## Fix

Replaced the two hardcoded operand names (`%.linearized9`, `%.linearized8`)
with FileCheck `{{%[A-Za-z0-9_.]+}}` regex patterns, matching the
structural shape (some SSA value selected against a literal `i1 true`)
without depending on its auto-generated name. Added a comment explaining
why, so a future session doesn't hardcode the same kind of fragile pattern
again. Did **not** touch `Linearize.cpp` itself -- the compiler behavior is
correct; only the test was fragile. Checked the companion unit test
(`LinearizeTest.cpp`) for the same anti-pattern: clean, no hardcoded
`.linearized<N>` names there.

**Verified:** updated test passes here; `ninja check-feme`: 3,589/3,589
Passed, 0 Failed, 3 Unsupported -- clean, 0 regressions. Single, separate
commit (`3ae810fc1fa0`).

## Takeaway for future lit tests in this file

Any `CHECK` line matching a `DiamondFlattener::flatten`-produced
`.linearized<N>`-style auto-named value (or any other value whose base
name is reused many times in one function, triggering LLVM's own
uniquing suffix) should use a FileCheck capture/regex instead of the
literal printed name, unless the test is specifically about name
stability itself (it normally isn't). This fix only touched one test;
worth a quick grep (`grep -rn '\.linearized[0-9]' feme/test/`) next time
a `Linearize.cpp` session starts, in case any other lit test added since
has the same latent fragility.

# Session: diagnosed the clean-build `chain.merge` contradiction as a binary provenance problem (2026-10-06)

## Outcome

The supplied `output.ll` is not the output of the current
`Linearize.cpp` implementation for the supplied test, even after accounting
for unstable SSA suffixes or platform differences. The current implementation
emits:

```
%chain.merge = select i1 %.linearized9, i1 true, i1 %.linearized8
br label %Flow72.Flow74_crit_edge
```

It also deletes bypass block `76`, threads `active.check.live` and
`exited.via.check`, and makes `loop.exit.guard` single-predecessor. The
reported output has none of those changes: it retains both divergent branches,
bypass block `76`, and the old two-predecessor `loop.exit.guard` phis.

The test was renamed to its current path by `41820edc94a6`, the same commit
that added the initial L377(a) chain repair. The current select-based repair
landed in `670f7c94abea`, and the permissive FileCheck expression landed in
`3ae810fc1fa0`. Therefore the current test file and the implementation behavior
shown in `output.ll` cannot come from one coherently built source revision.
A clean object/cache rebuild rules out an ordinary stale `.o`, but it does not
prove that the executable loaded the library just built or that CMake was
configured against the source checkout containing the test.

## Build-graph audit

The checked-in and generated dependency graphs are correct:

1. `feme/test/CMakeLists.txt` lists `feme-opt` in `FEME_TEST_DEPENDS`.
2. `feme-opt` links `FeMeTransformsCPU`.
3. `libFeMeTransformsCPU.a` directly depends on
   `Linearize.cpp.o`.
4. `Linearize.cpp.o` directly depends on this checkout's
   `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/Linearize.cpp`.

The local build uses `ccache`, has `LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS=ON` and
`CMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS=ON`, and is statically linked. Rebuilding
through `ninja -C build check-feme` rebuilt/relinked `feme-opt`; all 3,589
supported tests passed (3 unsupported), including the exact lit test. The
direct `feme-opt | FileCheck` command also passed and emitted `chain.merge`.
This rules out a missing `check-feme` target dependency in the repository.

## Leading clean-build explanation on macOS

If the reporter's build has `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`, the most likely remaining
cause is runtime resolution of an older `libFeMeTransformsCPU.dylib`.
Deleting objects and CMake/compiler caches does not change
`DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH`, or an `@rpath` that selects
a library from another build/install tree. In that configuration,
`build-rel/bin/feme-opt` may itself be freshly linked while the pass code being
executed still comes from an older dylib.

Run these on the failing Mac:

```
grep -E '^(CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY|BUILD_SHARED_LIBS|LLVM_ENABLE_ASSERTIONS|CMAKE_DISABLE_PRECOMPILE_HEADERS):' \
  build-rel/CMakeCache.txt
otool -L build-rel/bin/feme-opt | grep -E 'FeMeTransformsCPU|LLVM'
DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES=1 build-rel/bin/feme-opt --llvm \
  -passes=feme-cpu-linearize -disable-output \
  feme/test/Transforms/CPU/Linearize/checkblock-chained-divergent-check-bypass.ll \
  2>&1 | grep -E 'FeMeTransformsCPU|feme-opt'
```

If `otool` shows no FeMe dylib, this is a static build and the executable
itself is mismatched; compare `CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` with the test checkout and
run:

```
strings build-rel/bin/feme-opt | grep -c chain.merge
ninja -C build-rel -t query bin/feme-opt
ninja -C build-rel -t query lib/libFeMeTransformsCPU.a
```

The first command must be nonzero for a current static binary. For a shared
build, run the same `strings` check on the exact dylib path printed by
`DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES`, not on `feme-opt`.

## Environment and documentation

The session's default Vulkan ICD initially selected llvmpipe. Explicitly
setting `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` to
`build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json` confirmed
`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. No compiler or driver source changed, so there was
no behavior change to rerun Vulkan CTS against and no
`VulkanCTSReport.md`, `Vulkan14FeatureInventory`, or
`VulkanExtensionInventory` update was needed.

## Next step

Capture the `DYLD_PRINT_LIBRARIES` result from the failing invocation. It will
identify the exact dylib containing the old pass; if no dylib is involved,
`CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY` plus the two Ninja queries will identify the other
source/build tree that produced the executable.

## The OffloadTest "cache-persistence gap" was never a cache bug

Four prior sessions carried this forward as an unstarted item with no detail
beyond its name. Here's what it actually is:

- This repo's own `build/` directory is **already** configured with
  `-DLLVM_EXTERNAL_PROJECTS=OffloadTest` and everything else needed.
  `ninja -C build check-hlsl-feme-vk` builds/runs the whole 680-case suite
  in **~25 seconds**, because LLVM/clang/mlir/feme are already built there
  with a warm `ccache`.
- A prior session (roadmap `L192`) instead stood up a brand-new, separate
  build directory at `/home/dev/dev/offload-test-suite/build`. That
  directory's own CMake-generated include paths differ from `build/`'s, so
  almost none of `build/`'s cache applies -- a full ~5,400-target,
  ~15-minute rebuild every time, and the directory doesn't even persist
  across sessions (it didn't exist at this session's start).
- Fix: use `build/`, not a separate directory. Updated
  `feme/.instructions.md` so this doesn't get rediscovered again.

While chasing this I found `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` flaky under the suite's
default 12-parallel-worker run (`Failed to wait on Semaphore, VkResult = 2`).
Traced it to `Sync.cpp`'s own pre-existing `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS`
safety net (roadmap `L228(h)`/`(i)`, already documented, already has an
env-var override) being legitimately exercised by 12-way host CPU
contention. Not a new bug -- confirmed the design doc already explains this
exact scenario. No action taken; noted in roadmap `L380` so it isn't
re-investigated as new.

# Session: fixed 3 of 46 pipeline/api SIGSEGVs (L381/L382), found+fixed a 4th independent crash family (L384) and its own regression (L383) (2026-10-06)

## Confirmed device first
`vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` -> `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed
twice this session (start and end).

## What shipped, in commit order

1. **`L384`** -- `DescriptorSet::Layout` raw-pointer dangled after the app
   destroyed its `VkDescriptorSetLayout` (spec-legal). Root cause of
   `ds_resolve_sample_zero.*`'s own SIGSEGV, a **46-case** crash family
   found by exploring past the two already-tracked crashes below.
   Fix: by-value copy (mirrors `L305`). New test:
   `DescriptorTest.UsableAfterDescriptorSetLayoutDestroyed`.
2. **`L383`** -- fixing `L384` broke push-descriptor-set accumulation:
   `getOrCreatePushDescriptorSet` compared `getLayout()`'s *address* for
   identity, which only worked while `Layout` was a pointer. Found via a
   full unit-test-suite rerun, not targeted testing -- confirmed genuine
   regression via `git stash` A/B. Fix: track the original layout pointer
   separately in a new `CurrentPushDescriptorSetLayouts` map. Existing test
   already covers it, no new test needed.
3. **`L381`** -- `compatible_render_pass` SIGSEGV: a pipeline-library link
   can legally outlive the `VkRenderPass` every part was built against.
   Fix: cache each library's own `RenderTargets` eagerly, before the
   handle can go stale. Writing the regression test
   (`LinksAfterOriginalRenderPassIsDestroyed`) found **two more** latent
   bugs in the same path (unconditional `RenderPass` capture letting a
   non-owning library win a search; a dynamic-rendering pNext-scoping
   ambiguity) -- both fixed in the same commit, both found only by running
   the **full** suite after the initial fix, not by code review.
4. **`L382`** -- `pipeline_invalid_pointers_unused_structs` SIGSEGV: driver
   dereferenced `pViewportState`/`pMultisampleState`/`pDepthStencilState`/
   `pColorBlendState` even when rasterization is statically disabled and
   the spec says their contents don't matter. Fix:
   `isRasterizationStaticallyDiscarded` gate before every dereference.
5. Doc commits: `Roadmap.md` (new `L381`-`L384`, `L383(a)` rows, updated
   stability summary), `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new triage items 6-8).

## Confirmed device first

`vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` with the default `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`

and got `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed. Every CTS/test run this session

## What's fixed, right now

`ds_resolve_sample_zero*` CTS family: **0/120 Pass -> 48/120 Pass**.
Try it: `./build/tools/feme/unittests/Vulkan/FeMeVulkanTests
--gtest_filter="*ClassicRenderPassResolvesIntegerColorToSampleZeroNotAverage*"`
passes.

Two bugs found and fixed, both needed together — fixing only one does
nothing observable:

1. **`CommandBuffer.cpp`** (`buildRenderTargetBinding`): a classic
   `VkRenderPass` has no `resolveMode` field at all for color attachments
   (unlike dynamic rendering's `VkRenderingAttachmentInfo`). The spec still
   requires integer color formats to always resolve via sample 0. Fixed by
   forcing `View.ColorResolveMode = VK_RESOLVE_MODE_SAMPLE_ZERO_BIT` when
   `feme::cpu::isIntegerColorAttachmentFormat` is true.
2. **`ImageOps.cpp`** (`resolveSubpassColorAttachments`): a *second*,
   independent resolve pass that runs at `vkCmdEndRenderPass`/
   `vkCmdNextSubpass` (to catch any samples a subpass's own draws didn't
   cover) unconditionally box-filter-averaged every attachment, completely
   ignoring `ColorResolveMode` — silently overwriting fix #1's correct
   per-draw result, since this pass always runs last. Fixed by branching
   it on `ColorResolveMode` the same way the per-draw resolve already does.

Found bug #2 by debug-tracing three points end-to-end
(`buildRenderTargetBinding` -> `resolveDrawAttachments` ->
`Executor.cpp`'s per-draw resolve loop) and confirming each one computed
and threaded `SampleZero` correctly, yet the final pixel value was still
the average — meaning something *downstream* of the already-correct
per-draw resolve was overwriting it. That pointed straight at the
subpass-end resolve pass, which turned out to have its own entirely
separate, unconditional-average bug.

# Session: L387 root-caused and fixed (152/152 cases), L386 root-caused and scoped (2026-10-06)

Device check: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (confirmed start and end of session — the unset default resolves to lavapipe/llvmpipe, not FeMe).

## What's fixed

**`L387`** (`dEQP-VK.renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.primary_cmd_buff.suballocation.*` pipeline-creation failures): **all 152 of 152 cases now Pass.**

Root cause (confirmed via CTS source reading, `vktRenderPassTests.cpp`'s `findColorAttachments`/`fillRenderingAttachmentLocationsInfo`): a multi-subpass classic `VkRenderPass` translated to dynamic rendering gives every subpass's own pipeline the *same combined*, cross-subpass `pColorAttachmentFormats` list (e.g. `[intFmt, UNORM]` for a 2-subpass test), not a per-subpass subset. To disambiguate which attachment index a given subpass's fragment shader actually writes (and at which location), CTS chains a `VkRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo` onto that pipeline's own create info. FeMe had code for the already-known *dynamic* form of this state (`vkCmdSetRenderingAttachmentLocations`, fixed in a prior session's `L379(b)`) but nothing anywhere that looked for the *static*, pipeline-creation-time chained struct — so `validateStageInterfaces` assumed attachment index `I` always equals fragment-output location `I`, misattributing one subpass's real output to the wrong attachment and rejecting pipeline creation.

Fixed by adding `findRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo` (mirrors the existing `findRenderingCreateInfo` pNext-search pattern) and threading the resolved remap through `compileAndValidateStages`/`validateStageInterfaces`'s per-attachment check, falling back to identity when no such struct is chained (every other pipeline's behavior is unchanged).

Commits (already landed):
1. `[feme] Fix L387: honor VkRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo at pipeline creation` — the fix + `GraphicsPipelineTest.AcceptsRemappedColorAttachmentLocationsFromPipelineCreateInfo` (manually confirmed to fail with the exact real error *before* this fix, by stashing the source change and re-running just the new test).
2. `[feme] Update Roadmap/VulkanCTSReport for the L387 fix` — Roadmap.md (struck through) + VulkanCTSReport.md (item 13).

Verified: `primary_cmd_buff.suballocation.*` (5,935 cases) goes from 3,894 Pass / 152 Fail / 1,889 NotSupported to **4,046 Pass / 0 Fail / 1,889 NotSupported**. Wider `renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.*` sweep (28,898 cases) shows no regressions (11,317 Pass / 1,106 Fail / 16,475 NotSupported — the remaining 1,106 are unrelated, already-scoped families, e.g. `L386`). `FeMeVulkanTests`: 800/800 Passed (+1 new test). `ninja check-feme`: 3,600/3,603 Passed, 3 Unsupported, 0 Failed, 0 regressions. No `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md` change needed (internal correctness fix only).

## What's root-caused but not fixed

**`L386`** — the handoff's priority #2. Previous session's guess (an unresolved stage-IO global, a `CanonicalizeStage.cpp`-class bug) was **wrong**. Using the existing `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRECANON`/`FEME_DUMP_IR_POSTCANON` env vars against the single reproducer showed `spirv_var_25` is actually a **push-constant block** (address space 13), still unrewritten after `SPIRVPushConstantLoweringPass` runs.

Real root cause: the `ds_resolve_sample_zero` fragment shader's branchy resolve logic computes two different compile-time byte offsets (112 and 116) into the push-constant block along two branches, each via its own `getelementptr`, then **merges the two pointers with a `phi`** before one shared `load`. `SPIRVPushConstantLowering.cpp`'s `visitPushConstantUsers` only recognizes a GEP's user as a `load` or a further `getelementptr` — a `phi` user is unsupported by the file's own documented scope, so the pass rejects the *whole* function's push-constant access, leaving the global forever unresolved at JIT-link time.

This is genuinely a design-session item, not a quick fix: the rewrite (`lowerSPIRVPushConstantAccess`) is keyed per-terminal-`Load` with exactly one compile-time `BaseOffset` — incompatible with a load reached through a `phi` of pointers that have *different* offsets per incoming edge. A correct fix needs to sink the per-load bounds-check/load-and-replace logic to each `phi` edge's own GEP (replacing it with a scalar load in that edge's predecessor block) and build a parallel value-level `phi`, generalizing to nested `phi`s too. Scoped in `Roadmap.md` accordingly (same category as `L375`) — not attempted this session.

Commit: `[feme] Root-cause L386: push-constant phi-of-GEPs unresolved JIT symbol` — Roadmap.md + VulkanCTSReport.md (item 14), documentation/triage only, no source change.

## Not touched

**`L375`** — still untouched, still needs a dedicated design session (`DiamondFlattener` stale-postdom-tree assertion). Deliberately deferred again, per every prior session's own scoping.

No work done outside `feme/` this session — nothing found to isolate/fix in another subproject.

# Session: L386 fixed (phi-of-GEPs push-constant access), including a self-caught bug in the fix itself (2026-10-06)

Device check: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (confirmed start and end of session).

## What's fixed

**`L386`** (push-constant `phi`-of-GEPs, the remaining 24 `ds_resolve_sample_zero*` `input_attachments.render_to` cases): **fully fixed, all 24 cases now Pass.**

Extended `visitPushConstantUsers` to recognize a `phi` merging push-constant pointers with different compile-time byte offsets (reached via different control-flow edges), and `lowerSPIRVPushConstantAccess` to sink a bounds-checked load to each of the `phi`'s own incoming edges, merging the resulting *values* with a new `phi` that replaces the original pointer `phi`. The original shared `load` becomes dead and is removed.

## The self-caught bug (worth reading even if you skip everything else)

The first version of this fix passed its own unit test and `check-feme` cleanly, but crashed the real CTS reproducer with an LLVM assertion inside `DiamondFlattener::flatten` — the exact function `L375`'s own documented bug lives in. Natural read: "this is `L375`." That read was wrong.

What actually happened: `SPIRVPushConstantPhiEdge` cached a `BasicBlock *Pred` per edge at match time. `lowerSPIRVPushConstantAccess` processes plain loads (`Access.Loads`) *before* `phi` edges (`Access.PhiAccesses`). When an unrelated plain load's own GEP happened to live in the same original block as a `phi` edge's GEP, processing that plain load first split the shared block — replacing its terminator (which used to branch straight to the `phi`'s merge block) with a new conditional branch, and moving the real edge-to-merge branch into a new block. The `phi` edge's own rewrite then called `Edge.Pred->getTerminator()` on the stale pointer, grabbed the *wrong* instruction, and produced a `phi` listing a predecessor that was no longer real — invalid IR, caught by `LinearizePass` downstream as an unrelated-looking assertion.

Caught by running the LLVM verifier (`opt -passes=verify`) directly on IR dumped right before `LinearizePass`, instead of trusting the `L375` pattern-match. It found the real problem immediately: `PHI node entries do not match predecessors!`

Fix: store the incoming-value **index**, not the block pointer. Re-read `Phi->getIncomingBlock(Edge.Index)` fresh, immediately before each edge's own rewrite. This works because `BasicBlock::splitBasicBlock` always keeps every `phi`'s incoming-block entries pointed at the real current predecessor, no matter which pass caused the split — the index is the only thing that has to stay stable, and it does.

**Lesson for future sessions, stated plainly so it's not missed again**: when a new crash looks like a documented, deferred bug (same function, similar shape), verify independently before writing it down as the same bug. A verifier run or a diffed `gdb bt` takes minutes. Believing a pattern match costs a session.

## Verification

1. Lit test (`spirv-push-constant-lowering-phi.ll`, 4 functions): `FileCheck` passes AND output is LLVM-verifier-valid (added a 4th function this session specifically to regression-test the stale-predecessor bug — a `phi` edge sharing its predecessor block with an unrelated plain load).
2. Real CTS reproducer (`...ds_resolve_sample_zero.sub_framebuffer`): now passes end-to-end, no crash.

# Session: L388 fixed (library-linked attachment-location remap), L389 self-regression caught and fixed same session (2026-10-06)

Device check: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=$(find build -iname feme_icd.json) vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (confirmed start, mid-session, and end).

## What's fixed

**`L388`** (`graphics_pipeline_library.{suballocation,dedicated_allocation}.attachment_allocation.roll.*`, 278 cases): **fully fixed, all 278 now Pass.**

Same error class as `L387` (`fragment stage has no floating-point/integer output ... at location N`), but for `VK_EXT_graphics_pipeline_library`-*linked* pipelines. CTS's `GraphicsPipelineWrapper` chains `VkRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo` onto the fragment-output-interface *library part's own* create info (`setupFragmentOutputState`), never onto the top-level link call's — so `L387`'s own fix, which only ever reads `findRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo(CreateInfo.pNext)` off the create info it's handed, always came up empty for a linked pipeline. Exactly `L381`'s own `PrecomputedRenderTargets` bug shape (render-pass-related state owned by one library part must be captured at `captureGraphicsPipelineLibraryState` time and threaded forward as an explicit out-parameter, not re-derived from the synthesized link-call create info).

Fix: new `GraphicsPipelineLibraryState::ColorAttachmentLocations` field, captured/folded/threaded through `synthesizeLinkedGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo` as a new `PrecomputedColorAttachmentLocations` out-parameter, consumed by `compileGraphicsPipeline` in place of re-searching when supplied — mechanically identical to `RenderTargets`'s own plumbing.

**`L389`** (self-regression, found and fixed within this same session): 2 `SIGSEGV` crashes in `graphics_pipeline_library.local_read.{null_color_attachment_location_with_locationinfo,_before_identity}`, discovered purely as a side effect of re-sweeping the `graphics_pipeline_library.*` family to verify `L388`. **This is worth reading carefully — it's a mistake I made and caught in the same session, not a pre-existing bug.**

`gdb bt` pointed straight at `L388`'s own brand-new `captureGraphicsPipelineLibraryState` code (`std::vector::assign` on a null pointer). I didn't just assume it was new, though — I checked out the pre-`L388` version of the two source files, rebuilt, and reran the exact same CTS case: it passed. That's the confirmation this was a genuine same-session regression, not something that happened to exist already and only became reachable (the "look suspicious, go verify" habit from `L386`'s own post-mortem last session paid off immediately here).

Root cause: `VkRenderingAttachmentLocationInfo::pColorAttachmentLocations == nullptr` with a nonzero `colorAttachmentCount` is the spec-legal spelling of "identity mapping, no remap." Both of `L388`'s new call sites unconditionally did `vector.assign(ptr, ptr + count)` without checking `ptr` for null — and in fixing it I noticed `L387`'s own original `compileGraphicsPipeline` code had the exact same latent bug for monolithic (non-linked) pipelines, just never exercised by a null-pointer CTS case before now. Fixed both, with a null check mirroring the existing `ColorBlendAttachments::pAttachments` pattern already sitting right above in the same function.

Device check: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=$(find build -iname feme_icd.json) VK_DRIVER_FILES=$(find build -iname feme_icd.json) vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (confirmed start and end; plain `vulkaninfo --summary` without the env vars still reports the ambient `llvmpipe` default — expected, documented in `feme/.instructions.md`, not a bug).

## Start here: what's fixed vs. what's still open

**Fixed and CTS-verified this session: `L391`** (`VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT` ignored `loadOp` was never implemented). 60 CTS Fails → 0.

**Not fixed, two root-caused-but-deferred items:**
- `L375` (assigned top priority this session): two fix attempts tried, both failed, real mechanism now fully understood, no working fix found. Still blocking, still needs a dedicated design session.
- `L390`: root cause now understood (not just "found" — actually traced to the exact pattern and exact missing case), still needs implementation.

## `L375`: two failed fix attempts, then the real mechanism

This session resumed mid-investigation with a hypothesis from before compaction: "two separate `DiamondFlattener` instances reuse a stale PDT." Both of the two fix attempts built on that hypothesis:

1. Recompute `DT`/`PDT` right before `flattenLoopBodyRegion`'s own `DiamondFlattener` construction (mirroring an existing precedent elsewhere in the file) — rebuilt, retested against all 4 reproducers (`switch_continue_{geom,tessc,tesse}`, `graphicsfuzz.nested-for-loops-switch-fallthrough`). **Still crashed, identically.**
2. Recompute `DT`/`PDT` unconditionally inside `flatten()`'s own loop, before every `immediatePostDom` query. **Still crashed, identically.**

A `gdb bt` after attempt 1 failed showed the crash was inside a `flatten → flatten` recursive chain, not between two separate top-level instances — invalidating the original hypothesis outright, not just the fix.

Added temporary `errs()` prints (env-var gated, same convention the file already uses, removed before commit) at both `pred_begin(R)` sites plus an unconditional per-iteration print. Traced the real mechanism: **the same physical merge block gets visited by two independent top-level `flatten()` calls**, not one call's own stale state. The first call reaches it as a clean 2-predecessor diamond and processes it normally. A second, independent top-level call later reaches a different block its own walk hadn't covered yet, flattens *that* block's diamond, and its recursive arm reaches the *same* merge block a second time — but now with only 1 real predecessor, because the first call already consumed one of its two edges. **Recomputing PDT cannot fix this**: the predecessor count genuinely is 1 by the second visit. This is a generalization of the already-solved `CycleBoundaryMasks`/H120 mechanism (built for a very similar "reached twice" problem, but only for cycle-boundary blocks) to ordinary merge blocks.

Reverted all code changes (`git checkout --`) — the file is clean, no diagnostic code or failed fix remains. Documented the full finding in `Roadmap.md`'s `L375` row, explicitly steering the next session away from PDT-recompute ideas and toward a `FlattenedBlockMasks`-style memoization design.

**Why no fix this session**: the real fix needs to distinguish "this walk has fully reconverged past `Cur`" from "mid-walk, still heading forward" — unlike the cycle-boundary case, which always stops and records a terminal answer. That's a real design problem, not a patch, and two failed attempts already used up the session's safe experimentation budget for this item.

## `L390`: root-caused, not fixed (this is new progress, previously it was just "found")

4 CTS cases (`depth_stencil_mapping_to_no_index[_depth_clear|_stencil_clear]`, `input_attachments_without_mapping`) fail `vkCreateGraphicsPipelines` with `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED`. Previously scoped only as far as "swallowed error, needs `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1`." This session went further:

1. `FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS=1` on all 4 (not just 1) confirms one shared error: a `Dim::SubpassData` (dim code 6) image handle reaching `BoundResourceNormalizationPass` unconverted.
2. `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRENORM=1` shows the handle flows into `llvm.spv.resource.getpointer` (a raw storage-image texel pointer), not the dedicated `feme.stage.subpass.load` ABI a `subpassInput` read should use.
3. Traced to `ImageTexelPointerPattern` (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`): built for roadmap `R39`/`H8u`'s atomic-on-storage-image support, it lowers *any* image dimension the same way, with no `Dim::SubpassData` case the way `SubpassLoadPattern` has for plain `OpImageRead`. These 4 cases' depth/stencil subpass reads apparently go through `OpImageTexelPointer`, not `OpImageRead`, so `SubpassLoadPattern` never sees them.
4. Confirmed via the full sweep (below) that all 3 command-buffer variants hit this identically — 12 Fails total, not just the originally-scoped 4.

No code change: the real fix (a `Dim::SubpassData` special case in `ImageTexelPointerPattern`) touches a shared, high-traffic conversion pattern and deserves its own verified session.

## `L391`: VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT fixed — 60 Fails to 0

Picked up the carried-over "low-priority 30-minute triage" item (re-run the `renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.*` Fail bucket's largest sub-families through a quick check). Bucketed the 828 Fails: `primary_cmd_buff.random` (756, individually-seeded, too fragmented to usefully sub-bucket), `primary_cmd_buff.basic` (60), `local_read` (12, see `L390` above).

All 60 `basic` Fails share one substring: `resuming`. A `grep` for `RESUMING`/`SUSPENDING` across the whole Vulkan/Graphics layer found **zero matches** — `VK_RENDERING_SUSPENDING_BIT`/`VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT` were entirely unhandled, a missing-feature gap, not a subtle logic bug.

Per spec, a resuming instance's own `loadOp` must be ignored (treated as `LOAD`), but `vkCmdBeginRenderingKHR` applied it verbatim — and real apps/CTS specify the same `loadOp` (often `CLEAR`) on every begin call in a suspend/resume chain, so resuming re-cleared data the suspended instance had already drawn.

Fix: force every attachment's `LoadOp` away from `CLEAR` when `VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT` is set, reusing `applyClear`'s existing "LOAD/DONT_CARE/NONE are all a no-op" handling. `StoreOp` needed no change — this renderer already always preserves written memory regardless of `StoreOp` (no discard-on-store to skip), which is exactly `STORE`'s suspend-side spec behavior.

Added `DrawTest.DynamicRenderingResumingIgnoresLoadOp`. Confirmed it fails pre-fix via a `git checkout --`/rebuild A/B (first attempt at the test was actually broken — both the suspended and resuming draw used the same red color over overlapping areas, so the assertion passed even without the fix; caught this by actually doing the A/B check rather than trusting the test in isolation, then fixed the test to issue no draw on the resuming instance so the left-half color exclusively reflects whether the resume's own `CLEAR` was honored).

# Session: L390 fix completed and fully CTS-verified (0 Fail/28,898) (2026-10-06)

Device check: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=$(find build -iname feme_icd.json) VK_DRIVER_FILES=$(find build -iname feme_icd.json) vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (confirmed start and end; plain `vulkaninfo --summary` without the env vars still reports the ambient `llvmpipe` default — expected, documented in `feme/.instructions.md`, not a bug).

## tl;dr

Picked up `L390` exactly where the prior session's root-cause left off (a `subpassInput`/`usubpassInput` with no `input_attachment_index` decoration — a deliberate, spec-legal "read the current subpass's own depth/stencil attachment directly" shape). Implemented the fix, found and fixed **two** regressions along the way, added a regression unit test for each, and finished with a full 28,898-case CTS re-sweep of the whole `dynamic_rendering.*` family showing **0 Fail** (down from the 12 Fails this family has carried since `L391`'s own sweep last session). This closes out the `renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.*` family entirely for now — every previously-tracked Fail in it is gone.

## What actually shipped

- `StageOpKind::SubpassLoad` reused unchanged — no new op kind needed.
- `SubpassLoadPattern` (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`) now bakes one of two new reserved sentinel constants (`kSubpassLoadDirectDepthAttachmentIndex`/`kSubpassLoadDirectStencilAttachmentIndex`, added to `StageOps.h`) as the `attachment_index` operand instead of declining the match when `input_attachment_index` is absent.
- `lowerFragmentSubpassLoad` (`FragmentWrapper.cpp`) detects the sentinel at runtime and resolves it against `SubpassInputHeapCount - 2`/`- 1` — the last two slots of the per-draw subpass-input heap.
- `buildSubpassInputHeap` (`CommandBuffer.cpp`) always appends two trailing heap slots populated directly from `Draw.DepthStencil.Depth`/`.Stencil`, independent of whether any *indexed* subpass input is also in play.
- **Zero new ABI struct fields, zero new function parameters.** Smallest possible surface for the fix.

## Two regressions, two independent root causes (don't conflate them like I almost did)

1. **`Executor.cpp`'s `HasSelfReferencingDepthStencilInput` (`L330`) false-positived on every depth/stencil draw.** It scans every `SubpassInputHeap` entry's `Data` pointer against `DepthStencil.Depth`/`.Stencil`'s own pointer to detect a genuine feedback loop (shader reads what it's about to write). The two new trailing slots *always* equal that same pointer by construction — not because of a real self-reference — so the scan needs to simply skip them: `Draw.SubpassInputHeap.drop_back(std::min<size_t>(2, ...))`. A true feedback-loop self-reference can only ever happen through a *real*, indexed `subpassLoad`, never through this direct no-index mechanism, so excluding the last two slots from the scan is always correct, not just a workaround.
2. **My own interim attempt at fixing (1) broke a different CTS case family.** I first tried gating the two trailing slots' *construction* on `Any` (whether the draw already used the indexed subpass-input mechanism for *something*). This seemed reasonable until I read the actual CTS source (`vktDynamicRenderingLocalReadTests.cpp`) for `depth_stencil_mapping_to_no_index_depth_clear`/`_stencil_clear` and found their shaders read **only** the no-index depth/stencil input — zero indexed subpass input anywhere else in the subpass. `Any` is `false` for exactly the draws that need the direct slots, so gating construction on it was backwards. Reverted that gate entirely; fix (1) alone (excluding the slots from the *scan*, not gating their *construction*) is sufficient and correct on its own.

The lesson here (echoing last session's own "A process note," now a fourth session in a row where this mattered): when a fix for a regression itself causes a *second* regression, don't assume the two problems are coupled and need one combined gate. They were actually two independent, narrow problems, each with its own narrow fix. Trying to solve both with one conditional was the wrong shape from the start.

## Verification

1. New unit test `DrawTest.SubpassLoadReadsBackTheDepthAttachmentItWroteWithNoIndex` — reproduces regression (2)'s exact shape (never calls `vkCmdSetRenderingInputAttachmentIndices`, so `Any` stays `false` throughout). Passes alongside all 6 pre-existing `*SubpassLoad*` tests.
2. `FeMeVulkanTests`: 804/804 Passed (+1 new test, 0 regressions, including the regression-1 case `DepthStencilResolveSkipsAspectResolveAttachmentDoesNotHave` now passing again).
3. `ninja check-feme`: 3,605/3,608 Passed, 3 Unsupported, 0 Failed, 0 regressions.
4. CTS `local_read` sub-family (182 cases, the originally-targeted family): 105 Passed, 0 Failed, 77 NotSupported (`shader_object`, expected — no `VK_EXT_shader_object`). All 12 originally-Fail cases now Pass.
5. **Full `dEQP-VK.renderpasses.dynamic_rendering.*` re-sweep (28,898 cases, ran most of this session in the background due to heavy MSAA sub-families being slow):** 12,423 Passed, **0 Failed**, 16,475 Not supported, 0 Warnings, 0 Waived. This is the whole family, not just the targeted sub-family — confirms the fix is completely clean with no collateral damage anywhere else in `dynamic_rendering.*`.
6. `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`: checked, no change needed — this is an internal correctness fix to already-advertised `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering_local_read` functionality, not a new feature/extension-surface addition.

## A performance note for future sessions (not a bug, just a heads-up)

The full 28,898-case sweep took noticeably longer this session than `L391`'s own equivalent full sweep last session — the `multisample_resolve.layers_3.*samples_8*` sub-family in particular is very heavy (likely large multi-layer MSAA framebuffers being resolved on a CPU rasterizer) and can take minutes to clear a handful of cases, making the sweep *look* stalled when checked at short intervals even though it's genuinely progressing (confirmed via repeated `ps aux` CPU-time increments and advancing case names in the tail log). At one point the process briefly showed as `sleeping` on a `futex_wait_queue` with zero case-count progress for ~500 seconds, and `ps -eLf` showed **1,125 threads** for the single `deqp-vk` process — this is unusually high and is worth a future session's attention as a possible thread-pool-reuse gap in the CPU renderer under heavy multi-layer-MSAA load, though it eventually resumed on its own and the sweep did complete cleanly. Not investigated further this session (no reproducer isolated, didn't want to scope-creep away from `L390`), but flagging it explicitly here in case a future session sees an actual hang in a similar case shape.
