amber source of the one passing "sibling" test
(`b10g11r11-ufloat-pack32-highp-output-vec2`, PASS) against the failing one
(`...-output-float`, FAIL). The **only** difference between them is:
output type `vec2 frag_out[3]` + `color_in[i].xy` (passes) vs. `float
frag_out[3]` + `color_in[i].x` (fails). Everything else — vertex data,
pipeline setup, reference comparison — is identical.

Then checked every other scalar-output-array case in the whole 28-case
group:
- `r32-sfloat-highp` (scalar `float color_in[3]` input, scalar output) — PASS.
- `r16g16-sfloat-highp-output-float` (2-component `vec2 color_in[3]` input,
  `.x`-extracted to scalar output) — PASS.
- `b10g11r11-ufloat-pack32-highp` (3-component `vec3 color_in[3]` input,
  **3-component** output, no truncation) — PASS.
- `b10g11r11-ufloat-pack32-{highp,mediump}-output-float` (3-component
  `vec3 color_in[3]` input, truncated via `.x` to **1-component** output) —
  the only 2 FAILs in the entire 28-case group.

So the bug needs **both**: (a) a 3-component (`vec3`) dynamically-indexed
stage-IO input array, AND (b) truncation down to a 1-component scalar
output via `.x` extraction. 2-component truncation (`.xy`) and no
truncation both work fine; `vec3`→scalar is the one broken combination.
`b10g11r11` just happens to be the only format in this CTS group whose test
variants happen to use a `vec3` input — the format itself is not special.

This means the actual bug almost certainly lives in SPIR-V→LLVM lowering
of the dynamic `AccessChain`/`CompositeExtract` sequence for a
multi-component row with a component sub-index, most likely in
`StageIOArrayAccessChainPattern` in `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` (the
`Input`-storage composite-array dynamic-index pattern) — not in
`Executor.cpp`, not in `ImageFixture.cpp`'s format pack/unpack, and not in
`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`'s row-shape computation (all three were checked
and ruled out this session).

### L418(a) sanity check — reconfirmed DONE, no action taken

`git log --oneline --all | grep -i L418` shows real landed commits:
`b5405d8ec4cd` (precompute per-triangle fixed-point edge coefficients),
`ca109ef7b051` (unit test for it), `80ddd348a27d` (docs updated). Several
sessions' "done" status is correct — this was not memory drift. No further
action needed; stop re-checking this every session unless something
actually touches L418 again.

## Win: `output_location` pair fixed (2 of `L419(j)`'s 7 cases)

shape).

control flow is a standalone compiler feature (structurizer/divergence-
analysis scale), not a quick fix — did not attempt it this session.

## Win: `primitive_id.matching` fixed (1 of `L419(j)`'s remaining 2 untriaged)

Root cause: `Executor.cpp` numbered a geometry shader's
`gl_PrimitiveIDIn` by a running count of assembled primitives,
unconditionally. Per spec, that's only correct without tessellation —
*with* tessellation, every primitive one patch's tessellation generates
must share that patch's own ordinal index instead.

Fix: thread the generating patch's own index through a new parallel
shadow-vector pipeline mirroring the existing index-only vectors —
`PatchPrimitiveIDs` → `TessTriPatchIDs`/`TessLinePatchIDs` →
`AbsTriPatchIDs`/`AbsLinePatchIDs` → `PrimitivePatchIDs` — used only when
tessellation feeds the `Lines`/`Triangles` geometry-input assembly
(`Points`/`*WithAdjacency`, which never combine with tessellation, are
untouched).

Verified:
- `dEQP-VK.geometry.builtin_variable.primitive_id.matching`: Fail → Pass.
- `dEQP-VK.geometry.*`: 191/200 Pass, 0 Fail (9 Not Supported) — no
  regressions.
- `dEQP-VK.tessellation.*`: 646/1114 Pass, 30 Fail (confirmed pre-existing
  `L419(g)`, not new), 438 Not Supported.
- `ninja check-feme`: 3,722/3,725 Passed, 0 Failed, 3 Unsupported (+1 new
  test vs. prior baseline).
- New unit test `ExecutorTest.GeometryStagePrimitiveIDInMatchesSourcePatchNotRunningEmitCount`
  — confirmed red (fails pre-fix) / green (passes post-fix) via a manual
  revert-and-rerun, not just a single passing run.

Commits: `369a4d7969e2` (fix + unit test), `e9c61c85e848` (doc sync).

# Session: Merged `origin/main` into `cbieneman/feme`, fixed 2 build regressions, CTS sanity-verified

**Device check:** `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed (required `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` export first — fresh shell had no env, bare `vulkaninfo` showed `llvmpipe`).

**Task:** fetch upstream LLVM `main`, merge/rebase onto it, run FeMe tests, fix regressions.

## What happened, in order

1. Tried `git rebase origin/main` first — 6,144 commits, hit a real conflict at commit 347/6144 in a shared non-FeMe file (`DXIL.td`). A full linear rebase of this scale isn't worth it. **Pivoted to `git merge origin/main --no-edit`** instead (2 prior precedents in this branch's own history for the same call).
2. Merge produced only **5 conflicted files**, all shared SPIR-V/MLIR infrastructure, **none under `feme/`**:
   - `llvm/include/llvm/IR/IntrinsicsSPIRV.td`
   - `llvm/lib/Target/SPIRV/SPIRVInstructionSelector.cpp`
   - `mlir/include/mlir/Dialect/SPIRV/IR/SPIRVBase.td`
   - `mlir/lib/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/SPIRVToLLVM.cpp`
   - `mlir/lib/Target/SPIRV/Deserialization/Deserializer.h`
3. Resolved all 5. The one needing real judgment: `SPIRVToLLVM.cpp`'s `MulExtendedPattern` — both branches had independently written it. Checked whether upstream's version would even compile against the merged file's helper functions (it wouldn't — FeMe had refactored `createIntegerConstant` to a 4-arg signature, upstream's new code still called the old 5-arg form). **Kept FeMe's version**, discarded upstream's duplicate. Everything else in that file (FeMe's `ModfPattern`/`FrexpPattern`) was a pure addition, kept as-is. Committed as merge commit `23e5d72c6b38`.
4. **Build regression 1**: `mlir-tblgen` rejected 4 `DXSAOps.td` ops (`DXSA_Operand`, `DXSA_OperandImm`, `DXSA_IndexImm`, `DXSA_IndexRelImm`) — upstream's new "Strict Property Assembly Formats" rule requires every inherent attribute to be bound by name or covered by `prop-dict` in the `assemblyFormat`. Fixed by adding `prop-dict` (and `attr-dict`, which the verifier requires unconditionally alongside it — found this the hard way, first fix attempt produced a new error). This changes the *printed* syntax from `{imm = 0 : i32}` to `<imm = 0 : i32>` — cosmetic only, no IR semantics change. Committed in `0e02a7821173`.
5. **Build regression 2**: `AtomicLoadPattern` (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`) failed to compile — upstream added a new `isNoundef` bool parameter to `LLVM::LoadOp::create`'s convenience overload. Added `/*isNoundef=*/false` at the right position. Committed in `5ec7f932f921`.
6. Both fixes broke exactly 2 existing tests (`atomics.dxasm`, `interface1.dxasm`), purely because their `CHECK:` lines hard-coded the old brace-dict print syntax. Regenerated the real new output (`dxbc-as ... | feme-translate --import-dxsa-bin -`) and updated both files to match exactly. Included in the same commit as the `DXSAOps.td` fix (fix + its own test-sync, one coherent unit).
7. **`ninja check-feme`: 3,722/3,722 applicable tests Passed** (3 Unsupported, 0 Failed) — full green after the fixes.
8. **CTS sanity run** (not a full 3.25M-case re-triage — no behavior change was expected from either fix, so a full re-triage would just re-confirm the existing baseline at large time cost): ran every `dEQP-VK.{geometry,tessellation,rasterization,info}.*` case plus every case with `atomic` in its name (43,764 cases, chosen to cover both recently-active areas and the specific `AtomicLoadPattern` code path) via `feme/utils/run_vulkan_cts.py`. Result: **87 Fail, 2,940 Pass, 40,737 NotSupported, 0 DeviceLost/TimedOut**. Cross-referenced every failure against `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s existing baseline — **all 87 are pre-existing and already triaged** (30 tessellation-invariance `L419(g)`, 2 line_continuity `L419(j)`, 1 mandatory_features `L419(j)`/`D1`, 52 memory_model matching the documented baseline row, 2 terminate_invocation part of the documented 528-case `spirv_assembly` baseline). **Zero new regressions.** Documented in `VulkanCTSReport.md`, committed in `916362a4a861`.
9. Checked the offload-test-suite `VkBool32`/`WaveActiveMax` pattern per standing instruction: current local checkout (`main`, HEAD `2e72553`) already has both the FeMe-test-target cherry-pick (`9af8bce`) and the `VkBool32` fix (`2e72553`) applied on top — not silently dropped this time. No `check-hlsl-feme-vk` work done this session, so this was just a precautionary check, not exercised against a real discrepancy.
10. Inventories (`Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`): confirmed via grep, no changes needed — this was a merge/build-fix session, no feature/extension-surface change.

# Session: K6c -- shaderDrawParameters / gl_DrawID fix

**Task:** continue `K6a`'s bundle, picking `shaderDrawParameters` per the last session's "likely-cheap" flag.

## What happened, in order

1. Mandatory device check: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.
2. Traced the full pipeline: `CanonicalizeStage.cpp` maps `BaseVertex`/`BaseInstance`/`DrawIndex` builtin IDs correctly; `VertexWrapper.cpp`'s `loadVertexSystemValue` has real, working cases for all three. So far so "nearly free," as the roadmap claimed.
3. **Found the roadmap's claim was wrong**: `Executor.cpp` set `Inv.BaseVertex`/`Inv.BaseInstance` from real per-draw command fields, but hardcoded `Inv.DrawID = 0` always. Root cause: `feme::graphics::DrawCommand` (the vertex-pipeline draw struct) had no `DrawID` field at all -- unlike its mesh-pipeline sibling `MeshDrawCommand`, which already had one, working, for `vkCmdDrawMeshTasksIndirectEXT`. A real, 1/3 gap in a combined feature bit, not a pure advertisement fix.
4. Fixed it: added `DrawCommand::DrawID`, set it from `CommandBuffer.cpp`'s `readIndirectDraws` per-draw loop index `I`, threaded it into `Executor.cpp` instead of the hardcoded 0. Direct (non-indirect) draws needed no change -- the field's default `0` already matches `gl_DrawID`'s spec value for those.

# Session: `K6g` closed -- `samplerFilterMinmax` real min/max reduction math implemented

Device check: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed (twice -- re-checked after context compaction mid-session too, per standing instruction).

## What happened

Picked `samplerFilterMinmax` as the smallest of `K6a`'s 4 remaining real-implementation bits (prior session's recommendation). Unlike `K6b`-`K6f`'s pure advertisement gaps, this one needed actual math:

1. **CTS coverage was hiding.** A broad/exact mustpass grep for `filter_minmax`/`minmax` found nothing. Turned out this checkout's static mustpass `.txt` files **exclude the entire `sampler.view_type.*.{mag,min}_reduce` test area** -- confirmed by dumping `deqp-vk`'s full live case list (`--deqp-runmode=stdout-caselist`) instead of trusting mustpass. **Lesson banked for future sessions: when a mustpass grep comes up empty, cross-check the live case dump before concluding "no CTS coverage."**
2. **Implemented the real math** in `FeMeRuntimeCPU.c`: two new `femeRTv4f32Min`/`femeRTv4f32Max` helpers, threaded `ReductionMode`-conditional branching into every bilinear/trilinear/cube-seamless blend site (2D/1D/3D/cube, single-level and mip-blend variants). Depth-comparison paths left untouched (spec forbids combining with filterMinmax).
3. **Wired the Vulkan layer**: `Image.cpp`'s `Sampler` constructor now parses a chained `VkSamplerReductionModeCreateInfo` from `pNext`.
4. **Advertised it**: `Format.cpp` now sets `FILTER_MINMAX_BIT` wherever `FILTER_LINEAR_BIT` is set; `EntryPoints.cpp` flips the feature bit and both properties structs to `VK_TRUE`; `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp` adds the extension name.
5. **Caught and fixed a real regression along the way**: the initial `Format.cpp` rule (minmax bit follows linear bit) missed `D16_UNORM`/`D32_FLOAT` -- the spec's mandatory-minmax-format table requires these two single-component depth formats to support `FILTER_MINMAX_BIT` *independent* of `FILTER_LINEAR_BIT` (reduction only needs multiple taps, not real bilinear interpolation). Caught by a genuine `dEQP-VK.api.info.format_properties.d16_unorm` failure, not by inspection -- fixed directly in each format's switch case.
6. **Found and fixed a pre-existing doc-sync gap unrelated to this session's own change**: `AdvertisedPromotedExtensions.txt` was missing the `K6e`/`K6f` rows entirely, despite both being implemented, advertised, and tested (confirmed via `DrawTest.cpp`'s existing assertions and `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp`'s own code comments). Backfilled both rows using their `PhysicalDeviceInfo.cpp` comment wording, alongside adding the new `K6g` row -- noted as a prior-session gap, not misattributed as new work.

# Session: `K6i` closed -- `scalarBlockLayout` implemented via 3 struct-layout bug fixes

## What happened

Picked `scalarBlockLayout` per the prior session's recommendation -- `K6a`'s last 2 bits said to start from `getNaturalAlignmentIgnoringPacking` relaxation, not re-trace from scratch.

1. **Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` (standing instruction, every session).
2. **Generalized the existing single-level tight-array substitution** (`getTightVectorArrayType`/`getTightMatrixType`, used to represent a vector/matrix member at a scalar-tight offset below its natural SIMD alignment) to arbitrary nesting depth via a new recursive helper, `getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsOrMatricesType`.
3. **Bug #1**: the struct-member-building loop's plain type-conversion call had no retry for a single-level tight array, aborting the whole struct. Fixed via fallback to the new helper (also wired into `rewriteBlockAccess`'s standalone conversion call).
4. **Bug #2**: `layOutStructIfOffsetsMatch`'s alignment-overshoot pre-check unconditionally rejected a member placed below its own natural alignment, even in the packed-struct `AllowInteriorPad` retry tier that never actually needs that alignment. Found a real bug anyway: the rewritten array-peeling retry tier matched **bare, non-array** vector/matrix members too (peeling zero levels is a no-op), turning a should-be "skip, not applicable" into a hard failure. Bisected via a unit-test regression (`OutOfOrderOffsetInterfaceBlockLegalizes`) plus targeted `llvm::errs()` traces -- numbered-tag `notifyMatchFailure` suffixes pinpoint *which* branch fires, but raw value prints were what actually cracked this one. Fixed with an explicit "is this really an array" guard before peeling.
6. **Flipped `scalarBlockLayout` to `VK_TRUE`** in `EntryPoints.cpp`, updated the one unit test whose hardcoded expectation this flip broke (`PreVulkan12PromotionDedicatedFeatureStructsAreFullyOverwritten`), added 2 new lit tests for bugs #1/#2 (bug #3's regression guard is the pre-existing unit test above, kept as-is).

# Session: `K6j` closed -- nested-struct scalar-layout gap fixed, found new `K6k` SSBO bug

## What happened

Picked `K6j` per the prior session's recommendation (the 25-case `single_nested_struct`/`random.scalar.83` residual left over from `K6i`).

1. **Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` (standing instruction, every session).
2. **Built a minimal, isolated `feme-opt`-only MLIR reproducer**, bisected down from the real CTS struct shape to a 2-member struct: a nested, explicitly-offset struct member (itself containing a scalar-tight array-of-`mat3x3` member) immediately followed by a plain vector member, with no interior gap needed at all. Far faster to iterate on than re-running CTS each time -- instant pass/fail plus full error text.
3. **Traced via `--debug-only=dialect-conversion` twice**: once on the failing `spirv.AccessChain` (found it falls through every pattern, including `BlockAccessChainPattern`, to "no matched legalization pattern"), then on the `addressof` op that builds the resource handle -- found the handle intrinsic's result type was a degenerate `!llvm.ptr<12>` instead of a typed `VulkanBuffer` handle, meaning the *whole outer struct's own type conversion* silently returned null.
4. **Root cause**: `getTightNestedStructType` (the "tight" nested-struct re-conversion `convertOffsetStructTypeIgnoringDecorations`'s `VectorOnly` retry tier calls) had neither of that caller's own two safeguards for a scalar-tight array-of-matrix member: no fallback to `getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsOrMatricesType` when the ordinary array conversion fails outright, and no `substituteArrayOfMatrixElementType` correction for the sneakier case where it does *not* fail but silently substitutes the wrong (natural, too-wide) layout instead. Added debug `llvm::errs()` prints (same proven-effective technique as last session) to pin down exactly which of the two was happening -- it was the second, sneakier one: the matrix-array member "succeeded" with the wrong type, so the outer struct's offset-matching for the member after it never lined up.
5. **Fixed** by applying both of those safeguards inside `getTightNestedStructType`'s own array-member branch, removed the debug prints, added a new lit test mirroring the exact CTS struct shape.
6. **Ran a broader `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` regression sweep** (12,225 cases, since the fixed function is shared between UBO and SSBO conversion) and found 62 failures. Used `git stash` to rebuild the pre-fix `libfeme_vulkan.so` and re-ran just those 62 cases against it -- confirmed all 62 already failed at baseline, so **not** a regression from this fix. Tracked as new roadmap row `K6k` (a separate `RowMajor`-matrix SSBO `*_store_cols` bug, not yet grep-traced).

## CTS results

- `dEQP-VK.ubo.single_nested_struct.*`/`random.scalar.83` (145 cases): **145 Pass, 0 Fail**.
- Full `dEQP-VK.ubo.*` regression sweep (13,240 cases): **8,318 Pass, 0 Fail, 4,922 NotSupported** -- the prior session's 25 residual failures all closed, zero regressions (8,293 + 25 = 8,318, exact accounting).
- `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` regression sweep (12,225 cases): 4,687 Pass, 67 Fail (62 distinct), 7,471 NotSupported -- confirmed pre-existing via baseline re-run, new `K6k` row opened, not fixed this session.
- `ninja check-feme`: 3,731/3,734 Passed, 0 Failed, 3 Unsupported (pre-existing, unrelated); 1 new lit test added.

## Commits (2, plus this file)

1. `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`'s fix + new lit test.
2. Doc sync (`Roadmap.md`: `K6j` struck through, new `K6k` added; `VulkanCTSReport.md`: new section).

No `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md` changes needed -- `scalarBlockLayout` was already advertised as of `K6i`; this was a pure bug fix, not a feature-bit flip.

## Lesson worth repeating

"The conversion returned null" and "the conversion returned the wrong thing" are different bugs needing different fixes, and a function can have a safeguard for one but not the other. `getTightNestedStructType`'s array-member branch already *looked* like it had the right fallback (`if (!MemberTy) MemberTy = getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsOrMatricesType(...)`), and that fix alone built cleanly and even "improved" the reproducer's error output -- but the real failure mode here was the conversion silently succeeding with a wrong type, which no null-check will ever catch. Only `llvm::errs()`-printing the actual resulting LLVM type (not just pass/fail) surfaced the mismatch. When a null-guarded fallback doesn't fix a bug, check whether the guarded call is actually failing at all, or silently succeeding wrong.

# Session: K6k `RowMajor`-matrix SSBO column store/load fixed

**Fixed `K6k`.** `dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.single_basic_array.scalar.row_major_mat2_store_cols` and 53 sibling `2_level_array`/`3_level_array` cases now pass. 3 commits: regression test, fix, docs.

## What was broken

`buffer Block { float padding; mat2 var[3]; }` (SSBO, `RowMajor`) -- writing one column of `var[i]` silently wrote the wrong bytes, ignoring which column was requested. Not a crash, not a compile error: just wrong numbers. 62 CTS cases failed this way.

## Root cause

`getMatrixColumnAccess` in `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` only recognized a struct member that IS the matrix directly (`[member, colIdx]` -- 2 indices). It didn't know a member could be an *array* of matrices (`[member, elemIdx, colIdx]` -- 3 indices). When it declined to match, the access chain fell through to a different code path that doesn't understand `RowMajor` at all, and silently dropped the column index.

## How it was found (useful lesson, read this before guessing at MLIR reproducers again)

Two hand-written MLIR reproducers this session built from guesses at the shape both converted *correctly* -- a false "nothing's wrong here" signal that nearly derailed the investigation. The actual bug only showed up once the REAL SPIR-V was pulled straight from the CTS `.qpa` log's `<SpirVAssemblySource>` section (every `deqp-vk` run writes one). That log also had the GLSL source, which is how the `float padding;` member (shifting the matrix to struct index 1, not 0) was found -- a detail no amount of guessing reproduced.

**Takeaway for next time:** when debugging an SPIRVToLLVM lowering bug against a specific CTS case, pull the real `.qpa` log's `<SpirVAssemblySource>`/`<ShaderSource>` FIRST. Don't hand-write an MLIR guess until the guess is confirmed to match the real shape byte-for-byte (struct member order, decoration values, everything). A guess that "looks right" and compiles cleanly proves nothing.

## The fix

Peel through the member's own array levels (any number of them, so `2_level_array`/`3_level_array` are covered by the same code) before requiring the innermost type to be the matrix, consuming one more `AccessChain` index per level. ~20 lines, `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`.

One bug while writing the fix: moved a bounds check (`Op.getIndices().size() != MemberSelectorPos + 2`) earlier in the function without noticing a different, unrelated shape (`RWStructuredBuffer<Doggo>`-style whole-struct array element access) relied on indexing past that same bound and crashed on `ninja check-feme`. Caught immediately because check-feme is cheap to run after every change -- fixed with a one-line early-return guard.

## Verified

1. New lit test fails without the fix (`git stash` + rebuild), passes with it.
2. `ninja check-feme`: 3,732/3,735 pass (3 unsupported, pre-existing).
3. Full `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` sweep (12,225 cases): 4,687 -> 4,741 Pass, 67 -> 13 Fail. The 13 remaining failures (9 `random.scalar.*` + 4 `3_level_unsized_array.scalar.{bvec3,ivec3,uvec3,vec3}`) are confirmed **pre-existing** -- same failure on a before/after rebuild -- and unrelated to this fix's shape. Split off as new roadmap row `K6l`.

## Where `K6a` stands now

Still just `variablePointers`. Untouched again this session (picked `K6k` instead, per the prior session's own suggestion).

Pull each failing case's real SPIR-V from its `.qpa` log first (see lesson above) before guessing at the shape.
2. **(~half day, separate bug class)** `K6l`'s other residual: `random.scalar.41` plus 4 `3_level_unsized_array.scalar.*` cases fail with a *legalization* error (not a result mismatch) on a plain `vector<3x*>` member (no matrix involved) reached through a multiply-nested `rtarray`-of-`array`. Not yet triaged at all -- worth its own roadmap row once looked at, since it's unrelated to `RowMajor` matrices.
3. **(~1-2 days)** `variablePointers` is `K6a`'s only remaining bit. Start from the prior investigation's exact failure list (`PtrAccessChain` "explicitly marked illegal", unhandled `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`, `OpConstantNull` on pointer types).

# Session: K6l fixed (scalar-layout `RuntimeArrayType`-of-vector stride bug)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`** at session start, per standing instructions.

## What now works

`dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.random.scalar.{3,11,15,20,49,60,61,88}` (8 of K6l's 9 bundled cases) now pass. Full `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` sweep: 4,741 -> 4,749 Pass, 13 -> 5 Fail. `ninja check-feme`: 3,733/3,736 pass, 0 fail, 1 new lit test.

## The bug, in one paragraph

A trailing runtime-sized array of a bare 3-component vector (`vec3 d[]`) under scalar/tight layout (`-fvk-use-scalar-layout`) declares an `ArrayStride` of 12 bytes. But MLIR always reports a `vector<3xf32>`'s own DataLayout size as 16 bytes (rounds lane count up to the next power of two for SIMD-register reasons). The existing stride-mismatch-repair code in `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`'s `RuntimeArrayType` conversion only handled the *opposite* direction (stride wider than natural size, the ordinary std430 case) -- never this narrower-than-natural-size direction, which only scalar layout produces. Every array read silently computed the wrong byte offset.

## The real lesson this session re-learned (again)

1. The original roadmap guess for K6l ("8 of 9 cases are deeper `RowMajor` matrix nesting") was wrong. Don't trust a prior session's root-cause theory for an un-triaged case -- pull the real SPIR-V from the `.qpa` log and look.
2. Hand-reconstructing SPIR-V text from a `.qpa` log and round-tripping it through `spirv-as`/`mlir-translate`/`feme-opt` as *separate processes* hit two real-but-irrelevant MLIR SPIR-V-dialect parser/verifier quirks (`OpIAdd` signed/unsigned mismatch) that look exactly like the bug under investigation but aren't. `feme-translate --import-spirv-skip-verify` exists precisely to route around the first one; a hand-crafted minimal reproducer routes around the second (text re-parsing re-triggers a stricter check than the original in-memory op had).
3. The most reliable way to get the *authentic* SPIR-V a CTS case uses: a temporary `getenv`-gated dump of `pCode` bytes in `Pipeline.cpp`'s `copyShaderModuleWords`, rebuild just `libfeme_vulkan.so`, re-run with the env var set. Fast, byte-exact, no reconstruction-fidelity risk. (Reverted before committing, as always.)

Pull real SPIR-V from `.qpa` logs first, same lesson as above.
2. **(~1-2 days)** `variablePointers` is `K6a`'s only remaining bit. Start from the prior investigation's exact failure list (`PtrAccessChain` "explicitly marked illegal", unhandled `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`, `OpConstantNull` on pointer types).

# Session: K6m fixed (`RuntimeArrayType`-of-`array`-of-vector legalization bug)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`** at session start, per standing instructions.

## What now works

All 5 K6m cases pass: `dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.random.scalar.41` and `dEQP-VK.ssbo.layout.3_level_unsized_array.scalar.{bvec3,ivec3,uvec3,vec3}`. Full `dEQP-VK.ssbo.*` sweep: 4,749 -> 4,754 Pass, 5 -> 0 Fail. `ninja check-feme`: 3,730/3,737 pass, 0 fail, 1 new lit test.

## The bug, in one paragraph

`.41`'s real shape (confirmed via authentic SPIR-V dump): a trailing member `rtarray<array<2 x vector<3xsi32>, stride=12>, stride=24>` -- a runtime array whose element is itself a fixed array of a bare vector, one level deeper than K6l's direct `rtarray<vector>` shape. `convertArrayTypeIgnoringDecorations` (the plain `spirv::ArrayType` conversion) unconditionally returns null when a declared stride is narrower than a vector's natural size, instead of substituting a tight marker. That null propagates up through `RuntimeArrayType`'s own conversion, aborting the whole `AccessChain`'s legalization. The existing retry path for this mismatch (`getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsOrMatricesType`) needs a `Struct`/`Index` for matrix decorations and only accepts a top-level `spirv::ArrayType`, not `RuntimeArrayType` -- so it could never help here. Fixed by adding a decoration-free sibling helper and retrying through it inside the `RuntimeArrayType` conversion lambda.

## Process notes

1. Same "authentic SPIR-V dump" technique as K6l (temporary `FEME_DEBUG_DUMP_SPIRV_DIR` hook in `Pipeline.cpp`, reverted before commit) -- still the fastest, most reliable way to get a CTS case's real shader bytes.
2. Same text-round-trip artifact as before (`feme-translate`/`feme-opt` as separate processes re-triggers a harmless `OpIAdd` parser quirk) -- worked around with a hand-crafted minimal MLIR reproducer instead, same as last session.
3. One fix (the decoration-free `getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsType` retry) closed all 5 bundled cases in one shot -- the roadmap's own guess that the 4 `3_level_unsized_array` cases shared K6m's root cause one level deeper was correct, confirmed empirically rather than assumed.
4. Did not need to touch `getTightNestedArrayOfVectorsOrMatricesType` itself or `rewriteBlockAccess` -- fixing the `RuntimeArrayType` conversion lambda's own retry was sufficient; the recursive `TypeConverter.convertType` call inside it is what needed the extra fallback, not any of its callers.

## Next steps

1. **(~1-2 days)** `variablePointers` is `K6a`'s only remaining bit. # Session: K6a `PtrAccessChain`/`InBoundsPtrAccessChain` lowering added (296 -> 152 Fail)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`** at session start, per standing instructions.

## What now works

The entire 156-case `spirv.PtrAccessChain`/`spirv.InBoundsPtrAccessChain` legalization-failure cluster is closed -- 0 of the remaining 152 `variable_pointer` CTS failures are a `PtrAccessChain`/`AccessChain` legalization error. Full `variable_pointer` sweep (4464 cases, feature bits temporarily flipped for the sweep only): 296 Fail/676 Pass -> 152 Fail/820 Pass, 0 new failures. `ninja check-feme`: 3731/3731 pass, 0 fail, 7 unsupported (pre-existing).

## The bug, in one paragraph

Neither feme nor upstream MLIR had ever had a conversion pattern for `spirv.PtrAccessChain`/`spirv.InBoundsPtrAccessChain`. Per the op's own `build`/`verify` (`getElementPtrType` call, which never looks at `element`), the op's result type always equals plain `AccessChain`'s with the same trailing indices -- `element` only shifts the base address by `element` whole pointee-sized units first. Two shapes cover all 156 real cases: (1) `element` is compile-time-constant-zero (just a plain `AccessChain` in disguise), (2) `element` is dynamic/non-zero (real pointer arithmetic, needs a GEP shift first). A 3rd combination -- non-zero/dynamic `element` *and* real trailing indices together -- looked unneeded from an initial ~10-case sample, but a post-fix full bucketing run found 24 real cases needing it (the `opptraccesschain_float_*` family, stepping to a vector lane then selecting a component within it).

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **`FEME_VULKAN_LOG_CREATION_ERRORS` already existed** (`Diagnostics.cpp`) and would have saved several prior sessions' worth of ad-hoc debug-dump-hook effort triaging silent `VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED` failures. Check for an existing diagnostics knob before building a new one.
2. **A representative sample is not a proof.** The first ~10-case sample across every `opptraccesschain_*` sub-family missed a real combination (non-zero element + indices) that a full 296-case signature bucketing run later caught. Bucket the *entire* failure set by exact error signature before declaring a fix "covers everything" -- a partial fix that silently declines an untested shape looks identical to a complete one until the next full sweep.
3. **Re-expressing a newly created op as *another* new, still-illegal op for the dialect conversion driver to reprocess doesn't always converge**, even though it's a precedented, working idiom elsewhere in this file for a single level of re-expression. Chaining two levels (new `PtrAccessChain` -> new `AccessChain` over its result) failed silently: the second op's legalization attempt ran before the first had converted, its failure was never retried, and the whole rewrite rolled back to report the *original* op as unlegalizable -- a confusing symptom that looks exactly like "the pattern never matched at all." A direct, single-pattern GEP chain sidesteps the ordering hazard entirely. Worth remembering before reaching for "just create another SPIR-V op and let the framework handle it" again.
4. **A minimal MLIR reproducer isolates compiler bugs far faster than full CTS cycles.** Once the real SPIR-V shape was known (via the error message's own printed operand/type info, no dump hook needed this time), a 20-line hand-written `spirv.module` reproducer and `feme-opt --feme-convert-spirv-to-llvm` let me debug the ordering hazard above in minutes rather than re-running `deqp-vk` each iteration.

1. **(~1-2 days, new this session)** `K6n`: 124 cases, CPU-backend resource-handle-normalization architectural limitation (`"unsupported raised operation: ... register-bound resource handle ..."`). Not yet root-caused beyond signature-level bucketing -- likely the deepest, hardest-to-fix piece of the whole `variablePointers` feature, possibly needing a runtime dispatch mechanism rather than a lowering-pattern fix. Worth its own investigation session before committing to an approach.
2. **(~half day, new this session, "issue outside FeMe")** `K6o`: 16 cases, upstream-MLIR `OpConstantNull`-on-pointer-type deserializer gap (`getNullAttrForType` has no pointer-type case). Larger than `K6o`: needs new TableGen op definitions, deserializer cases, and likely a `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` lowering once the ops exist, before feme can even see a shader using them. Not yet attempted.

# Session: K6o fixed (`OpConstantNull`-on-pointer-type upstream-MLIR deserializer gap)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`** at session start, per standing instructions. Note: this requires `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/home/dev/dev/llvm-project/build/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json` to be exported first -- without it `vulkaninfo` silently falls back to `llvmpipe`. Future sessions: export this before the mandatory check, every time.

## What now works

A `spirv.module` containing `OpConstantNull %ptr_type` now deserializes, verifies, serializes, and lowers to LLVM (`llvm.mlir.zero`) correctly, round-tripping through both the MLIR textual form and real SPIR-V binary. Full `variable_pointer` CTS mustpass sweep (4459 cases, feature bits temporarily flipped for the sweep only): 152 Fail -> **140 Fail/3489 NotSupported/830 Pass**, with the `OpConstantNull`-on-pointer error signature confirmed entirely absent from all remaining failures -- the whole 16-case bucket closed, 0 regressions. `ninja check-feme`: 3731/3731 pass, unchanged. A targeted `mlir/test/{Target/SPIRV,Dialect/SPIRV/IR,Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM}` lit sweep (149 tests) found only 2 pre-existing, unrelated failures, confirmed via `git stash` to fail identically without this fix.

## The bug, in one paragraph

This was an **upstream-MLIR** gap (not feme-local), per the standing "issue outside FeMe" instruction: the SPIR-V deserializer's `getNullAttrForType` (`Deserializer.cpp`) handled every constant-null case except pointer types, falling through to `nullptr`. Fixed by representing a null pointer as a `spirv.Constant` with a `UnitAttr` value (there's no payload to store), threading that choice through all four places a constant must flow: the deserializer (produce the attr), `SPIRVOps.cpp`'s verifier/printer (accept + round-trip it), the serializer (`Serializer.cpp`, emit it back out as a fresh `OpConstantNull`, explicitly *not* deduplicated via the normal `constIDMap` path), and `SPIRVToLLVM.cpp` (lower it to `llvm.mlir.zero`). feme itself needed zero code changes since its own lowering file already calls upstream's pattern-population function.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **`constIDMap` is keyed purely by `Attribute`, not `(Attribute, Type)`.** A `UnitAttr::get(ctx)` is a single per-context singleton -- if I'd deduplicated it the same way every other constant kind does, two *different* pointer types' null constants would have aliased onto the same serialized `<id>`, a subtle correctness bug that wouldn't show up until a shader actually used two different null-pointer types together. Caught this by reasoning through the dedup path before writing the serializer code, not by hitting the bug. Worth remembering for any future "sentinel/marker value with no real type-specific payload" case.
2. **Print and parse are not automatically symmetric** for a custom op's assembly format. `ConstantOp::print` only appended `: type` for array/struct results; a `UnitAttr` value doesn't carry its own type (it's not a `TypedAttr`), so it printed with no type at all and silently failed to reparse. Caught via the new round-trip lit test actually failing on first attempt -- exactly why that test exists.
3. **`check-feme`'s ninja graph doesn't rebuild `mlir-opt`/`mlir-translate`** even when the MLIR libraries they link change. A stale-binary test failure masqueraded as a real regression until I noticed the error text didn't match my new code. Always `ninja mlir-opt mlir-translate` directly after touching core MLIR dialect/conversion code, before trusting a direct lit-test run.
4. **Full lit directory sweep > single new test file.** Running just the 1 new/updated test files would have missed nothing this time, but running the full `Target/SPIRV`+`Dialect/SPIRV/IR`+`Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM` sweep (149 tests) is what actually proved `verifyConstantType`/`ConstantOp::print` -- both shared, heavily-used functions -- didn't regress anything else. Worth the extra 2 minutes every time a shared verifier/printer changes.

Still not root-caused beyond signature-level bucketing -- likely the deepest, hardest-to-fix piece of the whole `variablePointers` feature, possibly needing a runtime dispatch mechanism rather than a lowering-pattern fix. The largest remaining bucket; worth its own investigation session before committing to an approach.

Needs new TableGen op definitions, deserializer cases, and likely a `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` lowering once the ops exist. Not yet attempted; larger effort than K6o's single-function fix since it needs new ops, not just a gap in an existing one.
3. **(standing, unresolved many sessions)** `backup-before-rebase-20261014` tag decision, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` vs `Release` decision -- neither revisited this session either.

# Session: K6n fixed (phi/select-merged resource pointers, 116/140 of cached fail-list passes)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`** at session start, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first (same standing requirement as every prior session). This session resumed a prior session's `git stash` -- found with `git stash list`, popped cleanly, picked up exactly where it left off.

## What now works

`feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp` now lowers a `variablePointers` shader that merges two resource pointers with `OpPhi`/`OpSelect` before a load/store -- previously this unconditionally failed as "unsupported raised operation ... register-bound resource handle the FeMe CPU target cannot normalize." Both same-handle (different index into one binding) and cross-handle (two different bindings) merges work, as does a null-check idiom (`phi [real_ptr], [null]`). CTS: the prior session's own cached 140-case fail-list, re-run from the correct CTS data directory (not a scratch dir), now has **116/140 passing (82.9%)**, up from 0.

## The bug, in one paragraph

`hasOnlySupportedPointerUses` only ever accepted a `GetElementPtrInst` as a valid continuation of a resource-handle pointer chain -- any `PHINode`/`SelectInst` consumer caused the whole handle to be rejected outright. Fixed by teaching it to accept those two instruction kinds too, recursing into the merge point's own downstream users, backed by a new `PointerMergeMap` (shared per-function, so it can span two separate `BoundHandle`s' own `lowerAccesses` calls for a cross-binding merge) that accumulates each incoming leg's `(DescriptorIndex, Offset)` and lazily builds a matching side-car phi/select once every leg has reported in.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **Poison consumed operands immediately, not eventually.** The first working version crashed on the very first real CTS case (`UNREACHABLE ... Use still stuck around after Def is destroyed`). Cause: `mergeIntoPhi`/`mergeIntoSelect` captured a leg's value into the new merge state but left the *original* phi/select's own reference to that leg dangling until some later pass finished rewriting it -- so when the caller erased the leg's now-fully-consumed instruction, the not-yet-finished original still pointed at dead IR. Fix: `PoisonValue::get(...)` the original's own operand the instant it's consumed, not when the whole merge finishes. General IR-rewriting lesson, not SPIR-V-specific -- worth remembering any time new IR is synthesized to replace use of an *existing*, still-alive instruction's operand rather than replacing the whole instruction atomically.
2. **`PHINode::incoming_values()` yields `Use&`, not `Value&`.** A lambda passed to `llvm::any_of`/`llvm::none_of` over this range needs `const Use &` and `.get()`. One-line fix, but would have silently failed to compile with a confusing template error without checking the actual range type first.
3. **Run the full cached fail-list from the CTS's own data directory, not a scratch dir.** Running from `/tmp/k6n_test` last session mis-reported 14 real cases as `ResourceError` (missing `.amber` files) rather than their true pass/fail outcome. This session re-ran from `/home/dev/dev/VK-GL-CTS/build/external/vulkancts/modules/vulkan` instead and got the real number (116/140, not 116/126) -- the 14 "missing" cases turned out to be real, in-scope-for-a-different-bucket (`K6p`) failures, not noise.
3. **A `git stash` left from a stalled session is often further along than it looks.** `git stash list` + `git stash pop` recovered ~90% of this session's eventual fix with zero conflicts -- re-deriving it from scratch would have cost most of a session on its own.

## Next steps

1. **(~1-2 days)** `K6q`: 2 cases, handle-level `OpPhi`/`OpSelect` merge (merging raw resource *handles* before `getpointer` is called, not pointers already derived from one). Deeper and architecturally distinct from this session's fix -- `hasOnlySupportedUses` (the handle-level checker) would need the `DescriptorIndex` itself to become phi-mergeable before any GEP/offset is known. Smallest case count of the three new buckets but possibly the hardest.
2. **(~half day)** `K6r`: 2 cases, storing a handle-derived pointer as a store's *value* operand (not its pointer operand) -- `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses` only checks the pointer-operand position today. Likely the smallest, most contained of the three new buckets -- good first pick for a fast win.
3. **(~1 day)** `K6s`: 5 cases, frag/tessc/tesse result-correctness bug -- pipeline builds and runs, output is wrong, zero normalization rejection. Needs its own investigation (not a legalization gap at all); start with a minimal single-buffer frag repro and CPU-backend tracing.
4. **(~1-2 days, "issue outside FeMe", standing)** `K6p`: 14-15 cases, `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`/`OpPtrDiff` (opcodes 401/402/403) entirely undefined in MLIR's SPIR-V dialect TableGen. Not attempted again this session (scope stayed on `K6n`).
5. **(standing, unresolved many sessions)** `backup-before-rebase-20261014` tag decision, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` vs `Release` decision.
6. **(standing)** `L419(j)` remaining untriaged items, `L418(a)` sanity re-check, deferred full `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/extension-manifest regeneration.

# Session: K6r fixed (pointer stored through a private global, loaded in another function)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` at session start, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first. Checked `git stash list`/`git log`/`git status` per the user's "last session stalled out" note: both existing stashes are stale, already-merged leftovers from older sessions (not this one) -- confirmed via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, neither popped.

## What now works

Both `dEQP-VK.spirv_assembly.instruction.graphics.variable_pointers.graphics.stores_private_single_buffer_tessc` and `...stores_private_two_buffers_tessc` now pass. A handle-derived (possibly `select`/`phi`-merged, roadmap K6n) pointer stored through an ordinary `Private`-storage global in one function and loaded back in a *different* function -- the shape a tessellation-control shader's barrier split produces -- now lowers correctly instead of failing pipeline creation. Full `variable_pointers` instruction-group re-run (1637 cases): 942 Pass/7 Fail, neither of this bucket's 2 cases among the remaining 7 (which are `K6s`/`K6q`/the known `feme-cpu-simdize` case). `ninja check-feme`: 3736/3743 pass, 7 unsupported, unchanged -- no regressions.

## The bug, in one paragraph

A tessellation-control shader with a group-sync barrier gets split by `splitTessellationControlEntry` (`CanonicalizeStage.cpp`) into two real, separately-dispatched LLVM functions: `main` (control-point phase) and `main.patchconstant` (patch-constant phase). A value computed before the barrier and read back after it has no SSA value that can cross that real function boundary, so it's threaded through an ordinary module-scope `Private` global instead. When that value is itself a handle-derived pointer, `LocalizePrivateGlobalsPass` correctly declines to localize the global (it's genuinely used by two functions), and `SPIRVResourceLoweringPass`'s `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses` then rejected the store outright ("store where pointer is not the operand", since the pointer is the store's *value* operand, not its *pointer* operand). Fixed by teaching it to recognize this shape and adding `lowerPointerMergeGlobalStore`, which replaces the pointer global with two new scalar globals (`i32` descriptor index, `i64` byte offset) and continues the existing phi/select-merge lowering machinery from each load's own result.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **"Isolated pass sequence works, real pipeline doesn't" was a false lead, not a pipeline-ordering bug.** I spent roughly half the session chasing why `LocalizePrivateGlobalsPass`+`SROA`+`mem2reg`, re-run in isolation on IR extracted verbatim from the real failing case, eliminated the problematic global cleanly -- while the real pipeline left it behind. The actual answer: my manual extraction only pulled out *one* function's worth of IR (the `main` stage), silently dropping the `main.patchconstant` function that also used the global. The isolated test was testing a different (single-function) problem than the real pipeline was solving. **Lesson: when an isolated repro "works" but the real system doesn't, check whether the repro captured the whole problem, including other functions/modules sharing state, before trusting the isolated result as evidence the bug is elsewhere.**
2. **Temporary, env-var-gated debug prints are worth adding early, not as a last resort.** A single `FEME_DEBUG_LOCALIZE_PRIVATE_GLOBALS` env var added to `LocalizePrivateGlobalsPass::run`/`usedByOneFunctionOnly` (reverted before committing) found the real answer -- two functions, `main` and `main.patchconstant` -- in one rebuild+run cycle, after roughly 2 hours of IR-archaeology guesswork hadn't. Should have added this an hour earlier.
3. **A genuinely multi-function-shared global can be the *correct*, intentional design, not a bug to "fix" by localizing harder.** My first instinct on seeing `usedByOneFunctionOnly` reject the global was "this check is too strict, relax it." The real fix left that check exactly as strict as before -- the two-function sharing is legitimate (SPIR-V's own `Private`-storage semantics genuinely span the barrier within one logical invocation), and the actual gap was one level downstream, in `SPIRVResourceLoweringPass`'s pointer-use analysis not having a case for "value flows through ordinary memory, across a real function boundary" at all.
4. **The existing `PointerMergeMap`/`mergeIntoPhi`/`mergeIntoSelect` design (from `K6n`) generalized cleanly** to a case its original author probably didn't anticipate (a *global*, not an SSA merge instruction, as the "other side" of a pointer-chain continuation) -- a sign the original design was sound, not over-fit to phi/select specifically.

## Next steps

1. **(~1-2 days)** `K6q`: 2 cases, handle-level `OpPhi`/`OpSelect` merge (merging raw resource *handles* before `getpointer` is called, not pointers already derived from one). Still not attempted -- `hasOnlySupportedUses` (the handle-level checker, distinct from the pointer-level checker this session and K6n both touched) would need the `DescriptorIndex` itself to become phi-mergeable before any GEP/offset is known. Likely the hardest of the three remaining small buckets.
2. **(~1 day)** `K6s`: 5 cases, frag/tessc/tesse result-correctness bug -- pipeline builds and runs, output is wrong, zero normalization rejection. Needs its own investigation (not a legalization gap); start with a minimal single-buffer frag repro and `feme-render`/CPU-backend tracing. Now the largest remaining `variablePointers` residual bucket.
3. **(~1-2 days, "issue outside FeMe", standing)** `K6p`: ~14-15 cases, `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`/`OpPtrDiff` (opcodes 401/402/403) entirely undefined in MLIR's SPIR-V dialect TableGen. Not attempted this session (scope stayed on `K6r`).
4. **(standing, unresolved many sessions)** `backup-before-rebase-20261014` tag decision, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` vs `Release` decision.
5. **(standing)** `L419(j)` remaining untriaged items, `L418(a)` sanity re-check, deferred full `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/extension-manifest regeneration.
6. **(standing)** offload-test-suite `VkBool32`/`WaveActiveMax` pattern check -- not exercised this session either, no `check-hlsl-feme-vk` work done (session stayed scoped to `K6r`'s compiler fix).

# Session: K6s fixed (uniform loop in divergent diamond left resource-call masks at placeholder `true`)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` at session start, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first.

## What now works

All 5 `K6s` cases pass: `writes_single_buffer_frag`/`_tessc`/`_tesse`, `writes_two_buffers_frag`/`_tessc`. The full `variable_pointers` instruction group (790 cases, this session's CTS data set) is now 790/790 Pass with the feature bits measured on transiently -- the entire group is clean. `check-feme`: 3737/3744 pass, 7 unsupported, 0 failed, no regressions. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 618/618 pass.

## The bug, in one paragraph

A uniform-trip-count loop (its own exit check never diverges) nested inside a divergent `if`, whose body contains only plain `feme.cpu.resource.*` calls (no `Discard`/`Demote`/other `StageOpKind` op), had every one of those calls' mask operand stuck at the compile-time placeholder constant `true` forever. `LoopLinearizer::linearizeCycle`'s `CycleHasMaskOps` scan -- the sole gate deciding whether the already-correct entry-mask-threading machinery runs on such a loop at all -- only recognized `StageOpKind` calls as a reason to engage. Fix: two lines, extend that scan to also match `feme.cpu.resource.*`/`feme.cpu.image.*` calls via the same matchers `applyStageMasks` itself already uses to mask them correctly once reached.

## What this session did, in order

1. Reproduced `writes_single_buffer_frag` directly: every output-buffer entry off by `+2111.0`.
2. Ruled out rasterizer duplicate-enumeration first (temporary `FEME_K6S_DEBUG_COUNT_PIXEL00` prints in `Executor.cpp`, reverted): the one real pixel is enumerated exactly once; summing per-tile quad counts across the draw gives 2112 -- exactly the extra-executions count plus one.
3. Dumped the compiled fragment IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR=1`, pre-existing aid): `WaveSize=4`/`QuadsPerWave=1`, so wave-calls == quad count == 2112. The 100-iteration loop runs unconditionally, fully scalar, every resource call hardcoded `i1 true`.
4. Traced `Linearize.cpp` to the exact gap: `CycleHasMaskOps`'s scan.
5. Fixed it, verified via `feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-linearize` on two synthetic reductions before touching the real CTS case.
6. Added a unit test, ran full `check-feme` and the `variable_pointers` CTS group, reverted all debug instrumentation (own session's and leftover VK-GL-CTS instrumentation from a prior session), committed in 3 pieces.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **A single-block-loop synthetic test and a header-distinct-from-latch synthetic test hit completely different code paths in the same function.** My first attempt at a unit test used a single-block loop (header == latch) and silently exercised an entirely different, already-correct early-return path (`return false; // No divergence: leave this real uniform loop alone.`) rather than the branch I'd just fixed. It built, ran, and failed its own assertion -- which looked at first like my fix didn't work, but was actually "my test doesn't test what I think it tests." **Lesson: when hand-writing a synthetic IR reduction of a real bug, match the real case's control-flow *shape* exactly (header vs. latch, which blocks are distinct), not just its semantic intent -- these passes branch on structural details, not just on "is there a loop with a resource call in it."**
2. **A rebuilt static library does not mean the tool that links it got rebuilt too.** After fixing the first synthetic-test issue, the fix still silently failed to trigger when tested via `feme-opt` -- because I'd only run `ninja FeMeTransformsCPU`/`FeMeTransformsCPUTests`, never `ninja feme-opt` itself, so the standalone tool was still linking a stale copy of the pass. `feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-linearize -S` turned out to be the fastest way to check a single pass's behavior on a hand-written `.ll` file, far faster than a full CTS round-trip -- but only once the binary itself was actually rebuilt.
3. **A full broad CTS sweep with a feature flag flipped on is not a substitute for a narrow, targeted regression check against the shipped config.** The `variablePointers` feature bits stay `VK_FALSE` in the committed build; a 70337-case sweep with them flipped on (to exercise the new masking path broadly) surfaced ~332 failures, almost all `variablePointers`-feature-gated residuals from `K6n`/`K6p`/`K6q` that are expected to exist and irrelevant to this fix's safety. The one category worth double-checking (`opphi.*`, 2/20 failing, not `variablePointers`-gated at all) was confirmed pre-existing by `git stash`-ing just the `Linearize.cpp` change, rebuilding, and re-running that one group -- same 2/20 failure count before and after. **Lesson: for a broad-impact compiler-pass change, a stash-and-rebuild A/B on the one suspicious sub-group is cheaper and more conclusive than trying to read or diff an entire 70k-case log.**

# Session: K6q fixed (handle-level phi/select merge of raw resource handles)

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` at session start, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first.

## What now works

Both `K6q` cases pass: `opphi_outer_struct_two_buffers_{first,second}_input`. The full `dEQP-VK.spirv_assembly.instruction.*.variable_pointers.*` group (1637 cases, feature bits measured on transiently) is now 948 Pass/1 Fail/688 Not Supported -- the 1 remaining failure is the pre-existing, already-documented, unrelated `workgroup_two_buffers` `feme-cpu-simdize` case (K6n), not a new regression. `check-feme`: 3740/3747 pass, 7 unsupported, 0 failed. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 621/621 pass (3 new tests added).

## The bug, in one paragraph

`hasOnlySupportedUses` (the handle-level checker in `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp`) required every user of a raw resource handle to be a direct `getpointer` call, with zero phi/select recognition at that level -- one layer earlier than `K6n`'s already-fixed pointer-level merge. The real CTS case's IR is a nested phi-of-phi merging two `handlefrombinding` calls across a diamond nested inside another diamond, with one incoming edge being a literal `poison` handle (a dead-edge artifact from control-flow linearization). Fix: mirror K6n's `PointerMergeMap`/`mergeIntoPhi`/`mergeIntoSelect` design one level earlier -- new `hasOnlySupportedHandleUse`/`hasOnlySupportedHandleMergeUses`, a `lowerHandleAccesses` extracted from `lowerAccesses` and parameterized by a generic handle value, and a `HandleMergeMap`/`mergeIntoHandlePhi`/`mergeIntoHandleSelect` that reuses the existing null-sentinel for poison edges.

## What this session did, in order

1. Verified the "stalled session, stash exists" boilerplate claim was false -- no stash anywhere in any of the three repos, clean working tree.
2. Selected `K6q` per the prior session's own suggested next action (smallest case count of the three remaining buckets).
3. Found the real dEQP-VK test names via the mustpass case list (the short names from prior docs matched 8 near-duplicates; needed the full `complex_types_compute` group name to disambiguate).
4. Reproduced both cases, dumped pre-normalization IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRENORM=1`), found the nested-phi-with-poison-edge shape.
5. Implemented the fix by mirroring K6n's design one level earlier (handle level, pre-`getpointer`), refactoring `lowerAccesses` into a generic `lowerHandleAccesses` so merge continuations can call back into it recursively.
6. Added 3 unit tests (direct phi merge, direct select merge, the real case's nested-phi-with-poison shape), ran the full `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` suite, then the full `variable_pointers` CTS group.
7. Reverted the transient feature-bit flip, ran full `check-feme`, updated `Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md`, committed in 4 pieces (fix, tests, docs, this file).

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **A handle-level merge and a pointer-level merge are structurally parallel but still need their own state type, even when one is a strict subset of the other.** `HandleMergeMap` only needs a single `i32` descriptor index per merge, versus `PointerMergeMap`'s `(DescriptorIndex, Offset)` pair -- reusing `PointerMergeMap` with a dummy offset field would have worked technically but would have muddied the type's contract (callers would need to know the offset field is meaningless at the handle level). **Lesson: when a new bug is "the same shape, one layer earlier/later" than an already-fixed one, resist collapsing the two into one generalized type unless the state really is identical -- a distinct, narrower type documents the actual invariant better than a shared one with an unused field.**
2. **The "same user-facing error signature" can still split into several architecturally distinct fixable buckets, and splitting them early (as `K6n`'s own session did) pays off two sessions later.** This session's whole job was made tractable because a prior session had already bucketed `K6n`'s 10 residual cases into `K6q`/`K6r`/`K6s` by exact cause, rather than leaving them as one lumped "10 more cases of the same thing" entry. Picking up `K6q` here required zero re-triage -- the Roadmap.md row already had the exact root-cause hypothesis written down, which turned out to be correct on the first reproduction attempt.

## Next steps

1. **(~1-2 days)** `K6n`-proper: ~124 cases, the largest remaining `variablePointers` bucket, CPU-backend resource-handle-normalization architectural limitation. Still not root-caused beyond signature-level bucketing -- `K6o`/`K6q`/`K6r`/`K6s` have all now been split off and closed, leaving only the original core bucket. Likely the deepest, hardest-to-fix piece of the whole feature; worth its own investigation session before committing to an approach, possibly needing a runtime dispatch mechanism rather than a lowering-pattern fix.
2. **(~1-2 days, "issue outside FeMe", standing)** `K6p`: ~14-15 cases, `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`/`OpPtrDiff` (opcodes 401/402/403) entirely undefined in MLIR's SPIR-V dialect TableGen. Not attempted this session (scope stayed on `K6q`). Needs new TableGen op definitions, deserializer cases, and likely a `SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp` lowering.
3. **(standing, unresolved many sessions)** `backup-before-rebase-20261014` tag decision, `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` vs `Release` decision -- neither revisited this session.
4. **(standing)** `L419(j)` remaining untriaged items, `L418(a)` sanity re-check, deferred full `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/extension-manifest regeneration.

# Session: K6p feme-local half closed (merge for OpPtrEqual/OpPtrNotEqual/OpPtrDiff), 2 bugs fixed, K6t opened

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` at session start, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first.

## What now works

4 of `K6p`'s 29 CTS cases pass (`simple_variable_pointers_ptr_equal`, `simple_variable_pointers_ptr_not_equal`, `different_wgs_equal`, `different_wgs_not_equal`). Full `*variable_pointer*` sweep (4464 cases, feature bits measured on transiently): 958 Pass / 3492 NotSupported / 14 Fail, zero regressions. `check-feme`: 3743/3750 pass, 7 unsupported, 0 failed. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 623/623 pass (2 new tests added). Also fixed a real segfault and a real invalid-IR-emission bug along the way -- both pre-existing, newly exposed rather than newly introduced.

## The bug, in one paragraph

Picked up a stalled prior session's in-progress, uncommitted `K6p` work (new `PointerCompareMap`/`mergeIntoCompare`/`mergeIntoDiff` machinery for `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses` to accept `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`/`OpPtrDiff`'s lowered `icmp`/`ptrtoint`+`sub` shapes) that had a duplicate-parameter build error. Fixing the build and exercising the new code paths against real CTS cases surfaced two latent bugs the new opcode support reached for the first time: an infinite-recursion segfault in the existing (unrelated) `lowerPointerMergeGlobalStore` recursion on a loop-carried pointer stored back into the same global each iteration (no cycle guard existed before), and an invalid `llvm.icmp`-on-opaque-resource-handle-type emission from upstream's generic `IComparePattern` when two *whole* resource handles are compared directly (no intervening `OpAccessChain`).

## What this session did, in order

1. Fixed the stalled build (duplicate `PointerCompareMap &Compares` parameter; missing `Compares` argument at one call site).
2. Ran the full 621-test `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` suite to confirm the threading fix introduced no regressions.
3. Spot-checked 2 CTS cases; found `variable_pointers_vars_ssbo_diff` segfaulting. Root-caused via `gdb` backtrace to an unbounded recursion in `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses`'s `GVLoad`-chasing path. Fixed with the same `Visited`-set guard pattern `K6q` already established, threaded through 4 recursive call sites.
4. Ran the full 29-case `opptr*` CTS set: 4/29 pass. Found 4 more cases emitting invalid LLVM IR (whole-handle `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual`). Root-caused to upstream's `IComparePattern` lacking an operand-type guard.
5. Fixed `IComparePattern` in `mlir/lib/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/SPIRVToLLVM.cpp` (an "issue outside FeMe") with a new `isICmpComparable` check; reran the full 149-test MLIR SPIRVToLLVM/SPIRV lit sweep to confirm zero regressions.
6. Ran the full `*variable_pointer*` CTS sweep (4464 cases): 958/3492/14, all 14 known, zero new regressions. Reverted the transient feature-bit flips.
7. Wrote 2 new unit tests for `mergeIntoCompare`/`mergeIntoDiff`. Both initially failed because the test IR's all-literal-constant bindings/indices let `mergeIntoCompare`/`mergeIntoDiff`'s own `IRBuilder<>` constant-fold the whole expression away -- correct pass behavior, wrong test assumption. Rewrote both tests' assertions to check the folded return value instead of an intermediate instruction shape.
8. Wrote a new FeMe-local lit test (`spirv-to-llvm-ptr-equal-whole-handle-invalid.mlir`) exercising the upstream `IComparePattern` fix using FeMe's own custom resource-handle type converter (the only way to construct the triggering shape -- no pure-upstream-MLIR reproducer exists).
9. Ran the full `check-feme` target (3743/3750 pass, 0 failed) to confirm zero regressions end-to-end.
10. Committed in 4 pieces: the isolated "outside FeMe" MLIR fix, the feme-local fix + both new tests, doc updates (`Roadmap.md`/`VulkanCTSReport.md`, including a new `K6t` row for the whole-handle-comparison residual), and this file.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **A generic, shared, already-widely-used pattern (`IComparePattern`) can still have a type-safety gap that's only reachable through a downstream project's own custom type converter, not anything in-tree.** The fix itself (an operand-type guard) is fully general and belongs upstream since it protects every future caller, not just FeMe -- but the *test* proving it fires can only live where the triggering IR shape can actually be constructed. Don't force a reproducer into the "wrong" test tree just to satisfy a "tests live next to the fix" instinct; put the fix where it's general and the test where it's reproducible, and say so explicitly in the commit message.
2. **"The merge instruction doesn't survive in the test's final IR" is not automatically a test bug to work around -- sometimes it's the pass correctly doing its job, and the fix is to assert on the right thing.** Both new unit tests used literal-constant resource bindings, which let aggressive (but entirely standard, `ConstantFolder`-default) constant folding collapse the entire synthesized expression down to its one correct literal answer. The lesson generalizes beyond this session: before "fixing" a test whose instruction-shape assertion fails, check whether the *value* is still correct -- if it is, the right fix is almost always to assert on the value, not to contort the input IR until an instruction survives that doesn't need to.

Needs a FeMe-CPU-backend-level resource-index comparison in `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp` (compare two `DescriptorIndex` values directly, no offset component since neither side went through `getpointer`) -- not yet attempted. Good next pick: smaller and more contained than `K6n`-proper, and now the only unattempted `K6p`-family residual.

Still not root-caused beyond signature-level bucketing. Likely needs a runtime-dispatch mechanism rather than a lowering-pattern fix; worth its own investigation session before committing to an approach.

# Session: K6t closed (whole-handle OpPtrEqual/OpPtrNotEqual), mergeIntoCompare null-pointer bug fixed

**Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`** via `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName`, with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported first -- checked at session start, mid-session, and again at the end.

## What now works

`K6t` (whole-handle `OpPtrEqual`/`OpPtrNotEqual` comparison, no `OpAccessChain` on either side) is fully implemented, tested, and CTS-verified. 6/8 targeted CTS cases pass (up from 0/8 -- previously a hard legalization failure); the 2 remaining are the pre-existing, unrelated `feme-cpu-simdize` groupshared limitation. Broader 29-case `opptr*` sweep: 8/29 pass (up from 4/29), zero regressions. `check-feme`: 3749/3756 pass, 0 failed. `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 629/629 pass (6 new tests this session). Full `llvm/test/Verifier/` suite (443 tests) and `feme/test/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/` lit suite (138 tests) both pass clean.

Also found and fixed a real, previously-latent bug in `mergeIntoCompare` (missing `ConstantPointerNull` handling) -- unrelated to `K6t`'s own scope, but only reachable once `K6t` let the triggering shader legalize far enough to execute for the first time.

## The work, in three layers (this is why it took a full session, not a quick pattern fix)

1. **New upstream LLVM intrinsic** `llvm.spv.resource.handleequal` (`IntrinsicsSPIRV.td`) -- needed because LLVM's `icmp` cannot operate on an opaque resource-handle target-extension type at all. While adding it, found the two operands were declared as independent `llvm_any_ty` placeholders (not enforcing same-type despite the doc comment's claim); fixed with `LLVMMatchType<0>`. New isolated `llvm/test/Verifier/` test (the "issue outside FeMe" piece).
2. **New FeMe-local `HandleCompareConversionPattern`** (`SPIRVToLLVMPatterns.cpp`) lowers `spirv.PtrEqual`/`spirv.PtrNotEqual` on a resource-handle operand to a call of the new intrinsic (negation via `xor`, not a second intrinsic). New lit test replaces the now-stale `-invalid` test that used to assert this shape failed to legalize.
3. **`SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp` CPU-backend dispatch** for the new intrinsic call: `mergeIntoHandleCompare` re-expresses it as `desc0 == desc1`; `foldSameOperandHandleCompares` folds a same-operand call to `true` before `collectHandles` runs (avoiding a use-list double-visit crash). 5 new unit tests.

## The null-pointer bug, in one paragraph

`mergeIntoCompare` (the existing pointer-level `icmp`-merge function, K6p's own) had no `ConstantPointerNull` special case, unlike its siblings `mergeIntoPhi`/`mergeIntoSelect`/the new `mergeIntoHandleCompare`. Because `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses` accepts *any* equality `icmp` regardless of the other operand's shape, a literal null never independently reaches `mergeIntoCompare`'s normal chain-walk -- the real side's own operand was left permanently `PoisonValue`, producing `icmp eq poison, null` that silently folds to a wrong constant. Unobservable before `K6t`: the triggering shader shape (`null_comparisons_ssbo_not_equal`) previously failed whole-handle legalization entirely, so this downstream path was never reached. Fixed by mirroring the same three siblings' sentinel-resolution pattern.

## What this session did, in order

1. Fixed the stale lit test (`-invalid` → positive-case `spirv-to-llvm-ptr-equal-whole-handle.mlir`, 3 cases).
2. Ran the full `feme/test/Conversion/SPIRVToLLVM/` lit suite (138 tests) and `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` (628 tests) -- both clean.
3. Ran `check-feme` (3748/3755 pass baseline before the null-fix).
4. Ran 8 targeted CTS cases (feature bits transiently flipped for measurement, reverted after); found the correct case-group name (`opptrnotequal`, not a suffix under `opptrequal`) after an initial wrong guess. 5/8 passed; `null_comparisons_ssbo_not_equal` failed with a sub-result mismatch; the 2 `_wg_` cases hit the pre-existing groupshared limitation.
5. Root-caused the `null_comparisons_ssbo_not_equal` failure to `mergeIntoCompare`'s missing null-handling (confirmed it was newly-exposed, not newly-introduced, by testing the pre-K6t baseline via a targeted stash).
6. Fixed `mergeIntoCompare`; CTS re-run: 6/8 targeted, zero regressions on the broader 29-case sweep (8/29, up from 4/29).
7. Added the new unit test for the null-fix; reverted the temporary feature-flag flip; reran `check-feme` (3749/3756, 0 failed) and `vulkaninfo` again.
8. Added the isolated upstream intrinsic test (`llvm/test/Verifier/intrinsic-spv-resource-handleequal.ll`), discovering and fixing the `LLVMMatchType<0>` gap along the way; confirmed via manual `llvm-as`/`opt` round-trip (after rebuilding both -- stale binaries silently miss new TableGen constraints).
9. Re-checked all 5 `opptrdiff.*` cases: one confirmed to hit the exact pre-existing CFG-linearization error text, confirming the residual isn't a new `K6p`/`K6t`-adjacent gap (the other 4 left as a follow-up rather than guessed at).
10. Updated `Roadmap.md` (struck through `K6t`, refreshed `K6p`'s own row) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new section). Checked `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md` -- no change needed (`variablePointers` still correctly `no`).
11. Split into 5 commits via precise `git add -p` hunk-level staging (not just whole-file splitting), since the null-fix and the K6t feature landed in the same two files: (1) upstream intrinsic + its test, (2) FeMe MLIR pattern + lit tests, (3) FeMe CPU-backend K6t lowering + its 5 unit tests, (4) the standalone null-fix + its 1 unit test, (5) doc updates. Rebuilt and reran the full unit/lit suites and `check-feme` after the split to confirm no commit boundary broke anything.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **When a bug fix and a new feature land in the same function/file because the feature's own work exposed the bug, `git add -p`'s per-hunk staging (not just per-file) is the right tool to keep them as separate, independently-revertable commits** -- worth the extra time over bundling "related enough" changes into one commit, especially when the bug is a real pre-existing defect rather than an artifact of the new code.
2. **A "4+ cases" scope estimate from a prior session's next-steps text can understate the real shape of the work once you dig in** -- `K6t` wasn't just a CPU-backend pattern (like `K6p`'s own closure was); it needed a genuinely new IR-level vocabulary (the intrinsic) because the fundamental operation (comparing two opaque handle values) has no existing LLVM instruction that can express it at all. Recognize this early (as soon as `icmp` on a target-extension type is confirmed impossible, not just "currently rejected") rather than assuming the existing `mergeIntoCompare`-style machinery can be directly reused.
3. **Re-verify prior sessions' "still the largest remaining bucket" framing against the actual, current `Roadmap.md` text before trusting it** -- this session confirmed (again) that `K6n`-proper was already closed in `Roadmap.md` despite several generations of next-steps prose still describing it as the largest open item. The next-steps text is apparently regenerated from a stale snapshot rather than the live document; always check `Roadmap.md` directly.
