# Agent thoughts: opptrdiff triage -- one false-rejection fixed, one new bug found (K6u)

**Next action for the next session:** pick `K6u` (restructure `mergeIntoPhi` to resolve a self-referential loop-carried-pointer backedge eagerly) or `K6n`-proper (the deeper CPU-backend architectural bucket). Both are real, both are hard; `K6u` is smaller and more contained.

## What I did, in order

1. Confirmed `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` (standing check, start of session).
2. Took the prior session's exact follow-up: root-cause the 2 of 5 `opptrdiff.*` CTS cases that weren't yet attributable to a known bucket (`variable_pointers_vars_ssbo_diff`, `variable_pointers_vars_ssbo_2_diff`).
3. Used `FEME_CPU_LOG_RESOURCE_NORMALIZATION=1` (a diagnostic flagged-but-untried by the prior session) -- got the exact rejection line in one shot instead of a manual IR trace: `"getelementptr with an unresolvable byte offset: %13 = getelementptr i32, ptr addrspace(11) %spirv_var_5.0, i32 -1"`.
4. Read `hasResolvableGEPByteOffset`/`computePointerOffset`: the function rejected *any* negative constant GEP offset outright, not just an unresolvable negative *variable* one. A `-1` index GEP is fully resolvable at compile time regardless of sign.
5. Fixed both functions: dropped the constant-offset negativity check, switched `computePointerOffset`'s constant-term materialization from `getZExtValue()` to a sign-extending `APInt::sextOrTrunc(64)` (zero-extension would have produced a huge garbage value for a true negative offset).
6. Built `feme_vulkan`, reran both CTS cases: normalization now succeeds (no rejection logged) -- **but both still fail**, now with a wrong computed value, not a rejection.
7. Didn't stop at "still fails, move on" -- dumped `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRENORM` again and traced why: both cases' shaders keep a forward and a backward SSBO-pointer iterator in `Private`-storage globals, each GEP'd by one element per loop iteration, feeding `OpPtrDiff`. `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses`'s *validation* phase has a `Visited`-set cycle breaker for exactly this self-referential phi/GEP loop shape, so it accepts it -- but `mergeIntoPhi`'s *rewrite* phase has no equivalent: it only recurses past a phi once every incoming edge's value is already resolved, and the loop backedge's own GEP can only resolve by first recursing into the phi. Permanent deadlock -- confirmed via the dump (the merged offset phi literally shows `undef` on the backedge).
8. Split this into two roadmap-accurate pieces rather than filing one vague "still failing" note: the negative-offset bug is genuinely fixed (K6p row updated); the deadlock is a new, separate, not-yet-fixed bug (new row, `K6u`).
9. Added an isolated (non-cyclic) unit test proving the negative-offset fix is correct on its own, independent of the separate loop-deadlock bug: `LowersPtrDiffThroughNegativeConstantGEPOffsetToOffsetSubtraction`.
10. Ran `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` (630/630 pass), then `check-feme` -- first run failed 1 test (`PhysicalDeviceProperties2Test.PreVulkan11Promotion...`) because I'd forgotten the standing temporary `variablePointers=VK_TRUE` flag flip from measurement was still in place; reverted it (`git checkout feme/lib/Vulkan/EntryPoints.cpp`), rebuilt, reran: 3750/3757 pass, 0 failed, 7 expected-unsupported.
11. Re-ran all 5 `opptrdiff.*` cases in the final (`VK_FALSE`) configuration: all 5 report `NotSupported`, confirming zero behavior change in the committed state.
12. Committed the code fix + its test as one commit, docs as a separate commit.

## What actually shipped (visible win)

- `hasResolvableGEPByteOffset`/`computePointerOffset` in `SPIRVResourceLowering.cpp` now correctly accept and materialize a negative-constant GEP offset (e.g. `getelementptr i32, ptr %p, i32 -1`) instead of rejecting it outright -- a real, independently-useful correctness fix, verified by a new non-cyclic unit test.
- Full 5-case `opptrdiff.*` bucket is now **completely triaged by individual root cause** (no more "fails without a printed diagnostic" unknowns): 2 CFG-linearization (pre-existing), 1 groupshared-simdize (pre-existing), 2 the new negative-offset bug (fixed) stacked with the new loop-phi-deadlock bug (not yet fixed, tracked as `K6u`).
- Zero regressions: `check-feme` 3750/3757 pass, `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` 630/630 pass, all 5 CTS cases still `NotSupported` in the default (committed) configuration.

## The real lesson this session learned

1. **A "fails to build" diagnostic isn't the end of the investigation just because it goes away.** Fixing the surface rejection (`hasResolvableGEPByteOffset`) let the pipeline *execute* for the first time on these two cases -- which surfaced a second, deeper, previously entirely-latent bug (`mergeIntoPhi`'s rewrite-phase deadlock) that the rejection had been silently masking. Always re-run after a fix and check the *actual* outcome, not just "does it still fail the same way."
2. **Validation-phase and rewrite-phase cycle-handling are not automatically symmetric.** `hasOnlySupportedPointerUses`'s `Visited`-set guard answers "is this structurally supported?" correctly for a self-referential loop-carried pointer PHI, but `mergeIntoPhi`'s rewrite logic (gate-until-all-edges-known, then recurse) has a completely different, incompatible control-flow shape that can't resolve the same cycle. A pass that both validates and rewrites needs to audit both halves for cycle-safety independently, not just reuse "the validator accepted it" as proof the rewriter will succeed.
3. **The previously-untried `FEME_CPU_LOG_RESOURCE_NORMALIZATION` diagnostic (flagged by name but not used in the prior session) was strictly faster than the manual IR trace it replaced** -- reached for it first this time, got the exact answer in one run instead of reverse-engineering the accept/reject logic by hand.

## Next steps

1. **(~1-2 days)** `K6u`: restructure `mergeIntoPhi` to resolve a self-referential loop-carried-pointer backedge eagerly -- e.g. create the `descidx`/`offset` phis up front (already done today) and recurse into a backedge's own GEP using those in-progress phi nodes themselves as its `Offset`/`DescriptorIndex` inputs (a legal forward SSA reference, since the phis already exist as instructions even before every incoming value is filled), rather than requiring every edge resolved before any recursion happens. Needs careful design around ordering (the GEP's own resolved value must be computed and fed back into the *same* phi's backedge slot without re-entering the same merge state) and a new unit test exercising a genuine 2-block loop (not just the straight-line/cross-branch shapes every existing phi-merge test uses).

   produced progress but not correctness -- `variable_pointers_vars_ssbo_2_diff`
   went from total garbage to a precise sign inversion (`2 == -2`).

   tolerating a slot landing on a *different* phi means that slot's real
   value can arrive via a separate top-level walk, but `mergeIntoPhi`
   unconditionally erased the phi right after its own recursion
   returned, before that later value arrived.

   `PointerMergeState::Erased` flag + `EraseIfComplete` check (run after
   every slot-filling call, not just the first). That alone still

   mutually-recursive chain can reenter the same phi's merge *from
   within* its own still-running top-level walk -- added a
   `RecursionActive` flag to defer the check until that walk fully
   returns. Both bugs caught by the new unit test, not by iterating on
   full CTS runs (much faster feedback loop).

   diamond merge with zero `DiamondFlattener` changes needed.

# Session: `K6z` fixed -- nested-sibling-cycle walk-through in `DiamondFlattener`

**What shipped this session** (3 commits, all `feme/` only -- no
outside-FeMe fix needed):
1. `feme: fix K6z nested-sibling-cycle rejection in DiamondFlattener`
2. `feme: add regression test for K6z nested-sibling-cycle fix`
3. `feme: update Roadmap.md/VulkanCTSReport.md for K6z fix`

**The bug, in one line**: a uniform loop whose body contained an
already-fully-linearized nested sibling loop (not just the loop's own
exit check) was always rejected as "unsupported," even though nothing
about it actually needed rejecting.

**The fix**: `DiamondFlattener::validate`/`::flatten` now walk straight
through a strictly-nested child cycle's header (detected via `CI.contains
(C, ChildHeader)`) to that cycle's own exit block, instead of stopping
there. Wired in via two new optional callbacks on `LoopLinearizer::
linearizeCycle`.

**Bonus bug fix, found by accident**: a dangling `llvm::function_ref`.
The `NarrowChildEntryMasks` lambda was an unnamed temporary passed
straight into `DiamondFlattener`'s constructor -- which only stores a
non-owning pointer to it. First real invocation later = SEGV with
`this=0x5`. Fixed by binding it to a named local first. Lesson banked:
**any lambda passed to something that stores it as a `function_ref` must
be a named local, never an inline temporary.**

**Why this took most of a session to test correctly** (useful lesson for
future `DiamondFlattener` work): my first regression test showed the
resource calls' mask operands staying `i1 true` after the fix, and I
spent a long stretch assuming that meant the fix was incomplete. It
wasn't. `makeActivePNPair()` only seeds a loop's own mask-phi with its
*non-backedge* incoming edge up front (`addLatchIncoming` adds the
backedge edge much later, after `flatten()` returns) -- so during
`flatten()`'s own walk, that phi genuinely has only one incoming value,
and `isKnownConstantMask`'s `lookThroughTrivialPhi` correctly treats it as
the constant `true` it currently is. Since nothing in this loop body ever
has a `discard`/`demote` (confirmed: that combination is its own,
separately-diagnosed "unsupported" shape, see
`unsupported-stage-op-in-uniform-loop.ll`), staying `true` is the
*correct* answer, not a masking bug. **If a future session hits "mask
operand stayed a constant, is that wrong?" again: check whether the loop
body has any real discard/demote first** -- if not, constant is correct.

**Numbers**:

- `ninja check-feme`: 3756/3756 Pass, 0 Fail.
- `check-hlsl-feme-vk`: 472 Pass/273 Unsupported/28 XFAIL/19 Fail (up
  from 465/273/28/26) -- **7 of the 24 cases attributed to `K6z` are
  fixed**: `matrix_single_subscript_load`, `matrix_swizzle_{one,zero}_
  based`, `CBuffer/Matrix/LayoutKeyword/{subscript,transpose}`,
  `BufferExact-error-array`, `Textures/Array.SRVToUAV.array`.
- The other 17 (`HLSLLib/*MemoryBarrierWithGroupSync`,
  `InterlockedCompareExchange/Exchange.resources.32`, `licm-hoist-load`,
  `Textures/SRVToUAV.array`, `particle-life`, all 10 `WaveOps/*`) still
  hit the **same diagnostic text**, but a **different, not-yet-confirmed**
  structural cause -- this fix was deliberately scoped to the one shape
  `matrix_single_subscript_load.test` actually needed, not a blanket fix
  for every "unsupported loop body shape" diagnostic. New roadmap row

- `VK-GL-CTS` targeted sample (before/after, full fail-list diff, run via

  `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*` 606/624 (up from 586/624, 20 fixed, 0 new

# Session: `L425` fixed -- `MergeVisited`/`ResolvedBlocks` false-conflict in `DiamondFlattener`

**What shipped this session** (3 commits, all `feme/` only -- no
outside-FeMe fix needed):
1. `[feme] Fix MergeVisited false-conflict in DiamondFlattener (L425)`
2. `[feme] Add regression test for L425 MergeVisited fix`
3. `[feme] Update Roadmap/VulkanCTSReport for L425 fix`

**The bug, in one line**: a loop whose own exit check and backedge
decision were fused into one `StructurizeCFG`-style `Flow` dispatch
block, with a divergent inner diamond already flattened earlier in the
same `linearizeCycle` call, was rejected as "unsupported" even though the
diamond was never actually contested -- it was already safely resolved.

**The fix**: added a `ResolvedBlocks` set (same whole-function lifetime
as `MergeVisited`) recording blocks a fully-successful flatten call
already committed. `validate()`'s conflict check is now "fail only if
seen in `MergeVisited` but *not yet* in `ResolvedBlocks`" -- the original
`L375` double-claim protection survives untouched for any still-pending
candidate; only safe pass-through of an *already-finished* call's own
diamond is newly permitted.

**Debugging lesson banked**: `FEME_DEBUG_LINEARIZE_TRACE` (a pre-existing
env var) answers "which code path engaged" in seconds, without writing
any new instrumentation -- check it before adding fresh `errs()` tracing.
This session's root cause was found by adding temporary `FEME_DEBUG_L425`
tracing at every `validate()` failure branch and watching exactly which
one fired and on which block; that tracing was fully removed before the
final build (verified via grep, zero matches remain).

**Why the precheck (`canFlattenLoopBodyRegion`) didn't catch this
earlier**: it always builds a fresh, throwaway `MergeVisited`/
`ResolvedBlocks` pair that never sees the fixed-point loop's own history
-- a pre-existing, documented, accepted possibility (the precheck and the
real call can structurally disagree; the `if (!MasksAtLatch)` diagnostic
catches it). No change needed there beyond threading the new parameter.

## What did NOT ship: the actual `L425(a)` fix

All 4 target cases now reach the identical `feme-cpu-wrap-entry` diagnostic -- confirmed one shared root cause. It's `EntryWrapper.cpp`'s `isLinearChain`: it can't recognize a barrier directly inside a `while`-loop's single-block body when the *header* (not the latch) owns the exit check. `walkBarrierFreeArm` hard-rejects any barrier in an arm it walks, by design (nested-arm barriers have no `outlineChain` representation).

I patched `isLinearChain` to special-case this one trivial shape (body = single block, unconditional branch straight back to the header). It worked -- `isLinearChain` accepted the shape -- but `splitAtGroupSyncBarriers`'s region-splitting code crashes one layer further down: a stale-parent `DominatorTree` assertion (`GenericDomTree.h:400`). That code assumes an invariant the newly-admitted shape doesn't satisfy. **I reverted the patch.** A diagnosed "unsupported" is better than a crash; shipping a crash in place of a clean error is a worse regression than not fixing the bug at all.

## Next action (pick this first, ~1-2 days): `L426`

1. Re-apply the reverted `isLinearChain` patch (described in roadmap row `L426`, not re-typed here -- read that row, it has the exact shape).
2. Repro: `/tmp/l425a/AllMemoryBarrierWithGroupSync/` -- `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<build>/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json ./bin/offloader -debug-layer src/pipeline.yaml shader.o`, crashes in under a second.
3. `gdb --args ./bin/offloader ...`, backtrace at the `DominatorTree` assertion, find what `splitAtGroupSyncBarriers` assumes.
4. Fix that assumption, rebuild `libfeme_vulkan.so` + `feme-opt` + `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`, re-run the 4-case repro set and `check-hlsl-feme-vk`.

# Session: `L426` fixed -- `matchLoopShape` generalized, all 4 `L425(a)` cases now pass; `isLinearChain` path confirmed a dead end

**Device check**: `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=<build>/tools/feme/tools/feme-vulkan/feme_icd.json vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` → `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Confirmed.

**Task**: `L426` -- fix the 4 cases stuck on `feme-cpu-wrap-entry`'s diagnostic, following last session's planned path (re-apply reverted `isLinearChain` patch, debug the `DominatorTree` crash).

## What shipped (2 commits, already committed to this branch)

1. `EntryWrapper.cpp` -- two bugs fixed in `matchLoopShape`/`collectClonableScalarRecurrence`, plus new lit test `entry-wrapper-loop-wave-persistent-mask-recurrence.ll`.
2. Docs: `Roadmap.md` (`L426` struck through, `L427` opened for the standing `offload-test-suite` build gap), `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new entry).

## The planned path was a dead end -- pivoted mid-session

Re-reproduced last session's `isLinearChain` patch + `DominatorTree` crash with `gdb`. The crash is inside `SROAPass` computing a fresh `DominatorTree` over a region function. Root cause: `splitAtGroupSyncBarriers`'s own region-calling code (`buildWrapper`) is a **strictly flat, call-each-region-once model with no looping construct at all**. No `isLinearChain` patch could ever make a loop backedge representable there. Abandoned this path entirely rather than sink more time into it.

## Actual fix: `matchLoopShape`'s own wave-persistent-induction machinery

`EntryWrapper.cpp` already has separate "barrier inside a uniform loop" machinery (`matchLoopShape`/`buildWrapperForLoop`) that structurally matches all 4 cases' shape. It still rejected them due to 2 bugs:

1. `matchLoopShape`'s induction-seed check only allowed a non-constant seed when the recurrence was loop-invariant (`NextValue == HeaderPhi`). A genuine (narrowing) recurrence with a non-constant seed was unconditionally rejected, even though the seed/store-back machinery (`spillValuesLiveAcrossBarriers`) already handles both cases identically. Fixed: now requires only that `NextValue` be an `Instruction`.
2. `collectClonableScalarRecurrence` never checked for vector types, so a per-lane mask recurrence got wrongly treated as "clonable into the wrapper's scalar loop" -- producing invalid IR (`select` with a `void <badref>` operand, caught via `FEME_OPT_DUMP_INVALID=1`). Fixed: reject any vector-typed instruction/phi-dependency.

## Debugging near-miss worth remembering

Early in this session I instrumented `matchLoopShape` with `errs()` traces before each `return std::nullopt;`, un-braced. This silently turned every instrumented `if` into an unconditional `return` (classic dangling-if-without-braces), making NONE of 12 traces fire while the function still returned `nullopt` -- a flatly contradictory signal that cost real time to run down. The compiler's own "misleading indentation" warning was the only tell. **Always brace an inserted statement when touching a single-statement `if` body.**

## Numbers

- `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`: 634/634 Pass (1 net new test).

# Session: `L429` fixed -- `EntryWrapperPass` `HeaderDerivedValues` poisoned by an already-erased `PersistentInduction` header phi

**Next action**: pick `L428` -- triage `check-hlsl-clang-feme-vk`'s
92-case failure list, starting with one `_mat.test` case. ~1-2 days.

**Device check**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` (with
`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` set to the build's `feme_icd.json`) -> `FeMe CPU
Vulkan Device`, confirmed.

## What got done

1. **Root-caused `L429` all the way down**, not just re-confirmed the
   symptom. Technique: `Pipeline.cpp`'s `FEME_DUMP_IR` dump point sits
   immediately before `EntryWrapperPass` runs; running
   `feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-wrap-entry` standalone on that dump
   reproduced the exact `undef`-mask bug outside the full pipeline, no
   `ninja`+`offloader` round-trip needed per iteration.
2. **Found the actual defect** (not the previously-hypothesized
   `feme-cpu-simdize` resource-atomic-widening theory):
   `EntryWrapperPass`'s `HeaderDerivedValues` mechanism clones a
   header-local, non-phi instruction once into the wrapper's own scalar
   `LoopHeaderBB`, valid only if its operand chain is loop-invariant or
   `ScalarInduction`-driven. Here it instead read a `PersistentInduction`
   header phi -- a genuinely per-wave value.
   `spillValuesLiveAcrossBarriers`'s reload-rewriting never touches uses
   still inside `Shape.Header` itself, so this use was never redirected
   to a reload; the header phi was then replaced with `poison` and
   erased, silently poisoning it, and the clone-once step baked that in
   permanently.
3. **Fixed it**: added `dependsOnPersistentInduction` +
   `cloneHeaderChainAt` in `EntryWrapper.cpp`. For `HeaderDerivedValues`
   entries that transitively depend on a `PersistentInduction`'s header
   phi, recompute the value fresh at each of its original use sites
   *before* `spillValuesLiveAcrossBarriers` runs, so the normal reload
   machinery picks it up naturally. One verifier-dominance bug found and
   fixed along the way (wrong clone-insertion order).
4. **Added a regression unit test**
   (`SplitsFlowMergeLoopWithHeaderDerivedValueFromWavePersistentRecurrence`)
   -- confirmed it fails (3 assertions) with the fix reverted, passes
   with it restored.
5. **Verified broadly**: `FeMeTransformsCPUTests` 635/635 (was 634);
   `check-hlsl-feme-vk` 791/792 (was 490 Passed/1 Failed in the same run
   shape -- `InterlockedAdd.resources.32.test` now passes), sole
   remaining failure the known `Mandelbrot.test` flake; both minimal and
   full real-test repros pass via `offloader` directly.
6. **Ran a targeted `VK-GL-CTS` check** (no prior `InterlockedAdd`-
   adjacent case list existed, so picked compute-atomic + loop/barrier
   groups): `opatomic*` 19/26 Pass (7 NotSupported, unrelated
   `vulkanMemoryModel` gap), `glsl.loops.*` 606/624, `glsl.demote.*`
   30/30 -- all unchanged from prior baselines, 0 regressions (expected:
   this is a CPU-backend/compute fix, not a graphics-loop-shape one).
7. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L429` struck through, correct root cause
   recorded) and `VulkanCTSReport.md`, each its own commit. No
   feature/extension surface changed, so the two inventories needed no
   edits -- confirmed, not skipped.

# Session: `L428` triaged -- two real Clang/LLVM SPIR-V bugs fixed outside FeMe; a third blocker (`spirv-val` shuffle gap) found and split off as `L428(a)`

**Next action**: pick `L428(a)` -- isolate a minimal 2-operand 16-wide
`shufflevector` IR test to determine whether the remaining
`spirv-val` `OpTypeVectorIdEXT`-shuffle rejection is a genuine LLVM
backend bug or an upstream SPIRV-Tools validator limitation. ~half day.

**Device check**: `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` returns
`llvmpipe` by default in this environment -- must set
`VK_ICD_FILENAMES` to the build's `feme_icd.json` first. With it set:
`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed.

## What got done

1. **Picked up `L428`** (triage `check-hlsl-clang-feme-vk`'s 92-case
   failure list) exactly where the prior session left off, starting
   with `Feature/HLSLLib/asin_mat.test` as instructed.

2. **Bisected the dominant `_mat.test` cluster (~40 of 92 cases) down
   to two independent, pre-existing bugs, both outside `feme/`**:
   - **Bug 1**: Clang's HLSL driver (`HLSL.cpp`) defaults to
     `-spirv-ext=all` when `-fspv-extension=` is unset, sweeping in
     the still-provisional `SPV_KHR_poison_freeze` extension, which
     the installed `spirv-val` rejects. HLSL's matrix-to-flat-vector
     packing (e.g. `asin(float4x4(...))`) produces a poison value,
     triggering this on any matrix-library call.
   - **Bug 2**: the SPIR-V backend's `requiresLongVectorEXT` assumed
     widths 8/16 could always use the native `Vector16` capability --
     but `Vector16` requires `Kernel`, illegal under Vulkan's `Shader`
     model. Any Shader module needing an 8/16-wide vector hit a hard
     `report_fatal_error`.

3. **Fixed both, each its own isolated, self-contained, tested commit**
   (per the standing "issue outside FeMe" instruction):
   - `8e39ea0bc0bc`: made `requiresLongVectorEXT`/`isLongVectorEXT`
     subtarget-aware (`CanUseVector16`); fixed a stale assertion in
     `getOpTypeVectorIdEXT` it exposed; new regression test
     `vector8-16-shader-vs-kernel.ll`. Full `llvm/test/CodeGen/SPIRV`
     (1356 tests): clean.
   - `49f6e56c765b`: excluded `SPV_KHR_poison_freeze` from the implicit
     `-spirv-ext=all` default. Updated existing
     `dxc_fspv_extension.hlsl`. Full `clang/test/Driver/*hlsl*`+`*dxc*`
     (39 tests): clean.

4. **Confirmed the real-world impact was zero on the 92-count** --
   not glossed over. Exact before/after test-name diff (not just
   counts) showed the identical 92 failures. Dug into *why*: every
   `_mat.test` file in the suite also exercises a `float4x4` (16-wide)
   shape, which hits a *third*, distinct, not-yet-fixed blocker even
   with both fixes applied -- `spirv-val` rejects the
   `OpVectorShuffle` sequence that reassembles a 16-wide
   `OpTypeVectorIdEXT` matrix row-by-row (`"Component index 16 is out
   of bounds for combined (Vector1 + Vector2) size of 16"`), even
   though the index is in-bounds for the true 32-element combined
   operand space. Looks like a `spirv-val` length-tracking gap for
   `OpTypeVectorIdEXT`, not a new bug of its own -- not yet confirmed
   which side should carry the fix. Split off as new roadmap row
   `L428(a)` rather than guessed at.

5. **Verified no regressions anywhere**: `check-feme` 3760/3768 (same
   1 pre-existing unrelated failure as every prior session since
   `L426`/`L429`, not touched); targeted `VK-GL-CTS` regression subset
   (`opatomic*`: 19/26 Pass/7 NotSupported/0 Fail;
   `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.*`: 606/624 Pass) byte-identical to the
   `L429`-session baseline, as expected (these fixes live in the
   SPIR-V *producer* path, not FeMe's own Vulkan *consumer* path the
   CTS exercises).

6. **Updated `Roadmap.md`** (`L428` struck through with full findings;
   new `L428(a)` row added, nested only one lowercase letter deep per
   the standing instruction) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new section).
   No `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md`/`VulkanExtensionInventory.md`
   update needed -- confirmed, not skipped: pure compiler-producer-side

   through, `VulkanCTSReport.md` new section, `FeMeCPUDesign.md`
   milestone-9 note updated, `Vulkan14FeatureInventory.md` rows
   annotated, `VulkanExtensionInventory.md` + its driving
   `PlannedExtensions.txt`/`CorePromotedNotAdvertisedExtensions.txt`
   moved `VK_KHR_variable_pointers` to "Implemented").

## What went sideways (useful if this recurs)

Writing the 2 new unit tests was not a straight line -- 3 separate false
starts, each informative:

1. First attempt used `@llvm.dx.thread.id` to drive the `select`'s
   condition (to make it genuinely divergent, matching the real CTS
   shape). This made the raw *global* itself get widened/broadcast by
   `FunctionWidener`'s own generic machinery *before* my code ever saw
   it, tripping an unrelated pre-existing "unrecognized broadcast" error
   (a raw global used directly as a `select` leg, with no intervening
   `getelementptr`, isn't a shape `hasOnlySupportedBroadcasts` was ever
   designed to accept). Fixed by using an opaque external `@cond()` call
   instead -- keeps the whole function uniform, no widening at all,
   still exercises the merge-retargeting logic directly.
2. The self-referential-phi test's loop had a thread-id-derived branch
   condition (needed, to match the real divergent-loop shape) but
   `runPass()` alone doesn't run `LinearizePass` first, so the divergent
   branch tripped SIMDize's own "divergent branch not removed" bail-out.
   Fixed by calling `feme::cpu::LinearizePass().run(*M, MAM)` before
   `runPass(*M)`, matching the existing pattern other loop/branch tests
   in the same file already use.
3. First test's final assertion (`isa<SelectInst>(&I) &&
   I.getType()->isPointerTy()`) failed even on a *correct* run, because
   the retargeted `select` legitimately still exists -- just now typed
   as plain `ptr` (address space 0), not `ptr addrspace(3)`. The check
   was testing the wrong thing; fixed to check address-space-3 pointer
   type specifically, matching every other test in the file's own
   convention.

Lesson for next time: when hand-writing an IR unit test for a
divergence-dependent code path, temporarily print the diagnostic handler's
actual message (`DiagnosticPrinterRawOStream`) and/or dump the module
after `runPass` -- guessing from `SawError`/bare assertions alone wastes
several rebuild cycles.

# Session: L302 closed, L432 opened -- a 9,795-case CFG-linearization gap found, root-caused, deliberately not fixed yet

## What happened

1. Confirmed device: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` via `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` (plain
   `vulkaninfo` still shows `llvmpipe` by default -- same every session).
2. Scanned `Roadmap.md` for open rows. Found `L302` (CTS sampling of
   `api.*`/`synchronization.*`, explicitly flagged "overdue many sessions")
   still had three unsampled batches. Picked it up.
3. **Hit a real methodology bug before trusting any result**: `run_vulkan_cts.py`
   inherits the caller's env rather than setting `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` itself, and
   each tool call is a fresh shell with no persisted state. Two batches ran
   against system-default `llvmpipe`, not FeMe, completely silently. Caught it
   by isolating one "Fail" case and re-running it standalone -- got a
   *different* result than the batch's own internal re-check of the same case
   name. That contradiction was the tell. Redid all three batches with
   `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` explicitly exported in the same bash call as the runner.
4. Results, all FeMe-verified this time:
   - Small/medium `api.*` leftovers (13,865 cases): 7,041 Pass, 6,823
     NotSupported, **1 Fail** -- already-known, already-filed won't-fix
     `L412(g)`. Clean.
   - `synchronization.op` (20,131 cases): 4,899 Pass, 5,437 NotSupported,
     **9,795 Fail** -- all one root cause (see below).
   - `copy_and_blit`/`image_clearing` (55,122 cases, previously skipped as
     "too large"): 23,108 Pass, 32,014 NotSupported, **0 Fail**. Clean.
5. The 9,795 sync.op failures all trace to one diagnostic:
   `feme-cpu-linearize: ... loop ... has a mask-affecting operation in its
   body but no recognized uniform exit check`. This was *known* (mentioned
   inside the already-closed `K6u`/`K6v` rows) but never given its own
   roadmap item. Dumped the real failing IR (`FEME_DUMP_IR_PRENORM=1`
   against `deqp-vk` directly, since the failure is *inside* `LinearizePass`)
   for `write_blit_image_read_image_compute.image_128_r32_uint_concurrent`:
   a plain `for(i=0;i<128;++i){load;store;}` loop where the real uniform
   check sits one *unconditional* hop past `Header`, and its exit routes
   through a shared `Flow`-style dispatch block with **phi-merged boolean
   operands** -- distinct from `K6v`'s already-fixed phi-less, one-hop-
   upstream-of-`Latch` shape.
6. Read `matchExitCheckWithRelay`/`recoverRelayExitCheck`/`isPureRelayBlock`/
   `OtherCondBrBlocks`/`DivergentCandidates` in `Linearize.cpp` in detail.
   Root cause confirmed: the existing "check lives somewhere other than
   `Header`/`Latch`" recovery path is gated on `isDivergentBranch` --
   it only ever promotes a non-`Header`/`Latch` block into the real-check
   role when that block is genuinely divergent. This shape's check and its
   merge block are both fully *uniform*, so neither is ever considered.
7. **Decided not to attempt the fix this session.** A forward-walk
   generalization of `K6v`'s promotion (mirroring `uniformRelayChain`'s
   existing backward walk) looks tractable in principle, but
   `OtherCondBrBlocks` has *two* members in this shape (not one), and
   `K6u`/`K6v`/`K6w` each took a full dedicated session for one distinct
   CFG sub-shape in this exact file. Filed it instead as `L432` (full
   root-cause writeup) with `L432(a)` breaking down the concrete fix steps,
   so a future session can start implementing immediately instead of
   re-deriving the root cause.
8. Closed `L302` in `Roadmap.md` (struck through); logged everything in
   `VulkanCTSReport.md`. No FeMe source changes this session, so reran
   `check-feme` (3762/3770, same pre-existing failure) and
   `check-hlsl-feme-vk` (492/492) purely as a sanity check, not because
   anything could have regressed.

## A flake worth noting but NOT a real bug

One single `vulkaninfo` call with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES`+`VK_DRIVER_FILES` both
set returned `llvmpipe` instead of FeMe -- looked like a serious new
both-vars-set loader bug at first. Retested 20+ times afterward (both vars,
just one var) and got `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device` every single time. Could not
reproduce. Treating it as a one-off transient (maybe a stray background
process mid-init at that exact moment), not a real finding. Flagging here
only so a future session doesn't waste time chasing it as a phantom "both
vars breaks things" theory -- it doesn't, as far as 20 repeated trials show.

## Wins

- `L302` fully closed -- the last standing "overdue many sessions" sampling
  gap is gone.
- Found the single highest-leverage known compiler gap in the whole project
  right now: one diagnostic, 9,795 cases in one CTS subgroup alone.
- Root-caused it precisely enough that a future session can start coding

- Caught a real methodology bug (env not persisting across tool calls) via
  cross-checking rather than trusting a single run -- exactly the kind of
  thing that could otherwise poison a whole session's conclusions.
- `copy_and_blit`/`image_clearing`, the two biggest previously-"too large"

# Session: L432(b)/L432(c) -- the `synchronization.op` CFG-linearization gap actually fixed, 1,259 cases flipped, one self-caught regression

Confirmed device: `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. ✅

## Do this first

Nothing blocking -- this session's work is committed, `check-feme` is
clean (modulo one pre-existing, unrelated failure), and the next open
item has its own next-step text below.

## What happened (in order)

1. Picked up `L432(a)`'s plan: add a forward-walk check-recovery helper
   (`findForwardExitCheckBlock`) to `Linearize.cpp` for the real CTS
   repro (`write_blit_image_read_image_compute.
   image_128_r32_uint_concurrent`).
2. The forward-walk alone wasn't enough -- traced the remaining failure
   to a *different*, narrower bug: `DiamondFlattener::run()`'s own
   whole-function validation pass poisons the shared `MergeVisited` set
   with zero rollback when it decides there's nothing to flatten,
   permanently "claiming" blocks `LoopLinearizer` itself still needs.
   Fixed that (`L432(b)`'s real fix) by reusing the existing
   `LastRegionVisited` tracking member inside `run()` for the first
   time, with rollback at both of its early-return paths.
3. Wrote and validated a new regression test
   (`DoesNotPoisonMergeVisitedWhenWholeFunctionPassDeclines`) --
   deliberately confirmed it fails without the fix and passes with it,
   not just that it passes.
4. Ran the mandatory `ninja check-feme` before committing anything (per
   standing instructions) -- caught a real regression this session's
   own forward-walk fix introduced: no divergence gate, so a genuinely
   divergent separate check (pre-existing test
   `loop-check-separate-carried-value.ll`) got claimed by *both* the
   new path and the pre-existing `OtherCondBrBlocks` machinery,
   crashing. Fixed (`L432(c)`) with a one-line divergence gate.
5. Confirmed (via `git stash` to a clean baseline) that the *other*
   `check-feme` failure (`entry-wrapper-loop-header-derived-value-in-
   suffix.ll`) is pre-existing and unrelated -- not something this
   session touched or needs to fix.
6. Re-verified everything: unit tests 638/638, `check-feme` 3763/3771
   (1 pre-existing unrelated failure, 0 new), target CTS repro Pass,
   full `synchronization.op` sweep 6,158 Pass (up 1,259) / 5,437
   NotSupported / 8,536 Fail.

## Why this took three distinct bug fixes, not one

The original `L432(a)` plan assumed one gap (no forward-walk check
recovery). The real system had three independent bugs stacked on top
of each other for this one CTS case to actually pass:
`findForwardExitCheckBlock` itself (new), the whole-function
`MergeVisited` poisoning bug it exposed (pre-existing, never triggered
before because nothing used to walk far enough to hit it), and the
divergence-gate omission in the new helper (caused by the new helper
itself, caught by `check-feme` before it ever reached a commit). This
is exactly why the standing "run `check-feme` before any commit"
instruction exists -- it caught a real crash that the targeted CTS case
and the unit tests alone would never have surfaced.

  flipped from Fail to Pass.

  via the mandatory `check-feme` run -- exactly the safety net it's
  there for.
- The remaining 8,536 `synchronization.op` failures all now collapse to

1. Picked up the prior session's exact handoff (scope one `K6z`/`L425` sub-shape): used `dEQP-VK.synchronization.op.single_queue.fence.write_image_tess_eval_read_image_tess_control.image_128_r32_uint`, already isolated and captured via `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRELINEARIZE=1` at session start.

Bisected a standalone `.ll` repro down to the smallest failing case via `feme-opt --llvm -passes=feme-cpu-linearize` (fast iteration, no CTS/Vulkan needed): a single `feme.stage.output.store.f32` call before an otherwise-uniform loop is enough to trigger the bug -- the loop shape alone does *not* reproduce it.

Root-caused: `DiamondFlattener::run()`'s commit path (taken when a mask-affecting op forces it, instead of the `L432(b)`-fixed decline path) never inserts its own visited blocks into `ResolvedBlocks` after committing -- unlike its sibling methods `flattenLoopBodyDiamond`/`flattenLoopBodyRegion`, which both do. 9. Committed in 3 separate commits: fix (`isLoopControlEdge`/`canReachBlock`), regression test, docs.

## Root cause, short version

`CycleInfo CI` is computed once per function and never recomputed, even though `linearizeCyclePostOrder` mutates the CFG between cycles (unlike `DT`/`PDT`, recomputed before every `linearizeCycle` call). Once an inner uniform loop is linearized, its own redundant-`Flow`-block collapse can sever a relay block's path back to the header -- but `CI.contains` still reports it as a cycle member (static snapshot, dominance unaffected too). This fooled `isLoopControlEdge` into treating the inner loop's exit check as an ordinary diamond when the *outer* loop's precheck later walked through it, tripping "empty diamond arm." Fixed `isLoopControlEdge` to fall back to a live, cycle-membership-bounded BFS (`canReachBlock`) whenever `CI.contains` says "still a member," rather than trusting the stale snapshot outright. A full `CI.compute(F)` mid-traversal recompute was rejected: `CycleRef` handles are only valid until the next recompute, and the post-order traversal holds them across recursive stack frames.

## Results at a glance

| What | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `synchronization.op.*` Pass | 8,670 | 14,694 |
| `synchronization.op.*` Fail | 6,024 | 0 |
| Target repro case | Fail | Pass |
| `check-feme` | 3763/3771 (1 pre-existing fail) | 3765/3773 (same 1 pre-existing fail) |

## Debugging-technique note for future sessions

The `L433`-session-inherited "re-run a failed `Quiet=true` `validate()`/`canFlattenLoopBodyRegion` call with `Quiet=false` to see the real diagnostic" trick is **not safe as-is**: `validate()` doesn't roll back its own `MergeVisited`/`LastRegionVisited` insertions on failure, so the second call starts from a dirtied state and can manufacture a false diagnostic. Fixed this session by snapshotting/restoring both sets around the probe (then reverted along with the rest of the debug instrumentation, since it was debugging-aid-only, not part of the shipped fix). If a future session reuses this re-run trick, reintroduce the snapshot/restore -- don't just re-call `validate()` naively.

## Why this one closed the *entire* remaining failure set (not a partial fix like L432(b)/L433)

Unlike `L432(b)`/`L433`, where the fix's blast radius was large-but-partial (1,259 and 2,512 of a larger remaining pool, respectively), this fix's 6,024-case blast radius was the *entire* remaining pool. Best guess: every CFG shape left in this diagnostic family's `synchronization.op` presence, by this point, happened to involve a since-collapsed child cycle's relay edge being misread by `isLoopControlEdge` -- i.e. the family had already been narrowed down (by `L432(b)`/`L433`) to cases that all shared this one specific staleness mechanism, even though the actual *surface* CFG shapes (single mask-op-adjacent loop vs. two nested loops) looked different.

# Session: L435 -- multithreaded device-create segfault root-caused as an external Vulkan-Loader race

Run `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` first thing, every session -- confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`. Repo tree was clean on start (summarized handoff said this session was mid-investigation, no edits applied yet).

## Where this picked up

Prior session (summarized) found a ~50-80%-reproducible segfault in `dEQP-VK.api.object_management.multithreaded_per_thread_resources.device` while running a fresh `api.*` sweep (`L302`'s own "start fresh with a different family" next step). Core-dump analysis had already pointed at the system Vulkan loader, not FeMe code, but hadn't confirmed it with a targeted ASan rebuild yet. This session's job: finish that.

## What got done (in order)

1. **Targeted mixed-instrumentation ASan build.** `FeMeVulkanCore`/`feme_vulkan` recompiled with `-fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer`, everything else (LLVM/MLIR static libs, `deqp-vk`, the system loader) untouched. Hit a real environment gap first: this clang install has **no bundled compiler-rt ASan runtime archive** for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` (`libclang_rt.asan_static.a` etc. don't exist, no apt package available either). Worked around it: `-fsanitize=address -fno-sanitize-link-runtime` (suppresses clang's own runtime auto-link) + explicitly `target_link_libraries(... /usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/15/libasan.a)` (the system GCC package's own static ASan runtime, ABI-compatible since both toolchains target the same Itanium C++ ABI/libstdc++ here). Verified this mixing actually works correctly with a standalone 5-line heap-overflow repro before trusting it on the real build.
2. **Ran the repro 8x against the instrumented build: 0 crashes, 0 ASan reports.** Same repro against a clean (reverted) rebuild: 5/10 crashes. This swing is the single most informative data point this session -- ASan's allocator (redzones + delayed-reuse quarantine) changes heap *reuse timing* enough to close the race window, without any FeMe code actually behaving differently. Classic signature of an allocator-timing-gated UAF/address-reuse race in code ASan never got to instrument (i.e., not in FeMe).
3. **Read every FeMe object on the crash path start to finish** (`Icd.h`, `EntryPoints.cpp`, `ProcAddr.cpp`, `Objects.h`, `PipelineCache.cpp`) -- no shared mutable state across concurrently-created `Device`s found. The one shared object (`PhysicalDevice`/`PhysicalDeviceInfo`) is computed once, never mutated.
4. **Read the actual CTS test source** (`vktApiObjectManagementTests.cpp` in VK-GL-CTS, not this repo) to confirm what the test actually does: many threads racing `vkCreateDevice`/`vkDestroyDevice` against one shared `VkPhysicalDevice`, with a `barrier()` specifically to force concurrent entry into the driver. This is exactly the gap the Vulkan spec's per-object external-synchronization rule doesn't cover -- it's the loader's own shared dispatch bookkeeping that has to handle it, not the ICD.
5. **Confirmed via web/GitHub research**: `KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Loader` issue #200 is the same general class of bug (`vkCreateDevice`/`vkDestroyDevice`/`vkGetDeviceProcAddr` dispatch-table race), closed 2022 by a mutex around `loader.instances`. The installed loader here (`libvulkan1` 1.4.341.0-1) is years newer, so this isn't literally that unpatched bug -- but it's the same *family* of "per-call sync isn't enough" loader bug.
6. **Confirmed not fixable here**: the loader (`/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libvulkan.so.1`) is a separately-installed system package, not vendored anywhere in `llvm-project`. Reverted the temporary ASan CMake diagnostic changes (`feme/lib/Vulkan/CMakeLists.txt`) before doing anything else.
7. **Documented it**: `Roadmap.md` new `L435` row (not struck through -- same precedent as `L428(a)`, a confirmed-external finding with no further in-repo action), `VulkanCTSReport.md` full write-up. Committed as a docs-only change (no code diff).
8. **Rebuilt + ran `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`**: 638/638, matching the pre-session baseline exactly -- confirms this session made zero code changes and zero regressions.
9. **Re-checked standing items**: `offload-test-suite` `feme`-branch drift still shows the same single remote-only commit (`0cc94c2`, unchanged) 1 behind / 8 ahead (ahead count grew by 1 vs. last session's "7 ahead" from ordinary local history, not new drift). `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` flake: confirmed still present (1 failure in 3 `check-hlsl-feme-vk` runs) -- still not picked up as its own item.
10. **Resumed the interrupted broader `dEQP-VK.api.*` sweep** (267,512 cases) via `feme/utils/run_vulkan_cts.py`'s crash-tolerant batch harness (launched async, `--workers 6`, no `--deqp-vk-arg` env-var mistake this time -- `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` has to be a real env var on the invoking shell, not passed through `--deqp-vk-arg`, which only forwards CLI flags to `deqp-vk` itself). Still running as this entry is being written; results not in yet.

## The ASan-no-runtime-archive gotcha (save future sessions the rediscovery)

This environment's clang (`clang-21`, from apt) has **no compiler-rt sanitizer archives installed** for `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu` -- `-fsanitize=address` alone fails to link (`cannot find .../libclang_rt.asan_static.a`). No `libclang-rt-21-dev`-style package is available via apt either (no candidate). The system **does** have the GCC package's own static ASan runtime (`/usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/15/libasan.a`, matching `libasan8`'s shared counterpart already used for `LD_PRELOAD` probes in earlier sessions). Workaround, verified to work correctly end-to-end:

```cmake
target_compile_options(<target> PUBLIC -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
target_link_options(<target> PUBLIC -fsanitize=address -fno-sanitize-link-runtime)
target_link_libraries(<target> PUBLIC /usr/lib/gcc/aarch64-linux-gnu/15/libasan.a)
```

Order matters: use `target_link_libraries` (not `target_link_options`/`-l:libasan.a`), so CMake places it *after* the target's own static archive on the link line -- static archives only resolve symbols from libraries listed afterward. Getting this backwards produces a wall of `undefined reference to '__asan_report_load1'`-style errors that look unrelated to link ordering at first glance.

## `api.*` sweep: done, this session

Completed (267,512/267,512 cases, 0 unrun): **116,730 Pass / 150,781 NotSupported / 1 Fail**. The harness's crash-recovery transparently absorbed the `L435` race (plus one `copy_and_blit` case that raced the same way) -- both reconciled to Pass once re-verified alone, no manual work needed. The 1 remaining Fail (`dEQP-VK.api.driver_properties.conformance_version`) is **by design**, not a bug: `FeMeVulkanDesign.md`'s own "Initial Non-Goals" require a truthful zero `VkConformanceVersion` rather than a false conformance claim, and this exact CTS case checks that a driver's conformance version isn't older than its claimed `apiVersion` -- which a genuinely zero value always is. Documented in `VulkanCTSReport.md`; no roadmap row opened, no fix applied.

## Next steps

1. **(~1 day, start fresh)** `api.*` is now at its intended design ceiling (1 expected-by-design Fail, 0 unexplained). Pick a *different*, not-yet-exhaustively-swept family next -- `copy_and_blit`/`image_clearing` (both only ever sampled by `L302`, same as `api.*` was before this session).
2. **(~15 min, cheap)** Clean up `/tmp/l435_*`, `/tmp/asan_run_*`, `/tmp/asan_instr_*`, `/tmp/mt_device_*`, `/tmp/clean_rebuild_*`, `/tmp/t2*` -- all regenerable, not yet deleted as of this writing.
3. **(standing, many sessions now)** `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` flake -- confirmed present again this session, still not picked up as its own item.
4. **(standing)** `offload-test-suite` `feme`-branch drift -- same single commit (`0cc94c2`), unchanged, still needs a decision from a session actually touching `offload-test-suite`.
5. **(low priority, future stress test)** If a future session touches multithreaded device lifecycle again and hits a similar crash, check this `L435` writeup first before re-deriving the ASan-no-runtime-archive workaround or re-reading the same FeMe object files -- they were already read clean this session.

In the process of cross-checking this against `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s big master table, found that table's `api` row is **stale** (says 21 Fail, actual current count per this session's own fresh re-sweep is 1) -- it's a frozen 2026-10-12 snapshot that many since-then sessions' fixes never got folded back into.

## What actually happened, in order

1. Confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, clean tree, no new `offload-test-suite` drift (still just `0cc94c2`).
2. Tried to generate case lists for `copy_and_blit`/`image_clearing` as separate families per the handoff -- got 0 cases both times. Turned out they're `dEQP-VK.api.copy_and_blit.*`/`dEQP-VK.api.image_clearing.*` subgroups, not top-level groups. (Lesson: always verify a group actually exists via `--deqp-runmode=stdout-caselist`'s `GROUP:` lines before trusting a name from a prior session's prose.)

Picked `synchronization` (64,872 total) since `L432`-`L434` only ever fixed its `.op` subgroup (20,131 of those cases) -- sweeping the whole family directly validates those fixes didn't miss anything in the other 9 subgroups.
4. **First launch attempt failed silently**: backgrounded the harness with a shell `&` inside a `sync`-mode bash call. The moment the tool call returned (right after the `&`), the session's shell process tree got torn down, killing the harness mid-run with no error surfaced. Lesson re-learned (should have remembered from the tool description): background work that needs to survive a `bash` tool call returning must use `mode="async"`, not shell-level `&`.
5. Relaunched correctly with `mode="async"`. Completed in ~1 minute (much faster than `api.*` -- `win32_keyed_mutex`'s 1,964 cases are instant `NotSupported` on this Linux host, and the family is a quarter the size of `api.*`).

This sweep was a **re-confirmation**, not new data. Still useful (zero regression after `L432`-`L434`, across every subgroup those fixes didn't directly touch), but not the "fresh family" I thought I was picking.

While looking at that table more carefully, noticed its `api` row says `21` Fail / `16` TimedOut -- but this session's own complete `api.*` re-sweep (and the prior `L435` session's) found only **1** Fail, **0** TimedOut. Read the table's preamble: it's an exact, frozen snapshot of one specific full 3,253,584-case run from 2026-10-12, explicitly "supersedes...all partial counts previously recorded," not a living document that gets row-edited after every subsequent fix. Many `L4xx` sessions since then fixed individual `api.*` cases without this one row being touched.

Every other row in that table (`pipeline`, `image`, `spirv_assembly`, etc.) almost certainly has the same staleness to some degree -- nobody's been going back to update this one master table after each individually-tracked fix.

The "pick a different, not-yet-swept family" framing from several recent sessions' next-steps was built on an implicit assumption that most `dEQP-VK.*` families still need their *first* sweep. That's not true anymore -- the 2026-10-12 full run (`## Per-group accounting` in `VulkanCTSReport.md`) already covers **every** group in the entire CTS, not just the ones broken out in the explicit table (the doc says outright: "all omitted groups have only Pass and NotSupported results"). # Session: L437 -- the Mandelbrot flake was never a flake: `lit` never passed the timeout env var through

## TL;DR

Confirmed device (`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`), clean tree, `offload-test-suite` drift unchanged (`0cc94c2`). Launched the multi-day full-CTS re-triage (3.25M cases, background, still running, ~190/1,800+ batches done -- not finished, don't expect it to be). While that ran, found the real bug behind `Basic/Mandelbrot.test`'s years-long "rare flake": **it isn't rare, isn't contention-dependent, and isn't a FeMe bug.** `offload-test-suite/test/lit.cfg.py` never passed `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` through to the test subprocess, so every session's `30000` setting was silently ignored and the ICD always used its hardcoded 5-second default. Under light load, 5 seconds was always enough, so it looked fixed. Under this session's heavy background sweep, it wasn't. One-line fix, in `offload-test-suite`, verified 5/5 FAIL -> 13/13 PASS under identical load.

## What actually happened, in order

1. Confirmed device, clean tree, `offload-test-suite` drift unchanged.
2. Generated the full `dEQP-VK.*` case list: 3,253,584 cases, matches the known 2026-10-12 baseline exactly.
3. Launched the full re-triage correctly this time with `mode="async"` (learned last session: shell `&` inside a sync call gets killed the instant the call returns). Confirmed running: 8 processes, batches being produced.
4. While it ran in the background, did the prior session's suggested "bigger Mandelbrot sample": 30 isolated runs. **Result: 30/30 FAIL.** Every prior session (most recently last session, 0/12) had seen this pass almost always. The one new variable: this session has the CTS sweep hammering 8 cores continuously (load average ~7.4/12).
5. First hypothesis: just contention, needs more timeout budget. Tried `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS=180000` (6x normal). **Still failed, in ~5.4 seconds** -- nowhere near 180s. That's the tell: whatever timeout is actually firing is not the one the env var controls.
6. Read `feme/lib/Vulkan/Sync.cpp`'s `vkWaitSemaphores` (line 943) and `vkWaitForFences`: both correctly call `applyWaitSafetyNet(timeout)`, which correctly reads `getSafetyNetTimeoutNs()`, which correctly parses `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` from the environment. The FeMe code is fine. So the env var must not be reaching the process at all.
7. Read `offload-test-suite/test/lit.cfg.py`: it calls `llvm_config.with_system_environment([...])` with a list of `VK_*` vars only -- `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` was never in it.
8. Read `llvm/utils/lit/lit/TestingConfig.py` to confirm how lit actually builds a test's environment: it is **not** a copy of the invoking shell's environment. It's a fixed allowlist (`PATH`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, sanitizer vars, a short fixed list) plus whatever `lit.cfg.py` explicitly adds. Anything not on that list is simply absent from the subprocess's env, no matter what's set outside lit.
9. This means `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS=30000`, set on the outer `ninja check-hlsl-feme-vk` command line since `L255` and re-confirmed as recently as `L431`, **has never once reached the actual test subprocess, in any session.** The ICD has always silently used its hardcoded `DefaultSafetyNetTimeoutNs` (5 seconds, `Sync.h`) instead.
10. Fix: added `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` to the `with_system_environment` allowlist in `offload-test-suite/test/lit.cfg.py`. One line.
11. Verified with a clean A/B, same heavy background load the whole time (load average ~7): reverted the fix via `git stash` -> **5/5 FAIL**. Restored it -> **10/10 PASS at the real `30000` build value, 3/3 PASS at `180000`.** 13/13 total.
12. Committed the fix alone in `offload-test-suite` (outside `feme/`, as required).
13. Ran `ninja check-hlsl-feme-vk`: **492/492 Passed, 0 Failed** -- while the CTS sweep was still running in the background the whole time. This is the test that would have failed before the fix.
14. Ran `ninja check-feme`: **3765/3773 Passed, 7 Unsupported, 1 Failed** -- the same pre-existing, already-tracked `entry-wrapper-loop-header-derived-value-in-suffix.ll` failure, not new. No FeMe source was touched this session, so this is expected, not a regression check surprise.
15. Updated `Roadmap.md` (`L437` row) and `VulkanCTSReport.md` (new section, plus noted the full re-triage is in-progress, not replacing the master table yet). Committed docs separately from the `offload-test-suite` fix, per the "small, separate commits" instruction.

## Why this matters more than a normal bugfix

This wasn't just "found and fixed one more bug." It silently invalidated the stated justification of several previous sessions' conclusions:
- `L431` ran `check-hlsl-feme-vk` and reported "492/492 Passed... confirming the flake stays fixed under full parallel load." That 492/492 was real, but the *reason* given (the 30s override holding) was wrong -- it passed because 5 seconds happened to be enough that day, not because the override worked.
- Every session that logged "Mandelbrot: N/M clean runs this session" as a standing low-priority item was, without knowing it, running an experiment gated on a variable (background system load) nobody had deliberately controlled for -- which is exactly why the failure rate looked random across sessions instead of settling to a stable low number.

General lesson: when an env var is "set" via an outer build/CI command, that is not proof it reaches the thing that's supposed to read it, if there's a test harness layer (like `lit`) in between with its own environment-hermeticity rules. Worth remembering for any other `FEME_*`-style knobs this project adds in the future that get set the same way (outer `cmake -E env` on a ninja custom command, consumed inside a `lit`-run test).

## Next steps

1. **(check-in, cheap)** The full-CTS re-triage (shellId from this session, `/tmp/l437_full_run/`) is still running, ~190/1,800+ batches in. A future session should check its progress first via `ls /tmp/l437_full_run/qpa/ | wc -l` and the report file, and only replace `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s master table once it's actually complete -- don't trust a partial count as final.
2. **(standing, now explained, probably closeable as "standing")** `Basic/Mandelbrot.test` -- no longer an open flake investigation. It was deterministic under sufficient background load and is now fixed at the actual root cause (lit env passthrough). A future session doesn't need to keep "spot-checking" it as a standing item; if it ever fails again, check first whether `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` is actually present in the failing subprocess's own environment (e.g. via `/proc/<pid>/environ`) before assuming a new regression.
3. **(standing)** `offload-test-suite` `feme`-branch-vs-`main` drift -- still the same single commit (`0cc94c2`), unchanged. This session *did* touch `offload-test-suite` (the lit.cfg.py fix), but that's a local, uncommitted-upstream change on top of the existing drift, not a resolution of the drift question itself -- still needs its own decision from a session that wants to actually reconcile it.
4. **(worth a quick look, ~15 min)** Grep `offload-test-suite/test/CMakeLists.txt` and `lit.cfg.py` for any *other* `FEME_*`-prefixed env vars set on the outer build command the same way `FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` was -- if any exist, they likely have the exact same silent-no-op bug and are worth checking/fixing in the same pass.
5. **(when the full re-triage finally completes)** Replace `VulkanCTSReport.md`'s entire master per-group table in one pass (per `L436`'s own recommendation), rather than patching individual rows piecemeal.

# Session: L439 -- closed the `offload-test-suite` "drift" as a false positive, verified sweep health

## TL;DR

Confirmed device (`FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`). Confirmed `/tmp/l437_full_run2/`'s detached full-CTS re-triage survived the session boundary and is still progressing (7 workers alive at session start, 9 by session end, load average ~8-10). Instead of re-deferring the standing `offload-test-suite` drift item for the Nth consecutive session, actually resolved it: the "7 ahead / 1 behind" status against `llvm-beanz/feme` is **not real content drift**. `git patch-id` proves the one "behind" commit (`0cc94c2`) is byte-identical in content to a commit already in this repo's own history (`b606d08`, a prior session's cherry-pick) -- `git log`'s hash-based ancestry check can't see that because `git cherry-pick` always produces a new commit object, even for identical content. Re-ran `check-hlsl-feme-vk` (492/492 Passed) as the no-FeMe-changes sanity check.

## What actually happened, in order

1. `vulkaninfo --summary | grep deviceName` (with `VK_ICD_FILENAMES` exported) -> `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`, confirmed.
2. Checked both repos: `llvm-project` and `offload-test-suite` both clean, consistent with the last session's end state.
3. Checked on `/tmp/l437_full_run2/`: `ps aux` showed the orchestrator plus 6-7 `deqp-vk` workers still alive, one full 1800/1800 batch already done, others mid-flight. The detached-launch fix from `L438` is confirmed working across a second session boundary now.
4. Looked at the handoff's 5 items: #1 (check-in) done; #2 (replace master table) not yet actionable, sweep still far from complete; #4/#5 already closed in prior sessions. That left #3, the standing `offload-test-suite` drift item, flagged "needs a decision" for several sessions running without anyone actually investigating it properly -- decided to do that this session since the user's task explicitly asks for a decision from a session touching that repo.
5. Re-fetched `llvm-beanz/feme`, re-ran `git log origin/main..llvm-beanz/feme` -- still just `0cc94c2`, touching only `CMakeLists.txt`/`test/CMakeLists.txt`/`test/lit.cfg.py`.
6. Diffed `0cc94c2`'s content against current HEAD for those same three files -- the only differences were this/prior sessions' own additive fixes (`FEME_VULKAN_SAFETY_NET_TIMEOUT_MS` allowlist line, the `with_system_environment` fix, one unrelated `%api_query` substitution). That strongly suggested `0cc94c2`'s own content was already present somewhere in local history under a different commit hash.
7. Scanned `git log` for a commit with the same author/date/message as `0cc94c2` -- found `b606d08`, a local cherry-pick from a prior session.
8. Ran `git show 0cc94c2 | git patch-id` and `git show b606d08 | git patch-id` -- **identical patch-id** (`47914dcf...`). This is a content hash that ignores commit metadata (parent, committer date, tree ancestry), so an identical patch-id is conclusive proof the two commits apply the exact same change. Confirmed: no real drift, ever. Every prior session's "needs a decision" framing was a false positive caused by comparing commit hashes instead of commit content across a cherry-pick boundary.
9. Documented the technique and the specific finding in `feme/.instructions.md` (new final section) so no future session re-flags this.
10. Added `L439` to `Roadmap.md`, `done`, depending on `L437`/`L438` (the two sessions that most recently re-flagged this item).

13. Re-ran `check-feme`: 3765/3773 Passed, 7 Unsupported, 1 Failed (`entry-wrapper-loop-header-derived-value-in-suffix.ll`) -- exact same known baseline as every recent session, not a regression. No FeMe source was touched this session, consistent with this result.
14. Final check-in on `/tmp/l437_full_run2/`: 9 `deqp-vk` workers still alive, 9 batches now have qpa output (up from 7 at session start) -- sweep is healthy and progressing at a similar rate to before.

## Why this matters

This is the fourth or fifth consecutive session to carry "`offload-test-suite` drift, needs a decision" as a standing item without anyone actually running the one diagnostic (`git patch-id`) that would settle it. The lesson generalizes beyond this one repo: whenever a workflow repeatedly resets a branch to upstream and re-applies the same local changes via cherry-pick (as documented already in `.instructions.md` for this exact branch), `git log A..B` ahead/behind counts are structurally unreliable as a drift signal, because cherry-pick is specifically designed to reproduce content under a new hash. Any future "N ahead / M behind" finding on a cherry-pick-based branch should be checked with `git patch-id` *before* being written up as unresolved, not after several sessions of re-deferral.

A real fix requires teaching the masked-loop path (`DiamondFlattener`) to recognize a body-level break-to-same-cycle's-exit edge as a *third* distinct edge kind (not "ordinary diamond merge", not "different cycle's boundary"), then thread a sticky, loop-carried "this lane already broke" mask -- conceptually like `HeaderDivergent`'s own `stayInLoop`, but generalized to N distinct break points, each needing correct exit-block phi-value handling for whichever break actually fired. `Linearize.cpp` is 5000+ lines with a long history of subtle regressions requiring careful, test-first, full-CTS-verified fixes -- this is a multi-hour-plus lift that needs its own dedicated session, not a tail-end addition to this one. Reducing and test-pinning the gap first (this session) makes that future session's job much faster: it gets a precise red/green target instead of having to re-derive the root cause from CTS again.

## Why abandoned, not iterated further

Neither mechanism in isolation is a net win:
- Widening alone: 18 -> 18, but trades 6 fixed cases for 6 different new ones.
- Widening + phi-completeness fix (either mechanism): 18 -> 24, strictly worse.

Iterating to find the *actual* scoping bug in the widening's `OtherCondBrBlocks` matching, and separately the `feme-cpu-simdize` interaction with newly-correctly-masked loads, are each their own multi-hour investigations (same order of effort as this session's whole investigation so far). Landing either half-finished risks a real CTS regression if a future session trusts the "net 18" number without re-checking case names -- already nearly happened here (step 4 looked like a no-op until case-by-case diffing caught it).

## Key technical finding worth keeping (don't re-discover this)

`applyStageMasks` has ~14 call sites across `Linearize.cpp`, many of which call it on `Masks`/`EntryMasks` phis **before** `addLatchIncoming` has filled in the backedge value. This is not a bug by itself -- many of those call sites rely on the resulting premature fold for legitimate reasons not yet fully enumerated. The only call site where the premature fold is actually wrong is the one this session's widening newly exposes (a uniform body-level break reduced from `conditional_break_fragment`). Any future fix must be scoped to that one call site/shape, not change `lookThroughTrivialPhi`'s behavior globally.

# Session: L419(t) -- landed the scoped L419(h) widening fix (6 cases), deferred the deeper masking sequencing bug it exposed

**Next action for a future session:** read "Next steps" item 1 below, then fix `DiamondFlattener::flattenLoopBodyDiamond`'s stale uniform/divergent judgment (it needs to re-run, or defer, once masking is known) before re-attempting the poison-placeholder fix.

## What happened, in order

1. Resumed with the full L419(h) fix (widening + `StopBlock` fix + poison-placeholder phi-completeness fix) stashed from a prior, now-summarized session. `git stash pop` and rebuilt.
2. Root-caused the `select_iteration_count_{fragment,vertex}` regression the poison-placeholder half of the fix reintroduces (6 cases, the exact same regression `L419(h)`'s own prior attempt hit independently): `do_while_dynamic_iterations.select_iteration_count_fragment`'s loop *header itself* has its own internal if/else (reading a uniform buffer via `feme.cpu.resource.load.raw.i32`, reconverging later -- not a loop exit). `DiamondFlattener::flattenLoopBodyDiamond`'s own early fixed-point pre-pass judges this diamond's branch uniform *before* masking has run (the call's mask operand is still constant `true` at that point in both builds) and permanently declines to flatten it. In baseline, the original phi-completeness bug keeps that mask at `true` even *after* masking finishes, so the branch genuinely never becomes divergent -- accidentally safe. With the poison-placeholder fix, masking correctly narrows it to the real `active.live` value later, making the branch genuinely divergent for the first time -- but `flattenLoopBodyDiamond`'s one-time verdict has already stuck, so the real divergent branch survives untouched into `feme-cpu-simdize`'s own independent, later `UniformityInfo` computation, which correctly rejects it. A real, distinct sequencing bug, confirmed via `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD=1`/`FEME_DUMP_DIVERGENT_BRANCH=1` diffing baseline vs. fixed IR.

## Why landed now, not iterated further to also fix the masking gap

The `flattenLoopBodyDiamond` staleness bug is a distinct, deeper architectural issue (a one-time judgment made from a pre-masking snapshot, never revisited) -- not a quick follow-on fix. Landing the widening alone is a strict, CTS-verified improvement (+6, -0) with no known risk; attempting to also fix the masking gap in the same session risks landing something with a real regression under time pressure, as nearly happened with this exact combination across two separate sessions now (this one and an earlier, now-summarized one that hit the identical `select_iteration_count` regression independently).

## Key technical finding worth keeping (don't re-discover this)

`DiamondFlattener::flattenLoopBodyDiamond`'s uniform/divergent judgment on a loop-body diamond is made and cached *once*, before `applyStageMasks` has necessarily finished narrowing any resource/image load's mask operand away from its as-lowered constant `true`. If a future masking-completeness fix (like the poison-placeholder one, reverted here) makes a previously-constant mask genuinely non-constant *after* that one-time judgment already ran, the now-really-divergent branch is never re-flattened and survives into `feme-cpu-simdize`'s own later, independent `UniformityInfo` check, which rejects it. Fix needs to either re-run the judgment after masking is known, or defer committing to "uniform, leave it" until masking is finalized -- not just for `select_iteration_count`'s specific shape, but for any diamond built from a resource/image load result.

# Session: L419(v) -- root-caused L419(t)'s "deeper masking bug" end-to-end, no fix landed yet

**Next action for the next session**: read `feme/docs/Roadmap.md`'s `L419(v)`
row, then open `feme/lib/Transforms/CPU/Linearize.cpp` at
`LoopLinearizer::collectUniformPassThroughRegion` (~line 3896) and
`isDivergentBranch` (~line 3938). That's the exact bug location now --
no more tracing needed, only fix design + implementation.

## What this session did (device check confirmed `FeMe CPU Vulkan Device`)

1. Picked up prior session's #1 next step: find the real "second, deeper"
   bug blocking `L419(t)`'s abandoned poison-placeholder phi-completeness
   fix, since `L419(u)` already disproved its attribution to
   `DiamondFlattener::flattenLoopBodyDiamond`.
2. Reapplied the poison-placeholder fix experimentally in
   `makeActivePNPair`/`addLatchIncoming`, rebuilt `feme-opt`.
3. Diffed a standalone repro's Linearize output with/without the fix:
   confirmed both resource-load calls' mask operands flip from literal
   `i1 true` to the real `i1 %active.live` phi once the fix is applied --
   exactly as predicted.
4. Rebuilt `libfeme_vulkan.so` with the fix, ran the real failing case
   (`dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.special.do_while_dynamic_iterations.select_iteration_count_fragment`)
   with `FEME_DUMP_DIVERGENT_BRANCH=1`. Got the smoking gun:
   ```
   feme-cpu-simdize: divergent branch in block '':   br i1 %.not, label %27, label %._crit_edge
   error: ... has a divergent branch; the divergence transform ... did not remove it
   ```
   That's `Header`'s own internal `if`/`else` -- confirmed as the exact
   branch that goes divergent once the poison fix's masking is correct.
5. Reverted the experimental poison-fix code (`git checkout --`), rebuilt
   the clean baseline, re-verified `select_iteration_count_fragment` still
   Passes (accidentally-safe baseline behavior, unchanged).

## The actual root cause (confirmed, not a hypothesis anymore)

`collectUniformPassThroughRegion` decides whether `Header` is safe to
leave completely untouched using `isDivergentBranch`, which reads
`UniformityInfo` computed **once**, before this pass's own masking runs.
At that snapshot, `Header`'s resource-load call still has its original
constant-`true` mask, so `Header`'s branch looks uniform and gets
accepted into the pass-through region -- never flattened into masked
form. Later in the *same* `linearizeCycle` call, `applyStageMasks`
correctly narrows that same call's mask to the loop's real
`active.live` phi (non-constant for `_dynamic_iterations` loops, since
trip count is genuinely per-lane). The call's result is now genuinely
divergent, but `Header`'s `CondBr` was never converted to masked form --
so `feme-cpu-simdize`'s own later, independent uniformity check
(correctly) flags it and bails.

Why only `_dynamic_iterations` siblings break: `_uniform_iterations`
loops (e.g. `conditional_break_fragment`) take a completely different,
simpler fast path (`L292`) that skips building an `active.live` phi
unless the loop body has a `discard`/`demote`/etc. op -- so there's no
masking event to go stale for that shape.

## Why no fix landed this session

Two candidate fixes, both architecturally non-trivial:
- **(a)** Two-phase restructuring: decide region membership *after*
  masking is known. Chicken-and-egg -- masking depends on knowing which
  blocks are in the region.
- **(b)** Teach `isDivergentBranch`/`collectUniformPassThroughRegion` to
  predict ahead of time that a load's constant-`true` mask *will* go
  non-constant once this cycle's own masking runs, and pessimistically
  treat it (and branches depending on it) as divergent up front.

Both need careful design + testing across every loop shape that
currently passes through this code path -- not a same-session fix given
the risk of silently breaking the 540/552 currently-passing baseline.
Full writeup is in `Roadmap.md`'s `L419(v)` row and
`VulkanCTSReport.md`'s matching section (already committed).

- `/tmp/l437_full_run2/` background sweep: 84,381 qpa files this session

## The crash (fixed, no caveats)

`dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.special.do_while_uniform_iterations.dowhile_trap_fragment`
crashed the whole sweep (exit 134) via `cast<PHINode>` in
`rethreadNestedEntryMasks`. Cause: `foldNowTriviallyConstantMaskPhis`
can legitimately fold a fully-uniform child cycle's masks to a plain
`Constant`, and this function assumed they were always still a
`PHINode`. Fixed with `dyn_cast`. Verified: crash gone, 638/638 unit
tests, this specific case passes in isolation.

## The image-corruption bug (fixed, no caveats)

`conditional_break_{fragment,vertex}` produced a wrong rendered image
(not a crash, not a clean failure -- silently wrong). Bisected via
`git stash` + `FEME_DUMP_IR_PRESIMD=1` diffing: `flattenKnownDivergentBranch`
was discarding a genuine loop break's per-arm masks because its
reconvergence point is the cycle's own exit block, not a local diamond
-- its own prior doc comment already flagged this exact shape as
unsound. Added a `CI.contains(SC, R)` containment check. Now fails with
a clean diagnostic instead of corrupting the image -- a real safety
improvement even though it is not yet a Pass.

## The net-regression problem (NOT fully fixed -- this is the blocker)

Full `dEQP-VK.glsl.loops.special.*` sweep (552 cases) with both fixes
above: **524 Pass / 28 Fail**. Compared the 28 failures against an
untouched `git stash` baseline re-sweep: **16 of them PASS on
baseline** (all 6 `conditional_break_*`, 2x `dowhile_trap`
fragment/vertex, 6x `nested*`), 12 are pre-existing, unrelated
`L419(h)` residuals. So this session's starting point (poison-seed +
crash/corruption fixes, no gating) was **-9 net** vs the pre-poison-seed
baseline of 533 Pass.

Root cause: the poison seed taints *every* cycle's masks from creation,
regardless of whether that cycle ever needs real masking. Tried to fix
with a `CycleNeedsRealMasking` predicate gating whether the poison seed
is even used, through three iterations:

1. **Divergence-only** (`HeaderDivergent || LatchDivergent || a
   genuinely divergent OtherCondBrBlocks member`): fixed
   `conditional_break` (6 cases) AND kept `select_iteration_count`
   (6 cases) working -- 530/552. But broke the brand-new unit test
   `loop-internal-break-with-mask-op.ll` (a body-level break gating a
   real resource store) -- its mask operand stayed `true` instead of
   narrowing to `active.sideeffect`. A real correctness regression, just
   one this specific CTS repro happened not to expose.
2. **Added `cycleHasMaskOps(C)`** to the predicate: fixes the unit test
   correctly, but also re-enables the poison seed for
   `conditional_break` (any real shader touches *some* resource), which
   reverts it back to the diagnosed failure -- 524/552, identical to no
   gating at all. **This is the version committed** -- it is the only
   one with correct, lit-tested masking semantics. `conditional_break`'s
   own fix (letting its widened `CheckBlock` path actually flatten
   correctly) is separate, unstarted work, not yet filed as its own
   roadmap row.
3. **Tried excluding a nested child cycle's own header/latch from the
   *outer* cycle's `OtherCondBrBlocks` collection**
   (`CI.getCycle(&BB) == C`), suspecting this explains the 10
   `dowhile_trap`/`nested*` regressions (confirmed via trace: the inner
   cycle's own exit block shows up again in the outer cycle's
   `OtherCondBrBlocks` scan). **This caused an infinite loop in
   `FeMeTransformsCPUTests`** -- reverted immediately, did not
   investigate why (budget ran out). The fix needs to happen in
   `flattenTaintedBranchesInRegion`'s own candidate walk instead, where
   it can't affect anything else `OtherCondBrBlocks` is used for.
